thread.speaker: Chair
thread.said: The Chair stated that DepEd, including its attached agencies, was proposing a total FY 2027 budget of R975.96 billion dollars and said the committee would examine whether appropriations translated into better learning opportunities, stronger schools, and better-supported teachers.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juan Edgardo Sonny M. Angara
thread.said: Secretary Angara identified the proposed FY 2027 DepEd net budget, including attached agencies, as 975960000000 dollars.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juan Edgardo Sonny M. Angara
thread.said: He said the FY 2027 net budget was 975960000000 dollars, or 39350000000 dollars lower than FY 2026. He added that the National Museum of the Philippines was the only attached agency receiving a higher proposed allocation.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juan Edgardo Sonny M. Angara
thread.said: He said personal services represented about 79 percent of the budget, at around 7 66000000000 dollars, while MOE declined by 33000000000 dollars and capital outlay decreased by 67000000000.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juan Edgardo Sonny M. Angara
thread.said: He presented proposed investments including 12090000000 dollars for the expanded career progression program, 3750000000 dollars for training 500000 teachers, and laptops for 50000 teachers. He also cited 17310000000 dollars for more than 4000 classrooms.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juan Edgardo Sonny M. Angara
thread.said: He cited PHP3.37 billion for digital transformation and internet renewal in over 14000 schools, 6400000000 dollars for textbooks and other learning materials, and 2630000000 dollars for inclusive education.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juan Edgardo Sonny M. Angara
thread.said: He said 11430000000 had been allocated for the feeding program to support 3690000 learners, but the department was asking for additional funding for inclusive education, governance, and innovation.

thread.speaker: Rep. Edgar
thread.said: Rep. Edgar challenged the reductions, citing decreases of 64.2 percent for basic education facilities, 55 percent for school-based feeding, 66.8 percent for textbooks and instructional materials, 25 percent for new school personnel positions, 77 percent for infrastructure for safer and resilient schools, 45 percent for computerization, and 50 percent for the Basic Education Curriculum. He also cited zero funding for several voucher and innovation items.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juan Edgardo Sonny M. Angara
thread.said: Secretary Angara said DepEd requested that the school-feeding program be maintained at the current year's level. He explained that the FY 2027 proposal supported 120 days of feeding, whereas DepEd hoped to extend it to 180 days, citing evidence of improved weight gain, attendance, and learning outcomes.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juan Edgardo Sonny M. Angara
thread.said: He explained that lower voucher funding would mean fewer beneficiaries, but said vouchers also helped decongest public schools by placing learners in nearby private schools.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juan Edgardo Sonny M. Angara
thread.said: He clarified that the consolidated voucher program, including JDVP and ESC, amounted to PHP 38000000000, a decrease of around PHP 3000000000 from the previous year.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juan Edgardo Sonny M. Angara
thread.said: On classrooms, he said the department had around 60000000000 for infrastructure and new classrooms in the current historic budget, representing around 18000 classrooms, with another 16000 through public-private partnerships. He said this would still leave a classroom deficit of more than 140000.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juan Edgardo Sonny M. Angara
thread.said: He said DepEd was giving 283000 laptops in the current year, against about 870000 teachers, but the FY 2027 budget contained funding for only 50000 laptops. He requested an additional 10 b.

thread.speaker: Rep. Nelson Legacion
thread.said: Rep. Nelson Legacion highlighted the reduction in MOE from 207000000000 in FY 2026 to 174000000000 in the FY 2027 proposal, a difference of 33000000000 pesos. He asked about the resulting per-learner allocation and its effect on school operations and services.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juan Edgardo Sonny M. Angara
thread.said: Secretary Angara said MOE items included school feeding and textbooks, acknowledging that the allocation per learner would be affected to the extent that MOE was reduced.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juan Edgardo Sonny M. Angara
thread.said: On the Special Education Fund, he said local autonomy produced mixed experiences and that DepEd did not have coercive power over the use of the SEF; if that authority lay with any agency, he said it was probably with DOF.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juan Edgardo Sonny M. Angara
thread.said: In response to Rep. Presley de Jesus, he said education currently accounted for about 14.3 percent of the national budget, compared with the 20 percent level discussed for Vietnam.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juan Edgardo Sonny M. Angara
thread.said: Secretary Angara explained that lower funding would shorten feeding from 180 days to 120 days and reduce the number of beneficiaries. He said classroom funding was falling from around 65000000000 for new classrooms to around 14000000000 or 13000000000, affecting the rate at which DepEd could address a classroom deficit of around 142000.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juan Edgardo Sonny M. Angara
thread.said: Responding to questions about the declining total budget, he said DepEd had proposed 1100000000000 to DBM but the final figure reflected competing agency requests and the budget process. He said the FY 2026 increase was largely the product of congressional insertion.

thread.speaker: Rep. Antonino Roman III
thread.said: Rep. Antonino Roman III cited FY 2027 capital outlay of 32330000000 compared with approximately 99447000000 in FY 2026, or roughly a 67.5 percent reduction, and asked why funding was falling despite the classroom shortage.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juan Edgardo Sonny M. Angara
thread.said: He attributed the lower capital-outlay level largely to the unusually high FY 2026 amount produced during the congressional stage, as well as possible limitations in collections. He said DepEd was using LGU capacity, had signed memoranda with about 350 plus LGUs, and expected implementation results to improve over a one-and-a-half- to two-year horizon.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juan Edgardo Sonny M. Angara
thread.said: After Rep. Roman asked whether the classroom priority master list was publicly available, Secretary Angara agreed to furnish the committee with the list. He said prioritization was based on a congestion index, particularly schools operating two or three shifts.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juan Edgardo Sonny M. Angara
thread.said: On senior high school vouchers and alleged ghost beneficiaries, he described five layers of validation involving the learner information system, central-office billing review, post-audit monitoring, regional and division inspections, and end-of-school-year validation. He reported 1 conviction from the RTC and 4 cases filed.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juan Edgardo Sonny M. Angara
thread.said: He said the National Educators Academy of the Philippines had a 3000000000 budget for teacher training and that the Education Center for Artificial Intelligence Research had 150000000 budget.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juan Edgardo Sonny M. Angara
thread.said: Secretary Angara confirmed that the capital-outlay reduction described by Rep. Elmer Catulpos was about two-thirds. On carryover funds, he explained that programs such as feeding and vouchers followed the school-year calendar and therefore carried into the succeeding year.

thread.speaker: Rep. Elmer Catulpos
thread.said: Rep. Elmer Catulpos questioned the classroom target of 700 in FY 2027 against 4869 in FY 2026 and a backlog stated in the transcript as 145024 thousand 964 classrooms funded in 2026. Secretary Angara said timing depended on LGU implementation and that over 30000 classrooms should be seen by the first few months of 2027.

thread.speaker: Committee Chair
thread.said: The Chair said the net-to-net budget increase from the FY 2026 NEP to the FY 2027 NEP was PHP 41300000000, but personal services accounted for a PHP 57800000000 increase, leaving a PHP 16000000000 cut in other components, including MOE and capital outlay.

thread.speaker: Committee Chair
thread.said: The Chair asked what would happen if school-based feeding remained at the FY 2027 NEP level of 11000000000 rather than the 26000000000 provided in the FY 2026 GAA.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juan Edgardo Sonny M. Angara
thread.said: He said the lower feeding allocation would reduce the cycle from 180 days to 120 days, eliminate universal feeding for Grade 1 while retaining it for kindergarten, and slow the expansion of central kitchens and hot meals.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juan Edgardo Sonny M. Angara
thread.said: He reported a current school-feeding utilization rate of 45.8 percent, while noting utilization had been 90 percent in 2025 and 81 percent in 2024 and that the program carried over because payments were made after the second semester.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juan Edgardo Sonny M. Angara
thread.said: On inclusive education, he said DepEd was short about 190000 to reach FY 2026 levels. On ARAL, he said all learners could still be covered, but DepEd might have to reallocate funds internally, including from maintenance funds, because the program was a priority.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juan Edgardo Sonny M. Angara
thread.said: Secretary Angara agreed to submit a reprioritized list of the department's augmentation requests to make the committee's review easier.

thread.speaker: Committee Chair
thread.said: The Chair requested the reprioritized list by Wednesday at noontime for consideration through the House budget amendments review subcommittee.

topics.topic: ARAL learning-recovery funding, including the requested 16000000000
topics.summary: Rep. Salvador Pleyto asked where ARAL funding appeared in the FY 2027 NEP and raised the need to compensate teachers and tutors fairly. DepEd answered that the NEP contained a 0 allotment, while it had proposed about 9.98 billion for implementation and 3.5 billion for tutor and teacher remuneration; the agency also reported coverage of about 6.7 million learners and substantial reading improvements. Iris Marie Montes separately pressed for the amount devoted to foundational literacy and numeracy, and Secretary Angara gave a ballpark estimate of at least 10 billion, or about 4 percent of the DepEd budget's learning systems and curriculum strand. Rep. Audrey Zubiri cited the prior 8.9 billion ARAL GAA budget, the reported results, and an estimated 1500 peso per-learner investment in supporting a request to increase funding to 16 billion. DepEd explained that the NEP exclusion reflected the treatment of prior congressional insertions rather than a rejection of the program. The committee expressed support but requested a reprioritized list from DepEd, so the final ARAL funding level remained pending.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish the FY 2027 funding actually included in the NEP for the ARAL learning-recovery program, the amount DepEd requested, and the program's funding and tutor-compensation requirements. Members also asked whether ARAL was producing measurable improvements and what would happen if its requested funding was not restored.
topics.agency_position: DepEd stated that the FY 2027 NEP contained a 0 allotment for ARAL even though the program had received congressional funding previously. The agency sought substantial funding for ARAL implementation, including tutor compensation and learning-recovery interventions, and argued that reported learning gains demonstrated the program's effectiveness and justified restoration or augmentation.
topics.outcome: The committee supported restoring or augmenting ARAL, but no final appropriation was adopted in the hearing. DepEd committed to submit a reprioritized list for the committee's consideration, leaving the requested funding unresolved pending budget review.

positions.position: Supported appropriate and fair compensation for teachers and tutors and manifested support for allocating the funding necessary to implement ARAL.
Pressed DepEd to identify the budget dedicated to foundational literacy and numeracy and to explain how learning-recovery outcomes were measured.
Supported increasing ARAL funding from 9000000000 to 16000000000, arguing that its per-student cost and reported results represented a strong investment.
Supported restoring or augmenting ARAL and other education programs, while requiring DepEd to submit a prioritized and rationalized funding list.

thread.speaker: Rep. Salvador Pleyto
thread.said: He asked for the exact amount appropriated for the ARAL program in the FY 2027 NEP and the specific program, activity, project, or unified account line item where it could be found.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juan Edgardo Sonny M. Angara
thread.said: He said there was a 0 allotment for ARAL under the 2027 budget, unlike the current year, when there was an allotment of around 9000000000 dollars for different ARAL components. DepEd had therefore proposed 9980000000 for implementation of the ARAL program.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juan Edgardo Sonny M. Angara
thread.said: He itemized the proposal as 1090000000 for compensation for 15800 ARAL tutors, 6000000000 for learning-recovery and remediation consultations, 1250000000 for summer program tutors, 1180000000 for external tutors, 4610000000 dollars for ARAL learning resources, 1750000000 dollars for tutor orientation, and 94000000 dollars for program management. The transcript's use of dollar labels is retained exactly as spoken.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juan Edgardo Sonny M. Angara
thread.said: He reported that the program reached 6700000 learners and that 4500000 fewer struggling learners were observed by the end of the school year. He also referred to 2500000 learners reading at grade level, although the surrounding wording was partly unclear.

thread.speaker: Rep. Salvador Pleyto
thread.said: He stressed that ARAL would cover reading, mathematics, and science, and that teachers already carried substantial workloads. He said tutors providing additional instruction should be properly and fairly compensated.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juan Edgardo Sonny M. Angara
thread.said: He said DepEd was requesting 3500000000 in total remuneration for ARAL teachers and tutors.

thread.speaker: Rep. Salvador Pleyto
thread.said: He manifested support for allocating the funding needed to implement ARAL successfully, describing learning recovery and helping children regain confidence as priorities.

thread.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Montes
thread.said: She asked what portion of the FY 2027 budget was dedicated specifically to addressing foundational literacy and numeracy amid the continuing learning crisis.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juan Edgardo Sonny M. Angara
thread.said: He pointed to the entire learning systems strand, including textbooks and the Bureau of Educational Assessment, as contributing to foundational skills and improved assessment performance.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juan Edgardo Sonny M. Angara
thread.said: He gave a ballpark estimate of at least 10000000000 for efforts addressing foundational skills, including 6000000000 for textbooks and a few billion for assessments.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juan Edgardo Sonny M. Angara
thread.said: When asked whether the amount represented about 10 percent of a proposed budget of 967 billions, he clarified that the learning systems and curriculum strand represented about 4 percent of the DepEd budget, with personnel services accounting for about 79 percent.

thread.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Montes
thread.said: She asked how DepEd evaluated whether its learning-recovery interventions produced actual improvements and what baseline assessment tools it used.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juan Edgardo Sonny M. Angara
thread.said: He cited the Comprehensive Rapid Literacy Assessment, the Early Language Literacy and Numeracy Assessment, the Philippine Informal Reading Inventory, and the Rapid Math Assessment. He said these were administered at the beginning and end of the school year, while literacy and numeracy knowledge-link tests were being pilot tested for consistent tracking from grades 1 to 12.

thread.speaker: Rep. Audrey Zubiri
thread.said: She asked what the final GAA budget for ARAL had been the previous year and how many students the program had helped.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juan Edgardo Sonny M. Angara
thread.said: He answered that the previous year's ARAL GAA budget was 8900000000.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juan Edgardo Sonny M. Angara
thread.said: He said ARAL covered 6700000 learners; 4500000 upgraded their reading skills, and over 2000000 were reading at the right level. He described the results as very encouraging and called ARAL a potential game changer.

thread.speaker: Rep. Audrey Zubiri
thread.said: She characterized the result as approximately a 75 percent success rate, based on 4500000 out of 6000000 students, although the transcript's denominator differed from the previously stated coverage.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juan Edgardo Sonny M. Angara
thread.said: He agreed that the program had achieved a very high success rate, saying the result was approximately at that level.

thread.speaker: Rep. Audrey Zubiri
thread.said: She noted that DepEd was requesting 16000000000 for ARAL in the current year and asked why the amount appeared not to have been included in the NEP.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juan Edgardo Sonny M. Angara
thread.said: He confirmed the 16000000000 request and explained that these were congressional insertions. He said DBM's practice was generally not to include non-NEP items from the prior year's GAA in the following year's NEP, apparently expecting Congress to make the necessary insertions again.

thread.speaker: Rep. Audrey Zubiri
thread.said: She calculated the prior funding at 1500 per student and argued that doubling the program from 9000000000 to 16000000000 represented a strong return on investment because it helped students return to the appropriate reading level.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juan Edgardo Sonny M. Angara
thread.said: He agreed that evaluating the program on a per-learner basis made the investment appear modest relative to its reported benefits and thanked the member for presenting that argument.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juan Edgardo Sonny M. Angara
thread.said: He said all students would be affected, but DepEd would be forced to reallocate funds internally, potentially cutting maintenance funds. He emphasized that ARAL was highly important and a game changer for learners falling behind.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juan Edgardo Sonny M. Angara
thread.said: He agreed that the ARAL request was among the priority programs for augmentation or restoration, while noting that the overall number was large. He proposed submitting a reprioritization to make the committee's work easier.

topics.topic: Teacher hiring, shortages, promotions, and career progression
topics.summary: The chair and several members examined DepEd's plans for teacher hiring, promotion, tutoring, and training. DepEd proposed about 12.09 billion for career progression, targeting more than 135000 promotions, but Secretary Angara acknowledged that about 100000 qualified teachers remained in the promotion backlog, leaving about 35000 effective new promotions. Rep. Tinio also elicited that the proposal had 0 funding for new teacher hiring despite a reported shortage of 14274 teachers and 58000 vacant teaching items. Rep. Pleyto sought fair compensation for ARAL tutors, and DepEd cited a proposed ARAL package of about 9.98 billion, including 3.5 billion in total teacher and tutor remuneration. Members further questioned teacher preparation, values education, mental-health staffing, and AI training; DepEd cited about 3 billion for teacher training, 2.9 billion for school counselor associates, and no FY 2027 AI line item. The hearing left additional hiring and ARAL support to the budget process, with commitments to reiterate promotion policy, monitor AI results, and pursue possible training partnerships.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish whether DepEd's proposed resources would address teacher shortages, qualified applicants awaiting appointment or promotion, fair compensation for additional tutoring, and meaningful career progression. Members also asked how teacher training, including AI and values education, would prepare teachers for changing instructional needs.
topics.agency_position: DepEd said the proposed budget prioritized career progression and training but contained 0 funding for new teacher hiring, despite a reported shortage of 14274 teachers and 58000 vacant teaching items. The agency supported fair compensation for ARAL tutors, sought funding for the program, and said it would continue teacher training, values education, and AI capacity-building while working through the budget process and available partnerships.
topics.outcome: The committee received answers on the promotion targets, promotion backlog, vacant teaching items, ARAL tutor compensation, and teacher-training initiatives. The central issue of 0 FY 2027 funding for new teacher hiring remained open, while DepEd's requests for ARAL and possible additional support were left to the succeeding budget process.

positions.position: Supported continued investment in teachers, including career progression, medical support, and additional teaching and nonteaching personnel, while insisting that appropriations produce measurable results.
Supported sufficient ARAL funding and fair remuneration for teachers and para-teachers performing tutoring beyond their regular duties.
Pressed for clearing the promotion backlog and questioned why the FY 2027 proposal provided 0 funding for new teacher hiring despite the stated shortage.
Sought assurance that qualified applicants would be appointed through a fair ranking and selection process when vacant teaching items existed.
Supported teacher education reform focused on critical thinking, facilitative instruction, project-based learning, and stronger local and regional leadership.
Supported stronger GMRC and values education, expanded teacher preparation, and adequate staffing and resources for school-based mental-health services.
Supported AI adoption to reduce teacher workload and improve learning, but sought evidence of results and adequate teacher training before additional funding.
Supported treating GMRC and values education as continuing character formation rather than merely as classroom subjects.
Supported increasing DepEd's budget and offered to help establish a memorandum of agreement for teacher-training support.

topics.topic: School counselor staffing and school-based mental-health funding
topics.summary: Members raised the shortage of licensed guidance counselors, the over-3000 vacancies, and the difficulty of recruiting professionals because of the master's-degree requirement. DepEd said it was hiring 10000 school counselor associates, had shortened the hiring period to 30 days, and had received over 20000 applications. The FY 2027 proposal funded 1800 positions, while DepEd requested 39000 positions and calculated that 11400000000 would be needed for a meaningful first tranche. Deployment would prioritize schools with high bullying or mental-health incidence, larger enrollment, congestion, and senior-high-school implementation, while maintaining equitable distribution. Members also pressed for greater mental-health funding and cautioned against relying excessively on security measures and potentially traumatic active-shooter drills. DepEd committed to provide progress and deployment data and described scholarship, training, social-emotional learning, and psychological-first-aid initiatives, but the requested funding increases were not finally resolved in the hearing.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish how many guidance counselor and school counselor associate positions DepEd had, how many were vacant or funded, whether qualified applicants were available, and how the positions would be deployed. Members also examined the funding needed for school-based mental-health services and the balance between mental-health interventions and school-security measures.
topics.agency_position: DepEd said the FY 2027 proposal funded 1800 school counselor associate positions, while the department was requesting substantially more to move toward one counselor associate per school. It said hiring for the 10000 existing items was underway, with over 20000 applicants, and that deployment would prioritize need, bullying and mental-health history, school size, and senior-high-school implementation while maintaining equitable nationwide distribution.
topics.outcome: The committee received DepEd's explanation of the counselor staffing gap, the ongoing hiring process, the applicant pool, and the proposed deployment criteria. The department's larger requests and the final level of mental-health funding remained subject to the budget process, while DepEd committed to provide hiring and deployment information.

positions.position: Mental-health programs should receive greater emphasis and funding than a school-securitization model, and active-shooter drills should reflect evidence of possible psychological harm.
DepEd needed to address the large gap between the national target of one counselor associate per school and the positions funded in the proposal.
The school-based mental-health program required adequate budget, resources, and qualified personnel.
Counselor associates were needed to provide learners with guidance and support outside the home, and their hiring and deployment required clarification.
DepEd should use scholarships and customized continuing-education programs to help counselor associates advance toward licensure.
Additional counselor positions should be distributed transparently, with attention to bullying incidence, enrollment, and schools without existing counseling personnel.
Congress should support increased mental-health funding and DepEd's mental-health initiatives in response to serious school incidents.

topics.topic: Classroom safety, bullying, violence, and learner protection
topics.summary: Members raised bullying, school violence, online harms, learner-rights implementation, and the need for mental-health and counseling personnel. DepEd said more than 30000 of over 36000 schools had functioning Child Protection Committees, all schools had learner formation officers, and hiring for 10000 school counselor-associate positions was underway after more than 20000 applications. Members questioned the use and possible harms of active-shooter drills; DepEd said drills were funded through school MOOE, had been postponed and toned down after psychiatrists' concerns, and remained subject to revision. DepEd cited proposed additional funding of about 100 million dollars for mental-health capacity building and 8000000000 for security measures, while a later safety discussion stated 54000000000 pesos, with the precise component unclear. Members also secured commitments on immediate protection for severe bullying, verification of a Grade 1 material, noncoercive Pride Month activities, reports on learner protection and gender-and-development compliance, and counselor-allocation data. The issue landed with ongoing implementation and reporting commitments, rather than a fully resolved determination of funding adequacy.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish how DepEd would prevent and respond to bullying, school violence, and online harms; protect learners; and fund school security and mental-health measures. Members also asked whether counselor vacancies, Child Protection Committees, reporting systems, drills, and related policies were adequately staffed, implemented, and monitored.
topics.agency_position: DepEd said learner protection required a combined approach involving Anti-Bullying Act implementation, Child Protection Committees and learner formation officers, mental-health and counseling personnel, school-community participation, reporting systems, and proportionate security measures. The agency acknowledged major staffing and funding constraints, said hiring and policy work were ongoing, and undertook to provide several reports, verify materials, reiterate protections against coercive activities, and coordinate with other agencies on online violence.
topics.outcome: The committee received DepEd's explanations of its anti-bullying, counseling, reporting, drill, and security measures, but significant staffing and funding gaps remained. DepEd undertook to submit reports, verify questioned materials, reiterate learner safeguards, and provide regional and district hiring data.

positions.position: Bullying and school violence were urgent and widespread problems requiring stronger DepEd action.
Learner protection and mental-health programs needed adequate staffing, curriculum support, and funding.
Mental-health and guidance-counseling funding should be prioritized over school securitization measures whose effectiveness and possible harms required scrutiny.
Schools needed concrete security resources and sufficient counselor staffing, with attention to furniture and facility gaps affecting learner safety.
DepEd needed to implement and document learner-rights protections, gender-and-development obligations, and safeguards concerning military use of schools.
Schools should immediately protect victims of severe bullying and ensure that instructional and Pride Month materials or activities were age-appropriate and not coercive.
Online violence and Internet and social-media risks required an interagency response and stronger education for learners.
Counselor positions should be distributed transparently and prioritize districts and schools with the greatest bullying and counseling needs.
School counselor associates were necessary to provide learners guidance and support beyond the home.

topics.topic: Textbook, instructional-material, and furniture procurement backlogs
topics.summary: Rep. Edgar and other members questioned the reduction in textbook and instructional-material funding and pressed DepEd on whether procurement would translate into delivery, particularly in remote schools. Secretary Angara said DepEd had procured all 105 curriculum titles and was pursuing a one-textbook-per-learner goal, but acknowledged delivery delays, including delays of 1 year. Rep. Amato and civil-society questions highlighted classroom and repair backlogs, while DepEd cited a backlog of roughly 142000 classrooms, more than 350 LGU partners, and a request for 98000000000 in infrastructure funding. DepEd said early procurement, regional or decentralized procurement, and PPP and LGU participation would improve absorptive capacity and delivery. Rep. Catulpos separately cited a drop in textbook procurement from about 19 billion to 6 billion and questioned the FY 2027 classroom target. DepEd did not resolve the funding and delivery concerns, and it undertook to verify whether a questioned grade 1 material was officially authorized.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish whether DepEd’s proposed FY 2027 procurement and infrastructure allocations would reduce backlogs in textbooks, instructional materials, classrooms, and related facilities, particularly in last-mile and poorer schools. Members also asked how DepEd would address delayed delivery, underutilization of funds, procurement decentralization, and the age appropriateness and authorization of learning materials.
topics.agency_position: DepEd said it had made significant progress in textbook procurement, including procuring all 105 curriculum titles, but acknowledged that timely delivery—especially to last-mile schools—remained unresolved. It attributed delivery and utilization improvements to early procurement, decentralization, regional procurement, and expanded participation by LGUs and PPP partners, while seeking larger infrastructure funding to address the classroom backlog.
topics.outcome: DepEd provided progress figures and identified procurement reforms, but members’ concerns about the sharp FY 2027 textbook reduction, delayed delivery to last-mile schools, classroom targets, and transparency of allocations remained open. Verification of the questioned grade 1 material was deferred to DepEd’s regional offices.

positions.position: He questioned the large reduction in textbook and instructional-material funding and pressed DepEd on whether procurement and delivery would improve.

topics.topic: Computerization, connectivity, and digital-transformation funding
topics.summary: The committee questioned DepEd's reduced Computerization Program, the funding for 50000 teacher laptops, undelivered computer packages, school connectivity, and the absence of a dedicated AI appropriation. Secretary Angara said prior computerization deliveries had been completed and that DepEd would improve tracking through early procurement and decentralization. He reported 99 percent internet coverage, 460 schools without internet, an aspiration for 100 Mbps minimum bandwidth, and a goal of reaching 10 to 12000 schools with AI tools from about 3000 schools. DepEd described AI applications for hazard mapping, teacher support, administrative work, and learner reading assessment, while warning that safeguards and teacher training were necessary. Angara said over 1000000 faculty and students had been trained and that 115000000 had been carved out in 20 26 for an AI research center, but there was no AI line item in the 20 27 budget. Members expressed support but left funding adequacy and the scale-up of digital services for the continuing budget process.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish whether DepEd's proposed computerization, connectivity, and digital-transformation funding would address prior delivery and absorptive-capacity problems, expand meaningful school and learner access to computers and the internet, and support responsible use of AI. Members also asked what specific AI uses, training, bandwidth, monitoring, and funding were in place.
topics.agency_position: DepEd said prior computer-delivery problems had been addressed and that it was improving tracking, early procurement, and regional decentralization to raise absorptive capacity. It supported expanding computer laboratories, internet bandwidth, teacher training, and carefully safeguarded AI applications, but acknowledged that the 20 27 budget contained no AI line item and that connectivity quality and access remained uneven.
topics.outcome: The agency answered that computer deliveries had been completed and described measures to improve procurement, tracking, connectivity, teacher training, and AI deployment. The committee received the explanations, but the adequacy of the reduced computerization funding, the 20 27 teacher-laptop allocation, bandwidth gaps, and the absence of a dedicated AI line item remained matters for the budget process.

Supported DepEd's AI adoption but sought specific use cases, purposeful teacher training, monitoring of results, and a funding basis for future expansion.

thread.said: He said DepEd would improve absorptive capacity through early procurement and later emphasized that hundreds of thousands of computers would be procured in the coming months.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juan Edgardo Sonny M. Angara

thread.speaker: Rep. Presley de Jesus
thread.said: He asked about computers in schools and whether DepEd was behind in providing computers for students and classes.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juan Edgardo Sonny M. Angara
thread.said: He said the goal was at least one computer laboratory in each school, while cautioning that excessive computer time could be harmful. He cited a possible limit of 1 to 3 hours a week in some countries and said consistent procurement of computer-lab equipment was attainable.

thread.said: He asked how DepEd would integrate AI over the next five years and prepare for increasingly capable artificial intelligence and robotics.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juan Edgardo Sonny M. Angara
thread.said: He said AI could help address teacher skills mismatches and support personalized learning. He warned that AI could diminish creative and critical faculties among younger children, so it should be introduced at the right age with safeguards and teacher training.

thread.speaker: Rep. Presley de Jesus
thread.said: He recalled seeing a school receive computers and internet together, expressed full support for DepEd, and said he would support the department's plenary report.

thread.speaker: Maria Nina Francesca Lacson
thread.said: She asked what types of AI DepEd intended to use, including possible predictive, language-processing, and other applications, and what specific use cases would help teachers.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juan Edgardo Sonny M. Angara
thread.said: He deferred the technical response to Undersecretary Mars Veloso, with the chair's permission.

thread.speaker: Undersecretary Mars Veloso
thread.said: He said DepEd was using AI for administrative pattern analysis and hazard mapping through Project Lake Task. For teachers, DepEd was enabling use of Google Gemini and Microsoft Copilot; for learners, it was exploring Reading Progress, which measures spoken reading and tracks omitted words.

thread.speaker: Maria Nina Francesca Lacson
thread.said: She said teachers viewed AI positively but asked how DepEd would train them to use the tools purposefully, rather than merely provide access.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juan Edgardo Sonny M. Angara
thread.said: He said DepEd had trained over 1000000 faculty and students with help from the United Nations and Google and intended to continue. He also cited Khanmigo, provided free to DepEd by Khan Academy, as a tool for personalized learning and teacher support.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juan Edgardo Sonny M. Angara
thread.said: He said scaling AI tools required strong bandwidth, with an aspiration of 100 Mbps minimum in many schools. DepEd aimed to reach at least 10 to 12000 schools by the end of next year and was then in about 3000 schools.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juan Edgardo Sonny M. Angara
thread.said: He said AI could help with analytics, lesson plans, quizzes, and checking, but that effective teacher training was essential to realize the benefits nationwide.

thread.speaker: Maria Nina Francesca Lacson
thread.said: She asked how much was currently allocated as a budget line item for AI and whether DepEd could seek more funding after measuring positive effects.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juan Edgardo Sonny M. Angara
thread.said: He said there was no AI line item in the 20 27 budget. For 20 26, DepEd had carved out 115000000 for an AI center for research, which he said had helped the department use data scientists and improve work involving large datasets and structural problems.

thread.speaker: Maria Nina Francesca Lacson
thread.said: She urged DepEd to monitor the positive effects of AI adoption so that the committee could better assess a request for more money the following year, and formally manifested her support for DepEd.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juan Edgardo Sonny M. Angara
thread.said: He thanked Representative Laxon and said DepEd would undertake the monitoring she requested.

topics.topic: Inclusive and special-needs education funding
topics.summary: Representative Sandania questioned the apparent reduction of special-needs education funding from about 1 billion to 850 million and proposed restoring or increasing the allocation. DepEd said the comparison was affected by congressional insertions in the prior budget and appealed for an additional 541.5 million to support staffing, facilities, equipment, schools, and multidisciplinary-team capacity-building. The agency said 81.6 million would construct six Inclusive Learning Resource Centers, bringing the projected total to 38 against a target of 1,642, and reported 10.8 million for learner-support-center enhancement. Representative Caroline Agiau sought additional funding for disability assessments and assistive devices, but the transcript did not provide the requested counts of learners awaiting assessment or lacking devices. The committee later identified a shortfall of about 190 million to reach FY 2026 levels for the group of programs that included SNED and requested a reprioritized list. The matter therefore landed with DepEd commitments for further submissions and with funding augmentation left for committee consideration.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish whether the proposed FY 2027 funding for special-needs and inclusive education was sufficient to implement the Inclusive Education Act. Members asked what additional funding would cover, how many Inclusive Learning Resource Centers could be built, and whether DepEd could provide adequate assessment, assistive-device, staffing, and learner-support services.
topics.agency_position: DepEd said the apparent reduction in special-needs education funding reflected the exclusion of prior congressional insertions from the NEP, rather than a change in the program's importance. The agency supported additional funding for staffing, facilities, equipment, teacher and multidisciplinary-team capacity-building, Inclusive Learning Resource Centers, and related inclusive services, and sought congressional consideration of its appeals.
topics.outcome: The issue was left for budget consideration rather than finally resolved. DepEd committed to provide additional learner-support-center information and a reprioritized list of requests, while the committee indicated that it would consider restoration or augmentation of SNED and related inclusive-education funding.

positions.position: Supported restoring SNED funding to 1000000000 and potentially increasing it to 2000000000, with funding for services, facilities, materials, personnel, and professional support.
Supported higher funding for disability assessment, assistive learning devices and technologies, indigenous learners with special needs, and inclusive education generally.
Supported restoring or augmenting funding for SNED and related inclusive-education programs and requested a prioritized list from DepEd for consideration.

topics.topic: School feeding, ECCD, and learner nutrition programs
topics.summary: Rep. Edgar flagged a 55 percent reduction in school-based feeding, and Secretary Angara said the proposed funding would support only 120 days rather than 180 days and would reduce coverage, including universal feeding for Grade 1. DepEd linked feeding to weight gain, attendance, and improved learning, and said ECCD responsibilities were shared with DILG, LGUs, DSWD, and the National Nutrition Council, with DepEd focused on curriculum and participation in the ECCD Council. Rep. Zubiri supported increasing ARAL funding from about 9 billion to 16 billion after DepEd reported that 6.7 million learners were covered and 4.5 million advanced reading levels. The committee chair questioned whether the 26 billion 2026 feeding allocation was being utilized, and DepEd reported 45.8 percent current utilization, with school-year carryover and higher historical rates. DepEd said it would submit a reprioritized list of priority programs, and the committee agreed to consider restoration or augmentation before the budget moved forward.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish how the proposed reductions would affect school-based feeding, including the number of feeding days, learner coverage, and nutrition and learning outcomes. Members also asked how DepEd's ECCD responsibilities related to day-care feeding and malnutrition response, and whether funding for ARAL and other foundational-learning programs should be restored or augmented.
topics.agency_position: DepEd stated that school feeding was strongly linked to improved weight, attendance, and learning outcomes, especially during the early years, and that the proposed level would reduce both the feeding cycle and coverage. The department supported restoring or augmenting funding for feeding and ARAL, sought an amendment to the school-feeding law, and offered to submit a reprioritized list of requests.
topics.outcome: The issue was not finally resolved in the hearing. DepEd explained the operational consequences of retaining the lower school-feeding allocation and committed to submit a prioritized restoration and augmentation list, while the committee undertook to consider the requests.

positions.position: Flagged the 55 percent reduction in school-based feeding as a significant concern.
Raised concern about ECCD, early-childhood feeding, malnutrition, and the fragmented assignment of responsibilities, and supported DepEd's budget.
Sought to understand the effect of funding reductions on feeding and foundational learning.
Supported increasing ARAL funding from 9000000000 to 16000000000 and pledged to support the program.
Supported reviewing restoration or augmentation of school feeding and other priority learner-support programs, subject to DepEd's reprioritized list.

topics.topic: Voucher programs and senior-high-school beneficiary controls
topics.summary: Rep. Edgar questioned a reported 100 percent reduction in senior-high-school voucher assistance and sought clarification of the FY 2026 and FY 2027 amounts. Secretary Angara said the consolidated voucher program, including JDVP and ESC, was PHP 38000000000, about PHP 3000000000 below the prior year. Rep. topics.topic: Teacher loans, APDS payroll deductions, and take-home pay
topics.summary: Rep. Adrian Amato raised teacher financial literacy, loan support, and the possibility of an annual allocation, while Secretary Juan Edgardo Sonny M. Angara said DepEd would examine the proposal and work with him. Rep. Roberto Nazal Jr. then questioned the legal basis and welfare effects of allowing APDS loans for up to 7 years, including the number of teachers with multiple loans and their average and median take-home pay. Secretary Angara said the arrangement was voluntary, complied with the GAA protection for 5000 in net take-home pay, and could give teachers longer repayment periods and lower payments. Rep. Nazal cited a reported rate of 3.5 percent per month, roughly 42 percent per year, and asked about lender oversight. DepEd stated that accredited lenders were subject to a 9.6 percent per annum ceiling, while higher-rate lenders were probably not accredited and fell outside DepEd's police power. The requested loan and take-home-pay data and specific legal basis were not resolved during the hearing.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish how DepEd legally authorized APDS automatic payroll deductions for loans of up to 7 years, whether extended loan terms helped teachers or prolonged indebtedness, and what teachers' take-home pay was after deductions. Members also questioned the interest-rate ceiling and DepEd's ability to police nonaccredited lenders.
topics.agency_position: DepEd said the 7-year APDS loan option was voluntary, was offered at teachers' request, and complied with the GAA protection requiring 5000 in net take-home pay to remain untouched. It stated that the interest ceiling for accredited lenders was 9.6 percent per annum, while lenders charging 3.5 percent monthly were not accredited, and acknowledged that DepEd did not have police power over such lenders.
topics.outcome: DepEd explained the voluntary nature of the 7-year option and stated the 5000 take-home-pay protection and 9.6 percent interest ceiling. The requested data and fuller legal explanation were not provided in the exchange, leaving those issues open.

topics.topic: National Museum operating, exhibition, and new-museum funding
topics.summary: Shirlyn Bañas-Nograles asked whether a building in her district could support a component museum, and Jeremy Barnes said the National Museum was developing a regional museum in Koronadal City while exploring Lake Sebu, General Santos, and other culturally significant locations. Barnes agreed to coordinate with her team about the offered premises. Secretary Angara said DepEd encouraged museum visits and stronger arts and culture education, while Representative Benitez supported early and sustained exposure to creativity. Barnes reported that the National Museum had opened its 5th museum under the administration in the last 3 years and was preparing facilities in several locations for 2027. He said MOE needed an augmentation of 65000000 and that 79000000 was proposed for exhibitions. Representative Zubiri supported the requests, warned against opening unfurnished or understaffed museums, and asked that Bukidnon be considered; Secretary Angara committed to the request, but no funding was approved during the hearing.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish whether the National Museum and DepEd could support new or component museums, including their staffing, operations, utilities, maintenance, and exhibitions. topics.outcome: The National Museum's proposed MOE and exhibition augmentations were identified as priorities, and members expressed support, but no appropriation or committee ruling was made in the transcript. Site-specific requests for General Santos-area facilities and Bukidnon were left for coordination and further consideration.

topics.topic: AI, curriculum reform, and teacher capability development
topics.summary: Members questioned DepEd's readiness to use AI, train teachers, upgrade the curriculum, strengthen GMRC and Values Education, and prepare learners for future work. Secretary Angara said AI could support teachers and personalized learning but required safeguards, age-appropriate introduction, teacher training, and stronger connectivity. DepEd cited about 3 billion for teacher training, 150 million for its eCare AI research center, and 115 million in 2026 AI-center research funding, while acknowledging no dedicated AI line item in the 2027 budget. Officials described GMRC teacher training for grades 1 to 10, values integration across subjects, and curriculum additions involving life skills, AI, and future skills. Members manifested support for DepEd's budget, and the agency agreed to monitor AI's effects and share relevant GMRC survey results.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish how DepEd would fund and implement AI, curriculum reform, teacher capability development, GMRC and Values Education, and future-skills preparation. Members also asked how AI would be used without weakening critical thinking, creativity, or human-centered education.
topics.agency_position: DepEd supported carefully governed AI adoption to assist teachers, personalize learning, analyze administrative and operational problems, and build future skills. It maintained that teacher training, appropriate age-based safeguards, connectivity, and continued curriculum and values-education work were necessary, and acknowledged that the 2027 budget contained no dedicated AI line item.
topics.outcome: The agency answered the members' policy questions and secured expressions of support, but AI funding remained partly unresolved because DepEd acknowledged there was no dedicated AI line item in the 2027 budget. DepEd undertook to monitor AI results and share relevant GMRC survey findings.

positions.position: Supported substantially greater national attention and investment in education, computers, connectivity, teacher training, and AI, and expressed full support for education in the plenary report.
Argued that teacher capability development and curriculum upgrading should accompany school construction and broader education investment.

Supported DepEd's AI partnerships and proposed monitoring results to justify additional future funding.

Supported arts and culture education and a cautious, non-prohibitory use of AI that improves literacy and numeracy without displacing creativity or critical thinking.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juan Edgardo Sonny M. Angara
thread.said: He said strengthening GMRC and Values Education was ongoing, while acknowledging that implementation depended on whether teachers were trained.

topics.topic: Tourism infrastructure, access roads, and interagency project priorities
topics.summary: Members questioned whether priority and emerging tourism destinations had adequate roads, visitor facilities, and related infrastructure, and whether DOT's promotional work was matched by national investments. DOT said promotions and infrastructure required equal resources, but road construction generally remained with DPWH through TRIP, while DOT funded facilities and coordinated with DPWH, DOTR, TIEZA, and local governments. DOT disclosed that 28 Tier 2 projects worth approximately 6.02 billion were proposed, but continuing and new TRIP projects were not included in the FY2027 NEP. Members also discussed a proposed 1.64 billion augmentation, a Region 6 allocation of about 50.8 million, and roughly 5.2 billion for TIEZA multiyear projects. DOT committed to destination inventories, regional planning, and follow-up on unresolved environmental and infrastructure matters, while the committee requested a list of TIEZA's ongoing multiyear projects.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish whether priority tourism destinations had adequate roads, facilities, and basic services, and whether DOT, DPWH, DOTR, TIEZA, DBM, and local governments were coordinating their investments. Members also asked how projects would be funded, continued, and prioritized across emerging, high-potential, and regional destinations.
topics.agency_position: DOT said infrastructure and promotion required equal attention, but responsibility for infrastructure was distributed among DOT, DPWH, DOTR, TIEZA, and local governments. DOT funded destination facilities and planning, coordinated through regional and convergence programs, and sought to record unfunded priorities in regional tourism development plans; it did not itself build access roads. The agency acknowledged that several proposed road and Tier 2 projects were not included in the FY2027 NEP and that further coordination and funding decisions remained necessary.
topics.outcome: The committee received DOT's explanations and several funding figures, but the absence of DPWH TRIP funding in the FY2027 NEP and the lack of a clearly identified formal interagency master list left major infrastructure priorities open. DOT undertook coordination, destination inventory, planning, and document-related follow-up, while members expressed support for budget augmentation and requested continuity funding for multiyear projects.

thread.said: Rep. Javi Benitez asked whether DOT's priority should be promotions, infrastructure, or costs, and requested the secretary's view on whether the priorities were equal.

thread.speaker: DOT Secretary
thread.said: The secretary said infrastructure and promotions should receive equal effort and resources. Promotions addressed current issues, but infrastructure and investment supported the entire ecosystem and were necessary for a sustainable industry.

She identified the New Manila International Airport in Bulacan and proposed railway connectivity between Bulacan and Clark as key transport projects, and said DPWH and DOTR had distinct responsibilities for roads, ports, airports, and transport infrastructure. She also said Siquijor and Siargao had been designated as pilot sites for infrastructure projects under a March 2026-approved MOA.

thread.speaker: Salvador Pleyto

topics.topic: TIEZA funding, travel-tax resources, and multiyear infrastructure projects
topics.summary: DOT presented about 1.64 billion in additional requests for its attached agencies, including about 1.31 billion for TIEZA infrastructure projects, while warning that travel-tax abolition could create funding implications. TIEZA said around 300 personnel could be affected if the travel tax were abolished. DBM said no FY 2027 national government subsidy tied to the proposed abolition was included because the measures had not been enacted, but TIEZA could use available collections and other resources. A minority member sought a tourism-destination inventory and received the Secretary's commitment. Howard Gintu raised the Region 6 allocation, clarified at 50800000 pesos after conflicting figures, and questioned the continuity of TIEZA's multiyear projects. TIEZA said almost all projects were multiyear and cited around 5.2 billion pesos for 2027; Gintu requested a project list for possible committee support.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish how much additional funding DOT's attached agencies, particularly TIEZA, were requesting; how travel-tax abolition could affect TIEZA resources and personnel; and whether ongoing tourism infrastructure projects, including projects in Region 6, had secure multiyear financing. Members also sought destination inventories and a list of ongoing TIEZA projects to support possible appropriations.
topics.agency_position: DOT and TIEZA presented travel-tax resources as important to tourism infrastructure and other priority programs. DBM said no national government subsidy requested in connection with proposed travel-tax abolition was included because the measures had not been enacted, but TIEZA could use available travel-tax collections, its corporate operating budget, and potentially other authorized sources. TIEZA stated that almost all of its projects were multiyear and that the 2027 amount was around 5200000000 pesos.
topics.outcome: The committee received explanations that travel-tax abolition had not yet resulted in a DBM subsidy because the bills remained pending, while TIEZA could use available resources and other authorized funding sources. The destination-inventory request was met with a commitment, but the requested list of ongoing TIEZA projects and the final protection of multiyear-project financing were not resolved during the excerpt.

positions.position: Supported DOT's budget and argued for additional support for tourism infrastructure, destination development, and an inventory of tourism destinations, particularly in Dinagat.

Opposed the reduction in Region 6 funding, advocated interregion or interprovince tourism planning, and sought protection and continuity for TIEZA's multiyear projects if travel-tax abolition affected financing.
Supported coordinated, sustainable tourism development and committed to the destination-inventory request.

topics.topic: FY 2027 DOT budget, OSEC funding, and proposed augmentation
topics.summary: Secretary Dita Angara Matai presented a total FY 2027 DOT budget of about 5.47 billion, including about 3.53 billion for DOT OSEC, and requested 82330000 in additional funding. She also asked the committee to restore the DOT's FY 2026 funding level, which was about 3.69 billion for OSEC. Representative Rufus Rodriguez supported the DOT budget and proposed augmentation, citing 82000000 for OSEC and 1600000000 for attached agencies; the transcript also contained an unclear rendering of the combined amount. Representative Javi Benitez asked about funding for Terra Madre Asia Pacific, and DOT officials said the 45000000 FY 2027 Tier 2 request had not been approved, despite a projected ROI of about 132 percent. The secretary committed to approach DBM, while another official said the DOT would seek other funding options and coordinate with the Tourism Promotions Board. The issue therefore landed with agency commitments but without a recorded final approval of the requested augmentations.
topics.question: What was the DOT's proposed FY 2027 budget, particularly for the DOT Office of the Secretary (OSEC), and what additional funding did the department seek? The committee also sought to determine whether members would support augmentation and whether specific unfunded tourism initiatives, including Terra Madre Asia Pacific, could be restored.
topics.agency_position: The DOT said its proposed FY 2027 funding was below the FY 2026 level but could sustain operations if resources were used more efficiently. It sought 82330000 in additional funding, requested restoration of its prior funding level, and undertook to pursue unfunded requests such as Terra Madre Asia Pacific through DBM and other available funding channels.
topics.outcome: The committee heard the DOT's request for additional funding and received support from Representative Rodriguez for augmentation, although no final committee ruling on the augmentation appears in the transcript. Terra Madre Asia Pacific remained outside the approved FY 2027 proposal, but the DOT committed to pursue DBM approval and identify funding options.

positions.position: Supported approval of the DOT budget and proposed augmentation for OSEC and the attached agencies, stated in the transcript as 1640000000 and later rendered as 1 64000000000.
Supported the DOT budget and urged restoration or approval of funding for Terra Madre Asia Pacific because of its tourism and economic returns.
Requested restoration of the DOT's FY 2026 funding level and additional funding for priority operational and tourism-development requirements.

topics.topic: Tourism promotion, domestic and international marketing allocations
topics.summary: The DOT presented 1000000000 for its FY 2027 branding campaign and said the campaign would combine international visibility with conversion into travel and spending. Members supported additional funding but questioned competitiveness, private-sector counterparts, infrastructure needs, and whether promotion could be separated from broader tourism reforms. On domestic and international marketing, the DOT stated that 60 percent of the branding allocation would target international markets and 40 percent domestic travelers, serving 13 key markets. It cited 69 percent growth for China, around 29 percent for Vietnam, around 30 percent for India, and a 17 percent South Korea decline addressed through 50000000 in campaign funding. The DOT also cited a training allocation of 198752000, pesos, while a member referenced 230000000 for training. The discussion ended with support for the budget, but without final action on the augmentation or a definitive destination-investment road map.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish how the DOT would allocate limited tourism-promotion resources between domestic and international markets, and whether the allocations were tied to measurable returns. Members also asked how branding, celebrity or influencer campaigns, training, and destination investment would support tourism competitiveness.
topics.agency_position: The DOT said the 1000000000 branding campaign would combine global awareness-building with conversion into travel and spending, while prioritizing international markets because of their value per peso. It stated that 60 percent would go to international marketing and 40 percent to domestic marketing, with targeted campaigns for 13 key markets, selected use of influencers or celebrities, and continued investment in training, infrastructure coordination, and destination development.
topics.outcome: The DOT explained the international-versus-domestic allocation as 60 percent to international marketing and 40 percent to domestic marketing, with targeted spending for 13 key markets and 50000000 for South Korea. Members generally supported augmentation, but the record did not establish final approval, a completed Tourism Promotions Board request, or a fully developed destination-investment road map.

Supported DOT budget augmentation but pressed the department to demonstrate competitiveness, branding, internal reform, and private-sector investment returns.

topics.topic: Domestic travel affordability, airfares, and possible fuel subsidy
topics.summary: Rep. Perci Cendaña raised the affordability of domestic travel and asked how the DOT would respond to volatile fuel prices, limited aircraft capacity, and infrastructure gaps. The DOT said island routes were expensive because turbopropeller aircraft carried only about 70 to 80 seats and airport limitations restricted supply, while larger aircraft and runway improvements could lower costs. It said a fuel subsidy modeled on Vietnam's program could help but was still finalizing the proposal and gathering data. Cendaña requested the DOTR's airport-improvement commitments and the DOT's FY 2027 contingency plan, while another member cautioned that affordability claims required actual investment and reforms. Rep. Elmer Catulpos later asked whether Filipinos traveled abroad because neighboring countries were 20 to 30 percent cheaper; the DOT answered that domestic tourism remained the backbone of the industry and cited 80 percent of tourism income as domestic. The matter landed with agency follow-up commitments and remained open pending the requested documents and subsidy details.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish why domestic airfares remained high, whether the DOT had a plan to make domestic travel more affordable—including a possible fuel subsidy—and how infrastructure, tourism promotion, and competitiveness measures would address the problem. Members also sought to clarify whether Filipinos were choosing foreign travel because neighboring destinations were cheaper and how the DOT balanced domestic and international marketing.
topics.agency_position: The DOT said domestic airfares were primarily pressured by fuel costs, demand and supply, limited aircraft capacity, and airport infrastructure constraints, particularly for island destinations. It supported continued airport improvements, was gathering data and finalizing a possible fuel subsidy proposal, and intended to use targeted tourism promotion, training, accreditation, branding, and private-sector partnerships to improve competitiveness.
topics.outcome: The DOT explained the structural and fuel-related causes of high domestic airfares and said airport improvements, airline support, and a possible fuel subsidy could help, but the subsidy proposal was still being finalized. The issue remained open pending the DOT's contingency plan, DOTR facility commitments, and further data on the proposed subsidy.

positions.position: Domestic travel needed to become more affordable and accessible, and the DOT should coordinate with the DOTR and CAB, provide a contingency plan, and secure airport improvements and possible fuel-support measures.
The committee needed to determine whether cheaper foreign destinations were drawing Filipinos away from domestic travel.
Claims that travel could become easier and more affordable should be supported by actual investments and reforms rather than becoming an overpromising branding message.
The DOT's request for a Tier 1 budget augmentation deserved support because tourism employment and industry investment were at stake.

topics.topic: Tourism destination inventory and integrated development planning
topics.summary: Members supported DOT budget augmentation while citing existing road maps for Cagayan de Oro, Bukidnon, Mindanao historical sites, and other destinations. Rep. Sergio Dagooc sought a coordinated inventory of tourism destinations, and the DOT secretary committed to it. Rep. Salvador Pleyto asked how high-potential destinations and access-road needs were integrated into DPWH and DOTR spending; DOT described interagency coordination but acknowledged that infrastructure funding was not included in the FY 2027 NEP. Members also proposed an integrated classification of top, rising-star, and hidden-gem destinations and interprovince tourism plans. DOT reported training, disaster-assistance, and regional funding figures, although the Region 6 amount was stated inconsistently. TIEZA said almost all projects were multiyear and cited around 5200000000 pesos for FY 2027, while a list of ongoing projects was requested for further committee action.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish how DOT and other agencies were identifying, prioritizing, and financing tourism destinations, particularly emerging and high-potential sites. Members also asked whether infrastructure plans were coordinated across agencies and provinces, and whether funding and multiyear projects would support those priorities.
topics.agency_position: DOT said it was coordinating with DPWH, DOTR, local governments, and other partners through regional tourism development planning, destination packages, convergence programs, and pilot-site arrangements. It maintained that DOT could fund tourism facilities and destination development but not roads, and acknowledged that infrastructure funding and an interagency prioritization mechanism remained incomplete.
topics.outcome: The committee obtained commitments on destination inventory and regional tourism development planning, but no formal interagency master list, specific high-potential-site inventory, or confirmed infrastructure funding allocation was produced. The request for TIEZA's multiyear-project list and the Region 6 funding concern were left for follow-up.

positions.position: Supported augmenting the DOT and attached-agency budgets to accelerate tourism development, including destination road maps and infrastructure.
Supported DOT augmentation and urged a coordinated inventory of tourism destinations, including emerging destinations with high potential.
Supported the DOT budget but pressed for synchronized infrastructure planning and assistance for specific access-road needs.
Opposed reducing Region 6 funding, advocated interregion or interprovince tourism planning, and sought protection for TIEZA multiyear projects.
Supported classifying destinations as top destinations, rising stars, and hidden gems to guide infrastructure and investment road maps.

topics.topic: Travel-tax abolition and its effect on DOT personnel and projects
topics.summary: The committee first asked about personnel consequences of abolishing the travel tax, and DOT said around 300 travel-tax personnel would be affected, with some terminated and others receiving separation incentives. A committee member also sought alternative financing for tourism, heritage and related projects. Representative Sergio Dagooc then asked DBM why TIEZA's requested subsidy and tourism-infrastructure funding were not augmented. DBM said the FY 2027 subsidy was not included because abolition bills remained under deliberation, but TIEZA could use available funds totaling about 2.355 billion, including the stated unobligated allotment and unreleased operations figures. DOT described its sustainable-tourism convergence program, which had conducted 13 trainings for 417 participants. The Secretary committed to the requested tourism-destination inventory, while no specific budget augmentation or deadline was resolved.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish the personnel consequences if the travel tax were abolished and how tourism infrastructure and related projects would be financed without that revenue. It also asked whether TIEZA could receive augmented funding and whether DOT would prepare an inventory of tourism destinations.
topics.agency_position: DOT and DBM indicated that abolition of the travel tax would affect around 300 travel-tax personnel, with some terminated and others offered separation incentives. DBM said no requested FY 2027 national-government subsidy for TIEZA was included while abolition bills remained pending, but TIEZA could use available travel-tax collections and other funds for priority tourism projects; DOT also committed to support the requested destination-inventory effort.
topics.outcome: DBM explained that the requested FY 2027 TIEZA subsidy was not included because travel-tax abolition measures remained pending, while identifying TIEZA funds and other financing avenues that could be used for tourism projects. The destination-inventory issue resulted in a general commitment from the DOT Secretary, but no specific augmentation or submission deadline was settled.

positions.position: Supported the DOT budget but pressed for tourism-infrastructure augmentation, protection and development of destinations, employment-oriented tourism investment, and an inventory of tourism destinations.
Sought an alternative financing source for tourism and heritage projects if the travel tax were abolished.

topics.topic: Women and child safety, anti-trafficking, and tourism safeguards
topics.summary: Sarah Elago asked the DOT about regional focal persons, training, monitoring, and referral systems for women and child safety and anti-trafficking in tourism areas. The DOT reported 19 activities and 931 participants for 20 25, 16 hires, 1 responsible personnel in each regional office, and 40 trainings with 2001 participants from January to July 20 26. It said regional offices coordinated with police and with DOJ, DSWD, LGUs, ECPAT Philippines, the PNP, and IACAT. Elago also raised the 20 25 trafficking report and asked about access roads to declared tourism destinations. The DOT said those projects were not funded in the 20 27 NEP and committed to further coordination with DPWH and TIEZA on continuity and implementation.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish whether the DOT had functional regional focal persons, training, monitoring, and referral systems to address trafficking, sexual exploitation, violence against women, and child safety in tourism areas. It also asked about continuity of access-road projects serving declared tourism destinations.
topics.agency_position: The DOT said its regional offices had designated personnel, conducted community training, monitored incidents, and coordinated with police and partner agencies on women and child protection and anti-trafficking concerns. It also said the access-road projects were not funded in the 20 27 NEP and that discussions with DPWH and TIEZA were still needed to determine continuity and implementation.
topics.outcome: The DOT provided descriptions of its focal-person, training, monitoring, police-coordination, and interagency referral arrangements, but the record did not establish the adequacy of their funding or coverage. Access-road continuity remained subject to further discussions with DPWH and TIEZA.

positions.position: She pressed the DOT for evidence of functional regional focal persons, training coverage, monitoring, referral mechanisms, and action on trafficking, sexual exploitation, and violence against women in tourism destinations.

topics.topic: Dive, marine, and environmentally sustainable tourism
topics.summary: Secretary Dita Angara Matai presented dive tourism as a high-value sector generating about 1.3 billion in revenue, with 29 clusters and 956 dive sites identified nationwide. She said annual dive-tourism revenue could rise to about 100.5 billion by 2030 from about 73 billion in 20 23, and reported 3 30 certified dive professionals and individuals as of June 20 26. The committee cited 15200000 pesos for dive-destination development, promotion, and sustainability and asked how environmental safeguards were incorporated. The PCSSD executive director answered that the commission worked with the Marine Science Institute, Coral Beach Watch, and DENR-related officials, and that all programs included environmental standards. Representative Javi Benitez later questioned the balance between promotions, infrastructure, and cost, and raised dynamite fishing affecting marine sanctuaries. The DOT said promotions and infrastructure required equal effort, while an agency official said DENR generally led enforcement and undertook to revert with the missing data.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish how the DOT and its attached agencies would develop dive tourism while protecting marine ecosystems and ensuring environmental sustainability. Members also asked whether the DOT helped protect marine sanctuaries and how tourism promotion would be balanced with infrastructure and enforcement against threats such as dynamite fishing.
topics.agency_position: The DOT and PCSSD presented dive tourism as a high-value growth sector that depended on the Philippines' marine biodiversity, but said development had to incorporate quality, health and safety, and environmental standards. PCSSD cited partnerships and coordination with marine-science, environmental, and DENR-related institutions, while the DOT said promotions and infrastructure required equal effort to support a sustainable industry.
topics.outcome: The committee received the agency's explanation of PCSSD's environmental partnerships and program standards, but the DOT's specific role in protecting marine sanctuaries and the data on dynamite-fishing incidents remained subject to a later response. The agency also stated that promotions and infrastructure should receive equal priority.

positions.position: Tourism promotion should not proceed without adequate infrastructure and effective protection of marine sanctuaries; the DOT should have a meaningful role when environmental threats affect destinations it markets.
Dive-tourism development and the use of 15200000 pesos for destination development and promotion should be examined for environmental-sustainability safeguards.
