topics.topic: Outbound travel, foreign arrivals, and tourism competitiveness
topics.summary: Rep. Perci Cendaña raised the effects of fuel prices, airline capacity, and airport limitations on domestic travel costs and asked for DOTR commitments and a 2027 contingency plan. The DOT attributed high island-destination airfares to limited supply and infrastructure, and said it was finalizing a fuel-subsidy proposal while pursuing airport improvements, training, accreditation, branding, and private-sector partnerships. Rep. Elmer Catulpos then asked whether Filipinos were choosing neighboring countries because they were 20 to 30 percent cheaper, citing 7650000 outbound Filipinos and 5870000 foreign tourists; the DOT responded that domestic tourism remained the backbone, with 134000000 domestic tourists in 2024 and roughly 6000000 to 6480000 foreign arrivals in 2025. The DOT said 80 percent of tourism income came from domestic tourism and 20 percent from inbound tourism, while international marketing received 60 percent of the branding allocation and domestic marketing 40 percent. It identified 13 key markets, cited growth in China, Vietnam, and India, and said 50000000 was being used to address a 17 percent South Korean decline. The agency also discussed influencers and homegrown talents such as SB19 and cited a 230000000 pesos training budget for 2027; requested documents and the fuel-subsidy proposal were not shown as delivered.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish why domestic travel remained costly and how the DOT would improve tourism competitiveness amid fuel-price pressures, infrastructure constraints, and a limited budget. Members also asked whether outbound Filipino travel and changes in foreign-tourist arrivals reflected cheaper competing destinations, and how the DOT was allocating and targeting its marketing resources.
topics.agency_position: The DOT said competitiveness depended on airline support, airport and runway improvements, strategic prioritization, private-sector participation, targeted international marketing, and stronger worker training and accreditation. It maintained that domestic tourism remained the industry's backbone, while international campaigns would focus on 13 key markets, including efforts to reverse the 17 percent South Korean decline.
topics.outcome: The DOT answered the questions with its planned airport coordination, competitiveness, training, branding, and market-specific strategies, but the transcript did not show submission of the requested DOTR commitments or 2027 contingency plan. The issue therefore remained open on the requested documents and on whether the proposed interventions would reverse cost and arrival trends.

positions.position: The member pressed for more affordable domestic travel, coordination with DOTR and CAB, airport improvements, a fuel-subsidy contingency plan, and competitiveness and branding reforms. thread.said: He asked about branding, discipline, and internal-process reforms following the 2023 Love the Philippines campaign and sought measures that would build public trust and congressional confidence.

thread.speaker: Dita Angara Matai
thread.said: Angara-Mathai said the department had changed its public tone and visual direction, emphasizing Philippine destinations and Filipino people rather than officials' faces. She said the Love the Philippines campaign would use a more joyful, people-centered approach.

thread.speaker: Dita Angara Matai
thread.said: She said the DOT was in talks with Bini and SB19 and that the department was giving them until September to respond regarding possible partnerships.

thread.speaker: a committee member
thread.said: On behalf of members present, the member publicly requested and urged Bini and SB19 to join the DOT campaign.

thread.speaker: a committee member
thread.said: The member questioned the basis for claiming that the Philippines would make tourism easier and more affordable, warning against overpromising without actual industry investments and reforms.

thread.speaker: Dita Angara Matai

thread.said: Catulpos cited 7650000 Filipinos traveling abroad in 2025 and 5870000 foreign tourists, and asked whether Filipinos were choosing Vietnam, Thailand, and other neighboring countries because they were 20 to 30 percent cheaper than domestic travel.

thread.speaker: Zenny Palunia
thread.said: Palunia acknowledged that outbound travel exceeded 7000000 but said domestic tourism remained the backbone of the industry. She cited 134000000 domestic tourists in 2024 and said the Philippines received around 6000000 to 6480000 foreign tourists in 2025, while emphasizing length of stay and tourism receipts.

thread.speaker: Zenny Palunia
thread.said: Palunia said the Philippines ranked number 1 in tourism receipts among neighboring countries under the WTTC report, with about US2000 dollars plus per traveler. She said tourism was the country's number 3 dollar earner, after BPOs and OFWs.

thread.said: The official said 80 percent of tourism income came from domestic tourism and 20 percent from inbound tourism by foreigners.

thread.speaker: a committee member
thread.said: The member asked how a hypothetical 1000000000 branding or marketing budget would be divided between international and domestic tourism, noting that different audiences respond to different celebrities, icons, and advertising approaches.

The objective was to increase arrivals or arrest declines in those markets.

thread.speaker: a DOT marketing official
thread.said: The official cited year-on-year growth of 69 percent in China, around 29 percent in Vietnam, and around 30 percent in India following marketing stimuli.

thread.speaker: a DOT marketing official
thread.said: The official described market-specific strategies, including China routes and visa-free travel for 12 days, expansion to 8 other gateways, and links between secondary cities such as Chengdu and Chongqing and destinations including Bohol and Palawan.

thread.speaker: a DOT marketing official
thread.said: The official identified Indian weddings as a priority niche because large wedding groups could stay and spend for extended periods, benefiting hotels, airlines, and other tourism stakeholders.

thread.speaker: a DOT marketing official
thread.said: The official said South Korean arrivals had declined by 17 percent and that the DOT had allocated 50000000 to arrest or minimize that decline.

thread.speaker: a committee member
thread.said: The member asked whether the DOT was considering celebrities or influencers from target markets, or Filipino tourism workers, for its campaigns.

thread.said: The official said the DOT was considering influencers and celebrities with strong pull in target markets, including homegrown talents such as SB19. topics.topic: PSA civil-registration funding and organizational capacity
topics.summary: The bill sponsor sought funding for a modernized civil registration system, including digitization, expanded access, and anti-fraud safeguards. The PSA supported the bill and said the existing civil-registration law dated to 1931, but requested a stronger civil registration office under Section 6. It said the PSA and local civil registrars lacked sufficient capacity to expand registration services and protect records from fraud. The DBM answered that any office creation or strengthening would require its usual evaluation and review under the government optimization program. It also recommended using "existing retirement laws" and clarified that the legal service in Section 61 referred to the PSA's existing legal service. The organizational and funding issues remained open.
topics.question: The committee was considering whether the substitute bill and its funding should provide for a stronger Philippine Civil Registry Office within the PSA, given the need to expand services and protect records from fraud. It also sought to establish how the proposed organizational changes would be evaluated by the DBM and how the bill's legal-service provision should be interpreted.

The DBM did not reject the organizational provision but said any creation or strengthening must undergo DBM evaluation and the government optimization program, and it requested clarification of the retirement-law and legal-service language.
topics.outcome: The PSA's request for a stronger civil registration office and greater organizational capacity was placed on the record, but the DBM said the proposal remained subject to its evaluation and the government optimization program. DBM also placed proposed drafting clarifications on the record; no final decision on the requested strengthening or funding was stated.

topics.topic: 10% PSA registration-income retention for immediate operations
topics.summary: Rep. Monique Lagdameo initially moved to delete the Section 78 provision concerning PSA-generated income. Rep. Rufus Rodriguez objected, arguing that PSA should retain 10% of registration income for immediate operations and modernization instead of waiting for congressional appropriations. DBM said it preferred the one-fund concept but deferred to the committee, warning that retention would reduce money entering the General Fund. The PSA-side author subsequently supported retaining the provision, while Rep. Romeo Momo cautioned that other earning agencies might seek similar treatment. The agency estimated the 10% at about 1.139 billion based on 2025 revenue. Lagdameo revised the motion to exclude the Section 78 deletion, and the chair approved it without objection.
topics.question: The committee sought to determine whether Section 78 should retain a provision allowing the PSA to use 10% of civil-registration income for immediate operations and modernization, rather than placing all such income in the General Fund. Members also asked how much the retained income would yield.
topics.agency_position: The DBM official maintained that DBM preferred the one-fund concept because it would provide flexibility during budget preparation and would preserve more resources for the General Fund. However, DBM deferred to the committee's decision on allowing PSA to retain 10% of generated income and did not object on the record to the committee's approval.
topics.outcome: The committee approved the revised motion excluding the proposed deletion of Section 78, so the 10% PSA income-retention provision was retained. The agency estimated the 10% at 1,139,000,000 based on 2025 revenue, while the broader policy concern about setting a precedent for other earning agencies was left as a caution rather than resolved.

topics.topic: Infrastructure master plan council size and agency overlap
topics.summary: Romeo Momo Jr. sponsored a thirty-year infrastructure master plan and a presidentially chaired MIND Council. DEPDEV argued that the CIDMP and council substantially overlapped with functions already assigned to DEPDEV and related bodies under Republic Act number 12145, while DBM addressed staffing and appropriations language. Rep. Rodriguez questioned the proposed council of 28 members and suggested reducing it to about 11, with Rep. Pomerangay supporting agency participation only as needed. Romeo Momo Jr. said the broad membership was intended to prevent conflicts among infrastructure plans and agreed to review the membership issue. The committee ultimately adopted amendments requiring use of DEPDEV's existing staffing complement, DBM evaluation and approval of designations, and more general appropriations language, then approved the measure subject to those amendments.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish whether the proposed master plan and MIND Council duplicated existing DEPDEV functions, and whether the council's proposed membership was workable. It also considered how the council secretariat would be staffed and whether DBM approval would be required.
topics.agency_position: DEPDEV said the CIDMP and MIND Council substantially overlapped with functions already assigned to DEPDEV, the ED Council, and the Infrastructure Development Committee under Republic Act number 12145, and recommended strengthening existing structures instead of creating parallel ones. DBM supported use of DEPDEV's existing staffing complement and required DBM evaluation and approval for any designation or creation of positions, while favoring more flexible appropriations language.
topics.outcome: The committee adopted amendments addressing staffing, DBM oversight, and appropriations wording, then approved the measure subject to those amendments. The broader dispute over whether the MIND Council duplicated DEPDEV and whether its membership should be reduced was discussed, but no specific reduction in council membership was adopted in the recorded proceedings.

topics.topic: Disaster risk financing, DREAM Funds, and insurance structure
topics.summary: Rep. Joseph Lara sponsored the DRFI framework, citing annual disaster-related asset losses of about 177 billion and an equivalent of about US3.5 billion dollars. OCD supported the measure but asked that its relationship with the existing DREAM Funds be clearly defined and protected against duplication. DOF supported prearranged financing, multilayered risk financing, and parametric insurance, while the Insurance Commission sought clearer boundaries over government assets, existing institutions, asset prioritization, and claims guidelines. Treasury objected to creating a special fund because of the regular budget process, trust-receipt treatment of insurance proceeds, and the one-fund policy. DBM recommended calling it a program funded through a GAA line item and requiring DBM review of positions. The committee adopted those amendments and approved the measure, although a member's parametric-insurance clarification received a garbled and unclear response.
topics.question: The committee was trying to establish how the proposed disaster risk financing and insurance framework would complement existing DREAM Funds and government insurance arrangements, and whether the proposed financing mechanism should be a special fund or a program. It also sought to clarify the respective roles of the Insurance Commission, Department of Finance, Bureau of the Treasury, DBM, and the proposed DRFIB.
topics.agency_position: The agencies supported the DRFI substitute bill but sought clearer boundaries and implementation rules. OCD supported the framework as complementary to the DREAM Funds; DOF supported prearranged financing and parametric insurance; the Insurance Commission requested clarification of coverage and government-insurance responsibilities; Treasury opposed creating a special fund under the one-fund policy; and DBM recommended treating the mechanism as a program funded through a GAA line item.
topics.outcome: The committee adopted the agency-backed amendments, converting the proposed DRFI special fund into a program, subjecting implementation to DBM guidelines, and requiring DBM evaluation and approval of positions. It then approved the DRFI measure subject to those amendments; the precise response to the parametric-insurance clarification was left unclear in the transcript.

topics.topic: Community Driven Development appropriations and implementation safeguards
topics.summary: Rep. France Pomeran sponsored the substitute bill institutionalizing CDD and described its community-participation, transparency, accountability, and poverty-reduction objectives. DSWD supported the measure without objection, including the appropriations provision and the inclusion of amounts necessary for continued implementation in the annual General Appropriations Act. DBM requested flexible language referring to prevailing community-participation procurement guidelines and fiscal safeguards for agreements with LGUs. The committee adopted both amendments and approved the measure subject to them. No specific peso amount was stated; the appropriations commitment was described as current agency appropriations and amounts as may be necessary for continued implementation.
topics.question: The committee was determining whether to institutionalize Community Driven Development (CDD) as a national strategy, provide appropriations for its sustained implementation, and establish safeguards for participation, procurement, LGU agreements, accounting, and auditing. It also considered whether the proposed implementation provisions required technical amendments.
topics.agency_position: DSWD supported the substitute bill, had no objection to it, and supported the appropriations provision for sustained implementation subject to applicable budgeting, accounting, and auditing requirements. DBM supported clarifying the bill so procurement would follow prevailing community-participation guidelines and LGU agreements would remain subject to existing fiscal-control laws and regulations.
topics.outcome: The committee approved the CDD institutionalization measure subject to amendments. The amendments incorporated flexible, prevailing procurement guidance and explicit compliance with existing budgeting, accounting, and auditing requirements for LGU agreements.

topics.topic: Medical education infrastructure and CHED funding
topics.summary: The bill sponsor and an author presented the proposed Philippine Medical Act as a modernization measure covering medical education, internship, postgraduate training, and physician regulation. PRC supported the bill and noted the proposed increase in PRB membership from six to seven and terms from three years to five years. PRC nevertheless questioned the creation and budget of the PGMEC and proposed adapting the existing CPSP program instead. CHED supported the bill but requested financial support for subsidiary bodies, an organic secretariat, data infrastructure, fee utilization, and state universities and colleges. PRC committed to submit its position, but the transcript recorded no final resolution on the funding or PGMEC issues.
topics.question: The committee was seeking to establish how the proposed Philippine Medical Act would affect medical education, postgraduate training, regulatory councils, and the budgets of PRC and CHED. It also sought the agencies' positions on the proposed postgraduate medical education committee and the financial and infrastructure requirements of the new functions.
topics.agency_position: PRC and the Board of Medicine fully supported the substitute bill but expressed reservations about the PGMEC, citing budget differences and proposing use of the existing CPSP program instead. CHED also fully supported the bill but asked that its new regulatory responsibilities be matched with funding for subsidiary bodies, an organic secretariat, data infrastructure, fee utilization, and support for state universities and colleges.
topics.outcome: The agencies supported the bill but identified unresolved funding and institutional-design issues. PRC undertook to submit its position on the PGMEC, while CHED recommended budget and infrastructure adjustments; no final funding decision was recorded.

positions.position: Supported the bill as necessary to modernize medical education, internship, postgraduate training, and physician regulation.

topics.topic: Resident and fellow compensation and DBM salary review
topics.summary: The DOH supported improving resident and fellow compensation but requested further study and a budgetary impact analysis. It identified the current entry-level resident classification as salary grade 21 and the proposed classification as salary grade 22. DBM warned that a fixed salary grade 22 minimum could distort hospital employee salaries and proposed using the revised compensation and position classification system, subject to DBM review and applicable rules. The sponsors accepted the DBM recommendations, including safeguards for the medical councils and budgeting, accounting, and auditing provisions. The committee approved the amendments and then approved the measure subject to those amendments, while the requested budgetary impact study remained unaddressed as a separate action.
topics.question: The committee was determining how the proposed compensation increase for residents and fellows should be evaluated, including its budgetary impact and compatibility with the government compensation system. It also considered DBM safeguards for the creation of medical councils and provisions affecting foreign medical graduates.
topics.agency_position: The DOH supported improving resident and fellow compensation, including review of the current salary classification, but called for further studies and a budgetary impact analysis. DBM opposed prescribing a fixed salary grade 22 floor because of possible salary distortions and instead sought application of the revised compensation and position classification system, subject to DBM evaluation and approval and applicable laws and regulations.
topics.outcome: The committee removed the fixed salary grade 22 floor and adopted DBM's revised compensation and position classification approach, subject to DBM evaluation and approval. The amendments and the Philippine Medical Act measure were approved without objection; the DOH's requested budgetary impact study was not separately resolved in the transcript.

topics.topic: Local-government performance incentives and SGLG funding
topics.summary: Rep. Albert Garcia sponsored a bill establishing a data-driven performance-measurement system for local governments and linking improvements to performance-based rewards. He cited a system covering about 42,000 barangayes, 1,400-plus local-government units, about 180 cities, and 82 provinces. DBM recommended removing national government agencies from the scope, requiring DBM approval for additional positions, coordinating with DILG on barangay bonuses, retaining the SGLG fund, and preserving the 2% operating-fund provision. Garcia accepted the DBM comments, and the committee adopted corresponding amendments, including retention of SGLG provisions and deletion of references to national government agencies. The committee approved the amendments and the measure, subject to style.
topics.question: The committee was determining how the proposed performance-measurement and meritocracy system would apply to local governments and barangays, including the treatment of national government agencies. It also examined whether the Seal of Good Local Governance (SGLG) fund, barangay performance-based bonuses, DBM approval requirements, and the 2% operating-fund cap should be retained or amended.
topics.agency_position: DBM supported adjusting the bill to remove national government agencies from its scope while retaining DBM approval for additional positions, coordinating with DILG on barangay performance bonuses, and preserving and harmonizing the SGLG fund provisions. DBM also supported retaining the 2% SGLG-fund operating provision, subject to drafting harmonization and style.
topics.outcome: The committee approved the amendments and then approved the measure subject to those amendments and style. The approved package removed national government agencies, retained the SGLG fund provisions, preserved the 2% phrase, and added DBM approval and DILG-DBM coordination requirements.

topics.topic: DFA FY2027 budget request, allotment classes, and utilization
topics.summary: The DFA presented an FY2027 request of about 35 billion, while its stated net level for the department and attached agencies was 35,170,000,000, 17% above the 2026 net. Maintenance and other operating expenses accounted for 54% of the request, personnel services for 39%, and capital outlay for 7%; major items included next-generation passport funding, the International Commitments Fund, ATN and legal assistance, ICT, and the building fund. The agency reported an 80% 2025 BUR and close to 53% utilization in the first half of the current year, attributing lower performance to delayed retrofitting, transferred ATN functions, deferred building projects, and changing passport demand. Members requested detailed spending and program documents, particularly for the Security Council campaign, ATN Fund, ICT, and ePassport allocations. Rodriguez supported placing 250,000,000 for cybersecurity and restoring 300,000,000 to the building fund, while the Foreign Service Institute sought MXN 6,500,000 for HMO coverage. The committee left the additional funding requests for written submission and subsequent consideration, with a deadline set for the following Wednesday.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish the DFA and attached agencies’ FY2027 funding requirement, the distribution of that request across allotment classes, the reasons for the increase, and the department’s utilization performance. Members also examined specific funding needs for passports, ICT and cybersecurity, buildings, consular operations, HMO, and permanent positions, and identified documents or augmentations to be submitted for further consideration.
topics.agency_position: The DFA presented the FY2027 request as necessary to sustain overseas and consular services, implement the next-generation passport, strengthen ICT and cybersecurity, maintain overseas properties, and support foreign-policy operations. It reported strong physical performance but acknowledged utilization constraints and committed to submit requested budget, expenditure, and program documents.
topics.outcome: The DFA’s proposed budget was presented and supported, but several augmentations and requests remained subject to written endorsement and later committee or plenary consideration. The agency committed to submit the requested ICT, ePassport, ATN, campaign-expenditure, and wish-list documents.

Supported assistance-to-nationals programs but sought stronger transparency on ATN guidelines and Security Council campaign expenditures.
Sought a detailed justification and breakdown of the ICT and ePassport allocations, particularly their security and data-protection components.
Supported the DFA budget and endorsed additional funding for cybersecurity and the building fund, as well as HMO and other agency requests.

thread.speaker: Rep. Niko Raul Daza
thread.said: Daza manifested support for the proposed FY2027 DFA and attached-agency budget in the amount of 35,000,000,000 pesos. He said the funding would support diplomacy, national interests, overseas Filipinos, and consular services.

thread.speaker: Secretary Maria Theresa Lazaro
thread.said: Lazaro said the DFA’s work remained anchored on national security, economic security, and protection of Filipinos overseas. She presented the FY2027 request as funding for national security, economic diplomacy, consular services, assistance to nationals, and organizational development.

thread.speaker: Secretary Maria Theresa Lazaro
thread.said: Lazaro said the department was seeking a total FY2027 budget of approximately 35,000,000,173, million. The final portion of the spoken figure was unclear in the transcript.

thread.speaker: Assistant Secretary Robespierre Bolivar
thread.said: Bolivar stated that the DFA was requesting PHP 35,000,000,000, representing 0.49% of the proposed national budget.

thread.speaker: Assistant Secretary Emilio Fernandez
thread.said: Fernandez reported that the FY2027 net level for the DFA and attached agencies was 35,170,000,000, a 17% increase from the 2026 net of PHP30.09 billion.

thread.speaker: Assistant Secretary Emilio Fernandez
thread.said: Fernandez said the proposed amount had increased by about 1,000,000,000 in 2026 and by some 6,300,000,000 in 2027.

thread.speaker: Assistant Secretary Emilio Fernandez
thread.said: Fernandez said the FY2027 net budget consisted of 54% for maintenance and other operating expenses, 39% for personnel services, and 7% for capital outlay.

thread.speaker: Assistant Secretary Emilio Fernandez
thread.said: Fernandez attributed the increase to salary and foreign-service-allowance tranches, the integration of the Technical Cooperation Council, initial next-generation passport funding of 2,800,000,000, foreign-exchange and inflation provisions, higher rents, and the maintenance-and-other-operating-expenses component of ICT projects.

thread.speaker: Assistant Secretary Emilio Fernandez
thread.said: Fernandez said there would be no FY2027 capital-outlay funding for the car-refleeting program or ISSP projects and no appropriation for opening additional foreign-service posts.

thread.speaker: Assistant Secretary Emilio Fernandez
thread.said: For personnel services, Fernandez cited funding for more than 3,000 personnel, PHP9.9 billion for foreign-service allowances, and about PHP345 million for terminal-leave benefits.

thread.speaker: Assistant Secretary Emilio Fernandez
thread.said: For maintenance and other operating expenses, Fernandez cited PHP 5,800,000,000 for passports, 3,000,000,000 for the International Commitments Fund, PHP1.2 billion for the ATN and Legal Assistance Fund, and additional ICT, Deployment Fund, and overseas-voting allocations. The ICT and Deployment Fund figures were unclear in the transcript; the overseas-voting figure was spoken as MXN45 million.

thread.speaker: Assistant Secretary Emilio Fernandez
thread.said: Fernandez said the building fund was 400,000,000 for redevelopment, acquisition, expansion, and major repairs of government-owned chanceries and official residences abroad.

thread.speaker: Assistant Secretary Emilio Fernandez
thread.said: Fernandez reported a 2025 financial-performance BUR of 80% and said utilization covered passports, the International Commitments Fund, building funds, the retrofitting project, ATN and Legal Assistance Funds, and car refleet­ing.

thread.speaker: Assistant Secretary Emilio Fernandez
thread.said: Fernandez attributed lower utilization to delayed headquarters retrofitting after an unsuccessful initial bid, the transfer of ATN functions to the Department of Migrant Workers, deferred building projects, and shifting passport demand after validity was extended to ten years.

thread.speaker: Assistant Secretary Emilio Fernandez
thread.said: Fernandez reported first-half utilization close to 53% and said the DFA would ensure proper utilization of remaining funds, hoping to equal or surpass the prior year’s result.

thread.speaker: DFA fiscal-management official
thread.said: The official said 70,000,000 pesos had been appropriated in 2025 and 2026 for the UN Security Council campaign, of which 52,500,000 was obligated, representing 75% utilization.

thread.speaker: Rep. Dadah Kiram Ismula
thread.said: Ismula requested expenditures by category for the Security Council campaign, including diplomatic missions, travel, representation, promotional activities, and other campaign-related expenses, together with a post-campaign accountability assessment.

thread.speaker: DFA fiscal-management official
thread.said: The official said that from 2022 to 2025, 1,000,000,000 was appropriated annually for the Assistance to Nationals Fund.

thread.speaker: DFA migrant-affairs official
thread.said: For 2026, the official cited 387 repatriation beneficiaries from January to July, dollars 559,000,000 for welfare assistance, 20,000,000 for medical assistance, 40,000,000 for shipment of remains, and a total of 2,884 beneficiaries for the first six months. The welfare-assistance currency and figures were spoken as transcribed.

thread.speaker: Rep. Dadah Kiram Ismula
thread.said: Ismula requested a copy of the guidelines governing use of the ATN Fund, including approval and denial criteria and approving authorities.

thread.speaker: Rep. Antonio Tinio
thread.said: Tinio asked about the proposed ICT expenditures of 956,610,000, the current-year ICT budget and utilization, and why the department required the proposed increase.

thread.speaker: DFA assistant secretary for ICT
thread.said: The official said ICT expenditures were reviewed through the interagency committee composed of DICT, DBM, and other agencies. The official described increases of 115% in the maintenance-and-other-operating-expenses budget and 400% in ISSP capital outlay as a shift toward enterprise-grade assets supporting cybersecurity, data protection, digital transformation, and strategic ICT systems.

thread.speaker: DFA assistant secretary for ICT
thread.said: The official cited ongoing ICT projects amounting to 511,000,000, including critical-infrastructure resilience, the eVisa system, and the passport system.

thread.speaker: Rep. Antonio Tinio
thread.said: Tinio asked for a breakdown of the ePassport budget, which he identified as 5,500,000,000, separately from the 956,000,000 ICT allocation, including services, providers, and spending for 2025, 2026, and proposed 2027.

thread.speaker: DFA assistant secretary for ICT
thread.said: The official said the DFA would comply and submit the requested ePassport and ICT breakdown. The official said a list was already available and would be sent to the committee.

thread.speaker: Secretary Maria Theresa Lazaro
thread.said: Lazaro identified cybersecurity as a priority because the DFA had been receiving repeated attacks, particularly while the Philippines chaired ASEAN. She initially stated the need as 10,000,000, then corrected or clarified it as 10,000,000 billion; the transcript is unclear.

thread.speaker: DFA fiscal-management official
thread.said: The official said DBM had reduced the DFA’s capital outlay by 500,000,000 and proposed a minimum cybersecurity request of 250,000,000, compared with an ICT capital-outlay requirement of 511,000,000.

thread.speaker: Rep. Eulogio Rodriguez
thread.said: Rodriguez said the committee would place 250,000,000 for cybersecurity on the record and support the DFA’s request.

thread.speaker: DFA fiscal-management official
thread.said: The official said the proposed FY2027 building fund was 400,000,000, reduced from 1.75 in the current year, and requested restoration of 300,000,000 that had been cut.

thread.speaker: Rep. Eulogio Rodriguez
thread.said: Rodriguez confirmed that the requested building-fund augmentation was an additional 300,000,000 and said it was reasonable and would receive his support.

thread.speaker: Foreign Service Institute official
thread.said: The Foreign Service Institute requested HMO coverage for almost 100 personnel amounting to MXN 6,500,000.

thread.speaker: Presidential Commission on Visiting Forces official
thread.said: The official said the commission would seek to convert 13 contractual positions into permanent positions to preserve institutional knowledge and fiduciary functions. The request was estimated at a little less than 3,000,000 in additional personnel-services costs, but was for a future year rather than FY2027.

thread.speaker: Rep. Eulogio Rodriguez
thread.said: Rodriguez requested a letter from the DFA to the appropriations chair detailing the department’s wish list, including the Foreign Service Institute HMO request, the building-fund augmentation, cybersecurity funding, and the proposed special provision on chancery and consulate leases.

thread.speaker: Committee chair
thread.said: The chair said additional DFA funding requests had to be properly endorsed and signed by the secretary and submitted by Wednesday of the following week.

topics.topic: Assistance to Nationals and Legal Assistance Funds for overseas Filipinos
topics.summary: The committee asked the DFA to clarify ATN and LAF coverage, appropriations, utilization, eligibility rules, and approval authority after the DMW assumed responsibility for more OFWs. The DFA said 1,000,000,000 was appropriated annually for the ATN Fund from 2022 to 2025 and reported 2,884 ATN beneficiaries from January to July 2026, including 387 repatriation beneficiaries. It also cited welfare assistance of dollars 559,000,000, medical assistance of 20,000,000, and shipment of remains of 40,000,000, although some wording and currency attribution were unclear. The DFA said it generally did not deny qualified requests and that its office handled recommendations below 20%, while the Secretary approved amounts above that threshold. Members requested the ATN guidelines and detailed ATN and LAF utilization records, including balances, expenditures, approvals, rejections, nonqualifications, and beneficiaries. The DFA also described ongoing coordination on distressed seafarers and safe passage through embassies, MWOs, DMW, the IMO, and bilateral channels.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish how the Assistance to Nationals (ATN) Fund and Legal Assistance Fund (LAF) were allocated, utilized, and administered, including which overseas Filipinos remained covered after the creation of the Department of Migrant Workers (DMW). It also sought beneficiary, expenditure, approval, rejection, eligibility, and utilization data, as well as the DFA's continuing assistance to distressed OFWs and seafarers.
topics.agency_position: The DFA said ATN and LAF assistance remained available to distressed overseas Filipinos within the DFA's mandate, particularly in countries without MWOs and for categories such as tourists, students, pilgrims, permanent residents, and dual citizens. It said qualified requests were generally approved rather than denied, while the DMW increasingly handled OFWs as more MWOs opened.
topics.outcome: The DFA explained the division of responsibility between the DFA and DMW and supplied partial ATN utilization and beneficiary figures. The committee requested additional ATN and LAF records and guidelines; the requested documentation was not submitted during the hearing.

positions.position: Supported the ATN program but sought transparency on utilization, eligibility, approval and denial criteria, and the final approving authority.
Pressed for detailed, country-level ATN and LAF approval data and a full accounting of balances, expenditures, and beneficiaries.
Raised the continuing need for assistance and safe-passage protections for OFWs and seafarers, including coordination with the IMO.

actions.action: Provide the committee a copy of the guidelines governing use of the ATN Fund.
Provide a report on ATN and LAF requests in countries without MWOs, including approvals, rejections, and nonqualification.

thread.speaker: Secretary Maria Theresa Lazaro
thread.said: Secretary Lazaro identified the protection of the rights and welfare of Filipinos overseas, including consular services and assistance to nationals, as one of the DFA's three foreign-policy pillars.

thread.speaker: Assistant Secretary Robespierre Bolivar
thread.said: Bolivar said there were 10,500,000 Filipinos overseas, including 2,700,000 overseas Filipino workers under the direct purview of the DMW. He said the DFA continued to assist other overseas Filipinos, including tourists, students, migrants, and spouses of foreign nationals.

thread.speaker: Assistant Secretary Robespierre Bolivar
thread.said: Bolivar reported almost 3,000 ATN Fund beneficiaries and 16 Legal Assistance Fund beneficiaries as of July 31. He also said the DFA had repatriated more than 1,000 human-trafficking victims and almost 2,000 Filipinos during the Middle East crisis.

thread.speaker: Representative Dadah Kiram Ismula
thread.said: Representative Ismula asked about ATN Fund utilization for Filipinos in distress abroad and sought the total ATN appropriations from June 2022 to June 2026.

thread.speaker: DFA fiscal management official
thread.said: The fiscal management official said that from 2022 to 2025, 1,000,000,000 was appropriated annually for the ATN Fund.

thread.speaker: Representative Dadah Kiram Ismula
thread.said: Ismula followed up by asking for the FY2026 ATN requests that were approved, denied, returned, or pending.

thread.speaker: DFA official responsible for assistance to nationals
thread.said: The official reported 387 repatriation beneficiaries from January to July, welfare assistance of dollars 559,000,000, medical assistance of 20,000,000, and shipment of remains of 40,000,000, for a total of 2,884 beneficiaries during the first six months of the year. The transcript's wording and attribution of the amounts were not clarified further.

thread.speaker: Representative Dadah Kiram Ismula
thread.said: Ismula asked for the specific guidelines and criteria governing approval and denial of ATN requests, including the final approving authority.

thread.speaker: DFA official responsible for assistance to nationals
thread.said: The official said a 2019 department order governed the ATN and LAF guidelines. The office prepared recommendations for approval for amounts below 20%, while amounts above that threshold required the Secretary's approval.

thread.speaker: Representative Dadah Kiram Ismula
thread.said: Ismula manifested a request that the DFA provide the committee a copy of the guidelines on the use of the ATN Fund.

thread.speaker: DFA official responsible for assistance to nationals
thread.said: The official explained that the ATN Fund covered repatriation, welfare, and other assistance for Filipinos in distress overseas, while the LAF covered the hiring of lawyers and retainers for OFWs overseas. The establishment of RA 11 thousand six hundred forty one in 2023 and the opening of more MWOs had lowered ATN utilization because the DMW assumed responsibility for more OFWs.

thread.speaker: DFA official responsible for assistance to nationals
thread.said: The DFA official said the DFA remained responsible for countries without MWOs and for tourists, pilgrims, students, permanent residents, and dual citizens worldwide. The DFA continued coordinating with the DMW where applicable.

thread.speaker: DFA official responsible for assistance to nationals
thread.said: The official said there were 42 MWOs in 31 countries, leaving about 67 embassies without an MWO. From January to July 2026, the ATN Fund assisted 2,884 beneficiaries, including 387 for repatriation, and the official cited five fifty nine for welfare assistance, medical assistance of 20,000,000, and 40,000,000 for shipment of remains.

thread.speaker: DFA official responsible for assistance to nationals
thread.said: The official said the DFA did not keep data on pending or rejected requests because it did not really deny qualified requests. If applicants qualified under the rules and the case was not under the DMW, the DFA moved to approve the assistance.

thread.speaker: Representative Antonio Tinio
thread.said: Tinio asked whether the DFA could provide a report for countries without MWOs showing ATN and LAF requests that were approved, rejected, or found to be nonqualifying.

thread.speaker: Representative Antonio Tinio
thread.said: Tinio requested a full ATN utilization status report, including the fund balance, expenditure categories, itemized expenditures, and the number of beneficiaries for each expense.

thread.speaker: Secretary Maria Theresa Lazaro
thread.said: On overseas voting, Secretary Lazaro attributed low turnout to multiple factors and said the DFA had met with COMELEC and established a technical working group to examine the capacity of foreign service posts and improve voter awareness, registration, and participation.

thread.speaker: Secretary Maria Theresa Lazaro
thread.said: Secretary Lazaro offered to provide a written paper explaining the various reasons for overseas voting difficulties, including technical and online-voting issues and region-specific obstacles.

thread.speaker: DFA official
thread.said: The official said OFWs and seafarers were already under DMW jurisdiction and that reports were coming from the DMW, which had its own monitoring mechanism. The DFA took charge where applicable and referred detailed matters to its migrant affairs officials.

thread.speaker: DFA migrant-affairs official
thread.said: The migrant-affairs official said 14 seafarers on the same ship, as well as remains, were being assisted through coordination among the MWO, the embassy, and DMW. The official emphasized that seafarers had the right to refuse work in areas determined to be dangerous and said embassies, MWOs, and DMW held regular meetings with manning agencies.

thread.speaker: Representative Sarah Elago
thread.said: Representative Elago asked about engagement with the International Maritime Organization and sought an update concerning seafarers' right to refuse sailing in higher-risk areas or corridors.

thread.speaker: DFA official
thread.said: The official said the DFA had previously raised safe passage for Philippine-flag vessels with the Iranian Foreign Minister, but that control of the situation had shifted. The DFA was therefore working through the IMO and bilateral channels, including with Panama, to address safe passage and seafarer protection.

thread.speaker: DFA official
thread.said: The official said the DFA would provide a detailed report, referring to a report sent two days earlier to Nairobi. The exact subject of the report was unclear in the transcript.

topics.topic: Consular-service expansion, satellite offices, and passport access
topics.summary: Rep. Niko Raul Daza supported the DFA budget and cited the funded forty third consular office in Katarman, Northern Samar as an example of service expansion. The DFA reported 42 consular offices, more than 1.5 million passports processed, and 35 passport on wheels activities as of 08/31/2026. Rep. Eulogio Rodriguez asked the DFA to account for distance, isolation, travel costs, and accessibility in underserved provinces and specifically raised a possible satellite office in Catanhuanes. The DFA said it was assessing existing and proposed offices under operational, fiscal, geographic, DBM, and Executive Order 45 criteria, while studying a satellite model and offering passport on wheels in the interim. Bukidnon and Virac-Catanhuanes requests, consular vehicles, and facility funding remained under review. Rep. Rufus Rodriguez supported an additional building-fund request of about 300 million and other DFA requests, subject to written submissions and further budget consideration.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish how the DFA was expanding access to consular services, particularly for provinces without a consular office, and whether new, satellite, or mobile facilities could address geographic isolation and travel costs. It also examined the funding and administrative requirements for proposed offices, vehicles, buildings, and related consular infrastructure.
topics.agency_position: The DFA said it was conducting a nationwide assessment of existing and proposed consular facilities, balancing demand and accessibility against proximity, operational viability, fiscal sustainability, DBM guidance, and Executive Order 45. It had no established satellite-office model but was studying a smaller Catanhuanes facility, while offering passport on wheels as an interim option; requests for Bukidnon, Virac-Catanhuanes, vehicles, and additional building funds remained subject to review and coordination with DBM.
topics.outcome: The DFA answered the accessibility and satellite-office questions and committed to provide a written status update and coordinate with DBM, while offering passport on wheels as an interim service. The proposed permanent facilities, vehicle requests, and funding augmentations were supported in principle but remained subject to DBM review and subsequent written budget action.

positions.position: Supported the DFA budget and endorsed bringing consular services closer to Filipinos, citing the funded forty third consular office in Katarman, Northern Samar.
Pressed the DFA to prioritize geographic accessibility and supported written follow-up and additional support for proposed consular facilities, vehicles, and building funds.
Manifested that she would not interpolate further if she received a commitment for a consular office in her Bukidnon district.
Raised a request for a consular office and regional access, although the transcript is unclear on the precise request.
Supported the DFA's consular and facilities requests, including the proposed additional 300,000,000 for the building fund and consideration of consular-office enlargement.

topics.topic: ePassport budget of 5,500,000,000 and procurement breakdown
topics.summary: Assistant Secretary Emilio Fernandez presented passport funding as a major component of the DFA's proposed budget, including 2,800,000,000 for initial next-generation-passport funding and PHP 5,800,000,000 for passports overall. Representative Antonio Tinio then questioned the separate proposed ICT allocation of 956,610,000 and asked what the agency was actually purchasing. The ICT official described a shift toward large-scale capital assets, cited 511,000,000 in ICT projects, and identified the ePassport and passport appointment system among the covered systems. Tinio requested a year-by-year breakdown of ePassport services, providers, and procurement for 2025 through 2027. The DFA committed to provide the list and said the passport database was maintained by a third-party government printer at its facility in Lima, Batangas. The spending breakdown remained pending, so the issue landed as committed rather than fully resolved.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish why the DFA proposed a large ePassport allocation separate from its ICT expenditures, and how the passport budget would be divided among services, providers, and related procurements. It also sought clarification on the location and security of the passport database.
topics.agency_position: The DFA said the passport allocation included implementation of the next-generation passport, while ICT expenditures supported broader cybersecurity, digital-transformation, infrastructure, and consular systems. It said the ePassport database was maintained by a third-party government printer at the provider's facility in Lima, Batangas, and undertook to submit the requested multi-year procurement and provider breakdown.
topics.outcome: The DFA answered the database-location question and committed to submit the requested breakdown of ePassport services, providers, and procurement by year. The composition and justification of the 5,500,000,000 allocation were not fully examined on the record.

positions.position: Tinio questioned the separation between the 5,500,000,000 ePassport allocation and the 956,610,000 ICT allocation, sought a detailed procurement breakdown, and raised concerns about passport-data privacy, security, and sovereignty.
The member sought confirmation that the passport database was physically maintained in the Philippines rather than in a cloud service or another country.

topics.topic: ICT budget of about 956.6 million, cybersecurity, and data privacy
topics.summary: Rep. Antonio Tinio questioned the DFA's proposed ICT spending of about 956.6 million and sought utilization data and a detailed breakdown of the separate ePassport budget of about 5.5 billion. The DFA explained that ICT spending had shifted toward major capital assets and identified cybersecurity, data privacy, digital transformation and consular systems as priorities. It said current ICT projects totaled 511,000,000 and committed to submit a year-by-year and provider-by-provider breakdown. In response to questions about passport-data security, the DFA said the passport database was maintained on a server at the Apo production facility in Lima, Batangas, rather than in an external cloud. Secretary Maria Theresa Lazaro and an ICT official sought cybersecurity funding, with the transcript containing an unclear initial reference to 10,000,000 followed by "Billion," while 250,000,000 was ultimately placed on the record as the minimum request. Rep. Rufus Rodriguez and the chair supported further consideration of the request, subject to a written, signed and endorsed wish list.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish how the DFA's proposed ICT expenditures and ePassport budget were allocated, how much had been utilized, and why the proposed ICT amount had increased. It also sought assurances about cybersecurity, passport-data privacy and sovereignty, and considered additional funding requests for cybersecurity and related ICT capital outlay.
topics.agency_position: The DFA said the proposed increase in ICT spending was a deliberate shift toward enterprise-grade capital assets needed for cybersecurity, data privacy, digital transformation and critical consular systems. It maintained that substantial cybersecurity funding was necessary because of repeated attacks and the sensitivity of passport data, and committed to submit Rep. Tinio's requested ICT and ePassport breakdown.
topics.outcome: The ICT and cybersecurity issues were not finally resolved through a detailed budget reconciliation. The DFA committed to submit the requested breakdown and written wish list, while the committee signaled support for considering 250,000,000 for cybersecurity and restoring about 300,000,000 to the building fund.

positions.position: Sought a detailed, year-by-year and provider-by-provider breakdown of ICT and ePassport spending and pressed the DFA to explain how passport data was protected and kept under Philippine data sovereignty.
Supported the DFA's proposed budget and manifested support for restoring 250,000,000 for cybersecurity, about 300,000,000 for the building fund, and the department's other documented requests.
Supported consideration of the DFA's additional requests, subject to a properly endorsed and signed wish list submitted by the following Wednesday.

topics.topic: Foreign-service building fund, facilities, and office accommodation
topics.summary: Eulogio Rodriguez asked how the DFA would bring consular services closer to residents of underserved and geographically isolated provinces, and the DFA said it was assessing 42 offices and considering a smaller satellite-office model for Catanhuanes. The chair proposed passport-on-wheels services while the request and DBM guidelines were pending, and the DFA undertook to provide a written status update. Jay Vergara raised a 31,000-square-meter LGO-funded consular site and related regional concerns. Rufus Rodriguez then sought the DFA's broader facilities and funding priorities; the agency identified cybersecurity, a special leasing provision, and the building fund. The committee placed 250,000,000 for cybersecurity on the record and supported restoring 300,000,000 to the building fund. The requests were not finally appropriated in the exchange; the DFA was required to submit a signed additional wish list for further committee consideration.

topics.topic: Foreign-service allowances, HMO, and permanent-position requirements

The Foreign Service Institute requested HMO coverage amounting to MXN 6.5 million for almost 100 personnel, and the VFA Presidential Mission requested 13 permanent positions requiring a little less than 3 million in additional PS. topics.topic: West Philippine Sea diplomatic protests and China provisional arrangement
topics.summary: Rep. Perci Cendaña asked the DFA to explain the written Philippines-China provisional arrangement for RORE missions, its negotiating authority, and whether it limited Philippine activities in the exclusive economic zone. Secretary Maria Theresa Lazaro said it was an exchange of notes limited to Ayungin Shoal, without prejudice to Philippine positions under UNCLOS and the 2016 arbitral award, and focused on information exchange for daily necessities. She committed to making the arrangement's details available, and reported 16 RORE missions without incident over two years. Rep. Brian Poe asked about diplomatic protests, and DFA officials reported 39 protests in 2026 and 296 from 2022 to 2026, while noting that diplomacy could take time to produce results. In the second round, Rep. Antonio Tinio challenged Chinese Embassy statements concerning construction materials and the arbitral award; the DFA denied that construction materials were covered by the arrangement and said it raised concerns through diplomatic channels. The complete text and the DFA's response to each public embassy statement were not fully resolved in the hearing.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish the scope, legal character, operational effect, and disclosure status of the Philippines-China provisional arrangement for rotation and resupply missions in the West Philippine Sea. It also examined the DFA's diplomatic protests against China and its response to public statements by the Chinese Embassy in Manila.
topics.agency_position: The DFA stated that the provisional arrangement was a limited exchange of notes for information exchange and the safe conduct of RORE missions at Ayungin Shoal, covering the reprovisioning of daily necessities and not requiring Philippine permission from China. It maintained that the arrangement was without prejudice to Philippine sovereignty, territorial claims, UNCLOS position, or the 2016 arbitral award, and said it had responded through diplomatic channels to Chinese positions and statements.
topics.outcome: The DFA clarified the arrangement's stated scope and said it did not contain a restriction on construction materials, but the complete terms were not disclosed in the hearing. The committee recorded the secretary's undertaking to share the arrangement's details, while questions about the DFA's public response to individual Chinese Embassy statements remained only partly answered.

positions.position: He pressed for disclosure of the complete provisional arrangement to the congressional committee, including in a confidential or executive session if necessary.

He supported continued diplomatic protests whenever Philippine sovereignty was violated and viewed the reduction in water-cannoning and laser incidents as a positive result of the whole-of-government approach.
He sought a definitive clarification of the arrangement's provisions and questioned the DFA's response to what he regarded as inflammatory Chinese Embassy statements.

actions.action: Provide the congressional committee with the details or complete terms of the Philippines-China provisional arrangement, including in executive or confidential session if necessary.
actions.who: Rep. Perci Cendaña and Secretary Maria Theresa Lazaro

thread.speaker: Rep. Perci Cendaña
thread.said: He asked about the nature and scope of the DFA-referenced arrangement with China concerning rotation and resupply missions, or RORE missions, in the West Philippine Sea.

thread.speaker: Secretary Maria Theresa Lazaro
thread.said: She said the provisional arrangement arose after the tense June 2024 incident involving Philippine personnel and at the request of security agencies. She described it as allowed under UNCLOS, without prejudice to the Philippines' positions and the 2016 arbitral award, and centered on information exchange.

thread.speaker: Rep. Perci Cendaña
thread.said: He asked whether the arrangement was written, specifically whether it took the form of an exchange of notes, and under whose authority it was negotiated.

thread.speaker: Secretary Maria Theresa Lazaro
thread.said: She confirmed that it was an exchange of notes and said the security agencies, particularly the NSC, were very much involved in the negotiations.

thread.speaker: Rep. Perci Cendaña
thread.said: He asked whether the arrangement limited the Philippines' ability to conduct resupply, rotation, repair, or other activities within its exclusive economic zone.

thread.speaker: Secretary Maria Theresa Lazaro
thread.said: She said it was a provisional arrangement limited to Ayungin Shoal and specifically concerned the Philippine vessel involved in RORE missions. She explained that RORE meant rotation and reprovisioning of necessities.

thread.speaker: Rep. Perci Cendaña
thread.said: He asked whether the DFA would provide the appropriate congressional committee with the complete terms of the arrangement, including in an executive or confidential session if necessary.

thread.speaker: Secretary Maria Theresa Lazaro
thread.said: She said the DFA was at the committee's disposal and confirmed that there had been 16 RORE missions over the past two years without incident.

thread.speaker: Rep. Perci Cendaña
thread.said: He said the committee would hold the secretary to her commitment to share the details of the arrangement made with China.

thread.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
thread.said: He asked about the status and results of Philippine diplomatic protests relating to the West Philippine Sea, noting that he understood 27 protests had been filed in the first half of the year.

thread.speaker: Secretary Maria Theresa Lazaro
thread.said: She said the DFA had issued 39 diplomatic protests in 2026. She identified a decrease in water-cannoning and laser incidents as the main observable change, while noting that Chinese military vessels continued to be cited by Philippine defense establishments.

thread.speaker: DFA executive director for maritime affairs
thread.said: He said the DFA had issued 39 protests in 2026 and 296 diplomatic protests from 2022 to 2026. He cautioned that results on the ground could take time because diplomacy had to work with security agencies and the National Maritime Council as part of a whole-of-government effort.

thread.speaker: Rep. Antonio Tinio
thread.said: He asked whether the provisional agreement or understanding with China was secret and requested that the DFA set the record straight on its existence and character.

thread.speaker: Secretary Maria Theresa Lazaro
thread.said: Citing the President's statement at a FOCAP meeting, she said the arrangement was intended to prevent miscalculation and escalation. She said it did not weaken Philippine sovereignty, territorial claims, UNCLOS position, arbitral award, or exercise of sovereign rights.

thread.speaker: Rep. Antonio Tinio
thread.said: He cited a Chinese Embassy statement referring to humanitarian resupply and opposition to construction materials or permanent facilities, and asked the DFA to clarify whether such restrictions formed part of the arrangement and whether its provisions could be disclosed.

thread.speaker: Secretary Maria Theresa Lazaro
thread.said: She said the DFA had responded that there was no reference whatsoever to construction materials in the provisional arrangement. She then described the arrangement as without prejudice to Philippine positions under UNCLOS and the arbitral award, and as an information exchange rather than a permission system.

thread.speaker: Secretary Maria Theresa Lazaro
thread.said: She said the operational side was handled by the Armed Forces, including Western Command, and the Coast Guard. The arrangement covered only daily necessities for rotation and reprovisioning, such as food, water, telephone and fuel.

thread.speaker: Secretary Maria Theresa Lazaro
thread.said: She explained that the information exchange involved notifying the counterpart foreign ministry that a boat or vehicle would go to the area and identifying the vessels that would be present. She again stated that 16 RORE missions had occurred in two years without incident.

thread.speaker: Rep. Antonio Tinio
thread.said: He criticized what he characterized as inflammatory Chinese Embassy statements on the West Philippine Sea and the arbitral award, and asked why the DFA had remained silent.

thread.speaker: DFA official for Asia Pacific Affairs
thread.said: The official said the DFA had noticed the Chinese Embassy's approach to public statements and had raised the matter with the embassy. He said foreign ministries and diplomatic representatives were the proper fora for exchanging and debating positions on the South China Sea.

thread.speaker: DFA official
thread.said: He said the DFA maintained regular interaction with the Chinese Embassy and the Chinese foreign ministry, and issued formal protests regarding specific statements and activities. He added that diplomatic protests were specific to China's position and were not always responses to public embassy statements, although some examples involved such statements.

thread.speaker: Rep. Antonio Tinio
thread.said: He asked whether the DFA had filed formal diplomatic protests specifically over the Chinese Embassy's public statements and whether the DFA had publicly called out the embassy.

thread.speaker: DFA official
thread.said: He reiterated that there had been 39 diplomatic protests in 2026 and weekly protests concerning Chinese activities. He said some protests since 2022 had addressed public statements, but did not state that every embassy statement had been the subject of a separate protest.

topics.topic: Austerity measures and DFA official-event spending
topics.summary: Rep. Percy Cendaña asked whether the DFA had held Independence Day celebrations in five-star hotels despite austerity directives. The Secretary answered that most foreign service posts had practiced austerity, but some important posts had held more elaborate events for major anniversaries, including the eightieth anniversary of Philippine-U.S. relations in Washington, D.C. topics.topic: UN Security Council campaign expenditures and outcome
topics.summary: Representative Dada Kiram Ismula asked why the Philippines lost its bid for a nonpermanent UN Security Council seat and how much had been appropriated and spent on the campaign. The DFA secretary attributed the loss to geopolitical issues and said a detailed explanation could be provided in writing. The DFA fiscal management official reported that 70,000,000 pesos had been appropriated for 2025 and 2026, of which 52,500,000 was obligated, or 75% utilized. Ismula requested a breakdown covering diplomatic missions, travel, representation, promotional activities, and other campaign expenses, as well as the DFA’s accountability and post-campaign assessment. The DFA did not provide those details during the exchange, and Ismula reiterated the need to account for taxpayers’ money.

topics.topic: Critical Minerals Agreement review and US-Philippines economic relations
topics.summary: Rep. Renee Co asked the DFA to submit the Critical Minerals Agreement or MOU with the United States and clarify whether the DFA had reviewed it. The DFA said the DENR led the agreement, with DTI and BOI involved, and that the DFA did not possess the document. DFA officials said the DENR and DTI had assessed the economic aspects, so the Office of International Economic Relations did not conduct a separate economic review, although the DFA concurred with the agreement. The agency said the arrangement could support value-added processing of copper and nickel, technological know-how, investment protection, and participation in chip, artificial-intelligence, and electric-vehicle applications. Rep. Co emphasized that the agreement had implications beyond one bilateral relationship and that the DFA should consider consistency with related agreements. The secretary committed to requesting the MOU from the concerned agency, but the scope of the DFA's review role remained partly unresolved.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish whether the DFA had reviewed the Critical Minerals Agreement or MOU between the Philippines and the United States, what role it played in clearing or assessing the agreement, and whether it could provide the committee with a copy. It also sought clarification on the agreement's broader implications for US-Philippines economic, trade, and political relations.
topics.agency_position: The DFA said it did not possess the Critical Minerals Agreement and had not conducted a separate economic review because the DENR and DTI were the lead and more competent agencies on the agreement's economic aspects. It said the DFA nevertheless concurred based on the lead agencies' assessment and considered the arrangement beneficial to Philippine processing capabilities and US-Philippines relations.
topics.outcome: The DFA did not provide the MOU during the hearing and said it would have to request the document from the concerned agency. The DFA's review role remained limited in the agency's account to being consulted or giving concurrence, while the broader question of the extent of its language and international-agreement review was not fully resolved.

positions.position: Rep. Co maintained that the agreement had broader economic, trade, political, and international implications and that the DFA's role should include reviewing consistency of language and compatibility with related agreements. She requested that the agreement be made available to the committee.

The secretary maintained that the DFA did not have the agreement but could request it from the concerned agency, and that the DFA concurred because the lead agencies had found it beneficial to the country.

The undersecretary supported the DENR and DTI assessment that the agreement could promote value-added processing, technological know-how, investment protection, and stronger relations with the United States and other participants.

topics.topic: Visiting-forces exercises, fishing-community assistance, and commission staffing
topics.summary: Rep. Pinho asked about the Visiting Forces Commission's implemented and prospective agreements and requested the complete agreement texts. The commission said five agreements were currently implemented, with France awaiting ratification and concurrence and the United Kingdom in the negotiation pipeline. It said no funding was currently needed for the Canada and New Zealand agreements because no activities had been scheduled, but requested 13 permanent positions costing a little less than 3,000,000 in additional personnel services. Rep. Rufus Rodriguez supported the request and undertook to help advance it, subject to DBM processing and a signed written submission. Rep. Antonio Tinio asked about fishing bans and lost catch or income during exercises; the commission said the AFP, local governments, DSWD, and sometimes United States forces provided or coordinated assistance. The commission committed to seek actual assistance data, leaving that documentation unresolved.

topics.topic: Overseas voting administration and 2025 turnout
topics.summary: Antonio Tinio raised the very low turnout in the 2025 overseas elections and asked about the DFA's voter-awareness, education, and information efforts after the introduction of online voting and counting. A DFA official said turnout was affected by various factors and cautioned against comparing the 2025 results directly with the 2022 elections. The official cited registration without subsequent voting, technical and online-voting difficulties, regional differences, and challenges faced by elderly voters. The DFA said it had established a technical working group with COMELEC to improve awareness and participation. It also committed to provide a paper with more detailed reasons for the difficulties in overseas voting.

An agency official reported that 14 seafarers were on the same ship and said seafarers could refuse work in areas determined to be dangerous. thread.said: The official said 14 seafarers were on the same ship and that assistance also covered the remains. The MWO and the Philippine embassy were coordinating, while seafarers' right to refuse work in areas determined to be dangerous was being recognized.

thread.speaker: DFA official
thread.said: The official said Philippine embassies, MWOs, and the DMW held regular meetings with locally based manning agencies, which had direct communication lines with some shipping companies.

thread.speaker: DFA secretary
thread.said: The secretary raised the need for engagement with the International Maritime Organization concerning seafarers.

thread.speaker: DFA secretary
thread.said: The secretary identified the seafarers' right to refuse sailing as an issue requiring an update, particularly in higher-risk areas or corridors.

thread.speaker: DFA secretary
thread.said: The secretary recalled that, in the first quarter, the DFA had sought safe passage for a Philippine-flag vessel in the Middle East and had spoken with the Iranian Foreign Minister. The secretary cautioned that the situation had changed and that the foreign ministry might no longer control the relevant circumstances.

thread.speaker: DFA secretary
thread.said: The secretary said the DFA could proceed through the International Maritime Organization, based in London, because of its influence. The DFA was also trying to engage workers, shipowners, seafarers' unions, and other stakeholders.

thread.speaker: DFA secretary
thread.said: The secretary said bilateral approaches were also being pursued, citing Panama and its 180,000 seafarers as an example of the relevance of bilateral engagement.

thread.speaker: DFA secretary
thread.said: The secretary said the DFA would be obliged to provide details and referred to a report begun two days earlier to Nayari. The exact reference to Nayari and the scope of the report were unclear in the transcript.

thread.speaker: DFA secretary
thread.said: The secretary thanked the Chair and concluded the exchange.

topics.topic: Repatriation of remains and overseas crisis assistance
topics.summary: Rep. Brian Poe asked how the DFA was assisting Filipinos affected by the Nepal crisis and sought an update on Sam De La Cruz’s remains. The DFA said it was working through the New Delhi embassy and an honorary consul in Kathmandu, with one Filipino missing amid reports of about 4,000 missing persons. On De La Cruz’s case, the DFA explained that his remains had been buried in Bosaso after his death in July 2018, and that pandemic, legal, logistical, and diplomatic obstacles had stalled exhumation. The DFA committed to renewing instructions to its Nairobi embassy to pursue the case with Somali authorities. Rep. Dadah Kiram Ismula then asked about ATN Fund use, and the DFA reported an annual appropriation of about 1 billion from 2022 to 2025, along with 2026 assistance figures including 387 repatriation beneficiaries and 2,884 total beneficiaries reported for the first six months. The member requested the ATN Fund guidelines, leaving the matter with a document submission and continued agency follow-up.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish how the DFA was assisting Filipinos affected by the Nepal crisis and whether it could secure the repatriation of Sam De La Cruz’s remains from Somalia. It also examined the scale, beneficiaries, approval rules, and documentation governing the Assistance to Nationals (ATN) Fund.
topics.agency_position: The DFA said it was coordinating through its regional diplomatic posts, honorary consul, international organizations, and local authorities to assist Filipinos affected by the Nepal crisis and identify the missing Filipino. It remained committed to pursuing the return of Sam De La Cruz’s remains and said ATN assistance was governed by a 2019 department order with defined approval authorities.
topics.outcome: The Nepal assistance and ATN utilization information were presented, while the Sam De La Cruz case remained dependent on renewed diplomatic engagement with Somali authorities. The DFA committed to pursuing the remains case and was asked to submit the ATN Fund guidelines.

positions.position: The DFA should continue pursuing the repatriation of Sam De La Cruz’s remains despite Somalia’s lack of response and the absence of a Philippine mission there.
The use of ATN funds required transparency regarding beneficiaries, approval and denial criteria, final approving authority, and the governing guidelines.

thread.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
thread.said: He asked whether the DFA had a complete list of Filipinos affected in Nepal and what assistance it was providing to Filipinos there.

thread.speaker: DFA Secretary
thread.said: She said the DFA had no foreign service establishment in Nepal and relied on the embassy in New Delhi, which had jurisdiction over Nepal, together with an honorary consul in Kathmandu. One Filipino was reported missing, and the DFA was working with international organizations and local authorities while seeking family DNA for matching with recovered bodies.

thread.speaker: DFA Secretary
thread.said: She said reports indicated about 4,000 missing persons in the Nepal crisis and that the search and identification process was continuing.

thread.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
thread.said: He raised the case of Sam De La Cruz, a 25-year-old migrant worker who died in 2018 while working on a fishing vessel and whose remains were reportedly buried in Somalia. He asked for an update on efforts to return the remains to the Philippines.

thread.speaker: DFA officer in charge of migrant affairs
thread.said: The officer confirmed that Sam De La Cruz, a former seafarer registered with GMM Global Maritime in Manila, died in July 2018 from cardiopulmonary arrest. The DFA said the case was complicated by the COVID-19 pandemic, Somalia’s practice of immediate burial under Islamic Sharia, the absence of a Philippine mission in Somalia, and other logistical concerns.

thread.speaker: DFA officer in charge of migrant affairs
thread.said: The Philippine embassy in Nairobi, which had responsibility for Somalia, had sent diplomatic notes but had not received an official reply from the Somali government. GMM had located the burial site in Bosaso and pursued permits and funding for exhumation, but negotiations with local officials stalled.

thread.speaker: DFA officer in charge of migrant affairs
thread.said: He said Bosaso was about 1,000 kilometers from Mogadishu.

thread.speaker: DFA officer in charge of migrant affairs
thread.said: He said that in 2025 the DFA had instructed the embassy in Nairobi to engage the Somali Embassy in Nairobi and convey the request to Mogadishu. Because no official reply had been received, the DFA would send instructions again to revive the matter.

thread.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
thread.said: He acknowledged the DFA’s tracking of the case and the difficulty caused by the lack of diplomatic ties and Somali nonresponse. He said the DFA should continue “knocking at their door” and assured migrant workers that the department would keep trying to bring home the remains.

thread.speaker: Rep. Dadah Kiram Ismula
thread.said: He asked about the ATN Fund and the total appropriations for assisting Filipinos in distress abroad from June 2022 to June 2026.

thread.speaker: DFA fiscal management official

thread.speaker: Rep. Dadah Kiram Ismula

thread.speaker: DFA migrant affairs official
thread.said: For 2026, the official reported 387 beneficiaries for repatriation from January to July. The official also cited dollars 559,000,000 for welfare assistance, 20,000,000 for medical assistance, and 40,000,000 for shipment of remains, totaling 2,884 beneficiaries for the first six months of the year.

thread.speaker: Rep. Dadah Kiram Ismula
thread.said: He asked for the specific guidelines and criteria used to approve or deny ATN requests, including the final approving authority.

thread.speaker: DFA migrant affairs official
thread.said: The official said a 2019 department order governed the ATN Fund and the Legal Assistance Fund. The office prepared recommendations for approvals involving certain amounts below 20%, while requests involving more than that were approved by the Secretary.

thread.speaker: Rep. Dadah Kiram Ismula
