thread.speaker: Rep. Patrin Gorazeta
thread.said: She asked PhilHealth and the DOH how YAKAP prevention activities went beyond screening and detection, including whether lifestyle-medicine counseling was available and how prevention would reach the barangay level.

thread.speaker: Rep. Patrin Gorazeta
thread.said: She said only 15 out of 47 facilities in her district were accredited under the GAMOT program, which she described as a significant gap.

thread.speaker: Rep. Patrin Gorazeta
thread.said: She questioned whether an accredited GAMOT center was required to have a pharmacist, adequate space, and a license to operate. She said these requirements were unrealistic for fourth-class municipalities that lacked funding and could not readily provide a pharmacist.

thread.speaker: Rep. Patrin Gorazeta
thread.said: She said GAMOT already had medicines for noncommunicable diseases but recommended adding medicines for hyperthyroidism and hypothyroidism, liver support and cirrhosis, vitamin B complex, and calcium.

thread.speaker: Rep. Patrin Gorazeta
thread.said: She said the YAKAP program was reaching almost 70% in her South District, but facilities remained hesitant to participate in GAMOT because of the accreditation requirements, particularly where provincial pharmacies were centralized.

thread.speaker: PhilHealth official
thread.said: The official said medicines for hyperthyroidism and hypothyroidism were already in PhilHealth's pipeline. PhilHealth was also reviewing the accreditation standards, which were then based on an FDA-licensed pharmacy.

thread.speaker: PhilHealth official
thread.said: The official said PhilHealth was considering minor guideline adjustments, including allowing four accounts per pharmacy, so larger provincial pharmacies could conduct outreach for rural health units. PhilHealth also planned to develop and accredit mobile pharmacies to address the limited availability of pharmacies in rural areas.

thread.speaker: PhilHealth official
thread.said: The official said the mental-health package had two tiers, general and specialist, and was based on the professional providing care rather than on a specific diagnosis. The package was therefore flexible enough to cover conditions such as bipolar disorder.

thread.speaker: PhilHealth official
thread.said: On prevention, the official said schools could serve as a setting for YAKAP promotion and preventive work. PhilHealth hoped YAKAP revenues could be used to hire permanent personnel dedicated to promotion and prevention.

thread.speaker: Congresswoman Kathrin
thread.said: She asked whether accreditation requirements for centers providing the expanded autism C package could be modified or simplified so more providers could participate.

thread.speaker: PhilHealth official
thread.said: The official said PhilHealth planned to unbundle the children-with-disabilities package, with a policy expected the following week, to allow more providers to participate. The official also described task-shifting, local training, provider mapping, and possible accreditation of professional societies to expand service availability without requiring every provider to maintain a fixed facility.

thread.speaker: Rep. Bong Suntay
thread.said: He said YAKAP and GAMOT were valuable programs but needed clearer guidelines because some providers allegedly abused them through numerous barangay medical missions. He asked PhilHealth to address providers who brought their services to barangays without patients clearly understanding the registration process.

thread.speaker: Dr. Beverly Ho
thread.said: Dr. Ho said PhilHealth and its stakeholders were developing a YAKAP 2.0 version and were completing consultations with providers and patient groups. Proposed enhancements included consent procedures, panel checking to confirm that patients were real and verified, and changes to provider incentives.

thread.speaker: Dr. Beverly Ho
thread.said: She said some providers performed only the first patient encounter because it carried a substantial incentive and did not continue the rest of the care. PhilHealth planned to adjust the incentives and performance-based financing, along with comprehensive IT-system changes.

thread.speaker: Dr. Beverly Ho
thread.said: Dr. Ho said the YAKAP 2.0 changes were expected to roll out toward the end of the year and early the following year, with the stated aim of addressing the reported implementation problems.

thread.speaker: Rep. Bong Suntay
thread.said: He asked PhilHealth to furnish the committee with a list of accredited YAKAP providers so complaints about allegedly improper or misleading medical missions could be reported and acted upon.

thread.speaker: Rep. Christopher
thread.said: He said YAKAP and GAMOT appeared effective over the long term but asked about the accreditation rule for transferring a patient from one accredited clinic to another, specifically whether the period was one year.

thread.speaker: PhilHealth official
thread.said: The official confirmed the one-year rule and explained that the first patient encounter and first tranche facility were relevant. A patient could transfer while the money remained with PhilHealth.

thread.speaker: Rep. Christopher
thread.said: He asked about the GAMOT pharmacy dispensing rule, noting that an accredited clinic could issue a receipt with three months of validity while the GAMOT pharmacy could dispense only one month's worth of medicines.

thread.speaker: PhilHealth official
thread.said: The official confirmed that the clinic receipt could be issued for three months of validity, while the GAMOT pharmacy could dispense only one month worth of medicines.

thread.speaker: Rep. Christopher
thread.said: He warned that the arrangement could allow a clinic to issue a receipt for three months while the patient received only one month of medicine. He urged strict implementation of the three-month rule.

topics.topic: Primary-care and super health-center standards and equipment
topics.summary: Secretary Edwin Mercado presented primary care as a DOH budget pillar and said HFEP covered facilities, infrastructure, and equipment with an allocation of about 14.5 billion. Perci Cendaña questioned the status of 1,823 health centers, and DOH reported 806 HFEP-funded super health centers, including completed, occupancy-ready, operational, and non-operational facilities. Rep. Audrey Zubiri sought additional support for Bukidnon and asked DOH to review the Moolog Bagong Filipinas health center allocation, which was 2,700,000 against a 19,000,000 request. Rep. JC Rahman Nava pressed for clear minimum services and equipment standards, citing two completed but unequipped super health centers that had remained unused for about two years. Secretary Mercado proposed a tiered spoke-and-hub model and committed to standards and a road map, while the Chair directed DOH to submit reverted HFEP-funds data before plenary. The standards, equipment funding, reverted amount, and requested local allocations were not finally resolved.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish whether DOH was setting clear, workable standards for primary-care facilities and super health centers, including the services and equipment each facility should provide. Members also asked whether facilities were geographically and financially supported, and what would happen to incomplete, unequipped, or reverted HFEP projects.
topics.agency_position: DOH said primary-care access was a core budget priority but acknowledged that licensing requirements had been too stringent and that standards would be revisited. The agency proposed a tiered, spoke-and-hub referral network, with basic primary-care services at the lower level and super health centers providing a higher level of care, potentially including outpatient surgery; it also undertook to coordinate on project deficiencies and submit reverted-funds data.
topics.outcome: DOH outlined a proposed tiered standard and referral-network model but did not provide final service classifications, an equipment plan for the cited unequipped centers, or the amount of reverted HFEP funds during the hearing. The Chair required DOH to submit the reverted-funds data before plenary, while Bukidnon and Moolog funding questions remained subject to coordination and review.

positions.position: Pressed DOH for an accounting of health-center targets and operational status, including why completed or partially completed super health centers were non-operational.
Argued that Bukidnon and a proposed Bagong Filipinas health center in Moolog were underfunded and requested a review of the allocations and the basis for provincial funding.

Argued that primary-care facilities needed explicit service and equipment standards, and that infrastructure-complete but unequipped super health centers should be integrated into the UHC referral network and supported with funding.

Supported developing tiered primary-care standards and prioritizing completion of active projects, while indicating that licensing, project implementation, and reverted-fund data required further action.

topics.topic: Hospital bed capacity, expansion, and tertiary-care access
topics.summary: Members asked the DOH to explain its hospital bed-capacity baseline, surge requirements, expansion plans, and regional distribution of facilities. The DOH cited efficiency measures, physical-plant expansion, HFEP, referral-network planning, and functional-bed-based staffing, while acknowledging major funding and personnel gaps. The agency reported a request of about 837 billion against an approved 353 billion, requested PHP19 billion for HFEP against PHP14.5 billion, and identified about 12 billion for hospital operations as priorities, although some figures were inconsistent or unclear. Members pressed for greater Mindanao funding, tertiary hospitals in island provinces, implementation of the Basilan Medical Center upgrade from 125 to 500 beds, and completion of ongoing hospital projects. The DOH committed to written responses, study of insulin-pump coverage, adjustments for project completion, and support for legislation authorizing hospital funding or conversion. The issue landed with commitments and follow-up obligations, but important allocation, staffing, timetable, and bed-capacity questions remained open.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish whether the DOH had a systematic plan and sufficient funding to expand hospital bed capacity, upgrade hospitals to tertiary level, and provide equitable access to higher-level care, particularly in underserved and island provinces. Members also asked how hospital projects, staffing, regional allocations, and PhilHealth-supported care would be prioritized and implemented.
topics.agency_position: The DOH said hospital access should be improved through efficiency measures, expansion of existing physical plants, HFEP-supported facilities, regional referral-network planning, and prioritization based on functional capacity and normative budgeting factors. It acknowledged funding and staffing gaps, supported legislative conversion or renationalization where authorized by law, and said several matters—including the Basilan Level 3 timetable and certain expansion figures—required further clarification or written submission.
topics.outcome: The DOH answered the committee's questions in broad terms and identified funding, staffing, infrastructure, and PhilHealth gaps, but several bed-capacity figures, allocation discrepancies, island-province criteria, and the Basilan implementation timetable remained unresolved. Written reports, further studies, legislative action, and project-level follow-up were required.

positions.position: Supported a systematic, administration-wide plan for expanding DOH hospital beds and requested a written report on accomplishments and future plans.
Supported restoring funding for PhilHealth indirect-member benefits, HFEP, and DOH hospital operations, and argued that island provinces required better tertiary-care access.
Argued that Mindanao's allocation was too small relative to its population and supported increased regional funding and expanded PhilHealth coverage for diabetes, including insulin pumps.
Pressed for implementation of the Basilan Medical Center Level 3 upgrade, including its mandated bed, infrastructure, equipment, and workforce expansion.
Pressed the DOH to improve absorptive capacity, distribute hospital funding more equitably, address staffing gaps in upgraded hospitals, and complete ongoing infrastructure projects.
Sought clear prioritization of hospitals with legislated bed-capacity increases and adequate staffing and capacity for Yakap centers.
Supported establishment or renationalization of a hospital in an underserved area where residents were more than three hours from a complete hospital and ICU.

thread.said: Mercado said the projected amount was about 2.44 while only 74 had been provided, producing a difference of almost 170. The currency and units were not clear in the transcript.

thread.said: Ho said PhilHealth's original proposal was based on an estimated premium per headcount of around 3.76. She later identified the expected benefit payout for indirect contributors as R244 billion and said 170 additional was needed to reach breakeven, assuming the same utilization rate.

thread.speaker: Edwin Mercado, DOH secretary
thread.said: Mercado identified DOH hospital operations as another priority, covering Metro Manila hospitals, regional hospitals, and GOCCs, at about 12,000,000,000.

thread.speaker: Rufus Rodriguez, vice chair

thread.speaker: DOH official
thread.said: The DOH official said Mindanao accounted for 15% of the share specific to regional health offices, compared with Visayas at 10%, Luzon at 34%, and the central office at 41%.

thread.speaker: Maximo Rodriguez Jr., committee member
thread.said: Rodriguez said Mindanao had about 28,000,000 people and argued that its share was too small. He urged an increase of at least 1% in the next budget season and said he would support increases in the plenary.

thread.speaker: Maximo Rodriguez Jr., committee member
thread.said: Rodriguez said remote areas of Mindanao lacked facilities and doctors and advocated a better regional health allocation and improved facilities.

thread.speaker: Audrey Zubiri, PhilHealth official

thread.speaker: Rufus Rodriguez, committee member
thread.said: Rodriguez asked for the DOH's policy and plan to ensure reasonable provincial access to tertiary or higher-level hospital services, noting that only 36 of 82 provinces had DOH-managed medical facilities.

thread.speaker: DOH official
thread.said: The official cited a five-pillar approach to efficient hospital operations and a health-facility development roadmap. thread.speaker: Rufus Rodriguez, committee member
thread.said: Rodriguez asked whether the DOH recognized the need to prioritize island provinces and whether it supported upgrading a medical center identified in the transcript as ABMC into a DOH-managed tertiary hospital.

thread.speaker: DOH official

thread.said: Rodriguez emphasized that island-province access to tertiary care was not merely a matter of convenience but could be a matter of life and death.

thread.speaker: PhilHealth official

thread.speaker: Yusop Alano, committee member

topics.topic: Hospital infrastructure site selection and structural safety
topics.summary: Bambi Emano questioned who selected the Northeastern Misamis hospital site, its reported 98% completion in phase two, the change from five stories to three, and the discovery of a fault-line concern in 2025. DOH said the local government had selected the site by donating the land, that the initial hazard map placed it more than two kilometers from the fault line, and that DPWH considered the reinforced or retrofitted three-story design acceptable. Emano disputed the account and requested the hazard map, technical report, and DOH site-selection guidelines. DOH committed to provide those materials and its decision before plenary. Yusop Alano asked about the timeframe and requirements for Basilan Medical Center's Level 3 upgrade; DOH cited a 2025 allocation described as 180 and another 80,000,000 for 2027, while identifying four specialty residency programs and a 500 kVA transformer as requirements. Romeo Momo separately raised DOH's 65.8% disbursement against 93.5% obligations, personnel gaps, regional allocation disparities, and completion funding for ongoing hospital projects. The principal safety issue therefore remained unresolved, but documentary and implementation follow-up was committed.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish who selected the sites for the Northeastern Misamis General Hospital and other hospital projects, whether the sites and structures were technically safe, and whether DOH had adequate plans, funding, equipment, and personnel to complete and operate upgraded hospitals. It also examined the basis for regional allocations and the completion of ongoing infrastructure projects.
topics.agency_position: DOH said the Northeastern Misamis site had been donated and effectively selected by the local government, while DPWH executed the project and determined the acceptability of the retrofit. DOH said it would review and submit the hazard map, DPWH report, site-assessment guidelines, and its decision before plenary. For hospital upgrades and staffing, DOH said Level 3 status depended on specialty residency programs, functional bed capacity, normative budgeting, and infrastructure and equipment requirements.
topics.outcome: The Northeastern Misamis site-selection and safety questions were not finally resolved during the hearing. DOH committed to submit the hazard map, DPWH report, site-assessment guidelines, and its decision before plenary; Basilan's upgrade requirements and the broader staffing and infrastructure concerns remained subject to implementation and funding follow-up.

Raised concerns about DOH's absorptive capacity, inequitable regional allocations, hospital staffing shortages, and the need to complete ongoing hospital infrastructure projects.

topics.topic: Tuberculosis-drug procurement and Global Fund transition
topics.summary: Rep. Iris Marie Montes asked Secretary Edwin Mercado what the DOH had inherited from the delayed TB-drug procurement and whether the procurement failure had been reviewed. Mercado said the process was being pushed forward, with almost 159,000,000 in Global Fund medicines committed and award targeted by the end of September, followed by delivery by the end of October or in November. He confirmed that the FY 2027 budget included 20,000,000 for TB in addition to Global Fund support, including MDR-TB and XDR-TB coverage. Montes then asked whether domestic financing would compensate for the Global Fund's tapering support, and Mercado answered yes while describing an ongoing transition. The delivery timetable was committed, but the procurement-failure review and the long-term financing framework remained insufficiently explained.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish what procurement problems the DOH inherited for tuberculosis drugs, when delayed supplies would be delivered, and whether the FY 2027 budget covered TB treatment needs. It also examined how domestic financing would replace declining Global Fund support, including for MDR-TB and XDR-TB.
topics.agency_position: The DOH said procurement delays were being addressed through a reconstituted directive, an agency-to-agency arrangement, and Global Fund-supported procurement. It stated that the FY 2027 budget included 20,000,000 for TB in addition to Global Fund assistance and that domestic financing would cover the transition as Global Fund support tapered.
topics.outcome: The DOH confirmed a FY 2027 TB allocation and said procurement would be awarded by the end of September, with delivery expected by the end of October or in November. The Global Fund transition framework and the adequacy of domestic financing remained only partly developed, and the review of the earlier procurement failure was not clearly resolved in the exchange.

positions.position: She pressed the DOH to account for the failed or delayed procurement, secure timely delivery of TB drugs and equipment, maintain coverage for MDR-TB and XDR-TB, and replace declining Global Fund support with domestic financing.
He maintained that procurement was being accelerated, that Global Fund assistance remained available during the transition, and that domestic funding was included for TB needs in FY 2027.

topics.topic: Vaccine procurement delays and routine immunization supply
topics.summary: Rep. Iris Marie Montes and Rep. Bong Suntay questioned DOH about delayed influenza and pneumococcal vaccine procurement and the failure to make timely awards. DOH attributed the delay to a protest by a disqualified bidder and a change in management, but said the protest had been resolved and procurement was expected by October or early November. Rep. Janette Garin warned that the pneumococcal conjugate vaccine delay could cause infants to miss doses scheduled at one and a half, two and a half, and three and a half months. DOH also reported that the 2026 immunization allotment was 10,200,000,000, with 1,400,000,000 obligated and 164,000,000 disbursed. A DOH official later said OPV and PCV routine vaccines remained affected by bidding and supply problems, with delivery hoped for by October or November and some recent procurement deliverable within thirty days to forty-five days. DOH committed to early procurement for 2027 and catch-up or boosting activities, but complete and timely delivery remained to be verified.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish whether DOH had procured influenza, pneumococcal, polio, and other routine vaccines on time, why procurement was delayed, and how the agency would prevent shortages from affecting beneficiaries. Members also asked about immunization funding utilization, vaccine coverage, and procurement plans for 2027.
topics.agency_position: DOH attributed the pneumococcal and influenza delays to a bidder protest and the need for an incoming secretary to conduct an independent legal and procurement review. The agency said the disputed procurement had been resolved, delivery was expected by October or November, and early procurement for 2027 had already been directed; it also acknowledged that OPV and PCV routine-vaccine supplies remained affected by bidding and supply problems.
topics.outcome: DOH said the delayed vaccine procurement had been resolved and that delivery was expected by October or November, but the record did not establish that all influenza, pneumococcal, OPV, and PCV needs had already been delivered. Early procurement for 2027 and catch-up vaccination were committed, leaving implementation and timely supply availability to be monitored.

positions.position: Vaccine procurement and influenza-vaccine rollout needed to occur early enough to cover the flu season and avoid wasting available resources.
Procurement protests and changes in management should not delay vaccine awards or harm seniors and other beneficiaries; DOH needed a concrete early-procurement solution.
The pneumococcal conjugate vaccine delay was serious because infants could miss the recommended schedule, and DOH should prevent a repeat in 2027.
The committee needed clear information on vaccine availability, immunization funding, program targets, and the children affected by stunting and wasting.

topics.topic: Medicine wastage, expired inventories, warehousing, and logistics
topics.summary: The issue was raised by Perci Cendaña, Deputy Speaker Ferjenel Biron, Rep. Janette Garin, and Rep. Salvador Pleyto. Members questioned the DOH's supply-chain allocation, central warehousing, recurring medicine expiries, double financing, and more than 90,000,000 in undistributed inventories alongside 34,000,000 in expired or nearly expired medicines. Secretary Edwin Mercado attributed the problem partly to paper-based inventory tracking and said about 60% of commodities were already procured regionally, with 40% downloaded centrally. Rep. Garin cited annual expiries of about 50 million in nutrition commodities and 300 million in mental-health medicines and urged redirection of usable stocks to assistance programs. The chair approved a request for data on expired, expiring, and near-expiring medicines, including regional offices, while the DOH also committed to review redirection and double-financing issues.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish the scale and causes of medicine expiries and undistributed inventories, including whether procurement, inventory controls, warehousing, and logistics were responsible. It also examined the DOH's supply-chain budget and whether procurement should be regionalized to prevent medicines from remaining in central warehouses.
topics.agency_position: The DOH attributed medicine expiries and distribution problems primarily to weak, paper-based supply-chain and inventory systems, while also identifying possible double financing between DOH procurement and PhilHealth reimbursement. It supported greater regional procurement, saying about 60% of commodities were already procured regionally, and committed to submit expanded expiry data and examine measures to redirect or better finance unused medicines.
topics.outcome: The DOH acknowledged supply-chain and inventory-control weaknesses, supported continued regionalization of procurement, and undertook to submit comprehensive expiry data covering central and regional operations. The audit-cited inventory amounts and the broader causes of recurring expiries remained subject to the requested reports and further review.

positions.position: Regional supply-chain allocations should account for differing geographic and logistical requirements rather than applying an apparently uniform amount.

Medicine expiries reflected serious procurement, inventory, warehousing, and distribution weaknesses, and procurement should be regionalized to prevent commodities from remaining in central warehouses.
Recurring expiries and double financing were unacceptable; unused cancer and mental-health medicines should be examined for redirection to medical assistance or cancer-support programs.
The DOH needed to account for expired medicines and undistributed inventories flagged by audit and explain why they were not deployed through medical and vaccination programs.

topics.topic: HIV prevention commodities and 2027 NHSP funding
topics.summary: Perci Cendaña questioned whether the 2027 budget could meet NHSP HIV-prevention targets amid shortages of condoms, lubricants, and HIV self-tests. He cited 1,200,000 condom beneficiaries requiring up to about 302.4 million annually, a lubricant shortfall of about 98.7 million, and an unclear HIV self-testing shortfall described as “twenty six to sixty three point nine million.” Secretary Edwin Mercado responded that the DOH would use a two-pronged approach involving Yakap, the OHAT program, and DOH data commodities, including testing. Cendaña then questioned the adequacy of a 10,000,000 regional supply-chain allocation, particularly where geography and logistics differed. The agency gave no substantive recorded response to that final question, and the issue remained unresolved.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish whether the DOH's 2027 allocation would be sufficient to meet the National HIV Strategic Plan (NHSP) targets, particularly for condoms, lubricants, and HIV self-tests. It also questioned whether the proposed regional supply-chain allocations were adequate given differing geographic and logistics requirements.
topics.agency_position: The DOH stated that HIV prevention and testing would be addressed through a two-pronged approach involving Yakap, the OHAT program, and DOH data commodities. It did not state that the 2027 budget definitively covered the cited commodity gaps and did not provide a recorded answer on whether the regional supply-chain allocations were adequate.
topics.outcome: The DOH offered a general account of its prevention and testing approach, but did not establish that the 2027 funding would close the identified commodity gaps. The logistics-allocation concern received no substantive recorded answer before the chair moved to the next member.

positions.position: He argued that the cited condom, lubricant, and HIV self-testing gaps raised doubts about whether the 2027 HIV allocation could meet NHSP targets, and questioned the adequacy of equal regional logistics allocations.
He presented Yakap, the OHAT program, and DOH data commodities as the agency's approach to covering HIV prevention and testing needs.

topics.topic: Mental-health budget, hotline demand, packages, and workforce
topics.summary: Congresswoman Kathrin questioned whether Yakap included prevention, whether GAMOT accreditation requirements were practical, and whether mental-health and autism packages could be expanded through simpler provider rules. PhilHealth said its mental-health package had general and specialist tiers, could cover conditions such as bipolar disorder, and was being expanded through more training and providers. Antonio Tinio separately questioned hospital MOE reductions, including an 11,000,000 NCMH cut, while DOH attributed the reductions to normative financing and broader revenue arrangements and agreed to submit hospital-level data. Renee Co pressed DOH on an NCMH cut described as 21% and 311,000,000, despite an estimated 12.5 million Filipinos with mental-health conditions and a decline from 1,500,000,000 in 2025. DOH reported 77,000 cumulative hotline calls since 2019, including 23,000 in 2024, and described MH Gap certification and salary-grade adjustments as workforce responses. The discussion ended with commitments to provide exact budget comparisons, current mental-health initiatives, and implementation details for the 2024–2028 strategic framework.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish whether DOH and PhilHealth's mental-health packages, prevention programs, medicines, and provider-accreditation rules were reaching communities, and whether budget reductions and staffing shortages were impairing service delivery. Members also asked how rising hotline demand, hospital MOE reductions, reimbursements, and the 2024–2028 mental-health strategic framework were being addressed.
topics.agency_position: DOH and PhilHealth said they were expanding mental-health coverage through general and specialist packages, MH Gap training, school-based prevention, hotline services, and additional provider and reimbursement mechanisms. They attributed hospital and NCMH MOE reductions primarily to normative financing and broader budget comparisons, but acknowledged the need to provide exact data and further details on initiatives and strategic-framework implementation.
topics.outcome: The agency answered the package, hotline, workforce, and financing questions but did not resolve the committee's concern over the scale and rationale of mental-health and hospital MOE reductions. DOH and PhilHealth undertook to review accreditation, expand training and provider capacity, and submit comparative budget and program information.

positions.position: Supported broader, community-level prevention and easier accreditation for GAMOT, autism, and other packages, and argued that staffing shortages prevented equipped DOH hospitals from operating at their intended level.
Questioned whether reductions in hospital and NCMH MOE were justified and sought explanations involving ZBB, reimbursements, and other financing sources.

Opposed reductions in mental-health funding in light of rising need and hotline demand, and pressed DOH for stronger workforce development, current program information, and implementation of the 2024–2028 strategic framework.

thread.said: She asked whether accreditation requirements for the expanded autism package could be simplified so more centers could provide the package.

thread.speaker: PhilHealth official
thread.said: The official said the children-with-disabilities package was planned for unbundling, which would allow more providers to participate. The official also described task-shifting, pilot training, provider mapping, and possible accreditation of professional societies rather than only fixed facilities.

thread.speaker: Edwin Mercado
thread.said: On hospital staffing, Mercado said some positions had few or no applicants because of residency, fellowship, specialty-accreditation, and salary-competitiveness requirements, particularly for occupational and physical therapists, developmental specialists, and speech pathologists.

thread.speaker: Edwin Mercado
thread.said: He said that, as of July 2026, DOH had 6,774 unfilled positions, mostly in DOH hospitals, and that the agency was tracking positions subject to the DBM guidelines.

thread.speaker: Antonio Tinio
thread.said: Tinio cited hospital MOE pressures, including an unclear spoken figure for Hirivo Memorial Medical Center and an 11,000,000 MOE cut for the National Center for Mental Health, and asked DOH to explain the reductions.

thread.speaker: Edwin Mercado
thread.said: Mercado said DOH hospital operating budgets in Metro Manila declined from PHP 30,000,000,000 in 2026 to PHP 26,900,000,000, a reduction of 10.2%, while the agency's projected MOE requirement was 31.7% higher than the grant amount.

thread.speaker: Agency official
thread.said: An agency-side participant proposed that DOH furnish the committee with each hospital's PhilHealth reimbursements, medical-assistance allocations, and actual MOE utilization, to determine whether higher MAIFIP and PhilHealth allocations contributed to the MOE cuts.

thread.speaker: Senior Vice Chair Garcia
thread.said: The chair recognized the proposal as a motion and asked whether it had a second. Antonio Tinio seconded it.

thread.speaker: DOH finance official
thread.said: The DOH finance official said hospital MOE levels followed DOH normative financing requirements, which could explain decreases from 2026, and referred to an allocation associated with implementation of CBB.

thread.speaker: Antonio Tinio
thread.said: Tinio asked for a response from the DOH Secretary on whether zero-balance billing and related financing arrangements justified the hospital MOE cuts.

thread.speaker: Edwin Mercado
thread.said: Mercado said DOH hospitals were allowed income retention and that the issue should be viewed in totality, including GAA financing and other revenue streams. He characterized the arrangement as a sector-wide approach involving overlapping sources of coverage.

thread.speaker: Renee Co
thread.said: Co raised the reduction in the DOH mental-health budget, including an NCMH MOE cut described as 21% and another NCMH budget cut of 311,000,000, and questioned the rationale given the estimated 12.5 million Filipinos living with mental-health conditions.

thread.speaker: Edwin Mercado
thread.said: Mercado said most DOH hospitals' MOE budgets had been cut across the board and that comparisons with 2023 and 2024 were needed because an unusual 2025 reallocation from DPWH to DOH may have affected the comparison. He undertook to provide the exact data and reasons.

thread.speaker: Renee Co
thread.said: Co said the national mental-health budget had fallen by half every year since 2025, from 1,500,000,000 to significantly smaller allocations, and asked whether the reductions were under PS, MOE, or another budget category.

thread.speaker: Edwin Mercado
thread.said: Mercado cited MH Gap-trained health workers, the NCMH crisis hotline, a medical-access program across 1296 sites covering almost 64% of cities and municipalities, PhilHealth's expanding mental-health program, and coordination with schools.

thread.speaker: Renee Co
thread.said: Co asked whether the NCMH hotline had experienced increases in call volume and changes in the types of calls, including suicide-related calls.

thread.speaker: Renee Co
thread.said: Co asked how many personnel were assigned to the hotline and whether they handled cases as well as calls.

thread.speaker: Edwin Mercado
thread.said: Mercado said the hotline had 38 open lines and eight dedicated lines, with trunk search operating 24/7.

thread.speaker: Renee Co
thread.said: Co raised the shortage of mental-health professionals, citing fewer than 2,000 licensed psychiatrists for roughly 110,000,000 Filipinos and severe shortages of psychologists, psychometricians, and school guidance personnel. She asked how DOH planned to increase the supply through state universities, colleges, and medical and educational institutions.

thread.speaker: Edwin Mercado
thread.said: Mercado said DOH was expanding MH Gap certification beyond its existing arrangements by engaging academic institutions and working with PCOBEV to authorize other certifying bodies, with more frequent certification intended to create a multiplier effect.

thread.speaker: Renee Co
thread.said: Co pressed whether the professional-supply gap was merely a certification issue, noting that trained professionals could leave for opportunities abroad and that compensation and quality of life also mattered.

thread.speaker: Edwin Mercado
thread.said: Mercado said DOH was addressing compensation by adjusting the salary grade for psychiatrists and psychologists from salary grade 18 to salary grade 20. He also cited PhilHealth income streams for facility-based and practice-based professionals, including psychiatrists, psychologists, and developmental pediatricians.

thread.speaker: Renee Co
thread.said: Co requested through the committee a copy of DOH's current mental-health initiatives, particularly those involving PhilHealth.

thread.speaker: Renee Co
thread.said: Co asked for an update on implementation of the Mental Health Strategic Framework 2024–2028, especially interventions affecting children.

thread.speaker: Edwin Mercado
thread.said: Mercado cited stronger peer-to-peer facilitator engagement in schools and a facilitator handbook for training peer groups. He said DOH would provide more concrete achievements from the last four years.

thread.speaker: Renee Co
thread.said: Co requested submission through the committee of the strategic-framework implementation update and reiterated that the mental-health budget needed to support implementation and the response to the mental-health crisis.

topics.topic: Health emergency allowances and barangay health-worker arrears
topics.summary: Rep. Eli San Fernando questioned the DOH on the 2027 health emergency allowance and unpaid arrears affecting health workers and BHWs. Secretary Edwin Mercado cited 741,000,000 as the verified amount and said 150,000 claims had been verified, while the member cited a 2026 survey reporting about 5.15 billion in unpaid arrears affecting 47,000 BHWs across 294 cities and municipalities. San Fernando also referenced the September 2025 release of 6,700,000,000 pesos for final payments and challenged the discrepancy between that payment history, the reported arrears, and the DOH's verified figure. Mercado said the reported amount had to be reconciled with DBM and that a grievance committee mechanism would address claims. The Chair directed the parties to share data and sources, but the arrears remained unresolved pending validation.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish the status of the 2027 health emergency allowance budget and the unpaid arrears of health workers, particularly barangay health workers (BHWs). It also sought a credible reconciliation of the reported arrears, the operation of the grievance mechanism, and the data needed to validate the claims.
topics.agency_position: The DOH said 741,000,000 and 150,000 claims had been verified, while the much larger reported arrears required reconciliation with DBM and further validation. It identified a regional grievance mechanism and data-sharing process as the means to resolve the discrepancy.
topics.outcome: The issue remained open because the committee did not reconcile the reported 5,150,000,000 in arrears with the DOH's verified 741,000,000. Data and source sharing, together with validation through the grievance mechanism and coordination with DBM, were identified as the next steps.

positions.position: He challenged the adequacy of the verified amount, highlighted the reported 5,150,000,000 in BHW arrears, and sought validation, data sharing, and a concrete response to unpaid claims.
The Chair directed the parties to share their data and sources to establish a common baseline for resolving the arrears discrepancy.

topics.topic: FDA digitalization, application backlog, staffing, and retained income
topics.summary: Ferjenel Biron raised the FDA's registration problems and asked about fully digitalizing the CDRR and medical device division. The FDA said the system would cost about 217 million in the transcript's marked figure, while the total MOE request was 589,000,000; it also reported retained income of about 2 billion and sought authority to access part of it. Rep. Dette Escudero later asked about the backlog, which the FDA estimated at about 19,000 applications, and linked it to limited manpower and financial resources. The FDA reported total manpower figures ranging from about 1,100 to 1,320, including 101 personnel in the drugs center, and said 124 posts were proposed for 2027. Officials described review timelines, defended digitalization as necessary beyond simply adding staff, and cited retained earnings of approximately 3,200,000,000. The FDA said modernization would significantly reduce the backlog and could be launched within 16 to 18 months after notice to proceed, while Rep. Dette Escudero expressed committee support.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish the FDA's application backlog, its staffing and financial constraints, and the budget and retained-income authority needed for digitalization. Members also asked whether modernization would materially reduce the backlog and how long implementation would take.
topics.agency_position: The FDA said the backlog resulted from rising application volumes, inadequate manpower, and constrained financial resources, and that additional personnel alone would not be sufficient. It sought congressional support for an in-house digitalization system, authority to use retained income through the SAGF, and additional staffing, while stating that modernization would significantly reduce rather than necessarily eliminate the backlog.
topics.outcome: The FDA's need for digitalization, additional staffing, and authority to use retained income was placed before the committee, with congressional support requested. The FDA projected a significant backlog reduction and a 16 to 18 month launch period, but did not assure complete elimination of the backlog.

positions.position: Supported full FDA digitalization, particularly for the CDRR and medical device division, and pressed for clarity on the congressional budget request and access to retained income.
Pressed the FDA to address the nearly 19,000-application backlog through staffing and modernization, questioned the distribution of personnel, and expressed support for the FDA modernization program.
Supported additional manpower and digitalization, but emphasized that the FDA needed authority to use retained earnings through the SAGF to augment its operating resources.

thread.speaker: Ferjenel Biron
thread.said: Ferjenel Biron said registration delays had become a problem and asked whether fully digitalizing the FDA, particularly the CDRR and medical device division, was the solution. He asked the FDA to elaborate on the budget Congress should provide.

thread.speaker: FDA official
thread.said: The FDA official cited a lack of personnel and a very high volume of applications. The CDRR, in collaboration with other centers, was developing an in-house, end-to-end digital system for processing and evaluating applications.

thread.speaker: FDA official
thread.said: The official said the system would require about R217 million, described as the minimum estimate. It would not be subscription-based and could eventually be replicated by other centers.

thread.speaker: Ferjenel Biron
thread.said: Ferjenel Biron asked for the total budget being requested from Congress.

thread.speaker: FDA official
thread.said: The official first identified the system cost as 217,000,000 approximately, then corrected the total requested MOE to 589,000,000.

thread.speaker: Ferjenel Biron
thread.said: Ferjenel Biron stated that 518,000,000 would be provided by Congress through the GAA and asked how much counterpart revenue would come from the FDA's retained income.

thread.speaker: FDA official
thread.said: The official said the FDA's retained income was approximately 2,000,000,000 based on current records.

thread.speaker: FDA official
thread.said: The official said the FDA could not access the retained income under the current system unless authorized, and hoped that R580 million dollars would be allowed from the SAGF.

thread.speaker: Ferjenel Biron
thread.said: Ferjenel Biron asked whether the FDA was presently unable to tap retained income until it submitted a business plan to DBM.

thread.speaker: FDA official
thread.said: The official confirmed this, while noting that former DG Teston had already submitted a five year development plan, which was one of the conditions for access.

thread.speaker: Rep. Dette Escudero
thread.said: Rep. Dette Escudero asked for the current FDA application backlog.

thread.speaker: FDA official
thread.said: The FDA official estimated the backlog at about 19,000 applications.

thread.speaker: Rep. Dette Escudero
thread.said: Rep. Dette Escudero asked for the main reason for the backlog.

thread.speaker: FDA official
thread.said: The official attributed the backlog to applications increasing every year, limited manpower, and limited financial resources. The official said the FDA's budget had remained at 517,000,000 since 2023 and that the agency could not keep pace without increased resources.

thread.speaker: Rep. Dette Escudero
thread.said: Rep. Dette Escudero clarified whether manpower was the problem.

thread.speaker: FDA official
thread.said: The official answered that both manpower and financial resources were problems.

thread.speaker: Rep. Dette Escudero
thread.said: Rep. Dette Escudero asked for the FDA's total manpower.

thread.speaker: FDA official
thread.said: The official initially answered 1,000, then clarified that the total for the whole Philippines was about 1,100.

thread.speaker: Rep. Dette Escudero
thread.said: Rep. Dette Escudero cited a report showing 1,322 personnel and asked how many were assigned to applications.

thread.speaker: FDA director general
thread.said: The director general clarified that the FDA had 1,320 total manpower, consisting of 917 plantilla positions and 415 contract-of-service personnel.

thread.speaker: FDA director general
thread.said: The director general reported 101 personnel in the Center for Drug Regulation and Research, 49 in the center for cosmetics, 76 in the center for food, and 80 in the center for devices.

thread.speaker: Rep. Dette Escudero
thread.said: Rep. Dette Escudero clarified whether 101 personnel in drugs were assigned to permits and applications, and compared the staffing level with the nearly 19,000 backlog.

thread.speaker: Rep. Dette Escudero
thread.said: Rep. Dette Escudero asked whether the FDA had computed or proposed to DBM the staffing needed for the 2027 budget.

thread.speaker: FDA director general
thread.said: The director general said the proposed number was roughly about double 100, then stated it as 124.

thread.speaker: Rep. Dette Escudero
thread.said: Rep. Dette Escudero confirmed that 124 posts were proposed for 2027 and questioned the concentration of pending applications in the drugs center.

thread.speaker: Rep. Dette Escudero
thread.said: Rep. Dette Escudero cited approximately 17,000 drug applications within the backlog and observed that this represented more than 90 percent, while the drugs center had 101 personnel. She asked why manpower could not simply be adjusted across applications or centers.

thread.speaker: FDA director general
thread.said: The director general said staffing depended on available positions, where applicants wanted to work, and qualifications. Personnel could not simply be transferred from one center to another, although contract-of-service personnel could augment manpower.

thread.speaker: Rep. Dette Escudero
thread.said: Rep. Dette Escudero asked about the drug-permit approval process, including whether approval by a country such as the United States could be recognized by the Philippine FDA.

thread.speaker: FDA official
thread.said: The FDA official said approval by another country had to come from a recognized Reference Regulatory Drug Authority, or RDRA. The FDA still had to verify the foreign approval and ensure compliance with country-specific requirements.

thread.speaker: FDA official
thread.said: The official gave review timelines of 45 working days for abridged review, 30 working days for verification review, and 65 working days for the collaborative review pathway.

thread.speaker: Rep. Dette Escudero
thread.said: Rep. Dette Escudero asked whether the facilitated review pathway's 30-day and 45-day timelines applied in practice or only on paper.

thread.speaker: FDA official
thread.said: The official said applications were released within 30 working days in monitored cases and that the FDA had implemented interventions to meet the desired timelines.

thread.speaker: FDA director general
thread.said: The director general said application inflows were seasonal. While additional manpower was needed, the FDA was asking Congress to support digitalization because it would ease the burden and improve application processing.

thread.speaker: Rep. Dette Escudero
thread.said: Rep. Dette Escudero said that, based on the FDA report, average applications received over the past five years were 219,000 and applications processed were about 205,000, leaving an average annual backlog of 23,000 since 2021. She asked whether the digitalization program would cost 217,000,000 for 2027.

thread.speaker: FDA director general
thread.said: The director general said the FDA was asking for Congress's support for the 217,000,000 digitalization program.

thread.speaker: Rep. Dette Escudero
thread.said: Rep. Dette Escudero raised the possibility of using retained earnings for modernization.

thread.speaker: FDA director general
thread.said: The director general estimated retained earnings at approximately 3,200,000,000.

thread.speaker: FDA director general
thread.said: The director general requested authority to tap the SAGF for the FDA digitalization program and to augment its MOO. The official said the MOO had remained at 517 since 2022, with 60% for one component and 40% for operations.

thread.speaker: FDA director general
thread.said: The director general said the FDA's nationwide regulatory work, international benchmarking, inspections, and post-marketing surveillance required substantial resources.

thread.speaker: Rep. Dette Escudero
thread.said: Rep. Dette Escudero asked for an assurance that the modernization program would completely eliminate the backlog.

thread.speaker: FDA official
thread.said: The FDA official did not guarantee complete elimination, but said modernization would be a significant intervention and would result in a significant drop in the backlog.

thread.speaker: FDA official
thread.said: The official estimated that, from the notice to proceed, the system would take 16 to 18 months to launch and could then be replicated for other centers.

thread.speaker: Rep. Dette Escudero
thread.said: Rep. Dette Escudero said the issue affected MSMEs and consumers because permit delays increased the cost of money. She expressed support for the committee backing the FDA modernization program.

topics.topic: Family planning, reproductive health, and protection-unit funding
topics.summary: Dadah Kiram Ismula raised birth spacing, postpartum coverage, and the gap between PhilHealth’s projected premium and payout requirements. PhilHealth said its packages supported IUDs, ligation, and vasectomy, but postpartum reimbursement currently covered only six weeks; it cited an original requirement of about 76 billion, a current allocation stated as PHP79, and a maximum projected annual payout of 500 billion. Ismulla requested a draft policy revision within thirty days and the chair requested supporting PhilHealth data. Assistant Minority Leader Sarah Elago then sought data on patient detention and asked for reproductive-health funding details. DOH cited 664,000,000 for family planning and reproductive health, 51,000,000 for protection-unit support in 51 hospitals, and said the amount included sexual-assault investigation kits. DOH undertook to provide breakdowns, review DOST-developed kits, and submit reports on gender and development, HIV policy, cancer control, and anti-detention data; cancer-fund expansion was described as including blood products and nutritional support.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish whether family-planning and postpartum services were adequately funded and whether PhilHealth’s proposed premium subsidy matched its projected requirements. It also asked for the funding breakdown and planned expansion of reproductive-health, women’s and children’s protection, sexual-assault kit, and cancer-support programs.
topics.agency_position: DOH and PhilHealth said existing PhilHealth packages supported birth spacing, but postpartum reimbursement currently ended at six weeks. The agencies acknowledged funding and data gaps, stated that reproductive-health and protection-unit funding was available, and undertook to provide detailed breakdowns and requested reports; DOH also said it would review expansion of cancer and sexual-assault-kit support.
topics.outcome: The issues were not fully resolved during the hearing. DOH and PhilHealth were directed or undertook to submit policy revisions, data, and program breakdowns, while the sufficiency of reproductive-health, protection-unit, postpartum, premium-subsidy, and cancer-support funding remained subject to review.

positions.position: Supported two- to three-year birth spacing and sought an extension of postpartum contraceptive financing through the first year. She also pressed PhilHealth to reconcile its premium-subsidy requirement and proposed allocation.

Pressed for stronger implementation of the Anti-Hospital Detention Act, detailed reproductive-health and protection-unit funding, access to sexual-assault investigation kits, expanded cancer aftercare, and submission of gender-and-development, HIV-policy, cancer-control, and anti-detention data.
Supported providing program and funding breakdowns, reviewing the role of DOST-developed kits, and expanding cancer-fund coverage to additional support items.

thread.speaker: Dadah Kiram Ismula

thread.speaker: Dadah Kiram Ismula

thread.speaker: Secretary Edwin Mercado

thread.speaker: Assistant Minority Leader Sarah Elago
thread.said: She asked for a breakdown of the reproductive-health subprograms and referred to 9,100,000,000 pesos for family health, immunization, nutrition, and responsible parenting.

thread.speaker: Secretary Edwin Mercado
thread.said: He said DOH could provide a list and breakdown covering commodities, women’s and children’s protection, safe motherhood, adolescent health, and family-planning program support.

topics.topic: Cancer, rare-disease, and expanded PhilHealth benefit packages
topics.summary: Representative Patrin Gorazeta pressed PhilHealth and DOH on prevention under Yakap, GAMOT accreditation barriers, additional medicines, mental-health coverage and autism providers. PhilHealth said it would review accreditation, expand provider training, unbundle the children-with-disabilities package and develop rare-disease coverage initially for 10 to 15 of 159 diseases. Vice Chair Rufus Rodriguez highlighted the overall budget gap, including the indirect-member benefit shortfall, the HFEP request and the roughly 12 billion requirement for DOH hospital operations, while the agency said actuarial work for rare diseases was not yet complete. Representative Maximo Rodriguez Jr. sought a larger Mindanao share and asked PhilHealth to study insulin pump coverage for diabetes, which PhilHealth committed to do. Representative Janette Garin raised DOH-PhilHealth double financing and reported roughly 50 million in nutrition commodities and 300 million in mental-health medicines expiring annually; the secretary committed to review alignment, medicine use and simplification of medical assistance. The hearing also produced commitments concerning island-province tertiary hospitals and faster Zero Balance Billing payments, but did not resolve the final funding and implementation requirements.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish whether PhilHealth and DOH could expand and effectively implement benefit packages for cancer, rare diseases, diabetes, mental health, autism and other catastrophic conditions. Members also examined the funding gap, provider and accreditation barriers, medicine wastage, hospital access, and the alignment of DOH and PhilHealth financing.
topics.agency_position: DOH and PhilHealth stated that they were expanding or preparing to expand coverage for mental health, autism and children with disabilities, rare diseases, catastrophic conditions and diabetes-related care. They also said they were reviewing accreditation standards, aligning DOH and PhilHealth financing, improving provider capacity, and studying additional benefits such as the insulin pump device, but several actuarial, utilization and implementation details remained incomplete.
topics.outcome: The committee obtained commitments to submit the rare-disease lists, study insulin-pump coverage, simplify or realign financing and medical assistance, review medicine wastage, and support island-province hospital legislation. However, the amounts needed for full rare-disease implementation, the final scope of expanded packages, and several utilization and reimbursement problems remained unresolved.

positions.position: Supported broader prevention, less restrictive GAMOT and autism-package accreditation, additional medicines for thyroid and liver conditions, and more specific mental-health coverage.
Supported restoring funding for PhilHealth indirect-member benefits, HFEP and DOH hospital operations, strengthening local medicine production, and implementing RA 10747 rare-disease coverage.
Supported a larger Mindanao share of the DOH budget and expansion of diabetes coverage to include insulin pump devices.
Supported renewed DOH-PhilHealth financial alignment, redirecting or better using medicines at risk of expiry, simplifying medical assistance, and correcting low immunization and HFEP utilization.
Supported prioritizing island provinces for tertiary care, upgrading an island-province hospital through legislation, and ensuring timely Zero Balance Billing payments.

thread.speaker: Representative Patrin Gorazeta
thread.said: She commended the Yakap screening package but asked what specific prevention programs, including lifestyle counseling, were being implemented and how prevention would reach the barangay level. She also asked about accreditation barriers under GAMOT, noting that only 15 out of 47 centers in her district were accredited.

thread.speaker: Representative Patrin Gorazeta
thread.said: She said requiring a pharmacist, facility space and a license to operate was unrealistic for fourth-class municipalities that lacked the budget to meet those requirements. She suggested adding medicines for hyperthyroidism, hypothyroidism, liver support, cirrhosis, vitamin B complex and calcium to GAMOT.

thread.speaker: Representative Patrin Gorazeta
thread.said: She asked whether the expanded mental-health package covered specific illnesses such as bipolar disorder and depression or was only a generalized package.

thread.speaker: PhilHealth official
thread.said: The official said medicines for hypo- and hyperthyroidism were already in the pipeline. PhilHealth was reviewing accreditation standards, considering arrangements such as allowing larger pharmacies to conduct outreach for rural health units, and developing mobile pharmacies for rural areas.

thread.speaker: PhilHealth official
thread.said: The mental-health package had two tiers, general and specialist, and was based on the professional attending to the patient rather than a particular diagnosis; it was therefore flexible enough to cover bipolar disorder and similar conditions. The official said PhilHealth was working with DOH to expand the number of providers trained to deliver the package.

thread.speaker: PhilHealth official
thread.said: For prevention, the official said schools could serve as settings for Yakap health promotion and preventive work. PhilHealth hoped Yakap revenues could be used to hire permanent personnel dedicated to promotion and prevention.

thread.speaker: Representative Patrin Gorazeta
thread.said: She asked whether accreditation requirements for autism and the expanded children-with-disabilities package could be simplified so more centers and providers could participate.

thread.speaker: PhilHealth official
thread.said: PhilHealth planned to unbundle the children-with-disabilities package, which it said would allow more providers to participate. It was also developing task-shifting and training arrangements, mapping provinces without developmental pediatricians, and considering accreditation of professional societies so members could rotate through local facilities without each provider needing a fixed facility.

thread.speaker: DOH-PhilHealth official
thread.said: The official said PhilHealth already covered benefits exceeding 1,000,000 for some conditions and had additional rare conditions in the pipeline. The agency intended to convert more catastrophic conditions into Z Benefits and develop modifiers based on patient age and other factors, using hospital-bill and provider data collected during the year.

thread.speaker: Vice Chair Rufus Rodriguez
thread.said: He asked how much DOH had requested for its budget, how much had been approved, and what amount had been cut.

thread.speaker: Secretary Edwin Mercado
thread.said: He said DOH requested 837,000,000,000 and that 353,000,000,000 was approved. The transcript rendered the difference as "R485 dollars initial request," which is unclear.

thread.speaker: Secretary Edwin Mercado
thread.said: He said the projected benefit payment for indirect PhilHealth members was about 2.44, while the amount provided was 74, leaving a difference of almost 170.

thread.speaker: PhilHealth President Beverly Ho
thread.said: She said the previous premium estimate was about 3.76 per headcount and that expected benefit payouts for indirect contributors next year were "R244 billion dollars" as rendered in the transcript.

thread.speaker: PhilHealth President Beverly Ho
thread.said: In response to the request for a reasonable restoration, she said an additional 170 was needed merely to reach breakeven, assuming utilization remained at the current rate.

thread.speaker: Vice Chair Rufus Rodriguez
thread.said: He urged PhilHealth to address the lack of mental-health practitioners in his area and asked DOH to identify its other priority requests.

thread.speaker: Secretary Edwin Mercado
thread.said: He identified the Health Facilities Enhancement Program as another priority, saying DOH requested PHP19 billion and received PHP14.5 billion. He also stated a PHP15.1 billion shortfall, although the figures as spoken are internally inconsistent.

thread.speaker: Secretary Edwin Mercado
thread.said: He identified DOH hospital operations as a third priority, with combined requirements of about 12,000,000,000 for Metro Manila hospitals, regional hospitals and GOCCs.

thread.speaker: Vice Chair Rufus Rodriguez
thread.said: He asked when the list of rare diseases under RA 10747 had last been updated, requested the list of 159 diseases and the diseases PhilHealth already covered, and asked how much DOH requested from DBM for full implementation of the law and how much was approved.

thread.speaker: DOH-PhilHealth official
thread.said: The official said the rare-disease list update would be checked. PhilHealth had developed rare-disease coverage intended for rollout within the year, initially covering 10 to 15 of the 159 rare diseases, generally those most common in the local market.

thread.speaker: DOH-PhilHealth official
thread.said: The official committed to submit the list of 159 rare diseases and the diseases initially covered by PhilHealth. The official said no actuarial estimate had yet been completed for rare-disease coverage.

thread.speaker: DOH-PhilHealth official
thread.said: The official said DOH funding for rare diseases primarily covered capacity building, a multisectoral forum, the rare-disease registry, and duties and taxes for medicines. NIH would procure medicines, while PhilHealth would begin covering medicines commonly available in the local market.

thread.speaker: DOH official
thread.said: The official said Mindanao accounted for 15% of the share for regional CHDs, compared with 10% for the Visayas, 34% for Luzon and 41% for the central office.

thread.speaker: Representative Maximo Rodriguez Jr.
thread.said: He urged PhilHealth to expand diabetes coverage, specifically asking it to study inclusion of the insulin pump device, which he described as expensive and scarce in the Philippines.

thread.speaker: PhilHealth official Audrey Zubiri
thread.said: She said PhilHealth would include the insulin pump device on its list of possible benefit expansions for study.

thread.speaker: Representative Janette Garin
thread.said: She asked Secretary Mercado to commit to restoring DOH-PhilHealth financial alignment to avoid double financing, particularly where DOH hospitals provide medicines or services later reimbursed by PhilHealth.

thread.speaker: Secretary Edwin Mercado
thread.said: He committed to alignment through the single-agenda work streams, including a separate finance work stream addressing hospital-related issues.

thread.speaker: Representative Janette Garin
thread.said: She said approximately 50,000,000 in nutrition commodities and approximately 300,000,000 in mental-health medicines expired or neared expiry annually, and asked whether unused cancer and mental-health medicines could instead be redirected to medical assistance or a Philippine Cancer Fund.

thread.speaker: Secretary Edwin Mercado
thread.said: He said DOH would look into the proposed redirection and that the long-term goal was for PhilHealth to pay for the medicines and commodities, eliminating double financing through alignment of the relevant circulars.

thread.speaker: Representative Janette Garin
thread.said: She asked whether the medical assistance arrangement could be simplified and brought back to the Medical Assistance Program so indigent and financially incapacitated patients needing renal, cardiac or cancer care could use it more effectively.

thread.speaker: Secretary Edwin Mercado
thread.said: He said simplifying the program was part of his directive and that DOH would examine the Medical Assistance Program.

thread.speaker: Representative Janette Garin
thread.said: She asked for immunization obligation and disbursement figures and later questioned the low utilization of HFEP, including whether lengthy documentary and design requirements caused projects to move back and forth between regional and central offices.

thread.speaker: Secretary Edwin Mercado
thread.said: For 2025 immunization, he stated an allotment of 10,200,000,000, with 5.7 obligated and 576,000,000 disbursed; for the carryover, he stated 6,500,000,000 obligated and 1,100,000,000 disbursed. The transcript's percentages and some year references are unclear.

thread.speaker: Secretary Edwin Mercado
thread.said: For 2026 immunization, he stated an allotment of 10,200,000,000, of which 1,400,000,000 was obligated and 164,000,000 was disbursed.

thread.speaker: Secretary Edwin Mercado
thread.said: For 2025 HFEP, he stated an allotment of 13,700,000,000, with 12.4 obligated and 47.03 disbursed. For 2026 hospitals, he stated 11.9, with 1,964,000,000 obligated and 16.4; the units and some figures are unclear.

thread.speaker: Secretary Edwin Mercado
thread.said: He stated that out of 20,483,000,000, 5,000,000,000 was obligated and 7.58 disbursed, with an obligation rate of 24.64 and disbursement of 15.04.

thread.speaker: Secretary Edwin Mercado
thread.said: He acknowledged that the historical process had been difficult but said the omnibus HFEP guidelines were intended to require complete applications, site conditions and other requirements before the budget was released.

thread.speaker: Representative Leo Rodriguez
thread.said: He asked for DOH's policy and plan to provide reasonable province-level access to tertiary, referral and specialty care, particularly in island provinces.

thread.speaker: DOH official
thread.said: The official cited a five-pillar hospital-operation framework, a specialty-hospital roadmap and the health-facility development plan. DOH intended to align HFEP with regional health-care referral networks and map the distribution of services so provinces could access tertiary and specialty care.

thread.speaker: Representative Leo Rodriguez
thread.said: He asked whether DOH would prioritize island provinces and support upgrading Eastern Visayas Medical Center into a DOH-managed tertiary hospital.

thread.speaker: DOH official
thread.said: The official said he had been appointed only three weeks earlier and needed to review the criteria for converting or upgrading a hospital. He indicated that legislative action would be needed before the department could proceed.

thread.speaker: Chair and Secretary
thread.said: The chair said members could help fast-track the bill and seek a Senate counterpart, while the secretary committed to support the proposal once enacted because the law would obligate DOH to fund it.

thread.speaker: Representative Leo Rodriguez
thread.said: He asked about the 2026 implementation of Zero Balance Billing, including reimbursement of health facilities and payment of doctors' professional fees.

thread.speaker: PhilHealth official
thread.said: The official said covered professional fees could be paid under the special provisions, including to private-practice doctors in private hospitals, although payment acceptance and processing remained concerns.

thread.speaker: PhilHealth official
thread.said: PhilHealth acknowledged that it needed to expedite payments to private hospitals and doctors so they would accept the applicable payment arrangements for eligible Zero Balance Billing patients.

topics.topic: Out-of-pocket health spending and regional allocation formulas
topics.summary: Secretary Edwin Mercado presented a proposed DOH budget of about 353.8 billion and said government spending had risen while out-of-pocket spending fell to 41.2% in 2025. Rep. Ismula questioned the gap between the requested PhilHealth premium subsidy and the NEP allocation; the agency cited a 76 billion headcount-based requirement, a current allocation spoken as PHP79, and projected payouts reaching 500 billion, although several figures were unclear. Members pressed for greater Mindanao and Bukidnon funding, with Mindanao reported at 15% of the CHD share and Northern Mindanao at about 17.45 billion, while Bukidnon requests substantially exceeded approved amounts. Rep. Rodriguez sought a concrete plan to reduce out-of-pocket spending, and the agency identified a target of about 37.8% by 2028 but said single-digit spending would require more fiscal resources. Members also challenged hospital allocation formulas, utilization, staffing, and no-balance-billing compliance. The agency committed to submit regional and hospital data, study insulin pump and assistance coverage, coordinate on HFEP conditions, and issue implementation guidelines within the year.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish whether the proposed DOH and PhilHealth allocations were sufficient to reduce household out-of-pocket health spending and whether the budget was distributed equitably across regions, provinces, and hospitals. Members also asked how allocation formulas, absorptive capacity, utilization, and health-service gaps affected the proposed amounts.
topics.agency_position: The DOH said government health spending and PhilHealth's share had increased while out-of-pocket spending had declined, and it identified a Philippine Development Plan target of reducing out-of-pocket spending to about 37.8% by 2028. It maintained that allocations were based primarily on hospital level, absorptive capacity, normative budgeting, utilization, and operational conditions, while acknowledging gaps in PhilHealth financing, provincial disaggregation, and implementation capacity.
topics.outcome: The committee obtained the agency's reported spending indicators, regional shares, and 2028 out-of-pocket target, but did not resolve the adequacy of the PhilHealth subsidy, the Bukidnon allocation, or the formula for regional and hospital funding. The DOH and PhilHealth undertook to provide data, study coverage and financing changes, coordinate on HFEP deficiencies, and issue no-balance-billing guidelines within the year.

positions.position: Mindanao's 15% share was too low relative to its population and service gaps; he supported increasing the DOH budget and expanding PhilHealth diabetes coverage, including study of insulin pump devices.
Bukidnon and Northern Mindanao required substantially greater support because Bukidnon had no DOH hospital and proposed HFEP and health-center allocations were inadequate.
The Philippines remained below the WHO bed-to-population standard and required better management of medicines and regionalized procurement.
DOH and PhilHealth should align financing to prevent double financing, reduce medicine wastage, simplify medical assistance, and improve immunization and HFEP utilization.

The committee needed a transparent, objective allocation formula, stronger one-stop hospital assistance, complete MAIP utilization data, and enforcement of the 10% private-hospital no-balance-billing bed requirement.
Regional allocations and staffing should reflect actual service needs, hospital capacity, and workforce gaps rather than concentrating resources in regions with more existing hospitals.
