thread.speaker: Secretary Edwin Mercado
thread.said: Secretary Mercado presented the proposed DOH budget as 353,800,000,000, distributed across five budget pillars.

thread.speaker: Secretary Edwin Mercado
thread.said: He reported that government health spending increased from 42.1% in 2023 to 46.5% in 2025, while Filipino out-of-pocket spending declined from 44.4% to 41.2%.

thread.speaker: Secretary Edwin Mercado
thread.said: He said the proposed budget constituted 4.9% of the 7,200,000,000,000 national budget and 1.1% of projected 2027 GDP, while the usual GDP health ratio was 8% to 10%.

thread.speaker: an agency official
thread.said: An agency official said the original proposed budget was upwards of 837,000,000,000, with 55,000,000,000 plus 19,000,000,000 for PhilHealth benefit improvement.

thread.speaker: Representative Dadah Kiram Ismula
thread.said: Rep. Ismula asked for the exact difference between the DOH and PhilHealth requirement for 2027 and the amount included in the NEP.

thread.speaker: an agency official
thread.said: The agency official stated the original requirement as 485,000,000,000, after first referring to a 42% difference.

thread.speaker: Representative Dadah Kiram Ismula
thread.said: Rep. Ismula asked whether the 2027 budget contained the full mandated premium subsidy for 41,800,000 indirect contributors.

thread.speaker: Secretary Edwin Mercado
thread.said: Secretary Mercado said the allocation was much below the amount requested. He cited an original headcount-based requirement of 76,000,000,000 and said the current allocation was only PHP79.

thread.speaker: Secretary Edwin Mercado
thread.said: He said projected payouts for indirect contributors could reach TWD 240,000,000,000 by the end of the year and at least TWD 244,000,000,000 the following year at the same utilization rate.

thread.speaker: Representative Dadah Kiram Ismula
thread.said: Rep. Ismula asked the agency to reconcile the 2027 PhilHealth requirement of PHP76,650,000,000 with the Universal Health Care Act.

thread.speaker: Secretary Edwin Mercado
thread.said: Secretary Mercado replied that total payouts for the following year were expected to reach a maximum of 500,000,000,000.

thread.speaker: Deputy Speaker Ferjenel Biron
thread.said: Deputy Speaker Biron cited the global benchmark of 10% of GDP for national health expenditure and asked about the adequacy of the proposed 353,000,000,000 budget.

thread.speaker: Secretary Edwin Mercado
thread.said: Secretary Mercado agreed that 10% was the standard benchmark, but said government accounted for 46% of total health-care spending, with the remainder coming from private spending.

thread.speaker: Representative Maximo Rodriguez Jr.
thread.said: Rep. Rodriguez asked what share of the DOH budget went to Mindanao and said the region's share should increase, noting its population of about 28,000,000.

thread.speaker: Secretary Edwin Mercado
thread.said: Secretary Mercado said Mindanao accounted for 15% of the share specific to the CHDs in Mindanao, compared with 10% for the Visayas, 34% for Luzon, and 41% for the central office.

thread.speaker: Representative Maximo Rodriguez Jr.
thread.said: Rep. Rodriguez said even a 1% increase for Mindanao could provide several billions and improve facilities in the region. He said he would support an increase in the budget in plenary.

thread.speaker: Representative Maximo Rodriguez Jr.
thread.said: Rep. Rodriguez asked PhilHealth to study expanded diabetes coverage, including insulin pump devices, which he described as expensive and currently available to relatively few patients.

thread.speaker: Audrey Zubiri
thread.said: Audrey Zubiri said PhilHealth would include insulin pump devices in its list of items to study for coverage expansion.

thread.speaker: Representative Audrey Zubiri
thread.said: Rep. Zubiri asked for the specific allocation for Bukidnon and how provincial allocations were determined.

thread.speaker: Secretary Edwin Mercado
thread.said: Secretary Mercado said the budget was currently disaggregated only to the regional level and that the DOH would provide the Bukidnon-specific amount. He cited 17,450,000,000 for Northern Mindanao, including DOH hospitals.

thread.speaker: Representative Audrey Zubiri
thread.said: Rep. Zubiri said local partners had requested 2,000,000,000 for Bukidnon but less than 5,000,000 had been approved. She asked whether allocation was based on population or another formula.

thread.speaker: Secretary Edwin Mercado
thread.said: The Secretary said HFEP funding required specified site conditions and that the DOH would coordinate with Rep. Zubiri's office regarding deficiencies and the reasons for the allocation.

thread.speaker: Representative Audrey Zubiri
thread.said: Rep. Zubiri requested review of funding for a Bagong Filipinas health center in Moolog. She said the local request was 19,000,000 but the approved amount was 2,700,000, which she considered insufficient.

thread.speaker: Representative Maximo Rodriguez Jr.
thread.said: Rep. Rodriguez asked for a concrete plan and timeline to substantially reduce out-of-pocket spending, citing about 44% in the Philippines compared with about 9% in Thailand.

thread.speaker: the DOH undersecretary for finance
thread.said: The undersecretary said out-of-pocket payment had fallen to 41% in 2025 from 44%, while PhilHealth's share of total health expenditure rose from 13.4% to 19.5%.

thread.speaker: the DOH undersecretary for finance
thread.said: The undersecretary identified the Philippine Development Plan target of reducing out-of-pocket payment to around 37.8% by 2028. She said reaching a single-digit share remained an aspiration requiring additional fiscal commitment.

thread.speaker: the DOH undersecretary for finance
thread.said: The agency described a clearer order of payment, with PhilHealth followed by other support, and said it was developing a process using the same statement of account for PhilHealth and DOH medical-assistance evaluators.

thread.speaker: Representative Robert Nassal
thread.said: Rep. Nassal asked whether regional and hospital allocations followed a scientific formula based on poverty, population, disease burden, patient volume, utilization, and actual need.

thread.speaker: Sheila Pabila
thread.said: Sheila Pabila said funds downloaded to DOH hospitals were determined by the level of the hospital and its absorptive capacity.

thread.speaker: Representative Robert Nassal
thread.said: Rep. Nassal requested, before plenary, complete MAIP allocations for 2024, 2025, and 2026 by region, hospital, and health facility, including additional downloads, augmentations, utilization, patients served, balances, and referring offices.

thread.speaker: Representative Robert Nassal
thread.said: Rep. Nassal asked why the statutory requirement that at least 10% of private-hospital beds be basic or ward accommodation with no balance billing had not been fully implemented.

thread.speaker: Secretary Edwin Mercado
thread.said: Secretary Mercado said the DOH was strengthening monitoring and was intent on implementing the requirement through licensing and related measures.

thread.speaker: Secretary Edwin Mercado
thread.said: In response to the request for clear guidelines, Secretary Mercado said they would be issued "within the year."

thread.speaker: Chair Romeo Momo
thread.said: Chair Momo questioned why the National Capital Region continued to receive the largest regional allocation despite its concentration of hospitals and beds. He asked whether population, poverty, disease burden, geographic isolation, bed shortages, and workforce gaps were allocation parameters.

thread.speaker: an agency official
thread.said: The agency official described a normative-budgeting approach using hospital case mix, occupancy rate, average length of stay, and the percentage shared, although the explanation was incomplete in the transcript.

thread.speaker: Chair Romeo Momo
thread.said: Chair Momo raised a reported staffing gap of 989 personnel at a hospital recently upgraded from level two to level three. He said the hospital had requested 185 positions costing 212,471,000, but DOH funding was only 4,000,000.

thread.speaker: an agency official
thread.said: The agency said staffing depended on operational capacity and functional or operating beds, with adjustments coordinated with DBM rather than based solely on full physical capacity.

thread.speaker: Chair Romeo Momo
thread.said: Chair Momo asked that funding be provided to complete an orthopedic and rehabilitation building, citing phase-one funding of 80,000,000, phase two of 50,000,000, and a 2027 phase-three requirement of 50,000,000.

thread.speaker: an agency official
thread.said: The agency official agreed to address allocation for equipment and facility completion, although the precise undertaking was unclear in the transcript.

hearings.title: COMMITTEE ON APPROPRIATIONS - BUDGET BRIEFING/HEARINGS OF THE FY 2027 PROPOSED BUDGET (DOE & ERC)

topics.topic: DOE FY2027 budget increase and agency funding priorities
topics.summary: DOE presented a proposed FY 2027 budget of about 5.58 billion, an increase of 25.74%, and attributed it mainly to gray geometry, mobile energy systems, and automation. Members questioned the increase, DOE’s 49% obligation rate, the separate emergency allotment of about 29 billion, and whether the projects would deliver lower rates, fewer outages, and lasting electrification. DOE said the projects would improve energy security, committed to provide fuel-marking data, and described plans for government-controlled strategic petroleum storage. ERC requested more than 700 million, or at least about 200 million plus, to complete distribution-utility rate resets, while NEA sought 7 or 10 billion to cushion electric cooperatives from system-loss elimination. Members broadly supported DOE and ERC, but final restorations and special provisions were left to subcommittee review, DBM consultation, committee action, and plenary.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish why DOE’s FY 2027 budget was increasing by roughly 25%, whether its existing and emergency resources were being properly utilized, and whether the proposed funding would improve energy security, electricity reliability, and consumer prices. Members also examined related unfunded priorities, ERC’s request for additional resources, system-loss reduction, and the development of government-controlled fuel reserves.
topics.agency_position: DOE maintained that its proposed increase was concentrated in three energy-security and modernization projects—gray geometry, mobile energy systems, and automation—and that it did not seek a further increase beyond the proposed budget. DOE supported additional ERC resources for rate resets and a strong regulator, while seeking special provisions and corporate-fund authority for energy-security measures. The agencies committed to provide utilization, fuel-marking, strategic-reserve, system-loss, and ERC funding details, but several requests remained subject to budget-subcommittee, DBM, committee, and plenary action.
topics.outcome: The committee generally supported DOE’s proposed budget and endorsed stronger ERC funding, but did not finally resolve the additional ERC, NEA, DOE special-provision, or reserve-related requests. DOE and ERC were directed to submit detailed information for review by the budget amendments review subcommittee, with DBM consultations and plenary action still required.

positions.position: Questioned the roughly 25% DOE increase but expressed appreciation for DOE’s explanation and sought resolution of the electric-cooperative CBA memorandum issue.

Pressed DOE to justify the balance among major projects, emergency resources, electrification, fuel marking, and strategic reserves, but ultimately manifested full support for the DOE budget and additional consumer-support funding.
Strongly supported DOE, ERC, and the energy agencies and advocated increasing their budgets to maximum levels.
Sought stronger accountability for technical and nontechnical system-loss elimination, more fiscal-space discipline, and a genuine government-controlled petroleum reserve.
Supported DOE and ERC and committed to advocate for requested restorations or augmentations, subject to fiscal-space limits and the required budget process.
Expressed full support for DOE and ERC while requiring detailed submissions and reserving final action for the budget amendments review subcommittee, committee, DBM discussions, and plenary.

actions.action: Provide DOE data comparing fuel imports and sales and information relevant to estimating illicit fuel entering the market.

thread.speaker: DOE Secretary Sharon Garin
thread.said: Secretary Garin said the requested budget would implement measures and programs that were not available during the oil crisis and would reduce the burden of a future crisis on the country and consumers.

thread.speaker: DOE Undersecretary Youssef Bacordo
thread.said: Bacordo presented a total proposed FY 2027 DOE budget of 5,580,000,000, an increase of 1,140,000,000 or 25.74% over the FY 2026 GAA of PHP 4,430,000,000. He said 36.4% would fund new operations and 63.6% would come from automatic operations under the special account in the general fund.

thread.speaker: DOE Undersecretary Youssef Bacordo
thread.said: DOE reported a 49% obligation rate as of August 31, 2026, projected a rate of 68.31% after the mobile energy system and automation procurements, and expected at least 95.89% utilization for 2026.

thread.speaker: DOE Undersecretary Youssef Bacordo
thread.said: He attributed the proposed increase principally to the gray geometry and seismic survey, mobile energy systems under the Total Electrification Project, and the integrated systems support project, including DOE automation.

thread.speaker: DOE Undersecretary Youssef Bacordo
thread.said: DOE said it was using 500,000,000 from current appropriations and 21,000,000 from continuing appropriations for mobile energy systems in 2026, and was proposing 600,000,000 in 2027 for at least 60 additional units. It also proposed 950,000,000 for ISSP, including 491,000,000 for automation and 458,000,000 for other ICPA requirements.

thread.speaker: Rep. Perci Cendaña
thread.said: Cendaña questioned why DOE was receiving an overall increase of more than 25% across personnel services, maintenance and other operating expenses, and capital outlays.

thread.speaker: DOE Secretary Sharon Garin
thread.said: Garin attributed the increase to the gray geometry project, mobile energy systems, and automation. She said gray geometry would provide information needed to identify domestic oil and gas resources, mobile systems would provide deployable emergency electricity, and automation would make DOE operations faster, more transparent, and data-driven.

thread.speaker: DOE Secretary Sharon Garin
thread.said: Garin said the gray geometry project would cost about 2,000,000,000 pesos as a continuing project, with funding provided in 2026 and another budget allotted for 2027.

thread.speaker: DOE Secretary Sharon Garin
thread.said: Garin said the increase was 25% of 2,500,000,000 and therefore small compared with increases for other agencies. She said DOE policies were intended to lower electricity rates through more indigenous oil and gas, more renewable energy, and better coordination between policy and regulation.

thread.speaker: Rep. Jan Rurik Padiernos
thread.said: Padiernos cited a proposed DOE budget transcribed as 5.5175000000000 and a separate 29,860,000,000 emergency allotment. He asked how Congress could evaluate DOE without consolidated accounting of regular, automatic, continuing, emergency, and Malampaya-funded resources, and what lasting improvements justified additional funding.

thread.speaker: DOE agency official
thread.said: The official reiterated that utilization was 49% as of August 31, that procurement delays had affected the mobile energy system and automation projects, and that DOE expected to reach 68.31% during September or early October and 95.89% by the end of 2026.

thread.speaker: DOE agency official
thread.said: DOE clarified that the additional emergency amount was approximately 29,000,000,000, transferred to PNOC in response to the fuel emergency and used for LPG, diesel, and gas-related activities. DOE said the funds remained available and would be separately liquidated once the emergency was lifted.

thread.speaker: Rep. Jan Rurik Padiernos
thread.said: Padiernos cited about 2,910,000,000 for the three highlighted projects and asked whether that was the proper balance when about 1,530,000 households remained without electricity. He asked how the projects would produce lower rates, fewer outages, and permanent rather than temporary electrification.

thread.speaker: DOE agency official
thread.said: DOE said the projects would strengthen energy security, while NEA—not DOE—was principally responsible for nationwide electrification. DOE identified 500,000,000 for mobile energy systems to be deployed to islands and said it would respect the budget decisions of DBM and the Executive.

thread.speaker: Rep. Jan Rurik Padiernos
thread.said: Padiernos asked whether DOE could quantify illicit fuel still entering the market and measure the effectiveness of fuel marking, citing 21,102,000,000 liters marked, 247,000,000,000 in taxes, and illicit fuel cases in Bataan.

thread.speaker: DOE Secretary Sharon Garin
thread.said: DOE said smuggling enforcement principally belonged to DOF, Customs, and BIR, while fuel marking monitored tax payment. DOE said it could compare imports with sales but did not have the calculation available during the hearing and would provide the data.

thread.speaker: DOE agency official
thread.said: The agency said data-sharing agreements with Customs and BIR and DOE’s automation and artificial-intelligence systems would permit stricter cross-referencing and help identify gaps and anomalies.

thread.speaker: Rep. Jan Rurik Padiernos
thread.said: Padiernos asked how much of the reported 49 days of diesel inventory and 54 days of gasoline inventory was actually owned or controlled by government and where PNOC would store it.

thread.speaker: DOE agency official
thread.said: The official said government normally did not buy stocks, although during the emergency it held diesel and less than a day of gasoline stock in a private storage facility. The official said Congress was examining the government’s role in a strategic petroleum reserve while avoiding excessive intrusion into private enterprise.

thread.speaker: PNOC agency official
thread.said: PNOC identified the tank farm as a priority project for the following year, with an initial phase of 1,000,000 barrels and a later phase transcribed as 15,000,000.

thread.speaker: Rep. Jan Rurik Padiernos
thread.said: Padiernos asked whether the plan was a genuine government-owned strategic petroleum reserve or merely emergency fuel purchases.

thread.speaker: PNOC agency official
thread.said: PNOC said the first 1,000,000-unit phase would be owned by PNOC, with later phases potentially involving private companies, joint ventures, or investment partnerships.

thread.speaker: Rep. Jan Rurik Padiernos
thread.said: Padiernos manifested full support for the DOE budget and for any additional budget that would help consumers.

thread.speaker: Rep. Rufus Rodriguez
thread.said: Rodriguez said he supported DOE and ERC and asked how much additional funding DOE was requesting.

thread.speaker: DOE Secretary Sharon Garin
thread.said: Garin said DOE was not asking for an increase and could manage its proposed budget, but supported additional funding for a strong ERC regulator.

thread.speaker: ERC agency official
thread.said: ERC said it had asked that more than 700,000,000 in unreleased proposed FY 2027 funding be reinstated, or at minimum that around 200,000,000 plus for consulting services and related maintenance and other expenses be restored. ERC said the funding was needed to complete rate resets for all distribution utilities in 2027.

thread.speaker: Committee chair
thread.said: The chair stated that ERC’s request was approved, although the later discussion indicated that additional details and budget-subcommittee review were still required.

thread.speaker: NEA agency official
thread.said: NEA said it had requested 7 or 10,000,000,000 to cushion the effect of eliminating nontechnical system losses among electric cooperatives.

thread.speaker: National Power Corporation official
thread.said: NPC said it was satisfied with the GAA as filed and would defer to ERC because ERC needed more support.

thread.speaker: Rep. Rufus Rodriguez
thread.said: Rodriguez expressed support for DOE, ERC, and the energy agencies and said their budgets should be increased to maximum levels in recognition of their response to the fuel crisis.

thread.speaker: DOE Secretary Sharon Garin
thread.said: Garin said DOE would work to eliminate both technical and nontechnical system losses if feasible. DOE planned to give cooperatives about six months to prepare optimal distribution plans and quantify the required funding, effort, and time.

thread.speaker: Rep. Edgar Erice
thread.said: Erice cited Meralco’s 5.6% system loss and asked whether utilities would comply with a system-loss elimination policy.

thread.speaker: DOE Secretary Sharon Garin
thread.said: Garin said Meralco’s nontechnical loss was 1% and that DOE was still finalizing the system-loss guidelines, particularly because electric cooperatives had different financial circumstances. She said she could not yet commit to a final plan for private utilities.

thread.speaker: DOE Secretary Sharon Garin
thread.said: Garin said DOE understood the limited fiscal space and would work out funding improvements for electric cooperatives without asking for an additional budget. She said the target was to finish the work before the next SONA.

thread.speaker: DOE Secretary Sharon Garin
thread.said: Garin said DOE had formulated a fuel-transition plan to reduce dependence on imported fuel through electric vehicles, exploration, and appliance electrification. She said government-owned storage was being developed through PNOC, with a proposed facility described in the transcript as 1,000,000,000 barrels and also as a 1,000,000-barrel storage facility; the wording is unclear.

thread.speaker: DOE agency official
thread.said: An agency official estimated total storage capacity at about 2,700,000,000 liters, while acknowledging that the figure included private storage.

thread.speaker: DOE agency official
thread.said: The agency said planning was under way for a strategic petroleum reserve with regional distribution and specified proportions of crude oil, diesel, and gasoline, including government control.

thread.speaker: Committee sponsor
thread.said: The sponsor said he was committed to helping the DOE family and to fighting for requested restorations, but emphasized that the requests had to pass through the budget amendments review subcommittee, the committee, and plenary because fiscal space was tight.

thread.speaker: DOE Secretary Sharon Garin
thread.said: Garin identified requested nonfunding provisions, including stronger government procurement of electric vehicles, and asked that PNOC be allowed to reserve 8,000,000,000 in corporate funds for a facility. She said DOE was not requesting an additional budget increase and supported increasing ERC’s resources.

thread.speaker: DOE Secretary Sharon Garin
thread.said: Garin said DOE collected 6,000,000,000 from Malampaya in the current year and expected collections of about 27,000,000,000 next year, an increase of about 21,000,000,000 that would go to the national coffers.

thread.speaker: ERC agency official
thread.said: ERC confirmed that its request for around 200,000,000 plus was for consultants and technical assistance needed to complete rate resets for all distribution utilities in 2027, after more than a decade without a rate-reset exercise.

thread.speaker: Committee chair Mika Suansing
thread.said: The chair requested detailed justification for ERC’s additional funding requirement so the budget amendments review subcommittee could determine the amount needed.

thread.speaker: ERC agency official
thread.said: ERC undertook to submit a narrative explaining how the additional consultancy funding would be used, including how it would free organic staff to work on lowering and ultimately removing system-loss charges from electricity bills.

thread.speaker: Committee chair Mika Suansing
thread.said: The chair deferred a DBM position on proposed special provisions to a separate discussion with DBM and said the matter would be settled, if possible, before plenary.

thread.speaker: Committee chair Mika Suansing
thread.said: The chair requested DOE and ERC’s prioritized list of unfunded or restoration items, including proposed special-provision language, by the following day for budget-subcommittee deliberation.

thread.speaker: Committee chair Mika Suansing
thread.said: The chair reiterated full support for DOE and ERC and said the committee would work within limited fiscal space to augment or restore items needed for the agencies to perform their mandates.

topics.topic: System-loss reduction, anti-pilferage, and electric-cooperative funding
topics.summary: Rep. Chukwish questioned ERC on the VAT treatment of the 12% system-loss charge and when consumers would see changes, while ERC said the BIR process and publication requirements had to be completed. DOE and ERC distinguished technical from nontechnical losses, described four phases of twenty five percent reductions for nontechnical losses, and said cooperatives needed about six months to prepare technical-loss plans. ERC identified November as the earliest hoped-for billing implementation and later clarified that the 7,500,000,000 figure was for nontechnical-loss work, with cooperative assistance to be assessed case by case. Members also pressed for cooperative subsidy reforms, safeguards against rooftop-solar costs being shifted to non-solar consumers, and action on stranded capacity. ERC requested more than 700 million and at least about 200 million for consulting and related operating expenses, while NEA requested 7 or 10 billion to cushion cooperatives; the chair approved the ERC request and the 8.2 reconsideration amount for NEA CTO electrification, although the unit of the latter figure was unclear. The agencies committed to further guidelines, consultations, cooperative assessments, and studies, but final funding and technical-loss obligations remained open.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish how technical and nontechnical system losses would be reduced, how their VAT and billing treatment would affect consumers, and how the effort would be financed without shifting costs to consumers or destabilizing electric cooperatives. Members also asked about cooperative subsidies, rooftop solar, stranded costs, and the adequacy of DOE, ERC, and NEA funding.
topics.agency_position: DOE, ERC, and NEA stated that nontechnical losses, particularly pilferage, should be eliminated through phased enforcement, consumer education, billing improvements, and cooperative support, with a stated objective of zero nontechnical loss and implementation potentially within one year. They said technical-loss reduction required cooperative-specific engineering plans and could not be rushed; funding would be assessed case by case and, where possible, obtained from cooperative earnings, loans, or existing resources rather than additional national funding.
topics.outcome: The agencies provided a phased plan and timetable, including a possible November billing implementation and a one-year objective for eliminating nontechnical losses. Funding, technical-loss targets for private utilities, the final treatment of VAT and stranded costs, and the adequacy of NEA support remained subject to further guidelines, studies, consultations, and budget action.

Demanded the policy basis and fiscal-space implications of eliminating technical and nontechnical losses, while questioning whether private utilities would comply.
Urged ERC to address stranded costs and excess contracted capacity so that solar adoption would benefit consumers rather than leave costs with captive customers.

thread.speaker: Rep. Chukwish
thread.said: Rep. Chukwish asked ERC Chair Francis Wang about the ERC's position on treating a 12% system-loss charge for VAT purposes.

thread.speaker: ERC Chair Francis Wang
thread.said: Wang referred to BIR resolution 26, series of 20 '26, and said the system-loss charge was treated as a government-mandated charge associated with lifeline subsidy and cost recovery for distribution utilities, subject to the commission's cap.

thread.speaker: Rep. Chukwish
thread.said: Rep. Chukwish asked when consumers could expect the agencies' coordination with the BIR to take effect.

thread.speaker: ERC Chair Francis Wang
thread.said: Wang said the agencies first had to distinguish technical from nontechnical losses, with nontechnical losses involving manmade losses such as pilferage.

thread.speaker: ERC Chair Francis Wang
thread.said: Wang said the resolution would become effective after publication and fifteen days, after which the BIR RMC would be involved in implementation.

thread.speaker: DOE Sharon Garin
thread.said: Garrin said system-loss reduction could not be implemented simply by ordering a lower charge because it required enforcement, consumer education, billing and collection efficiency, meter management, database cleansing, cooperative strengthening, and regulatory reform.

thread.speaker: DOE Sharon Garin
thread.said: Garrin said the work would take time and money, but DOE would figure out how to proceed without asking for additional funding. She said technical losses required evaluating transformers, meters, and electricity flow.

thread.speaker: DOE Sharon Garin
thread.said: Garrin said electric cooperatives would need about six months to prepare an optimal technical-loss reduction plan, after which ERC would set the limitations and rates.

thread.speaker: DOE Sharon Garin
thread.said: Garrin described a phased reduction of nontechnical losses by twenty five percent in each of four stages until nontechnical losses reached zero. She said DOE could report on technical losses in the first half of next year.

thread.speaker: ERC Chair Francis Wang
thread.said: Wang said the agencies had a plan and timetable for system-loss reduction and would implement it.

thread.speaker: Chair
thread.said: The chair asked ERC to provide the target for system-loss billing.

thread.speaker: ERC Chair Francis Wang
thread.said: Wang said the target was September for the BIR process and the effective direct fee and distribution-utility bill format. He said implementation issues could require reconciliation after distribution utilities issued bills.

thread.speaker: ERC Chair Francis Wang
thread.said: Wang said that after September or October, the earliest implementation would hopefully be November.

thread.speaker: A member
thread.said: A member asked how many cooperative subsidy applications remained pending.

thread.speaker: Agency official
thread.said: The official said all pending applications had been filed and that UCME allocations would be made as far as collected funds could accommodate them. The official described UCME as a revolving fund supporting continuous operations.

thread.speaker: A member
thread.said: The member asked whether the budget for 2026 and 2027 was almost the same.

thread.speaker: Agency official
thread.said: The official said UCME was collected from grid consumers and that NAPOCOR's own budget was not part of UCME, but the response did not clearly state whether the two budgets were the same.

thread.speaker: Rep. Sergio Dagooc
thread.said: Dagooc raised the issue of system-loss reduction under what the transcript rendered as 'ER was done one dash ninety four,' asking about the removal of nontechnical and technical losses.

thread.speaker: Agency official
thread.said: The official said new rules simplified the business-plan requirement and allowed communities to choose whether assistance would subsidize consumers or support cooperative infrastructure.

thread.speaker: Rep. Sergio Dagooc
thread.said: Dagooc asked whether subsidies could support system-loss reduction, including technical losses.

thread.speaker: Agency official
thread.said: The official said the agency would propose a revision and conduct public consultation with stakeholders.

thread.speaker: Rep. Tino
thread.said: Rep. Tino asked for the status of system-loss reduction and pressed the agencies on the distinction between technical and nontechnical losses.

thread.speaker: ERC official
thread.said: The official said nontechnical losses already had a plan, including a Gantt chart, joint work with DICT on e-reporting, consumer education, a proposed MOA with DILG and the PNP for anti-pilferage enforcement, and improvements in billing and collection. The objective was zero nontechnical loss, but implementation required time and funding.

thread.speaker: ERC official
thread.said: The official said technical-loss reduction required each electric cooperative to submit an optimal distribution development plan, including transformer and meter evaluation. Cooperatives needed six months to prepare, with the objective of reducing technical losses to zero or near zero.

thread.speaker: Rep. Tino
thread.said: Rep. Tino asked whether the proposed 7,500,000,000 budget covered technical system-loss reduction over four phases.

thread.speaker: ERC official
thread.said: The official clarified that the amount was for nontechnical-loss work, including reinforcement and measures related to pilferage, while technical improvements such as meters would require separate assessment.

thread.speaker: Rep. Tino
thread.said: Rep. Tino asked for further explanation of the 7,500,000,000 budget and whether it was intended for cooperative facility upgrades.

thread.speaker: ERC official
thread.said: The official said the funding could come from the cooperatives' earnings or loans that the agencies could facilitate. The official said assistance would be assessed case by case for 130 cooperatives, including ailing cooperatives and private distribution utilities.

thread.speaker: Rep. Jay Vergara
thread.said: Vergara asked how ERC evaluated rooftop solar, net metering, back-feed, and technical system losses, and what safeguards would prevent related costs from being shifted to non-solar consumers.

thread.speaker: ERC official
thread.said: The official acknowledged the possibility of cost and operational impacts as rooftop solar expanded. ERC was studying distributed energy resources, including batteries, and planned to revisit rate-setting and distribution-code rules after work on the 2026 Philippine Grid Code.

thread.speaker: ERC official
thread.said: The official said distribution impact studies and two-way metering would allow utilities to evaluate each connection, prescribe required investments, or refuse connections above the net-metering threshold unless the customer made specified investments. The official initially assessed the system-loss impact as minimal because exported energy would be consumed near the point of generation.

thread.speaker: Agency official
thread.said: An agency official said DOE and ERC would work on reformatting the bill parameters while maintaining the substance of the answer.

thread.speaker: ERC official
thread.said: The ERC official said ERC had requested reinstatement of more than 700,000,000 in unreleased proposed budget authority and, at minimum, sought around 200,000,000 plus for consulting services and related maintenance and other operating expenses. The funding was needed to complete distribution-utility rate resets in 2027 and support more efficient operations and lower system losses.

thread.speaker: Chair
thread.said: The chair stated that the ERC request was approved.

thread.speaker: NEA Administrator Daniel Mehta
thread.said: Mehta said NEA had requested 7 or 10,000,000,000 to cushion electric cooperatives against the effects of eliminating nontechnical system losses.

thread.speaker: NEA Administrator Daniel Mehta
thread.said: Mehta said electric cooperatives would be affected because NEA's mandate to extend lines to unserved and unviable CTOs could increase technical losses. NEA was committed to eliminating nontechnical losses but could not make the same commitment for technical losses.

thread.speaker: NEA Administrator Daniel Mehta
thread.said: Mehta said the NEP granted NEA 55,000,000,000. 5,000,000,000, the same amount as the prior year, including photovoltaic mainstreaming. He said his principal concern was cushioning cooperatives from nontechnical-loss elimination because their cash-flow tariff system did not provide a source for repayment.

thread.speaker: Rep. Rufus Rodriguez
thread.said: Rodriguez said NEA's proposed CTO electrification amount was 11,200,000,000 but only 2.9 had been provided, leaving 8.2 for reconsideration, and asked Mehta to confirm.

thread.speaker: NEA Administrator Daniel Mehta
thread.said: Mehta confirmed Rodriguez's figures.

thread.speaker: Chair
thread.said: The chair stated that the reconsideration request was approved.

thread.speaker: Rep. Edgar Erice
thread.said: Erice asked what figures and policy inputs supported the decision to eliminate technical and nontechnical system losses.

thread.speaker: DOE Sharon Garin
thread.said: Garrin said DOE had submitted documents and recommendations, but the final prioritization rested with the Office of the President. She said DOE understood the directive as requiring hard work toward eliminating both types of losses, subject to assessment and available resources.

thread.speaker: Rep. Edgar Erice
thread.said: Erice cited Metro Manila and Meralco's 5.6% system loss and asked whether they would comply with the reduction policy.

thread.speaker: DOE Sharon Garin
thread.said: Garrin said Meralco's nontechnical loss was 1% and was already among the lowest, but she could not yet commit to a final system-loss target for private utilities because guidelines were still being finalized.

thread.speaker: DOE Sharon Garin
thread.said: Garrin said DOE would not ask for additional budget for system-loss improvements and would find a way to fund cooperative improvements.

thread.speaker: DOE Sharon Garin
thread.said: Garrin said the target was to finish the system-loss work before the next SONA.

thread.speaker: A majority member
thread.said: A majority member asked ERC to review stranded costs arising when distribution utilities held excess contracted capacity after consumers adopted solar power.

thread.speaker: ERC official
thread.said: The official said ERC had advised distribution utilities to include carve-out provisions in power-supply agreements, renegotiate or unload excess contracted capacity to affiliates, or offer it through the reserve market.

thread.speaker: A majority member
thread.said: The member pressed ERC on whether stranded-cost charges would continue to burden consumers who could not install solar and urged consideration of the state's police power over contract protections.

thread.speaker: ERC official
thread.said: The official said post-2023 competitive-selection power-supply agreements already used a template with automatic carve-out provisions. ERC would study how to assist distribution utilities and their remaining captive customers with stranded capacities.

thread.speaker: A majority member
thread.said: The member asked whether nontechnical losses would be eliminated within one year while NEA continued extending lines to unserved areas that could increase technical losses.

thread.speaker: DOE Sharon Garin
thread.said: Garrin said DOE would review NEA's pending line-extension programs and simulate whether solar home systems would be preferable to extending lines to unserved and unviable areas, where extensions might add to technical losses.

topics.topic: ERC budget reduction, restoration, and regulatory capacity
topics.summary: The ERC chair presented a workload that included thousands of decisions and orders, rate resets after more than a decade, and system-loss regulation, while saying the FY 2027 allocation was below the commission's proposal. The ERC sought restoration of more than 700,000,000, or at least around 200,000,000 plus for consultants and related operating expenses. Secretary Sharon Garin and Rep. Rufus Rodriguez supported stronger ERC funding, with Rodriguez also referring to a 120,000,000 increase. NEA separately requested 7 or 10,000,000,000 to cushion electric cooperatives from nontechnical system-loss elimination. The committee chair asked for detailed justification and a prioritized list, and the ERC committed to submit a narrative explaining the consultancy requirement and its link to rate resets and system-loss reduction. No final restoration amount was adopted during the hearing; DBM-related special-provision questions were deferred for discussion before plenary.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish why the ERC's FY 2027 funding was reduced, how much additional funding was needed to sustain its regulatory workload, and whether the requested resources were tied to specific outputs such as rate resets and system-loss reduction. It also sought to determine what documentation the ERC would provide to support restoration or augmentation of its budget.
topics.agency_position: The ERC said its workload and regulatory responsibilities had expanded substantially, while its available FY 2027 funding was below its proposal. It sought restoration of more than 700,000,000, or at minimum around 200,000,000 plus for consultants and related operating expenses, to complete utility rate resets in 2027 and support system-loss reduction and eventual removal of system-loss charges.
topics.outcome: The committee expressed support for restoring or augmenting the ERC budget but did not record a final appropriation in the hearing. The ERC was required to submit detailed justifications and a prioritized list for review by the budget amendments review subcommittee, while the special-provision issue remained subject to consultation with DBM.

positions.position: Supported increasing or restoring the ERC budget and said the commission needed resources for its regulatory work.
Supported an increased ERC budget and additional regulatory capacity, while saying DOE itself was not requesting an increase.
Expressed full support for the DOE and ERC families and indicated that the committee would consider augmenting or restoring unfunded items, subject to fiscal space and supporting details.
Supported funding to cushion electric cooperatives from the effects of eliminating nontechnical system loss.

thread.speaker: ERC Chair Francis Juan
thread.said: The ERC said it regulated an electricity sector valued at around 4,190,000,000,000, while its proposed budget was 944,000,000.

thread.speaker: ERC Chair Francis Juan
thread.said: From January 2025 to June 2026, the ERC had issued 4611 decisions and orders, imposed 157,000,000 in fines, and directed refunds of around R71.3 billion.

thread.speaker: ERC Chair Francis Juan
thread.said: The ERC's GAA grew from 911,600,000 in 2024 to 931,000,000 in 2026, increases of roughly two percent and 0.04%. It proposed a 700,000,000 budget for 2027, but the net reflected the September or 44.67% below what it proposed; the wording and figure were unclear.

thread.speaker: ERC Chair Francis Juan
thread.said: The ERC said the variance was concentrated in maintenance and other operating expenses and capital outlay, including consultancy services intended to help complete rate resets for private distribution utilities and electric cooperatives and NGZP for 2027.

thread.speaker: ERC Chair Francis Juan
thread.said: ERC utilization rose from 28.08 in 2021 to 46.81 in June 2026; annual utilization was 84.2, up from 62% in 2023.

thread.speaker: ERC Chair Francis Juan
thread.said: With a budget of 931,000,000 in 2025, the ERC brought 354,000,000 in revenue to the government, or 121% above its projection.

thread.speaker: ERC Chair Francis Juan

thread.speaker: A committee member

thread.speaker: Secretary Sharon Garin

topics.topic: Electricity supply security, alerts, outages, and reserve capacity
topics.summary: The Chair and members examined whether the proposed DOE and ERC resources would prevent future alerts, outages, fuel shortages, and high-cost generation. DOE attributed the Visayas and Mindanao alerts to coinciding maintenance, defective coal-plant equipment, reduced hydropower and biomass output, and forced operation of remaining plants, while proposing up to 250 megawatts of Visayas battery storage and short-term deployment of about 200 to 300 megawatts. Members also questioned Iligan's reduced 8.75 megawatt firm allocation, DOE's 49% utilization rate, the excluded 29,000,000,000 emergency allotment, and the adequacy of government-controlled fuel reserves. DOE and PNOC described plans for a government-owned 1,000,000-barrel tank farm, while the reported national fuel inventory remained largely in private storage. ERC said it would address excess contracted capacity and review reserve-market pricing, but several allocation, outage, CBA, system-loss, and stranded-cost issues remained open. The committee requested written fuel and remittance reports and carried the matters forward for subsequent action.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish whether the proposed FY 2027 DOE and ERC resources would improve electricity supply security, reduce alerts and outages, secure fuel and reserves, and prevent consumers from bearing the cost of excess or unreliable generation. Members also asked what immediate and long-term measures would address constrained Visayas and Mindanao supply, plant outages, battery storage, firm-power allocations, and strategic petroleum reserves.
topics.agency_position: DOE and ERC maintained that the proposed programs would strengthen energy security through resource surveys, mobile energy systems, automation, battery storage, renewable integration, improved monitoring, and strategic fuel reserves. DOE attributed current alerts mainly to coinciding maintenance, defective equipment, reduced hydropower and biomass output, and forced operation of remaining plants, while ERC said market and contract mechanisms could mitigate congestion, excess capacity, and reserve-market costs.
topics.outcome: The committee received explanations and several forward commitments, but the underlying supply-security problems were not fully resolved. DOE and PNOC committed to written reports, battery deployment, plant monitoring, system-loss work, and development of government-controlled fuel storage; Iligan's added allocation, the CBA memorandum, stranded costs, and the full impact of outages remained subject to further action.

positions.position: Supported sustained energy-sector funding but demanded measurable preparedness targets for fuel reserves, reserve margins, transmission, storage, and consumer protection.
Accepted DOE's explanation that the budget increase supported energy-security projects, but pressed for resolution of the electric-cooperative CBA memorandum.
Sought additional firm or non-firm power for Iligan to address high electricity rates and supply instability, without requesting preferential treatment.
Pressed DOE and ERC for accountability regarding outages, line-rental charges, host-community remittances, and pending transmission claims.
Questioned whether DOE's budget and emergency resources were properly prioritized and sought consolidated accounting, fuel-marking data, and a genuinely government-controlled petroleum reserve.
Demanded explanations for repeated Visayas and Mindanao alerts and outages and sought immediate battery and fuel-supply measures.
Supported DOE funding but pressed for system-loss elimination, fiscal discipline, and reserves under government control rather than reliance on private storage.
Asked ERC to protect consumers from stranded costs caused by excess solar or contracted generation and supported reviewing contractual and reserve-market rules.

actions.action: DOE to submit host-community ER 194 remittance and audit records to the committee.
DOE to provide fuel-marking and import-versus-sales data after calculating the information.
PNOC to establish a first-phase 1,000,000-barrel tank farm and develop later phases of a strategic reserve.
DOE to submit a written report on emergency fuel stocks, including the five-day diesel supply, before the second round.
DOE to work toward eliminating technical and nontechnical system losses and prepare cooperative distribution plans, subject to further guidelines.
ERC to review assistance and contractual mechanisms for distribution utilities with stranded excess capacity and continue review of reserve-market pricing.

thread.speaker: the Chair
thread.said: The Chair framed the energy budget as preparation for national energy emergencies, citing grid alerts, fuel-price shocks, El Niño-related hydropower and peak-demand risks, and the need for measurable targets for reserves, grid margins, transmission, and storage.

thread.speaker: the Chair
thread.said: The Chair described the combined proposed energy-family budget as 56,100,000,000 and said it should support reliable, affordable, and secure energy.

thread.speaker: Youssef Bacordo, DOE undersecretary
thread.said: DOE reported that the country maintained an average available fuel supply of fifty days and had restored 24/7 electricity in Siquijor while addressing prolonged interruptions in Catanduanes.

thread.speaker: Youssef Bacordo, DOE undersecretary
thread.said: DOE said Task Force 200 was monitoring and facilitating 200 committed power projects; 48 were completed and commercially operational, adding 1,846.63 megawatts, including 12 battery energy storage projects totaling 229.37 megawatts.

thread.speaker: Youssef Bacordo, DOE undersecretary
thread.said: DOE projected 2027 revenues of 23,000,000,000 and proposed a total 2027 budget of 5,580,000,000, an increase of 1,140,000,000 or 25.74% over the FY 2026 GAA of PHP 4,430,000,000.

thread.speaker: Youssef Bacordo, DOE undersecretary
thread.said: DOE said it was proposing 600,000,000 for 2027 mobile energy systems, supporting at least 60 additional units, and 950,000,000 for ISSP, including 491,000,000 for automation.

thread.speaker: Youssef Bacordo, DOE undersecretary
thread.said: DOE identified a state-owned strategic petroleum reserve, Visayas, Mindoro, and Palawan energy master plans, generation-company accountability policies, and review of system-loss programs as energy-security priorities.

thread.speaker: Rep. Perci Cendaña
thread.said: Cendaña asked why DOE's budget was increasing by more than 25% and whether the proposed increase was justified.

thread.speaker: Sharon Garrin, DOE secretary
thread.said: Garrin attributed the increase primarily to the gray geometry resource survey, mobile energy systems for emergency deployment, and DOE automation, saying these were needed for energy security and faster, more transparent decisions.

thread.speaker: Sharon Garrin, DOE secretary
thread.said: Garrin said indigenous oil and gas, renewable energy, and better coordination between policy and regulation were intended to lower electricity prices.

thread.speaker: a DOE agency official
thread.said: The official said the electric-cooperative CBA memorandum was suspended while DOLE, the National Labor Relations Board, NEA, and labor groups developed rules through a tripartite council.

thread.speaker: Rep. Perci Cendaña
thread.said: Cendaña pressed whether the memorandum would be rescinded, noting that the answer was substantially the same as the previous year.

thread.speaker: a DOE agency official
thread.said: The official said the memorandum would eventually be rescinded if the tripartite council produced a resolution, but it remained suspended pending that process.

thread.speaker: Rep. Celso Regencia
thread.said: Regencia cited Iligan's reported increase from 13.6 per kilowatt hour to MXN 15.13 per kilowatt hour and asked why its firm allocation had been reduced to 8.75 megawatt and whether an additional 16.25 megawatt could restore the allocation to 25 megawatt.

thread.speaker: a power-sector official
thread.said: The official said allocations were reduced because the dependable capacity of Agus and Pulangi had declined. PISAM and its trading team would evaluate Iligan Light and Power's request and try to provide additional firm or non-firm allocation.

thread.speaker: Rep. Presley de Jesus
thread.said: De Jesus asked which plants were causing yellow and red alerts and how many megawatts they could deliver.

thread.speaker: the Chair
thread.said: The Chair said each TVI unit was one seventy six, with outages reducing available supply and contributing to yellow and red alerts. The exact unit and megawatt wording was unclear.

thread.speaker: Rep. Presley de Jesus
thread.said: De Jesus asked why line-rental calculations and collections had been suspended during congestion between the Visayas and Mindanao.

thread.speaker: the Chair
thread.said: The Chair said the suspension was requested because congestion caused line-rental spikes. ERC also sought recalculation and third-party auditing of payments and surplus allocations from 2021 to determine whether refunds were due.

thread.speaker: Rufus Rodriguez, DOE official
thread.said: Rodriguez reported that, as of 06/20/2026, DOE had remitted 1,800,000,000 for Northern Luzon host-community benefits, including 762,000,000 for electrification, 524,000,000 for a development fund, and 526,000,000 for watershed and rural health.

thread.speaker: the Chair
thread.said: The Chair requested that DOE submit the host-community remittance records to the committee.

thread.speaker: a DOE agency official
thread.said: DOE said it had roughly 160,000 pending right-of-way claims and planned to reduce them by 50,000 within two years through nationwide outsourced settlement, with a target of clearing the claims by 2034.

thread.speaker: Rep. Presley de Jesus
thread.said: De Jesus asked for the total peso cost of the pending right-of-way claims.

thread.speaker: a DOE agency official
thread.said: The official estimated the total cost at 220,000,000,000, based on a 2016 zonal valuation, while noting that public and unregistered land would not be paid.

thread.speaker: Rep. Jan Rurik Padiernos
thread.said: Padiernos questioned DOE's budget utilization because its presentation excluded a separate 29,860,000,000 emergency allotment, and asked how the committee could evaluate all regular, automatic, continuing, emergency, and Malampaya-funded resources together.

thread.speaker: Sharon Garrin, DOE secretary
thread.said: Garrin reported 49% utilization as of August 31, expected 68.31% after mobile-energy-system and automation procurement, and projected at least 95.89% utilization by the end of 2026.

thread.speaker: Sharon Garrin, DOE secretary
thread.said: Garrin clarified that the additional 29,000,000,000 had been transferred to PNOC for the fuel emergency, including LPG, diesel, and gas-related activities, and would be separately liquidated after the emergency was lifted.

thread.speaker: Rep. Jan Rurik Padiernos
thread.said: Padiernos asked why resource surveys, mobile energy systems, and automation—totaling about 2,910,000,000—were prioritized while about 1,530,000 households remained without electricity.

thread.speaker: Sharon Garrin, DOE secretary
thread.said: Garrin said the projects would improve energy security, while NEA remained the principal agency for nationwide electrification. DOE's 500,000,000 allocation would support mobile systems deployed to islands and emergency locations.

thread.speaker: a DOE agency official
thread.said: Regarding a proposed 3 to 5 gigawatts of demand from Paxilica, DOE said it was coordinating with the group and BCDA on timing, had more than 100 gigawatts of awarded renewable-energy service contracts, and considered the demand manageable without competing with ordinary consumers.

thread.speaker: Rep. Jan Rurik Padiernos
thread.said: Padiernos asked whether DOE could estimate remaining illicit fuel entering the market and identify the percentage of petroleum sold that was legitimate tax-paid fuel.

thread.speaker: Sharon Garrin, DOE secretary
thread.said: Garrin said DOE did not have the requested calculation immediately, but could compare imports and sales and provide data, with automation and data-sharing agreements with Customs and the BIR intended to improve detection.

thread.speaker: Rep. Jan Rurik Padiernos
thread.said: Padiernos asked how much of the reported forty nine days of diesel inventory was government-owned or controlled and where PNOC would store it.

thread.speaker: a DOE agency official
thread.said: The official said government normally did not buy stocks; during the emergency it held diesel stock and less than a day of gasoline stock in private storage. A strategic reserve was being developed while the government defined its role relative to private enterprise.

thread.speaker: a PNOC official
thread.said: PNOC said its priority for the following year was a tank farm, with phase one establishing 1,000,000 barrels and a later phase reaching 15,000,000.

thread.speaker: a PNOC official
thread.said: PNOC said the first 1,000,000-barrel phase would be government-owned, with later phases potentially involving private partnerships or joint ventures.

thread.speaker: Rep. Tino
thread.said: Tino asked about repeated yellow and red alerts, extended plant maintenance, generator outages, and possible penalties for plants that failed to supply.

thread.speaker: Yousef Marasigan, DOE official
thread.said: Marasigan attributed Visayas shortages to planned maintenance, reduced hydropower and biomass output, and two major coal-unit failures caused by a turbine-rotor manufacturing defect. Mindanao had been supplying up to 450 megawatts to the Visayas, while Luzon was assisting with 250 megawatts, but further Mindanao outages reduced the transfer nearly to zero.

thread.speaker: Yousef Marasigan, DOE official
thread.said: DOE said it was assessing generation-facility compliance under a department circular; penalties would be imposed by ERC. It had identified up to 250 megawatts of battery energy storage for Visayas ancillary services, with 150 megawatts already in place and undergoing testing.

thread.speaker: a DOE official
thread.said: DOE said new coal plants would take at least three years and gas plants five years, making integrated solar and battery systems the fastest short-term response. It described 200 to 300 megawatts of batteries as the short-term solution, with barges or diesel generation as a possible mid-term measure and new plants targeted from 2028 onward.

thread.speaker: Rep. Tino
thread.said: Tino asked whether the batteries would be solar-charged and how they would operate.

thread.speaker: Yousef Marasigan, DOE official
thread.said: Marasigan said the batteries would draw on excess generation, including renewable generation during peak renewable-output periods, and provide ancillary services. DOE noted that Visayas renewable energy was about 45% of the mix, compared with 25% nationally.

thread.speaker: Rep. Tino
thread.said: Tino requested a written report on the status and volume of the emergency fuel supply before the second round.

thread.speaker: an agency official
thread.said: The official described the emergency supply as 300,000 barrels, or one point something billion liters, equivalent to about five days of national diesel supply, with some stocks retained in PNOC and some in private storage.

thread.speaker: the Committee
thread.said: The agency said it could submit the requested fuel report by that day, for consideration in the second round.

thread.speaker: Sharon Garrin, DOE secretary
thread.said: Garrin said DOE had formulated a fuel-transition plan to reduce dependence on imported fuel, including electric vehicles, exploration, appliance electrification, and domestic reserves. She said the country was 99% dependent on imported fuel and targeted 50% by 2040.

thread.speaker: Sharon Garrin, DOE secretary
thread.said: Garrin said current reported fuel reserves were held in private facilities and that PNOC was working toward a government-owned 1,000,000-barrel storage facility.

thread.speaker: a PNOC official
thread.said: The official estimated total storage at about 2,700,000,000 liters, but clarified that the figure included private owners.

thread.speaker: an ERC official
thread.said: ERC said distribution utilities could use carve-out provisions, renegotiate excess contracted capacity, transfer it to an affiliate, or offer it in the reserve market to avoid stranded costs from excess solar or other contracted power.

thread.speaker: an ERC official
thread.said: ERC said power-supply agreements entered after the DOE competitive-selection policy and the 2023 rules already used a template with automatic carve-out provisions, and it would examine assistance for distribution utilities and captive customers with remaining excess capacity.

thread.speaker: an ERC official
thread.said: ERC said it was reviewing reserve-market pricing after public consultation and hoped to approve an offer below the existing reserve-market price of 25 pesos per kilowatt hour.

topics.topic: Strategic petroleum reserve, fuel storage, and emergency fuel allotments
topics.summary: The Chair framed the energy budget as requiring permanent preparedness after DOE secured more than 178 million liters of diesel for an emergency buffer. Rep. Jan Rurik Padiernos questioned DOE's separate emergency allotment of 29,860,000,000 and asked how much fuel the government actually controlled. DOE said an additional 29,000,000,000 had been passed to PNOC and would be separately liquidated after the emergency, but it did not provide a clear government-controlled days-of-supply figure. DOE undertook to provide data comparing fuel imports and sales to help assess illicit fuel and fuel-marking gaps. PNOC said it would begin with a 1,000,000-barrel tank farm and later expand it, while Sharon Garin said construction could be completed in a year and a half and would require about 8,000,000,000. Members supported the need for a strategic reserve, but the final government-controlled capacity and the inconsistent later-phase figures were left open.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish whether the Philippines had a government-controlled strategic petroleum reserve, how much emergency fuel was under government control, where fuel was stored, and how the reserve would be financed and expanded. Members also asked how DOE measured illicit fuel, whether private commercial storage was sufficient, and what documents or infrastructure commitments would follow.
topics.agency_position: DOE said the emergency fuel allotment was being retained and would be liquidated separately after the emergency ended. It supported a permanent, government-owned strategic petroleum reserve through PNOC, beginning with a 1,000,000-barrel tank farm and expanding through later phases, while acknowledging that current national storage figures largely reflected private commercial facilities. DOE also said it would provide import-versus-sales and fuel-marking data and use cross-agency data analysis to address illicit-fuel gaps.
topics.outcome: The agency committed to developing a PNOC-owned strategic reserve, beginning with a 1,000,000-barrel facility and scaling up, but did not provide a final figure for government-controlled days of supply. DOE also undertook to submit fuel-marking and import-versus-sales data; the extent of government control, the later-phase reserve size, and the financing details remained partly unresolved.

positions.position: The energy sector should receive sustained, measurable support, with the emergency response converted into funded and operational strategic fuel-reserve and storage capabilities.

DOE should account for emergency resources separately and transparently, determine how much fuel is under government control, and establish a genuine government-owned reserve rather than relying only on emergency purchases or private storage. He nevertheless manifested support for the DOE budget and additional consumer-protection funding.
The country should maintain a diesel reserve and develop storage under government control so it is less exposed to foreign supply disruptions and private-company dependence.
DOE should clarify foreign-linked fuel-storage projects and ensure that the Philippines' finite storage capacity and permitting authority are properly addressed.

thread.speaker: Chair
thread.said: The Chair said DOE had secured more than 178,000,000 liters of diesel to build an emergency fuel buffer and argued that the temporary response should become a permanent, rules-based preparedness mechanism.

thread.speaker: Chair
thread.said: The Chair noted that a strategic petroleum preserve had been established in policy since 2021 and supported by a completed study in 2022, but was not fully operational when the energy shock occurred.

thread.speaker: Chair
thread.said: The Chair said the combined proposed budget of the energy family was 56,100,000,000 and should specify targets for strategic fuel reserves, emergency procurement lead times, and storage completion.

thread.speaker: Rep. Jan Rurik Padiernos
thread.said: Padiernos asked how Congress could evaluate DOE without consolidated accounting of its regular, automatic, continuing, emergency, and Malampaya-funded resources, noting that the utilization presentation excluded a separate 29,860,000,000 emergency allotment.

thread.speaker: Rep. Jan Rurik Padiernos
thread.said: Padiernos followed up on the emergency allotment and its treatment in DOE's accounts.

thread.speaker: DOE official
thread.said: The DOE official said there was an additional 29.9, described also as 29,000,000,000, which had been given to DOE and passed to PNOC in response to the fuel emergency. The funds were allocated through PNOC entities for LPG, diesel, and gas, and DOE had decided not to release too much of the reserve while the emergency continued.

thread.speaker: DOE official
thread.said: The official said the emergency funds would require a separate liquidation, to be undertaken once the emergency was lifted.

thread.speaker: Rep. Jan Rurik Padiernos
thread.said: Padiernos asked whether DOE could estimate the amount of smuggled or illicit fuel entering the Philippine market annually and how it measured the effectiveness of the fuel-marking program. He cited 21,102,000,000 liters marked, 247,000,000,000 in taxes generated, about 674,520 liters of illicit fuel worth 22,440,000,000 in Bataan, and 39,146 liters of noncompliant fuel.

thread.speaker: DOE official
thread.said: DOE said smuggling was primarily a matter for DOF, Customs, and the BIR, while fuel marking monitored whether taxes had been paid rather than whether fuel had a DOE permit. DOE could compare imports against sales, but did not have the calculation available at the hearing and said it could provide the data later.

thread.speaker: DOE official
thread.said: The agency said it would provide the committee with data on the import-versus-sales comparison and was working with Customs and the BIR on data-sharing, automation, artificial intelligence, and stricter cross-referencing to identify anomalies.

thread.speaker: Rep. Jan Rurik Padiernos
thread.said: Padiernos asked how many of the reported 49 days of diesel inventory were actually owned or controlled by the government and where PNOC would physically store the reserve.

thread.speaker: DOE official
thread.said: The official said the government did not normally buy stock, although it had done so during the emergency. The response referred to diesel stock and less than a day of gasoline stock held in a private storage facility; the exact diesel figure in the transcript is unclear.

thread.speaker: DOE official
thread.said: DOE said Congress was examining a strategic petroleum reserve because of the importance of a government role, but that the role had to be defined without intruding excessively into private enterprise. The reserve's location and allocation would need to be planned strategically.

thread.speaker: DOE official
thread.said: The agency said PNOC was already working on establishing government-owned tanks and that the project was a priority for the following year.

thread.speaker: PNOC official
thread.said: PNOC said Phase One would establish a tank farm worth 1,000,000 barrels in the following year, with a later phase reaching 15,000,000; the transcript does not specify the unit for the latter figure.

thread.speaker: Rep. Jan Rurik Padiernos
thread.said: Padiernos asked whether the plan was a genuinely government-owned strategic petroleum reserve or merely emergency fuel purchases whenever a crisis occurred.

thread.speaker: PNOC official
thread.said: PNOC said the first 1,000,000-barrel phase would be owned by PNOC, while subsequent phases could involve private companies through partnerships or joint ventures.

thread.speaker: Rep. Jan Rurik Padiernos
thread.said: Padiernos manifested full support for the DOE proposed budget and for any additional budget that would help consumers.

thread.speaker: Rep. Edgar Erice
thread.said: Erice asked about maintaining a diesel reserve or capacity reserve to protect the country from future Middle East-related supply and price shocks.

thread.speaker: Sharon Garin
thread.said: Secretary Garrin said DOE had formulated a fuel transition plan because the country was 100% dependent on imported fuel, later qualified as 99%. She said the plan targeted 50% by 2040 through electric vehicles, additional exploration, and appliance electrification, while also recognizing the need for domestic reserves.

thread.speaker: Sharon Garin
thread.said: Garrin said PNOC, headed by President Chicoi Alvarez, was setting up a government-owned storage facility and hoped to establish 1,000,000,000 barrels, described in the same passage as enough for 1,000,000 barrels of storage, within the term. The transcript's barrel figures are internally inconsistent.

thread.speaker: Sharon Garin
thread.said: Garrin cited 47 days of storage capacity, apparently referring to total public and private capacity.

thread.speaker: PNOC official
thread.said: The PNOC official estimated that the 47-day capacity corresponded to about 2,700,000,000 liters.

thread.speaker: PNOC official
thread.said: PNOC clarified that the quoted figure referred to total country volume and regional storage, rather than an exclusively government-owned reserve.

thread.speaker: Rep. Edgar Erice
thread.said: Erice asked for a target for storage under exclusive Philippine government control, separate from private-company storage, and pressed whether the government would remain dependent on private facilities.

thread.speaker: PNOC official
thread.said: PNOC said planning was under way for a strategic reserve with regional distribution and specified proportions of crude oil, diesel, and gasoline. The official did not provide a final government-control target.

thread.speaker: PNOC official
thread.said: The official referred to five days of private storage; the precise relationship of this figure to the broader reserve discussion was not fully explained.

thread.speaker: Rep. Tino
thread.said: Tino expanded his questions on foreign energy programs to fuel storage and noted that PNOC's fuel was stored in commercial facilities.

thread.speaker: Rep. Tino
thread.said: Tino asked DOE to clarify the fuel-storage information and provide the committee with details regarding the facilities and related foreign programs.

thread.speaker: Rep. Tino
thread.said: Tino asked about a reported 1,000,000-barrel fuel storage facility or depot associated with the United States and whether DOE would be involved or whether it would be purely commercial.

thread.speaker: Sharon Garin
thread.said: Garrin said DOE had not been officially informed about the reported facility. She added that any energy or fuel project would have to go through DOE for permits.

thread.speaker: Sharon Garin
thread.said: Garrin said DOE was pushing for its own strategic reserve and infrastructure through PNOC, with construction hopefully completed in a year and a half. The project would start at 1,000,000 barrels and be scaled up; PNOC would need about 8,000,000,000 and would use corporate funds.

topics.topic: Total electrification and off-grid solar, batteries, and fuel support
topics.summary: DOE presented Mobile Energy Systems and a proposed 2027 allocation of about 600 million for at least 60 units, while members questioned whether much larger resources were needed to close the remaining electrification gap. Rep. Nassal was told that total electrification required roughly 8 to 10 billion annually, compared with receipts of about 2 to 3 billion, although parts of the household and timeline figures were garbled. Rep. Stephen Tan raised an approved but unfunded off-grid solar project, fuel shortages, pole relocation, submarine-cable resilience and solar-plant fees; DOE and NEA undertook follow-up actions. Rep. Jan Chan pressed for targeting high-poverty and geographically isolated areas, while DOE and NEA said Mindanao and disadvantaged areas were priorities but did not provide exact regional allocations. The chair approved reconsideration of additional CTO-electrification funding after NEA confirmed the figures cited for its proposal and grant. A minority member also proposed a 200 million solar-and-battery alternative to line extensions, receiving agreement in principle but no recorded implementation details.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish how the proposed budget would accelerate total electrification, particularly in off-grid, geographically isolated and high-poverty areas, and whether solar-battery systems could substitute for costly line extensions. Members also asked what funding, fuel support, infrastructure and policy changes DOE, NEA and related agencies would provide.
topics.agency_position: DOE and NEA supported accelerating total electrification through the Total Electrification Program, Mobile Energy Systems, photovoltaic mainstreaming, solar-home systems and solar-plus-battery projects, while recognizing that funding remained insufficient. The agencies favored targeted deployment in Mindanao, geographically isolated and disadvantaged areas, and high-poverty communities, but several site-specific funding, fuel, fee-waiver and infrastructure questions required follow-up.
topics.outcome: The hearing produced commitments to follow up on specific off-grid solar, fuel, pole-relocation, submarine-cable and transmission concerns, and the chair approved reconsideration of additional CTO-electrification funding for Mindanao. The broader funding requirement, exact number and cost of remaining CTOs and households, poverty-targeted allocations, and the proposed 200,000,000 solar-battery provision were not fully resolved in the transcript.

positions.position: Supported expressly authorizing DOE to access legally earmarked special-fund revenues, provided DOE clearly identified lawful programs, and supported increasing resources for total electrification.

Pressed for funding of approved off-grid solar, adequate fuel allocation for islands, pole-relocation assistance, resilient submarine connections, fee relief for a donor-supported solar plant and faster Visayas transmission development.

Called for electrification resources to be targeted to regions with high absolute poverty and poverty incidence, and sought continued support for offshore-wind development and related port and grid infrastructure.
Supported reconsideration of the gap between NEA's CTO-electrification request and the amount in the NEP, particularly for Mindanao, and approved the reconsideration during the hearing.
Advocated changing the CSP and electrification framework to allow solar panels and battery storage, after technical and economic evaluation, instead of extending lines to some rural areas.
