actions.action: DOE and NEA would discuss the approved off-grid solar design with Rep. Tan and follow through on possible 2027 funding.
Rep. Tan would submit a letter identifying the island with insufficient fuel allocation.
NEA would coordinate with the relevant officials on pole-relocation advances and prioritize the affected lane expansions.
DOE and NEA would conduct a cost-benefit analysis of a submarine cable or another technology for the island connection.
NEA would check the status and possible waiver of fees for the donor-supported solar plant.
DOE would complete further Visayas energy-master-plan simulations and present the solution, with October mentioned as the expected timing.
DOE would issue a final energy mix after another simulation at the end of the year.
The committee approved reconsideration of the gap between NEA's CTO-electrification proposal and the amount granted in the NEP.
The committee and agency representatives manifested agreement to consider solar panels and battery storage instead of line extensions where technically and economically appropriate.
An agency report was requested on the DOE/PNOC diesel purchase for NAPOCOR during the energy-price crisis.

thread.speaker: DOE undersecretary Youssef Bacordo
thread.said: DOE reported that household electrification had reached 94.93% as of December 2025, with around 28,750,000 households energized out of 30,280,000 potential households.

thread.speaker: DOE undersecretary Youssef Bacordo
thread.said: DOE said its Total Electrification Project was procuring Mobile Energy Systems that would provide renewable, rapidly deployable and modular electricity solutions for disaster response and electrification.

thread.speaker: DOE undersecretary Youssef Bacordo
thread.said: For 2026, DOE was using 500,000,000 from current appropriations and 21,000,000 from continuing appropriations. For 2027, it proposed 600,000,000 for at least 60 additional Mobile Energy System units.

thread.speaker: DOE undersecretary Youssef Bacordo
thread.said: DOE said it was conducting green-energy auctions covering off-grid areas and planned programs involving solar and other renewable technologies.

thread.speaker: Rep. Robert Nassal
thread.said: Nassal asked whether expressly placing the 20% authority in the 2027 special provision was intended to ensure DOE could access funds already earmarked by law. He cited 2025 and 2026 appropriations from the same fund.

thread.speaker: DOE secretary Sharon Garrin
thread.said: The secretary said the 20% share could be based on about 10,000,000,000 in the current year and potentially triple that the following year because of a new discovery. She said DOE was not the only recipient because the calculation also covered GOCCs, but DOE would appreciate fuller access and would make do with what it received.

thread.speaker: Rep. Robert Nassal
thread.said: Nassal asked how much DOE expected to receive under the 20% authority and what specific programs, projects and expenses would be funded.

thread.speaker: DOE secretary Sharon Garrin
thread.said: The secretary identified possible uses including regional offices, green buildings, automation, grid-management work, assistance to ERC, and energy research and development. She said DOE had many programs in place but usually received about 1,000,000,000.

thread.speaker: DOE secretary Sharon Garrin
thread.said: The secretary projected Malampaya collections alone could reach 27,000,000,000 in 2027 and said 20% would be 5,400,000,000.

thread.speaker: Rep. Robert Nassal
thread.said: Nassal asked whether improved access to earmarked funds could be used to accelerate total electrification, including the number of CTOs and households still without electricity as of 08/31/2026 and the cost of electrifying them.

thread.speaker: DOE secretary Sharon Garrin
thread.said: DOE said it had a Total Electrification Program apart from the NEA budget, with about 500,000,000 available, and asked that the impact of increasing it to about 2,000,000,000 be considered.

thread.speaker: agency official
thread.said: The official stated that the current total-electrification budget was 500,000,000 per year and that more than 2,000,000 households remained to be addressed. The remainder of the answer was garbled but referred to annual requirements and a completion timeline.

thread.speaker: agency official
thread.said: The official said the government needed 8 to 10,000,000,000 a year, but received only about 2,000,000,000 to 3,000,000,000 per year.

thread.speaker: Rep. Stephen James Tan
thread.said: Tan asked whether an off-grid solar plant whose technical design had reportedly been approved, but which was awaiting funding, would be included in the 2027 budget.

thread.speaker: NEA administrator
thread.said: The NEA administrator said the project appeared to fall under Total Electrification Project funding and that the site would be checked for photovoltaic mainstreaming or solar-home-system deployment. DOE and NEA undertook to discuss the matter with Tan and follow through on the funding.

thread.speaker: Rep. Stephen James Tan
thread.said: Tan raised an island in his district that could provide 24-hour service but lacked sufficient fuel allocation, and asked that the problem be resolved in the coming budget cycle.

thread.speaker: DOE official
thread.said: DOE asked for the island's name and said the matter could be checked, particularly if it was a SPUG area. The official also suggested redesigning the system to reduce dependence on diesel.

thread.speaker: NEA administrator
thread.said: The NEA administrator said he would meet with the relevant secretary on pole relocation and had requested at least 300,000,000 to cover electric-cooperative advances. He said 2026 DPWH allocation was 50,000,000 and promised to place the lane-expansion relocations high on the list.

thread.speaker: Rep. Stephen James Tan
thread.said: Tan asked whether an island approximately 1.5 kilometers from the mainland could be connected through a submarine cable rather than overhead poles to improve resilience during typhoons.

thread.speaker: DOE official
thread.said: DOE said a submarine cable was possible but required a cost-benefit analysis. If it was not viable, another technology would be considered, and the agency would discuss the matter with Tan's team.

thread.speaker: Rep. Stephen James Tan
thread.said: Tan asked whether fees of roughly 100,000 a month could be waived for a solar project in SAMELCO I that had received roughly 60,000,000 in European Union assistance.

thread.speaker: NEA administrator
thread.said: NEA said it would check the status of the charges. The administrator noted that collections or spending might be needed to cover operation and maintenance of the solar plant.

thread.speaker: Rep. Stephen James Tan
thread.said: Tan asked about upgrading the Luzon-Visayas transmission line to avoid power shedding in Regions 8 and 6, noting that the plan reportedly placed the upgrade in 2032.

thread.speaker: DOE secretary Sharon Garrin
thread.said: DOE said it was developing a Visayas energy master plan after completing work for Mindoro and Palawan. The agency said each major island might need to become more independent in its energy supply rather than relying continually on inter-island connections, and promised to present the plan after another month of simulation.

thread.speaker: NAPOCOR president Coco Nograles
thread.said: Nograles said the island had sufficient generators but was operating for eight hours. NAPOCOR committed to study the economics of increasing service; current peak demand was 108 kilowatts.

thread.speaker: Rep. Jan Franz Chan
thread.said: Chan asked how NEA would apply the proposed poverty-targeting provision in the 2027 rollout and how many CTO energization projects would be located in regions with the highest poverty counts, including Bicol.

thread.speaker: DOE official
thread.said: DOE said it had directed NEA to prioritize Mindanao, while the NEA administrator would provide further information on Bicol.

thread.speaker: NEA administrator
thread.said: NEA said its direction covered geographically isolated and disadvantaged areas and that most SEP funding had been dedicated to Mindanao. It mentioned Region 5 and areas including Albay, but did not provide exact regional figures.

thread.speaker: DOE secretary Sharon Garrin
thread.said: DOE said it was revising guidelines to increase host-community benefits from one centavo per kilowatt to three centavos per kilowatt and to give the host cooperative a right of first refusal in the competitive selection process.

thread.speaker: Rep. Jan Franz Chan
thread.said: Chan asked whether the administration still supported a Philippine energy-plan target of 21 gigawatts of offshore wind by 2040, supplying about 21% of electricity, and what budget support was needed for ports and grid preparation.

thread.speaker: DOE secretary Sharon Garrin
thread.said: The secretary could not confirm the percentage target but said DOE continued to push offshore wind and was conducting another energy-mix simulation. She said a final mix would be issued at the end of the year and would still include offshore wind.

thread.speaker: DOE official
thread.said: An agency official said the offshore-wind green-energy auction was ongoing for 3,300 megawatts.

thread.speaker: NEA administrator Daniel Mehta
thread.said: Mehta said line extensions to unserved and unviable CTOs could increase technical system losses, but the energy family was working to contain and eventually eliminate nontechnical system losses.

thread.speaker: DOE secretary Sharon Garrin
thread.said: DOE said it was scheduling a Mindanao green-energy auction combining solar with batteries and had directed NEA to prioritize Mindanao energization. DOE said additional available resources should also support Mindanao and transmission improvements.

thread.speaker: NEA administrator Daniel Mehta
thread.said: Mehta said the NEP granted NEA 55,000,000,000, then corrected or clarified the figure as 5,000,000,000, the same amount as the prior year, including photovoltaic mainstreaming. He expressed concern that eliminating nontechnical system losses could financially strain electric cooperatives.

thread.speaker: Chair Rufus Rodriguez
thread.said: The chair stated that NEA had proposed 11,200,000,000 for CTO electrification but had been given 2.9, leaving 8.2 for reconsideration. The NEA administrator confirmed the figures, and the chair said the reconsideration was approved.

thread.speaker: minority member
thread.said: A minority member proposed that, after economic and technical evaluation, solar panels and battery storage be used instead of line extensions in rural areas served by electric cooperatives.

thread.speaker: minority member
thread.said: The member proposed 200,000,000 for the solar-and-battery alternative and asked that the special provision permit use of the technology for electrification.

thread.speaker: committee chair and agency officials
thread.said: The proposal to use new technology instead of line extensions was met with agreement during the hearing, although no detailed implementing language or allocation was recorded.

topics.topic: Transmission upgrades, congestion charges, and NGCP reliability
topics.summary: Members raised concerns that inadequate firm power, delayed transmission projects, congestion charges, and NGCP performance were contributing to high rates and reliability risks. PISAM said Iligan's allocation had fallen because Agus and Pulangui dependable capacity declined and committed to evaluate an increase from 8.75 megawatt toward the requested 25 megawatt. DOE and Transco cited planned or proposed connections for Catanduanes and Eastern Samar, a Visayas master plan, storage, and third-party construction, but several projects remained subject to funding and approvals. ERC said LLCC suspension applied only during congested trading intervals and committed to review disputed collections. Transco reported roughly 160,000 right-of-way claims and an estimated 220,000,000,000 settlement cost, with a target to settle 50,000 claims in two years and clear them by 2034. Members also obtained commitments for the PNPP1 feasibility study, NGCP performance and dividend records, and updates on Negros-Panay Line 2 and CNP approval.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish whether transmission constraints, congestion charges, delayed interconnections, and NGCP performance were contributing to reliability problems and higher electricity costs. Members also asked what DOE, ERC, Transco, NAPOCOR, and NEA would do, and what documents or project updates they would provide.
topics.agency_position: DOE and its attached agencies said that generation and transmission constraints were being addressed through project prioritization, third-party construction, island and Visayas master planning, storage, system-operations improvements, and coordination with NGCP. ERC maintained that LLCC suspension applied only during specified congested trading intervals and said it would review disputed collections. Several matters, including the Eastern Samar and Negros-Panay upgrades, remained subject to funding, approvals, NGCP implementation, or further study.
topics.outcome: The hearing produced multiple agency commitments to evaluate allocations, submit documents, study or accelerate transmission projects, review LLCC collections, and provide NGCP performance information. However, the major transmission projects and the LLCC dispute remained dependent on approvals, funding, NGCP implementation, or further review.

positions.position: Iligan should receive a fair and practical increase in firm or non-firm power allocation because it hosts major power assets and consumers faced high rates.
Congress should carefully scrutinize new private distribution franchises, particularly where a small-capital entrant could enter the area of a well-performing cooperative.
Catanduanes needed an emergency response to high diesel-based generation costs and a long-term transmission interconnection, potentially including a submarine cable.
Eastern Samar required urgent 69 kV and northern-line upgrades, and ERC needed to clarify and correct the continued collection of LLCC after suspension.
Off-grid solar, reliable fuel allocation, pole-relocation funding, resilient island connections, and faster Visayas transmission upgrades were needed to reduce outages and line-rental costs.
DOE and NEA should prioritize electrification and host-community benefits in high-poverty areas, while maintaining offshore wind as part of the country's long-term energy mix.
Congress should obtain accountability and performance information on NGCP, accelerate Negros-Panay and related transmission projects, and address the grid's capacity to absorb renewable energy.

thread.speaker: Rep. Celso Regencia
thread.said: He raised rising electricity costs and supply stability in Iligan City, stating that the local charge increased from 13.6 per kilowatt hour in July 2026 to MXN 15.13 per kilowatt hour in August, an increase of MXN 1.52 or 11.19%.

thread.speaker: Rep. Celso Regencia
thread.said: He said Iligan hosted Agus-Pulangui assets with combined dependable capacity of approximately 279 megawatt, but firm allocation to Iligan Light and Power had been reduced to 8.75 megawatt.

thread.speaker: Rep. Celso Regencia
thread.said: He asked why Iligan's firm allocation had been reduced to 8.75 megawatt and whether the assessment considered actual demand, supply needs, and consumer impact. He also asked whether an additional 16.25 megawatt could be provided, restoring the allocation to 25 megawatt as an interim measure.

thread.speaker: PISAM official
thread.said: The official said PISAM reevaluated its supply contracts in 2026 and reduced cooperative allocations because the dependable capacity of Agus and Pulangui had declined. Allocations were based on the actual capacity of the power plants.

thread.speaker: PISAM official
thread.said: The official committed that PISAM and its trading team would evaluate Iligan Light and Power's request and try to increase its firm, or if necessary non-firm, allocation.

thread.speaker: NEA administrator
thread.said: The administrator agreed that a congressional franchise was indispensable for an electric cooperative to operate and distribute power. Functioning cooperatives, except in extreme cases, should be supported in franchise renewal.

thread.speaker: Congressman DiCasson
thread.said: He asked whether the generation market and transmission sector were competitive or monopolistic. The agency answered that EPIRA was intended to make generation competitive, while transmission operated under the franchise of NGCP as a sole operator.

thread.speaker: DOE official
thread.said: The official said transmission was under a franchise granted to NGCP and that there was only one operator. Distribution utilities and electric cooperatives had exclusive franchises in their respective areas.

thread.speaker: Congressman DiCasson
thread.said: He asked whether DOE had a division or bureau that conducted feasibility studies on the entry of a new private distribution utility and its economic impact on a local area.

thread.speaker: Electric Power Industry Management Bureau official
thread.said: The official said the bureau monitored distribution utilities, including cooperatives, through distribution development plans and power supply procurement programs. It monitored private utilities but did not assess an incoming new franchise holder.

thread.speaker: Congressman DiCasson
thread.said: He asked whether a private distribution company with paid-up capital of only 5,000,000 would have to build its own lines, substations, and transformers or could interconnect with or acquire an existing cooperative's facilities.

thread.speaker: DOE Secretary Sharon
thread.said: The Secretary said DOE could not approve or reject a franchise because that power belonged to Congress. Once granted, the franchise holder would have responsibility to deliver the public utility service, including putting up required infrastructure.

thread.speaker: Congressman DiCasson
thread.said: He asked whether it was fair to allow an unproven private distribution company with 5,000,000 paid-up capital to enter the franchise area of a triple-A cooperative that was performing well.

thread.speaker: NEA administrator
thread.said: The administrator said NEA would defer to Congress on whether to grant a new franchise, but said the existing cooperative was performing well and should not be given up on. He cited improvement from more than 1,000,000,000 to 120,000,000 and its triple-A rating.

thread.speaker: Rep. Rufus Rodriguez
thread.said: He asked DOE to support an emergency arrangement or temporary subsidy for Catanduanes because diesel generation costs and fuel prices were driving electricity rates, while also pursuing a long-term supply solution through competitive selection.

thread.speaker: DOE official
thread.said: The official said DOE could not commit to a subsidy because it was not authorized to provide one. DOE would instead form a task force, assess the cooperative and diesel supply, work with NAPOCOR, and pursue a longer-term reduction in diesel dependence.

thread.speaker: Rep. Rufus Rodriguez
thread.said: He asked for a long-term transmission solution for Catanduanes, including the transmission development plan, an interconnection project, a submarine cable, regulatory approvals, engineering services, and right-of-way work.

thread.speaker: Transco/NGCP official
thread.said: The official confirmed that the Catanduanes connection was included in NGCP's transmission development plan and could be prioritized. Transco would begin system operations on the island, which was expected to improve reliability and possibly reduce costs.

thread.speaker: DOE Secretary Sharon
thread.said: The Secretary said DOE had issued a circular allowing third-party construction, subject to coordination with NGCP. Transco had identified three projects and would work with NGCP and DOE to advance them.

thread.speaker: Rep. Presley de Jesus
thread.said: He asked how many megawatts were unavailable from the affected power plants during the outage and alert period.

thread.speaker: Agency official
thread.said: The official said each unit of TVI was one seventy six, with the unit of measurement unclear in the transcript, and that the outage reduced available supply and contributed to yellow and red alerts.

thread.speaker: Rep. Presley de Jesus
thread.said: He asked why line rentals had been suspended during congestion and how the resulting allocations would be corrected.

thread.speaker: ERC official
thread.said: The official said that when the Visayas-Mindanao interconnection was congested and line rentals spiked, ERC asked the market operator to suspend calculation and collection and collect only necessary amounts from customers and generators. ERC also sought recalculation and a third-party audit of payments and NSS allocations from 2021 onward to determine whether refunds were needed.

thread.speaker: DOE official
thread.said: Based on audit and monitoring records as of 06/20/2026, the official said remittances for Northern Luzon totaled 1,800,000,000, including 762,000,000 for electrification, 524,000,000 for the development fund, and 526,000,000 for watershed and rural health.

thread.speaker: DOE official
thread.said: The official said National Capital Region benefits totaled 8,000,000, including 4.44500000, 2,000,000 for DLF, and almost 2,000,000 for water management. The transcript's first NCR figure is unclear.

thread.speaker: Committee chair
thread.said: The chair asked the agency to submit the host-community remittance and audit information to the committee, and the agency agreed.

thread.speaker: Transco official
thread.said: The official said there were roughly 160,000 pending right-of-way claims, largely because of difficulties settling compensation and court processes.

thread.speaker: Transco official
thread.said: The official said Transco would begin an outsourced nationwide right-of-way settlement program, targeting 50,000 claims in two years and aiming to clear all claims by 2034 before the NGCP concession agreement ends.

thread.speaker: Transco official
thread.said: The official estimated the total cost of settling the claims at 220,000,000,000, based on a 2016 zonal valuation, while noting that unregistered and public land would not be paid for.

thread.speaker: DOE official
thread.said: Responding to Rep. Marco Anko's question on the Transco-NGCP dispute, the official said DOE continued to respect the concession agreement and was implementing the arbitral ruling issued in February 2025.

thread.speaker: Rep. Marco Anko
thread.said: He requested that DOE and Transco submit a written explanation of the matters involving NGCP and Transco, with a copy furnished to him.

thread.speaker: DOE and Transco officials
thread.said: The officials agreed to comply with the committee's request for a written explanation.

thread.speaker: Rep. Marco Anko
thread.said: He requested DOE's feasibility study on PNPP Unit One, saying the study was needed for House Bill 8567 and policy decisions on PNPP1 and future nuclear plants. He also submitted a copy of the subpoena that had been prepared but not served.

thread.speaker: DOE official
thread.said: The official said the hard copy of the feasibility study would be submitted to the committee by Friday or Monday, subject to the agreement with KHNP.

thread.speaker: Rep. Marco Anko
thread.said: He objected that the committee might receive a different copy from Korea and insisted on the exact copy held by DOE.

thread.speaker: DOE official
thread.said: The official explained that a confidentiality agreement prohibited photocopying or transmitting DOE's existing copy because the study had been provided as a KHNP grant. The official agreed to compare the incoming copy with DOE's copy and certify it.

thread.speaker: Rep. Sheen Gonzales
thread.said: He asked for the status of the Eastern Samar 69 kV sub-transmission line project, which was intended to address brownouts and low voltage.

thread.speaker: DOE/Transco official
thread.said: The official said the technical and financial feasibility study was ready and the project was awaiting DBM downloading and approval by the Office of the President. The line was described as close to 200 kilometers.

thread.speaker: Rep. Sheen Gonzales
thread.said: He also asked about upgrading the northern area's 128 kV line, which served three or four municipalities experiencing low voltage.

thread.speaker: DOE/Transco official
thread.said: The official said the northern upgrade would be prioritized through an investment fund for sustainable capital expenditure. The Secretary also directed Transco to study the transmission lines and visit the area.

thread.speaker: Rep. Sheen Gonzales
thread.said: He asked why LLCC or line rental charges continued after the ERC's August 5, 2026 suspension, citing an August 25, 2026 letter from the Independent Electricity Market Operator.

thread.speaker: ERC Commissioner Jan Rurik Padiernos
thread.said: The Commissioner explained that ERC's August 13, 2026 order suspended line-rental imposition only during trading intervals when congestion existed in the major Visayas-Mindanao interconnection. Line rentals could still be imposed during other intervals, and ERC would examine the specific case with the market operator.

thread.speaker: ERC official
thread.said: The ERC committed to look into the matter and resolve the issue.

thread.speaker: Rep. Stephen James Tan
thread.said: He asked whether funding for an approved off-grid solar plant would be included in the FY 2027 budget.

thread.speaker: DOE and NEA officials
thread.said: The officials said they would discuss the project with the member, verify whether it was under TEP funding, and follow through on the funding.

thread.speaker: Rep. Stephen James Tan
thread.said: He raised inadequate fuel allocation for an island that could provide 24-hour power and said he would submit the island's name in a letter.

thread.speaker: DOE Secretary Sharon
thread.said: The Secretary said NAPOCOR could determine whether the island was a SPUG area and redesign the supply arrangement to reduce dependence on diesel.

thread.speaker: Rep. Stephen James Tan
thread.said: He said an electric cooperative had already spent about 13,000,000 since 2023 for pole removal and relocation caused by road widening.

thread.speaker: NEA administrator
thread.said: The administrator said NEA had requested at least 300,000,000 for cooperative pole-relocation advances, while 2026 DPWH allocation was 50,000,000.

thread.speaker: Rep. Stephen James Tan
thread.said: He asked whether a nearby island connection approximately 1.5 kilometers from the mainland could be converted to a submarine cable to improve resilience to typhoons.

thread.speaker: DOE Secretary Sharon
thread.said: The Secretary said a submarine cable was possible but required a cost-benefit analysis. DOE would check the option and consider another technology if the submarine cable was not economically viable.

thread.speaker: Rep. Stephen James Tan
thread.said: He said a European Union-donated solar project had received roughly 60,000,000 and asked whether monthly fees of roughly 100,000 could be waived.

thread.speaker: DOE and NEA officials
thread.said: DOE said NEA would check the status of the request. NEA said the fees might be needed for operation and maintenance but would examine how to address the request.

thread.speaker: Rep. Stephen James Tan
thread.said: He asked about the Luzon-Visayas transmission upgrade, citing power-shedding and high line-rental concerns in Regions 8 and 6. He said the planned upgrade was reportedly scheduled for 2032.

thread.speaker: DOE Secretary Sharon
thread.said: The Secretary said DOE was developing a Visayas master plan that would examine whether major islands should become more independent in meeting their energy needs rather than relying continuously on Luzon-Visayas-Mindanao interconnections. The initial major islands identified were Panay, Negros, Cebu, Bohol, Leyte, and Samar.

thread.speaker: DOE Secretary Sharon
thread.said: The Secretary said Panay had at one point paid about 3 pesos per line rental and said the Visayas master plan would be presented after further analysis, with the transcript indicating October.

thread.speaker: NAPOCOR President Coco Nograles
thread.said: He said the island had sufficient generators but was operating for only eight hours. NAPOCOR would study the economics of expanding service; current peak demand was 108 kilowatts.

thread.speaker: Rep. John Chan
thread.said: He asked how NEA would apply the proposed budget's poverty-prioritization provision and how many 2027 energization projects would be located in areas with the highest poverty counts. He cited 1,735,690 poor Filipinos and 279,220 poor families in Bicol.

thread.speaker: NEA administrator
thread.said: The administrator said funding was directed particularly to geographically isolated and disadvantaged areas, with the majority of the relevant funding dedicated to Mindanao. NEA was also working on allocations for Region 5, including Albay, but did not provide exact figures.

thread.speaker: NEA administrator
thread.said: The administrator said national electrification had increased from 75% to 89% in electric-cooperative franchise areas.

thread.speaker: Rep. John Chan
thread.said: He asked about the plan to increase ER 194 benefits from 1% to 3% for communities hosting geothermal plants, particularly in Region 5.

thread.speaker: DOE Secretary Sharon
thread.said: The Secretary clarified that the increase was from one centavo per kilowatt hour to three centavos, not from 1% to 3%. DOE had also loosened utilization rules and revised competitive-selection-process guidelines to give the host cooperative the right of first refusal.

thread.speaker: NEA administrator
thread.said: The administrator said NEA had begun aggregating the baseload requirements of Luzon and Visayas cooperatives to obtain economies of scale.

thread.speaker: Rep. John Chan
thread.said: He asked whether the Philippine Energy Plan target of 21 gigawatts of offshore wind by 2040, supplying about 21% of national electricity, remained the administration's working target.

thread.speaker: DOE Secretary Sharon
thread.said: The Secretary could not confirm the 21% figure but said DOE continued to push offshore wind. DOE was running another simulation and expected a final energy mix by the end of the year, with offshore wind still included.

thread.speaker: DOE official
thread.said: The official said the offshore-wind green energy auction was ongoing for 3,300 megawatts.

thread.speaker: DOE official
thread.said: The official said existing ports might support six to eight tons per square meter, while an offshore-wind port required about 30 tons per square meter. A Greenfield Port was targeted for completion in the fourth quarter of 2027 or first quarter of 2028.

thread.speaker: Javi Benitez
thread.said: He asked whether the failure to complete repairs on a known defect affecting a critical 500 kilowatt line and the resulting delay constituted a violation of NGCP's concession obligations, and whether DOE had referred the matter to ERC.

thread.speaker: ERC official
thread.said: The official said ERC would examine the incident, determine whether it affected NGCP's reliability performance, and act accordingly.

thread.speaker: Javi Benitez
thread.said: He asked about the status and funding of Negros-Panay transmission Line 2 and the final approval of the CNP line. He said the backbone had cost 68,000,000,000, carried only 90 megawatts, and faced renewable-energy curtailment risks.

thread.speaker: DOE/Transco official
thread.said: The official said the Granada KV substation line was a DOE priority and that DOE was working with NGCP to fast-track it. The CNP line was scheduled for 2027, and DOE would report back after its NGCP transmission-development-plan session the following week.

thread.speaker: DOE Secretary Sharon
thread.said: The Secretary said DOE was also pushing for 50 megawatts of batteries in Negros as an alternative means of storing power. She said NGCP reportedly had average annual dividends of 20,000,000,000, although she could not state its exact profit.

thread.speaker: DOE Secretary Sharon
thread.said: She said ERC had regulatory authority over NGCP performance, while DOE could issue policy. She suggested that Congress could review NGCP's performance through the relevant franchise and energy committees.

thread.speaker: DOE digitalization official
thread.said: The official said DOE was establishing a digital front door, consolidating regulatory data, and integrating with NEA, ERC, and other attached agencies. The 2026 budget for the infrastructure was 350,000,000, with a larger 2027 request to scale it up within a two-year deadline.

thread.speaker: Javi Benitez
thread.said: He requested a root-cause analysis of the May 13 line incident, a year-by-year table of NGCP dividends and construction spending, and updates on Line 2 and final CNP approval.

thread.speaker: DOE/Transco officials
thread.said: The officials committed to provide the requested materials within the week.

topics.topic: Electric-cooperative franchises, CBA obligations, and distribution competition
topics.summary: Rep. Perci Cendaña pressed NEA on the suspended electric-cooperative CBA memorandum and asked whether it would be rescinded. NEA said a tripartite technical working group was developing rules and that the memorandum could be rescinded after a September 10 meeting and subsequent resolutions, but Cendaña noted that the same answer had been given the previous year. Rep. DiCasson questioned franchise expirations in 2028 or 2029, the exclusivity of cooperative distribution areas, and the suitability of a private applicant with 5,000,000 in capital compared with a cooperative with about 1,500,000,000 in assets. NEA and DOE said Congress controlled franchise grants, while functioning cooperatives generally merited renewal and franchise holders had to provide the required infrastructure and service. Rep. Sergio Dagooc raised labor demands including grocery allowances of up to 6,000 pesos monthly and laundry allowances of 500 to 600 pesos monthly, which NEA said cooperatives could not afford. ERC said new system-loss rules could support consumers or cooperative infrastructure and committed to propose revisions and consult stakeholders, including Mindanao cooperatives.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish how the DOE, NEA, DOLE, and other agencies would resolve electric-cooperative collective-bargaining disputes and whether a memorandum affecting cooperative CBAs would be rescinded. It also examined the necessity of cooperative franchises, the possible entry of private distribution utilities, and whether revised system-loss rules could support cooperatives and consumers.
topics.agency_position: The agencies maintained that the CBA memorandum was suspended because electric cooperatives had industry-specific circumstances, but said it could be rescinded after the tripartite council adopted resolutions. They supported renewal of functioning cooperative franchises, deferred franchise-grant decisions to Congress, warned that excessive CBA benefits could undermine cooperative finances, and said revised system-loss rules could allow consumer subsidies or infrastructure support subject to stakeholder consultation.
topics.outcome: The CBA memorandum remained suspended, with possible rescission deferred until the tripartite council produced resolutions; Rep. Cendaña remained dissatisfied with the delay. The agencies supported functioning cooperatives and committed to consultation and possible revisions on system-loss rules, but the record did not resolve whether any new private franchise would be granted.

positions.position: Pressed for rescission of the suspended CBA memorandum and criticized the lack of progress after the same answer was given the previous year.

Supported franchise renewal for functioning cooperatives and questioned the fairness of allowing a private distributor with 5,000,000 in paid-up capital to enter the area of a high-performing cooperative.
Expressed strong support for service-oriented electric cooperatives and called for congressional support and intervention.
Raised concerns that excessive CBA demands could damage cooperative finances and sought revised system-loss rules and consultation with Mindanao cooperatives.

actions.action: Convene the Electric Cooperative Industry Tripartite Council technical working group and hold the next meeting on September 10.
Develop resolutions that could lead to rescission of the suspended CBA memorandum.
Provide an agency opinion when a congressional franchise committee requests one on a private distribution applicant.
Propose revised system-loss rules and conduct public consultation with stakeholders.
Invite Mindanao stakeholders, particularly electric cooperatives, to discuss the ongoing activity that had caused concern.

thread.speaker: Rep. Perci Cendaña
thread.said: Rep. Cendaña raised the collective bargaining agreement issue and referred to the memorandum as illegal.

thread.speaker: NEA official
thread.said: The official said the situation had been addressed through discussions with the Secretary of Labor and various groups. A technical working group under an Electric Cooperative Industry Tripartite Council would develop rules governing CBAs, with DOLE, the National Conciliation and Mediation Board, NEA, and labor groups participating.

thread.speaker: NEA official
thread.said: The memorandum remained suspended because of peculiarities in the electric-cooperative industry. The official said the issue would be resolved through the tripartite council, with representation from the federation and labor groups.

thread.speaker: NEA official
thread.said: The official said the next meeting was scheduled for September 10 and that, once the tripartite council reached a resolution, the rules would be placed within the framework being developed.

thread.speaker: Rep. Perci Cendaña
thread.said: Rep. Cendaña said the question had been raised the previous year and that the answer was substantially the same.

thread.speaker: NEA official
thread.said: The official responded that many CBAs had already been resolved, while acknowledging that some agreements could affect the operations of electric cooperatives. NEA was seeking a way to address the labor demands.

thread.speaker: Rep. Perci Cendaña
thread.said: Rep. Cendaña again asked whether the memorandum would be rescinded.

thread.speaker: NEA official
thread.said: The official said it would eventually be rescinded, rather than merely suspended, if the tripartite council produced the necessary resolutions.

thread.speaker: Rep. Perci Cendaña
thread.said: Rep. Cendaña noted that this had also been the answer the previous year and that a year had passed.

thread.speaker: Rep. DiCasson
thread.said: Rep. DiCasson said electric-cooperative franchises were generally understood to expire in 2028 or 2029, with four exceptions. He noted that one cooperative had already received another twenty-five years of authority in the previous Congress.

thread.speaker: Rep. DiCasson
thread.said: He asked whether the Secretary or administrator agreed that a congressional franchise grant was indispensable.

thread.speaker: NEA administrator
thread.said: The administrator agreed that a congressional franchise grant was indispensable.

thread.speaker: Rep. DiCasson
thread.said: Rep. DiCasson asked whether, without a franchise, an electric cooperative or distribution utility could operate and distribute power.

thread.speaker: NEA administrator
thread.said: The administrator agreed that a utility could not operate or distribute power without the required franchise.

thread.speaker: NEA administrator
thread.said: The administrator said functioning electric cooperatives should generally receive congressional support for franchise renewal, although extreme cases might not merit renewal.

thread.speaker: Rep. DiCasson
thread.said: Rep. DiCasson asked whether the generation market was competitive or monopolistic and included the transmission sector in the inquiry.

thread.speaker: DOE official
thread.said: The DOE official said EPIRA was intended to make generation competitive, allowing as many players as possible. The official said transmission operated under a franchise held by the National Grid Corporation of the Philippines and had a sole operator.

thread.speaker: DOE official
thread.said: The official said a distribution franchise established the cooperative's authority to conduct distribution business and made the service exclusive within its area.

thread.speaker: Rep. DiCasson
thread.said: Rep. DiCasson asked whether the DOE had a bureau or division that conducted feasibility studies and assessed the economic impact of a new private distribution utility entering a local area.

thread.speaker: DOE official
thread.said: The official identified the Electric Power Industry Management Bureau, which monitored distribution utilities, including cooperatives, through distribution development plans and power supply procurement programs. The bureau assessed compliance but did not assess a new franchise holder or incoming franchise applicant.

thread.speaker: Rep. DiCasson
thread.said: Rep. DiCasson cited Bicolite and Power Corporation's paid-up capital of 5,000,000 and asked whether a private distributor receiving a franchise would have to build its own lines, substations, and transformers or could interconnect with or acquire cooperative facilities.

thread.speaker: DOE Secretary
thread.said: The Secretary said the executive branch did not assess or approve franchises because that power belonged to Congress. Once granted, the franchise holder had to comply with its terms and, as a public utility, had the responsibility to provide the required service, including its own infrastructure if necessary.

thread.speaker: Rep. DiCasson
thread.said: Rep. DiCasson asked whether it would be fair to allow an unproven private distributor with only 5,000,000 in paid-up capital to enter the area of an electric cooperative that was performing at the highest NEA rating.

thread.speaker: NEA administrator
thread.said: The administrator said NEA would defer to Congress on whether to grant a new franchise. The administrator nevertheless said the cooperative was performing well and that NEA was not giving up on it.

thread.speaker: NEA administrator
thread.said: The administrator described the cooperative as having improved from more than 1,000,000,000 to 120,000,000 and said fresh capital could improve reliability and operations.

thread.speaker: NEA administrator
thread.said: The administrator confirmed that the cooperative had received a Triple-A rating for the last five years under NEA's categorization rules.

thread.speaker: committee chair
thread.said: The chair expressed strong support for service-oriented electric cooperatives and said Congress needed to intervene and support them, particularly in rural and urbanizing areas.

thread.speaker: committee chair
thread.said: The chair asked about a franchise applicant with paid-up capital of 5,000,000 and sought the agency's opinion on the adequacy of that capital.

thread.speaker: DOE official
thread.said: The official said the agency would provide an opinion when requested by the congressional franchise committee. The official compared the 5,000,000 figure with an Iloilo cooperative whose assets were about 1,500,000,000 and characterized 5,000,000 as very modest.

thread.speaker: NEA official
thread.said: In response to Rep. Sergio Dagooc, the official said several labor-union demands were exorbitant and could violate the cash operating-budget structure or working-capital requirements of electric cooperatives.

thread.speaker: NEA official
thread.said: The official cited grocery allowances of up to 6,000 pesos a month and said cooperatives could not afford them. The official also cited laundry allowances of 500 to 600 pesos a month, along with water and utility allowances and discounts on electricity consumption.

thread.speaker: NEA official
thread.said: The official warned that imposing unaffordable demands could cause a cooperative to fold up and said the issue would ultimately concern what the cooperative could actually provide.

thread.speaker: NEA official
thread.said: The official referred to DOLE training and negotiations between labor unions and management, emphasizing that negotiations could not require benefits beyond the cooperative's resources.

thread.speaker: Rep. Sergio Dagooc
thread.said: Rep. Dagooc asked about consultation with DOLE and the development of a CBA template.

thread.speaker: Rep. Sergio Dagooc
thread.said: Rep. Dagooc raised the system-loss reduction rules, including a reference to an unclear provision transcribed as “one dash ninety four,” and asked about the treatment of technical and nontechnical losses.

thread.speaker: ERC official
thread.said: The ERC official said new rules had simplified the business-plan requirement and allowed the community to decide whether available support would subsidize consumers or help cooperatives finance infrastructure.

thread.speaker: ERC official
thread.said: The ERC official undertook to propose a framework and conduct public consultation with stakeholders before proceeding.

thread.speaker: ERC official
thread.said: The official said the ERC would try to propose revisions to the circular and consult stakeholders on technical losses.

thread.speaker: Rep. Sergio Dagooc
thread.said: Rep. Dagooc placed on record that Mindanao stakeholders, particularly electric cooperatives, would be invited to discuss an ongoing activity because cooperatives and Mindanao legislators were alarmed.

topics.topic: ERC rate-setting, WESM overcharges, refunds, and consumer protection
topics.summary: The ERC said it had directed refunds of around 71.3 billion and attributed 70 billion to Meralco's delayed rate reset, but Rep. Chukwish sought the exact WESM overcharge and a clearer refund account. The ERC responded with a technical explanation of locational marginal pricing, congestion, line losses, and settlement-surplus allocation, while referring to interim measures, a longer-term market-operator solution, and a third-party audit. Rep. Robert Nassal questioned why consumers paid for projected capital investments before completion and called for independent verification that charges funded useful investments. The ERC said it had shifted to performance-based regulation, using forecast costs, capital expenditure, returns, depreciation, and regulatory-asset-base calculations over four- or five-year periods. The ERC also sought around 200,000,000 plus for consulting services and related MOE to complete all utility rate resets in 2027, and Rep. Rufus Rodriguez said the request was approved according to the chairman. NEA separately requested 7 or 10 billion to cushion electric cooperatives from eliminating nontechnical system losses.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish how the ERC set distribution-utility rates, including whether consumers were charged for projected investments before completion, and how WESM pricing flaws and market-settlement surpluses would be addressed through refunds. It also examined the ERC's budget needs for completing rate resets and supporting system-loss reduction.
topics.agency_position: The ERC said it was implementing performance-based, forward-looking rate regulation while limiting recovery to approved asset values, returns, depreciation, and other recognized revenue-requirement components. It maintained that rate resets, WESM settlement measures, audits, and consumer-focused regulation were needed to protect consumers, but the transcript did not provide a clear exact WESM overcharge or refund amount.
topics.outcome: The ERC answered the rate-setting question by explaining its performance-based methodology and said recovery was tied to approved asset values and regulatory-period resets. The exact WESM overcharge and refund requested by Rep. Chukwish remained unclear in the transcript, while the ERC's rate-reset funding request was stated to have been approved according to the chairman.

positions.position: Pressed the ERC for the exact WESM overcharge and a clear account of consumer refunds rather than only a technical explanation of LMP and settlement mechanics.
Argued that consumers should pay returns only for investments actually made and useful to them, and called for independent and transparent verification of charges.
Supported additional ERC resources for completing rate resets and stated that the ERC request was approved according to the chairman.

thread.speaker: ERC Chair Francis Nusi Juan
thread.said: The ERC said its mandate included protecting consumers, ensuring that retail rates reflected prudent and reasonable cost recovery, and penalizing abuse of market power. It said it regulated transmission and distribution as well as competitive generation and supply.

thread.speaker: ERC Chair Francis Nusi Juan
thread.said: The ERC said the regulated electricity sector was valued at around 4,190,000,000,000, while its proposed budget was 944,000,000.

thread.speaker: ERC Chair Francis Nusi Juan
thread.said: For January 2025 through June 2026, the ERC said it had issued 4611 decisions and orders, imposed 157,000,000 in fines, and directed refunds of around R71.3 billion.

thread.speaker: ERC Chair Francis Nusi Juan
thread.said: The chair said 70,000,000,000 of the directed refunds came from Meralco's actual weighted-average-tariff filing during the period when its rates had not been reset by the earlier commission.

thread.speaker: ERC Chair Francis Nusi Juan
thread.said: The ERC said it had restarted rate resets for private distribution utilities and required them to file their actual weighted-average tariffs.

thread.speaker: ERC Chair Francis Nusi Juan
thread.said: For 2027, the ERC committed to fair, evidence-based rate setting and to completing rate resets for private distribution utilities and electric cooperatives.

thread.speaker: ERC Chair Francis Nusi Juan
thread.said: The ERC said it had approved the final determination for one Group A private distribution utility under performance-based regulation, would complete Group B resets within the year, and targeted Group C and D resets in 2027.

thread.speaker: ERC Chair Francis Nusi Juan
thread.said: The ERC said new electric-cooperative rates were targeted for implementation starting in January. It linked the resets to the eventual removal of the system-loss charge and to efforts to reduce distribution-utility system losses.

thread.speaker: Rep. Chukwish
thread.said: Rep. Chukwish asked for the exact overcharge to consumers associated with the WESM pricing mechanism and the June 2021 pricing model, citing reports of a technical flaw and possible consumer refunds.

thread.speaker: ERC Chair Francis Wang
thread.said: The chair gave a technical explanation of locational marginal pricing, describing how the market-management system and optimization model account for the system marginal price, line losses, and congestion at each node.

thread.speaker: ERC Chair Francis Wang
thread.said: Using an example, the chair said a 100 megawatt supply could require an additional 2% to account for line losses, producing 102 megawatts of supply. The exact wording of portions of the example was unclear.

thread.speaker: ERC Chair Francis Wang
thread.said: The chair distinguished the system marginal price from locational marginal prices, explaining that LMPs vary across nodes because of line-loss and congestion costs.

thread.speaker: ERC Chair Francis Wang
thread.said: The chair said the net settlement surplus was distributed under an ERC-approved allocation formula reflecting congestion and differences among LMPs. He referred to the market-management system and the central registration and settlement system as computing the settlement automatically.

thread.speaker: Rep. Chukwish
thread.said: Rep. Chukwish said he understood the technical explanation but reiterated that his question was about the straightforward consumer-refund issue.

thread.speaker: ERC Chair Francis Wang
thread.said: The chair described an interim measure involving the collection and allocation of trading amounts and a longer-term solution involving the system or market operator. He also referred to a third-party audit and the extent of distribution-utility participation, although the technical details were partly garbled.

thread.speaker: Rep. Chukwish
thread.said: Rep. Chukwish said he would await the WESM refund and other actions, including matters involving a 12% VAT and system losses. He then ended his questioning.

thread.speaker: Rep. Robert Nassal
thread.said: Rep. Nassal asked why consumers were being charged rates based on projected or future capital investments before those investments were completed, given IPIRA's requirement that rates recover prudent and reasonable economic costs incurred.

thread.speaker: ERC official
thread.said: The ERC said it had shifted from the previously used RORP methodology to an internationally accepted performance-based rate-setting methodology, pursuant to the applicable legal and regulatory framework.

thread.speaker: ERC official
thread.said: The ERC explained that performance-based regulation was forward-looking, unlike a historical-cost approach, and used building blocks such as forecast efficient operating expenses, capital expenditure, return on the rate base, depreciation, and taxes to determine the revenue requirement.

thread.speaker: ERC official
thread.said: The ERC said the regulatory asset base included rolled-forward assets and capital expenditures procured before or during the regulatory period. It said distribution-utility regulatory periods were generally four years, while the NGCP period was five years.

thread.speaker: ERC official
thread.said: The ERC said consumers did not pay the entire value of a capital-expenditure project immediately; recovery reflected the asset's approved value, the weighted average cost of capital, and depreciation over the asset's life. It added that delayed projects would be addressed in the rate-reset process.

thread.speaker: ERC official
thread.said: The ERC said rate resets occurred after each four-year or five-year regulatory period, with a reset in the final year. The transcript does not clearly capture the complete response on the treatment of delayed projects.

thread.speaker: Rep. Robert Nassal
thread.said: Rep. Nassal said investments were a business risk and consumers should pay a fair and reasonable return only for investments actually made and useful to them. He called for an independent and transparent mechanism to verify that every peso charged was invested and benefited consumers.

thread.speaker: Chair
thread.said: The chair said he totally agreed with Rep. Nassal's concern before moving to the next interpellator.

thread.speaker: Rep. Rufus Rodriguez
thread.said: Rep. Rodriguez asked how much additional funding the ERC needed, focusing on the resources required to complete the distribution-utility rate resets.

thread.speaker: ERC Chair Francis Nusi Juan
thread.said: The ERC said it had written the Secretary and the Speaker seeking reconsideration and reinstatement of the unreleased portion of its proposed 2027 budget. It said the request for consulting services and associated maintenance and other expenses was around 200,000,000 plus.

thread.speaker: ERC Chair Francis Nusi Juan
thread.said: The chair said the ERC intended to finish rate-reset applications for all utilities in 2027, but without the requested support that timetable was at risk. He linked the work to more appropriate utility rates, improved efficiency, and the President's call to remove the system-loss charge.

thread.speaker: Rep. Rufus Rodriguez
thread.said: Rep. Rodriguez stated that the ERC's request was approved according to the chairman. The transcript does not identify a formal budget action or amount beyond the ERC request.

thread.speaker: NEA Administrator Daniel Mehta
thread.said: The NEA administrator said the agency had written the Speaker's office requesting 7 or 10,000,000,000 to cushion the effect of eliminating nontechnical system losses among electric cooperatives.

thread.speaker: NEA Administrator Daniel Mehta
thread.said: The administrator said electric cooperatives could be affected because extending lines to unserved and unviable areas contributed to system losses. He said the NEA was determined to implement the President's pronouncement, at least as to nontechnical losses; the remainder of the statement was cut off.

topics.topic: System-loss VAT and consumer billing implementation
topics.summary: Rep. Chukwish asked ERC Chair Francis Wang to clarify the treatment of the 12% VAT on system-loss charges and when consumers would see it in their bills. The ERC and DOE said implementation required BIR coordination, publication and effectivity steps, classification of technical and nontechnical losses, and phased work by electric cooperatives. Secretary Sharon said cooperatives would need about six months to prepare technical-loss plans and described 25% reduction stages toward eliminating nontechnical losses, with a possible report in the first half of the following year. Wang later identified September as the target for the BIR and billing-format process and said November was the earliest implementation after resolving September and October issues. An agency official cited 200,000,000 in support of the ERC budget because of the technical demands of the work.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish the ERC's position on applying 12% VAT to system-loss charges and when consumers would see the treatment reflected in their bills. It also sought a timetable for reducing system losses and implementing the related billing changes.
topics.agency_position: The DOE and ERC said the 12% VAT and system-loss billing treatment required coordination with the BIR, classification of technical and nontechnical losses, and a phased implementation rather than an immediate across-the-board reduction. They presented September as the target for the BIR and billing-format process, with November identified as the earliest implementation after resolving September and October issues.
topics.outcome: The agencies provided a target timetable but acknowledged that billing and reconciliation issues remained. The issue therefore landed with an agency implementation plan and November as the earliest stated implementation point, rather than as an immediate consumer-billing change.

positions.position: He pressed the ERC to clarify its VAT position and asked when consumers could expect the change to appear in their bills.

She supported a phased reduction of system losses, emphasized the operational work required to address technical and nontechnical losses, and said the DOE would not seek additional funding for that work.
He supported coordinated implementation with the BIR, DOE, and distribution utilities, subject to resolution publication, billing-format changes, reconciliation, and other implementation issues.

actions.action: Coordinate with the BIR and related energy agencies on the VAT treatment and implementation of system-loss charges.
Classify system losses as technical and nontechnical and implement a phased reduction program, including system evaluation by electric cooperatives.
Prepare a technical-loss reduction plan within about six months and subsequently have the ERC set limitations and rates.
Report on technical losses, potentially in the first half of the following year.
Target September for the BIR and billing-format process, resolve implementation and reconciliation issues, and proceed with the earliest implementation in November.

thread.speaker: Rep. Chukwish
thread.said: Rep. Chukwish asked ERC Chair Francis Wang about the ERC's position on the 12% value-added tax on system-loss charges.

thread.speaker: Francis Wang, ERC chair
thread.said: Wang referred to a BIR resolution identified in the transcript as “26, series of 20 '26.” He said the system-loss charge was treated as a government-mandated charge connected with lifeline subsidy and related allowances.

thread.speaker: Francis Wang, ERC chair
thread.said: Wang stated that the system-loss charge and the cost recovery of distribution-utility system losses were subject to the applicable commission treatment. The transcript's wording on the precise VAT and regulatory treatment is partly unclear.

thread.speaker: Rep. Chukwish
thread.said: Rep. Chukwish said he understood that the ERC would coordinate with the BIR and asked when consumers could expect the change.

thread.speaker: Francis Wang, ERC chair
thread.said: Wang said that before implementation, the ERC would work with the Department of Energy and the energy family to classify system losses as technical or nontechnical. He identified nontechnical losses as including man-made losses.

thread.speaker: Francis Wang, ERC chair
thread.said: Wang said the resolution would become effective after publication and a fifteen-day period, after which the BIR memorandum circular would be implemented. The transcript's wording on the exact BIR instrument is unclear.

thread.speaker: Sharon, DOE secretary
thread.said: Secretary Sharon said system-loss reduction could not be achieved simply by directing the ERC to impose a lower figure. She described enforcement, consumer education, billing and collection efficiency, meter management, database cleansing, electric-cooperative efficiency, institutional strengthening, and regulatory reforms as necessary steps.

thread.speaker: Sharon, DOE secretary
thread.said: Sharon said electric cooperatives would need about six months to evaluate their systems, including transformers and electricity flow, and prepare an optimal technical-loss reduction plan. She said the ERC would then set limitations and rates in tandem so the burden on consumers would be properly managed.

thread.speaker: Sharon, DOE secretary
thread.said: Sharon described a phased approach, including 25% reductions until nontechnical losses reached zero, and said the department could report on technical losses “maybe, the first half of next year.” She also said the department would not ask for additional funding for the work.

thread.speaker: Francis Wang, ERC chair
thread.said: Wang said there was a plan and timetable for addressing technical and nontechnical losses and that the agencies would carry it out.

thread.speaker: DOE undersecretary or agency official
thread.said: An agency official asked whether ERC Chair Wang would respond regarding the target billing date for system losses.

thread.speaker: Francis Wang, ERC chair
thread.said: Wang said the target was September for the BIR process and for the effective direct-fee treatment in the distribution-utility bill format. He explained that implementation issues remained, including removing or resolving system-loss items after the bill was generated.

thread.speaker: Francis Wang, ERC chair
thread.said: Wang said distribution utilities would collect the corresponding energy purchases and reconcile the corresponding system-loss amount after the month concerned. He said the earliest implementation after September and October would be November.

thread.speaker: DOE undersecretary or agency official
thread.said: The agency official said the ERC needed support because the matter was highly technical and referred to support for the ERC budget. The official then stated that the amount was 200,000,000.

topics.topic: Renewable-energy expansion, auctions, and agricultural-land safeguards
topics.summary: The DOE reported that renewable energy had reached about 25.04% of the 2025 generation mix, with 20.7 gigawatts awarded through the Green Energy Auction and another 25 gigawatts planned for auction through 2035. Rep. Presley de Jesus questioned whether failed renewable-energy contracts should be canceled and whether generation costs required regulation; the DOE favored safeguards, reported about 33 contracts totaling about 1.3 gigawatts, and said more than 100 contracts had been canceled or were being canceled. Rep. Marco Anko raised concerns about solar projects and requested hydrological review, to which the DOE committed a report. Rep. Salvador Pleyto asked how renewable targets could be met while protecting about 3,000,000 hectares of agricultural land; the DOE cited possessory-rights requirements, DA coordination, LGU ordinances, and farm-compatible solar development. Rep. Reneko questioned incentives affecting indigenous communities and the environmental classification of waste-to-energy; the DOE cited prior informed consent, emissions safeguards, and the statutory classification but said it lacked authority to reclassify the technology. Several records and policy questions were left for follow-up, so the issue was committed rather than fully resolved.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish how the DOE would expand renewable-energy capacity while protecting agricultural land, enforcing renewable-energy service contracts, safeguarding consumers and communities, and addressing the environmental and legal treatment of waste-to-energy projects. Members also asked what safeguards, studies, records, and policy changes the DOE would provide or undertake.
topics.agency_position: The DOE supported accelerated renewable-energy deployment through auctions and programs including ground-mounted solar, agrosolar, offshore wind, solar on irrigation canals, and waste-to-energy, but said projects had to comply with land-use, permitting, community-consent, contractual, and emissions requirements. It favored safeguards and stronger generator accountability rather than direct generation-cost regulation, and said it could not reclassify waste-to-energy without a change in the law.
topics.outcome: The DOE's renewable-energy expansion plans were presented as supported by auctions, new project types, and consumer-access programs, but questions about agricultural-land protection, hydrological review, contract cancellations, indigenous safeguards, and waste-to-energy records remained subject to further review or reporting. The DOE maintained that it could not reclassify waste-to-energy without legislative action.

positions.position: Supported stronger safeguards against generation costs and pressed the DOE to cancel renewable-energy service contracts that failed to deliver promised capacity.
Sought scrutiny of solar projects, including hillside development, and requested hydrological and related studies.
Supported renewable-energy expansion but urged protection of prime agricultural and rice-producing land and development of farm-to-energy applications.

Asked for stronger protection of indigenous communities in the granting of renewable-energy incentives and urged reconsideration of waste-to-energy's classification as renewable energy because of health and environmental concerns.

The agency committed to include the hydrological-study matter in its next report and report back.
The DOE was asked to consider stronger or amended guidelines addressing indigenous-community displacement in renewable-energy projects receiving incentives.
