thread.said: He said that if 5,000,000 were used for classrooms, the amount would be only three to 3,500,000, as spoken.

thread.speaker: Jose Teves Jr.
thread.said: He pressed for an increase, proposing 7,000,000 rather than 5,000,000 per barangay.

thread.speaker: DILG Secretary
thread.said: The secretary said DILG had actually asked for 10,000,000, but the DBM/PBM process allowed only 5,000,000. He said Congress could adjust the amount and that DILG would welcome an increase to 7,000,000.

thread.speaker: DILG Secretary
thread.said: He acknowledged a shortage of 2,000 classrooms in Cavite and said he understood Rep. Yakino's concern.

thread.speaker: A member
thread.said: A member asked about the change from 10,000,000 to 5,000,000 per barangay, the physical and financial accomplishment rates, and DILG's audit and verification of EL CAC beneficiaries.

thread.speaker: DILG Secretary
thread.said: The secretary explained that DILG facilitated barangay-level consultations so residents and barangay officials could identify priority programs funded through the Barangay Development Program.

thread.speaker: DILG Secretary
thread.said: He reported delivery rates of 99.86% for 2021, 100% for 2022, 98.48% for 2023, 90% for the original 2024 allocation, and 71% for an additional 5,000,000 released toward the third or last quarter of 2024. He reported 29% performance for 2025 and said 2026 projects had not yet been completed because funds were released only in the second and third quarters.

thread.speaker: A member
thread.said: The member asked that the accomplishment documents be resubmitted to the committee.

thread.speaker: DILG Secretary
thread.said: The secretary agreed to provide copies of the documents to the committee.

thread.speaker: DILG Secretary
thread.said: He said DILG was responsible for monitoring and evaluating the LGSF, had hired 700 engineers and program evaluation officers, and required LGUs to upload project progress regularly to the SubayBayan portal.

thread.speaker: A member
thread.said: The member requested full financial and physical performance audit information and a disbursement breakdown for prior-year Barangay Development Program funds.

thread.speaker: DILG Secretary
thread.said: The secretary said DILG could provide physical project completion status and fund releases, but scrutiny of how funds were used was left to the Commission on Audit. He added that SBDP projects were subject to third-party monitoring by CSOs and NGOs.

thread.speaker: A member
thread.said: The member asked whether DILG received the reports of third-party monitors.

thread.speaker: DILG Secretary
thread.said: The secretary confirmed that DILG received the reports and agreed to provide the committee a copy.

thread.speaker: A committee official
thread.said: When asked when the report would be submitted, the response was Tuesday of the following week.

thread.speaker: Rep. Caroline Agyao
thread.said: Rep. Caroline Agyao asked how many EL CAC barangays there were nationwide.

thread.speaker: DILG Secretary
thread.said: The secretary reported 840 target barangays in 2021, 1,406 in 2022, 958 in 2023, 864 recipient barangays in 2024, 780 in 2025, and 808 in 2026, for a total of 5,608 barangays since 2021.

thread.speaker: Committee chair
thread.said: The chair directed that the barangay coverage data be submitted to the committee.

thread.speaker: DILG Secretary
thread.said: The secretary said the 2025 allocation was 10,000,000 per barangay, that DILG proposed 10,000,000 for 2026 but it initially appeared as 5,000,000, and later corrected the record by saying 2026 received 10,000,000.

thread.speaker: DILG Secretary
thread.said: He clarified that 2025 had 2,500,000 per barangay, 2026 had 10,000,000, and 2027 was reduced to 5,000,000. He said the 2027 figure was the proposal of the national task force and local community council.

thread.speaker: DILG Secretary
thread.said: He said recipient barangays had at some point been under the influence of communist terrorist groups and had already been cleared by the Armed Forces of the Philippines.

thread.speaker: DILG Secretary
thread.said: He said the program guidelines provided a menu including school classrooms, health centers, water systems, and electrification. He said municipal-level coordination was intended to prevent duplication with projects of other agencies.

thread.speaker: DILG Secretary
thread.said: He clarified that funds were downloaded directly to municipalities, which implemented the projects, while DILG monitored and supervised implementation.

thread.speaker: DILG Secretary
thread.said: He explained that the Barangay Development Program was one of four projects under the LGSF, alongside the growth equity fund, support and assistance for participatory budgeting, and financial assistance to local governments.

thread.speaker: DILG Secretary
thread.said: He clarified that the LGSF was administered by the Department of Budget and Management, rather than DILG.

thread.speaker: CSO representative
thread.said: On behalf of civil society organizations, the CSO representative questioned why a separate LGSF should be retained after the increased National Tax Allotment, what fiscal gaps it addressed, and how the government prevented duplication or substitution of LGU resources.

thread.speaker: DILG official
thread.said: The official said the estimated 2027 National Tax Allotment for LGUs was about 1.32 to 1.4 trillion pesos, divided among 82 provinces, 149 cities, 1,493 municipalities, and more than 42,000 barangays. He said the proposed LGSF of 58,000,000,000 provided additional resources for water and sanitation systems, farm-to-market roads, electrification, health centers, and other basic services.

thread.speaker: DILG Undersecretary Jed Mabilog
thread.said: Undersecretary Jed Mabilog said LGSF funds were released directly to local governments, while DILG monitored and evaluated implementation through engineers and project evaluation officers deployed to provinces and regions.

thread.speaker: DILG Undersecretary Jed Mabilog
thread.said: He said DBM handled validation and vetting through a portal where LGUs uploaded project proposals. DILG therefore did not handle the principal duplication review, and the matter could be referred to DBM.

thread.speaker: CSO representative
thread.said: The CSO representative asked how projects were identified, endorsed, validated, procured, and monitored; how local councils, CSOs, sectoral representatives, and communities participated; and what safeguards prevented duplication, conflicts of interest, and undue procurement influence.

thread.speaker: DILG Undersecretary Jed Mabilog
thread.said: Undersecretary Mabilog said local governments identified priority projects and handled procurement. DILG used three-tier monitoring: local project monitoring committees including CSOs, DILG's own second-party monitoring, and third-party monitoring by CSOs and NGOs, supported by the SubayBayan portal.

thread.speaker: DILG Undersecretary Jed Mabilog
thread.said: He referred to an allocation of 63,000,000 for DILG monitoring and evaluation and said 560,000,000 was used for salaries of engineers and project evaluation officers. These figures were spoken in the context of LGSF monitoring and evaluation.

thread.speaker: CSO representative
thread.said: The CSO representative asked about the basis for the relative allocations for participatory budgeting and SBDP, including the proposed SBDP change from PHP8.08 billion to an unclear higher amount, and requested plans for expanded CSO and community participation.

thread.speaker: DILG Undersecretary Jed Mabilog
thread.said: Undersecretary Mabilog said SBDP addressed basic-service needs in barangays previously influenced by communist groups and sought to regain public trust through grassroots consultations. He cited 10,000,000 per barangay for 2026 as an example of funding for locally identified priority projects.

thread.speaker: DILG Undersecretary Jed Mabilog
thread.said: He said the support and assistance fund for participatory budgeting had an allocation of 1,000,000,000 for 2026, including water-system projects amounting to PHP 13,300,000 and evacuation centers amounting to 25 point something million pesos.

thread.speaker: CSO representative
thread.said: The CSO representative asked for the basis of the proposed 2027 SBDP increase, citing 9,740,000,000 in the 2027 proposal versus R8.8 billion in the 2026 General Appropriations Act, and requested needs assessments, utilization and completion data, selection criteria, per-barangay and per-project allocations, audit findings, complaints, outcomes, and open-data publication.

thread.speaker: DILG Undersecretary Jed Mabilog
thread.said: Undersecretary Mabilog said the apparent 2027 increase was actually a decrease per barangay: 808 barangays were covered in 2026, while 1,904 were to be covered in 2027. He said DILG had requested 19 point something billion pesos so each barangay could receive 10,000,000 as in 2026, but the allocation was reduced to 5,000,000.

topics.topic: BFP fire-truck procurement, repair, stations, and emergency capacity
topics.summary: Members repeatedly questioned DILG and the BFP about fire-truck shortages, station gaps, procurement corruption, repair and replacement, and emergency-response capacity. The agency said it was pursuing a government-to-government procurement with South Korea for about 1,500 trucks, with a maintenance contract and a stated cost advantage over prior purchases and Japan. Officials said BFP fire-code collections were remitted to the national treasury, while DBM released only about 1 billion annually, leaving the BFP with limited access to funds despite collections and earmarks totaling several billion pesos. Members cited municipalities without stations or trucks and shortages in protective equipment, while the BFP requested search-and-rescue trucks, ambulances, Unified 911 operating funds, and additional recruitment. The committee noted or supported possible trust-fund and appropriations action, and Rodriguez manifested an intent to seek approval of the requested increases. The Korea procurement remained under negotiation, with technical specifications and a written status update requested, so the issue landed as a supported but not fully resolved commitment.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish how the BFP would finance, procure, maintain, and distribute fire trucks, rescue vehicles, ambulances, stations, and related equipment; how much it collected and actually received from fire-code fees; and whether the proposed government-to-government procurement with Korea would address national shortages. Members also asked about procurement safeguards, repair and replacement needs, station gaps, and emergency-response capacity.
topics.agency_position: DILG and the BFP said procurement reforms and government-to-government purchasing, particularly with South Korea, would reduce corruption and lower unit costs while expanding the number of trucks acquired. They maintained that BFP fire-code collections were remitted to the national treasury but that DBM released only a limited portion, and asked Congress to support fuller use of the trust fund for trucks, stations, ambulances, rescue equipment, maintenance, and recruitment.
topics.outcome: The committee generally supported the proposed Korea government-to-government procurement and the BFP's requests for additional trucks, stations, ambulances, rescue equipment, operating funds, and manpower. However, fuller access to fire-code collections, final procurement terms, supplier selection, and the requested budget increases remained dependent on congressional action, DBM releases, and further agency submissions.

positions.position: Supported the government's government-to-government fire-truck procurement plan and pressed for budget support during the appropriations process.

Supported the Korea government-to-government approach and indicated support for releasing or appropriating fire-code collections for trucks, stations, ambulances, rescue equipment, and additional manpower.
Supported a special provision or other appropriations action allowing greater use of fire-code-fee collections for BFP needs and moved for additional funding from the trust fund.
Supported the BFP's requested increases for search-and-rescue trucks, ambulances, operating expenses, and recruitment, and manifested an intent to move for approval of the requested increases.
Pressed for fuller access to fire-code collections to address station, truck, protective-equipment, and rescue-equipment shortages.
Sought transparency on the Korea procurement, including supplier selection, the role of Philippine contractors, the unresolved negotiation status, and a written update.
Pressed DILG and the BFP to improve local disaster preparedness, water-rescue capability, equipment distribution, and training in flood-prone areas.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juanito Victor Remulla
thread.said: Secretary Remulla said fire-truck funding came from BFP fire-inspection collections. He said almost 44,500,000,000 was collected for fire-code fees but remitted directly to the national treasury, and that only 2 point only 1,000,000,000 was committed by the treasury that year.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juanito Victor Remulla
thread.said: He reported that DILG was completing a government-to-government transaction with Korea for 1,500 trucks over the next four years, intended to cover all municipalities. He said the arrangement would remove corruption concerns associated with BFP procurement.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juanito Victor Remulla
thread.said: He described the procurement as a four-year, 1,500-truck replacement program costing 40% less than previous fire trucks and including a maintenance contract so municipalities could maintain the vehicles.

thread.speaker: Committee chair
thread.said: The chair referred to a DBM report involving 72% collection in one year, 100 fire trucks, and more than 40 fire stations in one year. The exact context and amount associated with the reported collection were unclear in the transcript.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juanito Victor Remulla
thread.said: Secretary Remulla corrected the collection figure, saying, "It's 25% collection." When the chair suggested Japan as another procurement option, he said Japan was 30% more expensive and that Korea was the best option at that time.

thread.speaker: Representative Bong Teves
thread.said: Representative Teves cited a BFP budget of 2,900,000,000, increasing from 35,000,000,000 in 2026 to 38,000,000,000 in 2027. He also cited capital outlay declining from 1,400,000,000 in 2026 to 362,000,000 in 2027.

thread.speaker: Representative Bong Teves
thread.said: Teves asked about fire protection and cited 67 new fire stations, eight rescue trucks, and an additional 2,000 PFE personnel for emergency and rescue response.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juanito Victor Remulla
thread.said: Remulla said the capital-outlay reduction resulted from reconstituting the BFP procurement program. He said reforms and systems had been instituted to reduce procurement, recruitment, and deployment corruption and that capital outlay would increase in calendar year 2027.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juanito Victor Remulla
thread.said: Remulla said the BFP collected 4,500,000,000 a year and remitted the entirety to the national treasury. He later said the BFP received only 30% of what it remitted.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juanito Victor Remulla
thread.said: He said DILG had entered a long-term deal for 1,500 trucks for the next three years and expressed hope that the arrangement would address the committee's concerns.

thread.speaker: Representative Edgar Erice
thread.said: Erice cited a total amount in the FY 2027 budget document of 3,430,000,000,427,988,000. The transcript's presentation of this figure may be garbled, but the amount is retained exactly as spoken.

thread.speaker: Representative Edgar Erice
thread.said: Erice said 20% of fire-code fees was remitted to concerned LGUs and 80% went to the national government under a trust fund. He cited a balance as of 12/31/2025 of 10,536,154,803 pesos and 81 centabos.

thread.speaker: Representative Edgar Erice
thread.said: Erice questioned why the BFP's request was only 33,000,427,000 pesos despite the reported collections and trust-fund balance. He also cited 108,000,000 pesos plus and an amount of only 3,400,000,000 pesos; the surrounding figures were unclear.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juanito Victor Remulla
thread.said: Remulla answered that the BFP asked for all of the available funds but DBM provided only a portion. He said the department was constrained by the DBM allocation.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juanito Victor Remulla
thread.said: Remulla said, "We always ask for everything, but they only allot us 1,000,000,000 every year."

thread.speaker: Secretary Juanito Victor Remulla
thread.said: He said a fire truck costing 16,000,000 of equal quality could cost 10,000,000 under a government-to-government grant. He said the lower cost would allow the BFP to acquire more trucks.

thread.speaker: Representative Edgar Erice
thread.said: Erice said the request did not cover the number of fire trucks needed nationwide and moved for consideration of an additional amount for the BFP, to be taken from collected fire-code fees under the trust fund.

thread.speaker: Committee chair
thread.said: The chair said the proposed additional funding request was duly noted and supported releasing the DBM-held resources for fire trucks, stations, ambulances, and rescue equipment.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juanito Victor Remulla
thread.said: Remulla said the BFP had 5,000 nurses on its payroll but too few ambulances. He said additional funding would allow the BFP to acquire class one ambulances rather than only patient-transfer vehicles.

thread.speaker: Committee chair
thread.said: The chair cited BFP personnel of 40,000 and recruitment of 2,000 per year, saying it would take twenty years to reach the required manpower. He said the proposal was for 4,000 per year to address the problem in ten years.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juanito Victor Remulla
thread.said: In response to Representative Rufus Rodriguez's question on repairing or replacing fire trucks, Remulla reiterated the planned government-to-government purchase of 1,500 trucks from South Korea. He said broader assistance to municipalities depended on Congress releasing the BFP trust fund.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juanito Victor Remulla
thread.said: Remulla said the long-term agreement would assure the supply of trucks and that procurement reforms had reduced corruption, allowing the BFP to buy more fire trucks.

thread.speaker: BFP official
thread.said: The BFP official presented five budgetary requests totaling 33,400,000,000 pesos. The first was restoration of 200,000,000 for eight collapse-structure search-and-rescue trucks; the official asked the chair to allocate two of the trucks to his locality.

thread.speaker: BFP official
thread.said: The official requested 1,800,000,000 pesos for 74 collapse-structure search-and-rescue trucks to give provincial fire offices rescue capability, 373,000,000 pesos for Unified 911 operating expenses, and 287,000,000 pesos for 82 ambulances.

thread.speaker: BFP official
thread.said: The official requested an additional quota of 2,000 F01 recruits on top of the 2,000 recruited yearly, to reach ideal BFP manning requirements in ten years instead of twenty years. The official restated the overall amount as 3,400,000,000 pesos; the transcript also contains the figure 3,427,000.

thread.speaker: Representative Rufus Rodriguez
thread.said: Rodriguez manifested that, at the proper time, he would move for approval of the DILG and attached-agency budgets with all requested increases, including the BFP requests.

thread.speaker: BFP official
thread.said: The BFP official said DBM provided only 1,000,000,000 pesos each year. In response to questions on modernization, the official confirmed that the collections were intended for BFP modernization, including fire stations, fire trucks, personal protective equipment, and rescue equipment.

thread.speaker: Representative Robert Raymond Estrella
thread.said: Estrella cited 2025 BFP collections of 4,300,000,000, spending of 1,684,000,000, and accumulated earmarks of 11,280,000,000. He also cited 107 municipalities without activated fire stations, 64 without either a fire station or fire truck, shortages of 20,854 fire coats, 22,000 gloves, and 36,000 fireman's hoods.

thread.speaker: BFP official
thread.said: The BFP official said there was a proposal for full utilization of fire-code-fee collections to address the shortages and acquire the necessary items under the modernization program, subject to congressional support.

thread.speaker: BFP official
thread.said: Asked about bidding for 500-gallon fire trucks and the number of bidders, the official said the BFP was moving toward government-to-government transactions with counterpart governments in the region for that year's procurement. He said the approach would reduce cost and allow more trucks to be acquired.

thread.speaker: Committee chair
thread.said: The chair said one fire truck would be allocated for a municipality in Nueva Vizcaya and that additional fire trucks and fire stations requested for other localities would be included in the FY 2027 budget. The chair said supporting documents would be submitted.

thread.speaker: BFP official
thread.said: The BFP official reported an entrapment operation involving a personnel member allegedly engaged in recruitment anomalies in Region 3. The official said the Secretary's instructions were to eradicate corruption in recruitment and procurement of fire trucks and equipment.

thread.speaker: BFP official
thread.said: The official said the BFP's ideal manning requirement was 78,000 nationwide, while its authorized strength was only 43; the transcript is unclear whether the latter figure was abbreviated or incomplete. With 2,000 recruits per year, the official said it would take twenty years, and requested an additional 2,000 per year.

thread.speaker: DILG agency official
thread.said: The official said the proposed government-to-government procurement with South Korea remained under advanced discussion. Korean agencies would form two committees to screen proposed suppliers against technical specifications supplied by the Philippines and recommend suppliers to the Philippine side.

thread.speaker: Representative Antonio Tinio
thread.said: Tinio clarified whether suppliers would be Korean suppliers identified by the Korean government and asked about the role of Philippine contractors, given prior controversy. The official confirmed that the process was still under negotiation and that technical specifications were being refined.

thread.speaker: DILG agency official
thread.said: The official said the BFP expected to submit the finalized technical specifications by the following day and would continue coordinating with the Republic of Korea.

thread.speaker: Committee chair
thread.said: At Tinio's request, the committee directed the agency to submit a written, detailed update on the proposed procurement.

thread.speaker: Representative Anna York
thread.said: York asked how the BFP was preparing for flooding and water rescue, including whether it could identify flood-prone areas and place boats and trained responders in localities such as Pampanga.

thread.speaker: BFP official
thread.said: The BFP official said the bureau played a vital role in flood response and that BFP units had watercraft and life vests. The official said equipment would be distributed geographically according to local fire-station needs.

thread.speaker: BFP official
thread.said: The official committed to helping build local disaster-management capacity through continuous training and to acquiring necessary equipment for localities exposed to hydrometeorological hazards.

topics.topic: PNP additional funding, mobility, staffing, and regional equipment
topics.summary: The chair presented the DILG's proposed budget of about 32.5 billion, including about 142.5 billion for the PNP, and linked public-safety funding to school security and law-enforcement capability. Mark Huanko supported the DILG budget but pressed for implementation of the Lingayen road project, recovery of disputed PNP property, and replacement of aging vehicles; the PNP committed to act, investigate, coordinate, and report back. The agency said 95% of the Mahindra vehicles acquired in 2010 and 2011 were beyond economic repair, and Huanko requested 231 vehicles for the district's 231 barangays. Mica Gonzales asked about recruitment into violence and permanent police presence near schools, and the agency said sensitive details could be discussed in executive session while school police presence was already policy. Rufus Rodriguez cited Region 10 mobility deliveries and supported additional PNP funding; the PNP chief confirmed an additional request of 2,025,000,000 after initially stating conflicting figures. A majority member also raised DILG field-office staffing shortages, and the agency said a government optimization plan was being prepared.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish whether the DILG and PNP had sufficient funding, vehicles, personnel, and regional equipment to meet public-safety needs. Members also asked about the implementation of a Lingayen police-road project, recovery of disputed PNP property, school-area police deployment, and proposed staffing increases for DILG field offices.
topics.agency_position: The DILG and PNP supported additional operational capacity through vehicles, capital outlays, recruitment, school-area police presence, and field-office staffing. The PNP committed to pursuing the Lingayen road and property matters, accounting for vehicle needs, updating the member, augmenting police forces in the next recruitment or fiscal-year cycle, and seeking an additional request identified as 2,025,000,000.
topics.outcome: The hearing produced agency commitments on the Lingayen road and property matters, vehicle accounting, police augmentation, school-area deployment, and a field-office optimization plan. The PNP additional request was identified as 2,025,000,000, but final congressional action on that request and the vehicle allocations remained subject to the budget process.

positions.position: Supported the DILG's public-safety priorities and proposed budget, including PNP information technology, capability enhancement, and school-security measures.

Supported the DILG budget, particularly for Region 1, and pressed for implementation of the Lingayen road project, recovery of disputed PNP property, and replacement or reassignment of aging police vehicles.
Sought stronger action against recruitment into violence and confirmation that police presence near schools would be maintained as a policy.
Supported additional PNP funding and regional mobility resources, including the PNP's additional request of 2,025,000,000.
Supported augmenting DILG local-operations staffing and considering additional LGU-funded staff for municipalities.

topics.topic: School-violence prevention, active-shooter drills, and school police presence
topics.summary: The Chair and several members raised concerns about school violence, online recruitment into violence, firearms used by minors, and the need for faster police response. DILG and PNP officials said police were already present during school entry and dismissal and that barangay tanods would be allowed inside schools under a joint memorandum circular. Officials reported 50 school-related incidents involving minors, a 97% five-minute 911 response compliance rate, and a PNP operations increase of about 15 billion. The agencies proposed nationwide active-attack drills with DepEd, a youth ambassadors program, coordination with DICT and NTC on malicious online sites, and expanded Unified 911 vehicles. The Secretary also proposed stricter firearm-safekeeping inspections and penalties, while members questioned the emphasis on video games and stressed broader social and mental-health factors. The agencies committed to refine and submit drill guidelines, but the hearing left the definite schedule, dedicated budget line, and firearm-enforcement data unresolved.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish what DILG, the PNP, DepEd, LGUs, and attached agencies were budgeting and implementing to prevent school violence, monitor online recruitment into violence, secure firearms, conduct active-attack drills, and ensure rapid police response. Members also asked whether police presence near schools could be made permanent or assigned to individual schools.
topics.agency_position: DILG and the PNP stated that school security required layered measures: police presence during student entry and dismissal, barangay tanod augmentation inside schools, coordination with DepEd, online-threat monitoring with DICT and NTC, active-attack drills, Unified 911 response, and stricter firearm-safekeeping rules. The PNP reported 97% compliance with a five-minute response target for 911 calls, but officials did not identify a dedicated school-drill budget line or provide all requested firearm-enforcement data.
topics.outcome: The hearing established a package of planned or ongoing measures—school police presence, barangay tanod augmentation, DepEd coordination, active-attack drills, online-site coordination, firearm-safekeeping reforms, and expanded emergency response. The committee did not receive a separate school-drill budget line, a definite drill date, or the requested firearm-license enforcement counts, leaving implementation and funding details open.

Proposed exploring a one-school, one-police model, asked how the PNP's increased funding would translate into school protection, and requested data on firearm-license enforcement.
Questioned whether limited police staffing could realistically cover schools and sought stronger measures for school-threat checking and firearm security.

topics.topic: Firearms control, safekeeping, and police use of firearms
topics.summary: Rep. Dadah Kiram Ismula, Rep. Rolando Valeriano, Rep. Edgar Erice, Renee Co, Rep. Robert Raymond Estrella, and Anna York Bondoc questioned the DILG and PNP about firearm safekeeping, loose firearms, mobilization protocols, and school safety. The agency said 800,000 uniformed personnel were covered by firearm-responsibility rules, but acknowledged that firearms in the Tacloban and Zamboanga incidents had not been properly secured. Officials proposed advance-notice PNP inspections of lawful firearm owners' homes, stronger penalties for irresponsible safekeeping, and repeal of the Robin Padilla law; they repeatedly cited 98% as the share of firearm violence or firearm-related cases involving loose or unlicensed firearms. The PNP said it had only 2,000 body cameras for 320,000 personnel and was procuring another 10 or 20,000, while acknowledging that firearms carried during mobilizations may have reflected a mistake. For school security, officials cited barangay tanods, police coordination, active-attack drills, online-platform coordination, and community participation, but said assigning police to each of about 56,000 schools was impractical. The committee requested reports on the mobilizations, the Zamboanga mistaken-identity case, and the DILG's firearm-regulation recommendations; data on license suspensions and related cases was not supplied.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish how the DILG and PNP were preventing firearms from being misused, particularly firearms issued to uniformed personnel or legally owned by civilians. Members also asked about controls during police mobilizations, penalties for irresponsible safekeeping, school security, and whether additional enforcement, inspection, identification, and accountability measures were needed.
topics.agency_position: The DILG and PNP said firearm owners and custodians were responsible for secure safekeeping, but acknowledged that the two school-shooting incidents reflected failures in that responsibility. They supported revising the IRR to permit advance-notice inspections of firearm storage, imposing stronger penalties for irresponsible or illegal possession, and repealing the Robin Padilla law to make loose-firearm offenses non-bailable. They also maintained that school security required coordinated police, barangay, education, and community measures rather than a dedicated police officer for every school.
topics.outcome: The agency's proposals for IRR amendments, home inspections, stronger penalties, and repeal of the Robin Padilla law were presented but were not enacted during the hearing. The committee requested investigative and policy documents, while the requested statistics on firearm-related license suspensions and cases remained unanswered.

positions.position: Supported stronger safeguards and accountability for government-issued firearms, including improved safekeeping protocols, inspections, and penalties for owners whose firearms were used unlawfully.
Pressed for proactive firearm controls and future-prevention measures following school shootings.

Sought concrete school-security measures, data on firearm-related license suspensions and cases, and stronger protection of schools using the PNP's increased budget.
Pressed for practical school protection and stronger controls over firearms that could be accessed by minors, while recognizing that police resources could not cover every school continuously.

thread.speaker: Rep. Dadah Kiram Ismula
thread.said: She asked about findings from the Zamboanga City school-shooting incident and whether alleged online groups had influenced the child involved.

thread.speaker: DILG agency official
thread.said: The official said the Department of Education and DILG were preparing a memorandum circular to allow barangay tanods inside schools to augment security and inspect bags. The PNP was also required to be present during student ingress and egress.

thread.speaker: Rep. Dadah Kiram Ismula
thread.said: She said the Tacloban and Zamboanga incidents indicated failures in the handling of government-issued firearms and asked about PNP and DILG protocols for issued firearms.

thread.speaker: DILG agency official
thread.said: The official said there were 800,000 uniformed personnel across the PNP, AFP, NBI, Bureau of Customs, BJMP, and BFP, with two incidents of unauthorized firearm use. Protocol required personnel to remain responsible for their firearms and keep them under lock and key when not in their possession.

thread.speaker: DILG agency official
thread.said: The official said one firearm in the Tacloban case had been left on a table and another in the Zamboanga case had been left in a car. The official proposed amending the IRR to allow the PNP, with notice, to inspect the homes of lawful firearm owners and their safekeeping procedures.

thread.speaker: DILG agency official
thread.said: The official argued that firearm ownership was a privilege granted by law rather than a constitutional right, and that PNP inspection of firearm storage could therefore be required subject to notice and proper procedures.

thread.speaker: DILG agency official
thread.said: The official said the current cases involved reckless imprudence resulting in homicide and argued that firearm owners should face a greater penalty when their guns were used for illegal purposes.

thread.speaker: Rep. Dadah Kiram Ismula
thread.said: She asked about PNP operations involving mistaken-identity arrests and the safeguards being developed to prevent such incidents.

thread.speaker: DILG agency official
thread.said: The official said almost 4,000,000,000 in PNP savings from the 2026 and 2027 budgets had been accumulated for a PNP community ID. The system would use biometrics and consolidated records to establish one national identification record and reduce mistaken identities.

thread.speaker: DILG agency official
thread.said: The official said multiple government IDs could cause several names to appear during an arrest and claimed that one person could accumulate five 400 phones using different government IDs; the wording and figure were unclear in the transcript.

thread.speaker: Rep. Dadah Kiram Ismula
thread.said: She asked whether there was a budget award or reward when an arrest was found to involve mistaken identity.

thread.speaker: DILG agency official
thread.said: The official said there was no reward for mistaken identity, but the incident would be investigated.

thread.speaker: Rep. Dadah Kiram Ismula
thread.said: She asked what action would be taken against PNP personnel in cases involving mistaken-identity arrests.

thread.speaker: DILG agency official
thread.said: The official said personnel would first face an administrative investigation. If malicious intent were established, the matter would be forwarded to Napolcom for disposition.

thread.speaker: Rep. Dadah Kiram Ismula
thread.said: She asked about the reported mistaken-identity case involving the Alphad family in Zamboanga City.

thread.speaker: DILG agency official
thread.said: The official said the agency would gather the information and return to the member before the session started.

thread.speaker: DILG agency official
thread.said: In response to Rep. Rolando Valeriano, the official said the IRR should be revised so the PNP could give advance notice, inspect firearm premises, use a safekeeping checklist, and remind owners of proper practices.

thread.speaker: DILG agency official
thread.said: The official said there were over 4,000,000 legal handguns in the country, held by uniformed personnel and private owners, and argued that the PNP should inspect how they were secured.

thread.speaker: Rep. Rolando Valeriano
thread.said: As chair of the public order and safety committee, he asked what proactive measures were planned to prevent future shooting incidents.

thread.speaker: DILG agency official
thread.said: The official urged Congress to repeal the Robin Padilla law and said 98 percent of violent crimes were committed with loose firearms rather than lawful firearms. The official also proposed banning Roblox in the Philippines, asserting that its online communities could encourage violent tendencies among children.

thread.speaker: DILG agency official
thread.said: The official requested additional funds for the BJMP if the Robin Padilla law were repealed, arguing that increased arrests of people possessing loose firearms would require more jail capacity.

thread.speaker: Rep. Edgar Erice
thread.said: He asked why the country should not adopt much more restrictive gun-ownership rules similar to those of Japan, Singapore, South Korea, and China.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juanito Victor Remulla
thread.said: Secretary Remulla said 98% of gun violence involved illegal or loose firearms and called on Congress to repeal the Robin Padilla law and make loose-firearm offenses non-bailable. He said 98% of gun owners were responsible and that the remaining 2% of firearm-related violence by lawful owners was comparatively minimal.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juanito Victor Remulla
thread.said: Secretary Remulla said firearm ownership was a privilege, not a right, and proposed amending the IRR to allow police to schedule inspections of every gun owner's home. He linked the proposal to the two school shootings, which he said involved legally issued firearms belonging to uniformed personnel.

thread.speaker: Renee Co
thread.said: She cited BP 880's restriction on police carrying firearms during mobilizations and asked why police, particularly civil-disturbance-management commanders, had brought guns into rally areas.

thread.speaker: DILG agency official
thread.said: The official said the presence of firearms may have been a mistake and would be investigated. The official said frontline responders were unarmed, while support groups at the rear could augment the response, and maintained that no firearms were drawn or used against rally participants.

thread.speaker: Renee Co
thread.said: She requested the civil-disturbance-management ground deployment plan, operation report, and official incident logs concerning the mobilizations.

thread.speaker: DILG agency official
thread.said: The official agreed to provide the requested mobilization documents to the committee by that afternoon.

thread.speaker: Renee Co
thread.said: She asked how the department would ensure that police assigned to homes and school zones treated children appropriately and did not create a culture of fear. She also challenged explanations that school shootings were caused principally by video games.

thread.speaker: DILG agency official
thread.said: The official said a full account of the shooters' backgrounds could not be given in open session but could be discussed in executive session. The official maintained that video games played a large part in the shooters' descent into violent conduct.

thread.speaker: Renee Co
thread.said: She said violence arose from compounded factors, including media, bullying, social experience, and a broader culture of violence, rather than video games alone.

thread.speaker: Rep. Robert Raymond Estrella
thread.said: He asked how many cases in 2024, 2025, and to date involved irresponsible possession, storage, transfer, or access to firearms, and whether licenses had been suspended when a firearm was accessed by an unauthorized person or minor or used in a crime.

thread.speaker: PNP official
thread.said: The official said the firearms used in the Tacloban and Zamboanga incidents had been investigated and that cases for reckless imprudence resulting in homicide had been recommended or filed against the custodians. The official did not provide the requested totals for license suspensions or cases.

thread.speaker: PNP official
thread.said: The official said the PNP was considering amendments concerning legally obtained firearms and stronger penalties for illegally possessed firearms, particularly those used in crimes. The official repeated that 98% of firearms used in crimes were loose firearms.

thread.speaker: Committee chair
thread.said: The chair noted that DILG already had numerous recommendations and asked the agency to submit all of them to the committee.

thread.speaker: Anna York Bondoc
thread.said: She asked how the PNP was addressing threats to schools and distinguishing the risks posed by registered and unregistered firearms, including firearms held by licensed personnel who might leave them accessible to children.

thread.speaker: PNP official
thread.said: The official said the firearms recovered from the Tacloban and Zamboanga incidents were registered firearms except for one. The official said cases had been prepared against the persons responsible for safeguarding them and recommended higher penalties for unlicensed firearms, which the official said accounted for about 98% of firearm-related cases.

thread.speaker: Anna York Bondoc
thread.said: She questioned whether police could realistically patrol every elementary school and asked how school safety would be maintained with limited police personnel.

thread.speaker: PNP official
thread.said: The official said there were about 42,000 barangays and approximately 56,000 schools nationwide, making one dedicated police team per school impractical. The official advocated coordinated work among police, other law-enforcement agencies, barangay tanods, and the community.

topics.topic: PCW budget cut and gender-based violence services
topics.summary: Rep. Sarah Elago questioned the PCW and ECCD Council budget reductions, regionalization plans, gender-and-development compliance, and the adequacy of local gender-based violence services. The PCW said the cut would mainly affect expansion to Mindanao, sought another 30,000,000 for that purpose, and reported 488 agencies in its gender mainstream system with about 77.46% compliance. Secretary Juanito Victor Remulla said DBM had cut the submitted budget and that restoration could make it more effective, while the ECCD Council reported a gap affecting 3,743 centers. DILG and PNP officials said local governments should address many frontline services within their budgets and committed to corrective or enforcement action on personnel-related violence and insensitive materials. The NCMF later reported inadequate Hajj medical funding, citing 95 pesos per pilgrim from a spoken allocation of 600 16,000 pesos, and requested support for three priority programs. The committee directed the NCMF to submit its request, and members expressed support, but the funding issues were not finally resolved.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish how the reduced PCW and ECCD Council allocations would affect regionalization, gender-and-development compliance, child development centers, and frontline services for survivors of gender-based violence. It also examined whether NCMF's reduced medical allocation for Hajj and its priority programs required additional funding.
topics.agency_position: The PCW said the proposed cut would chiefly constrain regionalization, particularly expansion to Mindanao, while it could live with the rest of the allocation. The DILG and PNP said local governments should fund local protection and training needs, while the PNP stated that it took personnel-related violence seriously and would file appropriate charges. The NCMF said its Hajj medical allocation was inadequate and requested additional funding for medical needs and three priority programs.
topics.outcome: The PCW and ECCD Council funding gaps were identified, with possible PCW restoration and a proposed child development center line item, but no restoration was approved during the exchange. The NCMF was directed to submit its written funding request and received an expression of committee support; the requested amounts remained subject to subsequent budget action.

topics.topic: ECCD Council budget cut and child development centers
topics.summary: A committee member raised the scale of the child development center and day-care network and asked how the early childhood system would be supported. Secretary Juanito Victor Remulla said day-care centers were primarily funded through barangays and other LGUs, with additional infrastructure potentially involving DPWH and the provinces, because 96% of the DILG budget covered operating expenses or salaries. He cited an allocation of about 124 million for early-childhood feeding and capacity building. Representative Sarah Elago then questioned the 2027 ECCD Council figure of 232,000,000 pesos and asked how the cut would affect the council's mandate. The secretary said DBM had reduced DILG's submitted budget and that restoration could be requested, while the ECCD Council warned that the cut would limit center rehabilitation and the procurement of learning materials, furniture, fixtures, and other contents. Elago said she would propose a special line item for child development centers, but no restoration or final funding action was recorded.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish how the ECCD Council's reduced 2027 allocation would affect its mandate, regional services, and child development center infrastructure. It also examined which government level or agency was responsible for funding additional day-care centers and their contents.
topics.agency_position: DILG said additional day-care center funding was principally a barangay, provincial, DPWH, and other LGU responsibility because most of the DILG budget covered operating expenses and salaries. Secretary Remulla said DILG's submitted budget had been reduced by DBM and could be restored, while the ECCD Council said the cut would significantly limit rehabilitation and the provision of learning materials, furniture, fixtures, and other center contents.
topics.outcome: The committee received the agency's explanation that the cut resulted from DBM's reduction of the submitted budget and that the cut would affect center rehabilitation and contents. Restoration was raised but not finalized, while a special child development center line item was proposed for later consideration.

topics.topic: BFP recruitment integrity, manpower, and personnel needs
topics.summary: Perci Cendaña raised alleged BFP recruitment slot-selling and sought clarification on the agency's controls. Secretary Juanito Victor Remulla said prior slot prices ranged from 200,000 to 800,000 per slot and referred the matter to the BFP chief, who described the online e-hiring system and confirmed a recent Region Three entrapment operation involving recruitment anomalies. The BFP said future recruitment would be fair, transparent, and based on merit and fitness. The chief reported that DBM provided about 2,000 recruits annually against a stated ideal manpower requirement of about 78,000; the transcript also gave an authorized strength of 43, with the unit unclear. He said the current rate would require twenty years and sought an additional 2,000 recruits per year. The Chair welcomed the agency action, but no approval of the additional recruitment request was recorded.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish whether BFP recruitment slots had been sold, whether the agency had detected and acted on recruitment-related corruption, and what controls were in place to prevent a recurrence. It also examined whether BFP's manpower level was adequate and whether additional annual recruitment authority was needed.
topics.agency_position: The BFP said it had detected and acted on a recruitment anomaly through an entrapment operation involving personnel in Region Three, and that e-hiring, online applications, system-generated examinations, and immediate results would reduce opportunities for slot-selling. It committed to fair, transparent, merit- and fitness-based recruitment, while stating that the agency needed more than the 2,000 recruits currently provided annually to address its manpower shortfall.
topics.outcome: The BFP confirmed that a recruitment anomaly had been exposed and acted on, and the Chair accepted the explanation that the matter had reached the bureau. The broader request for additional annual recruitment remained an agency appeal rather than a recorded committee approval.

positions.position: He treated alleged recruitment slot-selling as a serious issue requiring clarification and agency accountability.
He welcomed the fact that the anomaly had reached the BFP office and insisted that future hiring be based on applicants' qualifications and merit.
He said the recruitment case had been officially solved and supported new procedures intended to make slot-selling almost impossible.
He maintained that the BFP's anti-corruption and e-hiring mechanisms were functioning, while seeking increased annual recruitment to address the agency's manpower deficit.

thread.said: The chief confirmed that a recent entrapment operation in Region Three involved BFP personnel engaging in recruitment anomalies and corruption. He said an applicant had reported the matter with the help of CIDG Region Three.

thread.speaker: Chief Kwanchu
thread.said: He said the secretary's instruction was to eradicate corruption and anomalies not only in recruitment but also in the procurement of fire trucks and other BFP equipment. He maintained that the bureau's mechanism for detecting and addressing anomalies was working.

thread.speaker: Chief Kwanchu
thread.said: He again described e-hiring as an online process conducted at the applicants' doorstep, with online examinations and immediate results. He said the system addressed corruption at the start of recruitment, although an anomaly had unfortunately occurred at the last stage.

thread.speaker: Chief Kwanchu
thread.said: The chief said the secretary was cleansing the agency of anomalies and expressed confidence that the irregularity exposed by the entrapment operation could be addressed in succeeding recruitment cycles.

thread.speaker: Chair
thread.said: The Chair said it was good that the matter had reached the BFP office and expressed hope that applicants would be hired nationwide on the basis of qualifications and merit.

thread.speaker: Chief Kwanchu
thread.said: The chief assured the committee that recruitment would be based on merit and fitness and would be fair and transparent. He said DBM provided 2,000 recruits each year, while the BFP's present strength was far below the ideal manpower requirement of 78,000 for the entire country; the transcript stated that authorized strength was only 43, but the unit or context was unclear.

thread.speaker: Chief Kwanchu
thread.said: He said that recruiting 2,000 annually would take twenty years to complete the stated manpower requirement and expressed hope for an additional 2,000 recruits per year. He reiterated that recruitment would be transparent, fair, and based on merit and fitness.

thread.speaker: Chair
thread.said: The Chair closed the exchange by identifying additional manpower, along with equipment, fire trucks, and fire stations, as matters of interest at the grassroots level.

topics.topic: BJMP jail congestion and facility construction
topics.summary: Rep. Rufus Rodriguez asked BJMP about its budget request and the funding needed to address severe jail congestion. BJMP identified an additional request of 229,157,000 for jail-facility construction and cited further requirements involving Cagayan de Oro and Region 10, including 100,000,000 for Region 10 and a combined figure summarized as 800. The committee also raised problems caused by separate records systems among municipal and provincial jails, BJMP, and BuCor, while Secretary Juanito Victor Remulla advocated combining the agencies and creating common computerized records. Rep. Antonio Tinio questioned BJMP's restriction of visits primarily to direct family, lawyers, and doctors, especially for PDLs needing support from others. BJMP explained that most facilities were locked visitation spaces but agreed to submit its standard operating procedure and study possible changes. Funding support was expressed, but the construction figures and agency-consolidation proposal were not finally resolved in the recorded exchanges.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish how BJMP would address jail congestion, including the additional funding needed for jail-facility construction and projects in Region 10. It also examined how detainee records could be consolidated across jail systems and whether BJMP visitation rules improperly excluded non-direct-family visitors.
topics.agency_position: BJMP identified jail congestion as its principal operational problem and sought additional funding for jail-facility construction, including projects in Region 10 and Cagayan de Oro. On visitation, BJMP said its policy generally allowed direct family, lawyers, and doctors to visit, but it accepted that the standard operating procedure should be submitted and reviewed in light of the concerns raised.
topics.outcome: The committee received BJMP's congestion-related funding figures, and Rep. Rodriguez stated that he would push for the requested increases, but no approval ruling was recorded in this topic segment. BJMP committed to submit its visitation standard operating procedure for committee review; the broader proposal to consolidate jail records and agencies remained open.

positions.position: Supported additional BJMP funding for jail construction and Region 10 projects and said he would push for the request.
Questioned the restriction of visits to direct family and sought written guidelines and possible review of the policy for non-direct-family visitors.
Sought a common computerized records system across municipal jails, provincial jails, BJMP, and BuCor to prevent record problems from delaying appropriate PDL treatment or release.

topics.topic: Youth programs, NYC budget, and ICT modernization
topics.summary: A committee member questioned the NYC's proposed budget reduction of about 19,000,000 and the omission of requests for Muslim and creative youth summits and ICT modernization. The NYC explained the summit proposals and identified an ICT request of 24,000,948, while acknowledging that only two people handled procurement and that additional personnel-services funding was needed to absorb more funds. Rep. Dadah Kiram Ismula and Jambaranda pressed the NYC on programs, data, and curriculum for out-of-school youth; the NYC cited a 2,500,000 youth entrepreneurship allocation, support for a Magna Carta, and interagency coordination, but said available data was incomplete. Jambaronda also sought broader SK training and compliance, leading DILG to commit to revisiting modules and issuing further guidance. Members additionally requested active-shooter-drill guidelines and information on political-dynasty recommendations, with agencies undertaking to submit or obtain the requested materials. The budget increase itself remained unapproved in the transcript.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish whether the National Youth Commission's reduced 2027 budget could support its expanding youth mandate, including Muslim and creative youth summits, ICT modernization, youth mental-health and entrepreneurship programs, SK training, and services for out-of-school youth. Members also sought specific agency commitments, data, and interagency coordination on youth safety and political-dynasty concerns.
topics.agency_position: The NYC said its youth mandate was primarily advocacy, policy, coordination, and capacity building, while acknowledging that its budget and staffing constrained implementation and absorptive capacity. It supported additional funding and personnel services, particularly for ICT modernization, youth entrepreneurship, SK training, research, and expanded youth programs, but said it lacked police power and certain data, which required coordination with DILG, DepEd, COMELEC, and other agencies.
topics.outcome: The NYC budget issue was not finally resolved: the committee chair expressed support for restoration or increases, while the NYC acknowledged both unmet program requests and staffing-related absorptive-capacity limits. The committee obtained commitments for additional documents, revised SK guidance, active-shooter-drill guidelines, and follow-up with COMELEC.

positions.position: Supported restoring or increasing the NYC budget because the commission's partner organizations and youth responsibilities were expanding despite the proposed reduction.
Pressed for concrete interagency programs for out-of-school youth that would support return to school or safe, non-discriminatory employment.
Advocated expanded and better-timed SK training, stronger compliance and reporting, and prioritization of an out-of-school-youth curriculum.
Sought prompt, evidence-based active-shooter-drill guidelines that addressed children's mental health and requested documentation on NYC recommendations concerning political dynasties.
Supported a whole-of-government response to harmful online content influencing children, including coordination among DICT, DILG, Congress, and other agencies.

thread.speaker: Rep. Percival Cendaña
thread.said: He cited school-violence incidents and cases linked to nihilistic violent extremism, and asked what DILG and the PNP were doing to monitor and apprehend online-linked extremism.

thread.speaker: Secretary Juanito Victor Remulla
thread.said: He said harmful online sites influencing children were beyond the government's direct control at home, and urged a whole-of-government effort involving DICT, DILG, other agencies, and Congress to filter or ban dangerous sites.

thread.speaker: DILG official
thread.said: The official said the NYC was allocating support for youth mental-health hubs and peer-to-peer facilitators, and was mobilizing facilitators in areas with incidents. The NYC was also working with a DSWD program and cash-for-work volunteers on mental-health support.

thread.speaker: DILG official
thread.said: The official described NYC support as limited and said the agency had proposed an anti-bullying summit for the following year, which had been approved by DBM.

thread.speaker: DILG official
thread.said: The official said NYC had partnered with Meta and was conducting Meta camps by province and at selected sites, with a direct reporting line for bullying incidents.

thread.speaker: A committee member
thread.said: The member noted a 6.11% NYC budget decrease amounting to more or less 19,000,000 pesos, and asked about unapproved requests for a Muslim youth summit, a creative youth summit, and ICT modernization.

thread.speaker: NYC chair
thread.said: The NYC chair said the Muslim youth summit would implement its partnership with the National Commission on Muslim Filipinos under a historic MOU. The creative youth summit would involve the Philippine Creative Industries Development Council, the Film Development Council, and NCCA, with activities in Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao and participation by ambassadors such as SB 19.

thread.speaker: A committee member
thread.said: The member asked the NYC to explain its 24,000,000 peso ICT modernization request.

thread.speaker: NYC chair
thread.said: The NYC chair clarified that the request was 24,000,948, based on its ISSP plan and already approved by the TICT. The systems would cover general services management, government accounting, budget and treasury, and procurement information and management, improving transparency and accountability.

thread.speaker: A committee member
thread.said: The member asked how many youth organizations were registered as NYC partner organizations and how many had been registered the previous year.

thread.speaker: NYC chair
thread.said: The NYC chair said about 10,000 youth organizations were registered, with the number steadily increasing over the previous two years. He said the previous year's figure was definitely less than the current number.

thread.speaker: A committee member
thread.said: The member argued that a growing number of registered youth organizations was inconsistent with a 6% budget decrease, saying the budget reduction did not make sense and that the NYC budget should be restored or increased.

thread.speaker: Committee chair
thread.said: The chair said he supported the member's position on restoring or increasing the NYC budget.

thread.speaker: NYC chair
thread.said: The NYC chair acknowledged an absorptive-capacity problem and said the commission had submitted an optimization plan. He requested increased personnel services because only two people handled procurement, limiting the commission's ability to absorb additional funds.

thread.speaker: Rep. Dadah Kiram Ismula
thread.said: She cited PSA research that 17.4 of Filipinos aged 5 to 24 were not in school and asked what programs were included in the 2027 budget for out-of-school youth.

thread.speaker: NYC official
thread.said: The official said out-of-school youth were invited to the NYC's events, including pride parades and other activities, and that the NYC supported legislation of a Magna Carta for out-of-school youth.

thread.speaker: Rep. Dadah Kiram Ismula
thread.said: She asked whether the NYC coordinated with other agencies so young people could resume schooling or, if of working age, obtain decent employment without exploitation or discrimination.

thread.speaker: NYC official
thread.said: The official said the NYC served as secretariat of the National Advisory Council, chaired by DepEd, where these concerns were raised quarterly. He said the NYC's role was mainly advocacy and policy, supplemented by small programs supporting youth economic opportunities.

thread.speaker: NYC official
thread.said: The official said the youth entrepreneurship program had 2,500,000 allocated for 2027. The NYC was also partnering with DOT and DTI for the Philippine National Creative Youth Summit, including arts-and-crafts opportunities for out-of-school youth.

thread.speaker: Rep. Dadah Kiram Ismula
thread.said: She asked about a DTI youth program for people aged 18 to 30.

thread.speaker: NYC official
thread.said: The official answered that the NYC also had the Young Farmers Challenge, if he was not mistaken, in partnership with the Department of Agriculture.

thread.speaker: Jambaranda
thread.said: She asked what the NYC planned to do after the SK elections.

thread.speaker: NYC official
thread.said: The official said the NYC continued to offer SK training and was printing SK 101 books that included SK auditing guidelines. The NYC was also signing an MOU with the Philippine Association of Local Government Accountants or the relevant local-government accountants' association to help pre-audit SK plans.

thread.speaker: Jambaranda
thread.said: She asked which SK manual the NYC was using and how the training materials would reach nearly 2,000 municipal federations.

thread.speaker: NYC official
thread.said: The official said the NYC would train local youth development officers and provincial youth development officers as trainers. He cited limited capacity: 10 area offices with two people per office, and again requested additional personnel services positions.

thread.speaker: Jambaranda
thread.said: She proposed that SK federation officers receive training before or around federation elections rather than waiting until afterward, and asked DILG to coordinate with NYC on the training.

thread.speaker: DILG official
thread.said: The official said the law required a one-day orientation before SK chairpersons assumed office. DILG would revisit the modules with the Local Government Academy and the NYC to enhance that one-day training.

thread.speaker: NYC official
thread.said: The official said the NYC did not have police power and had to refer SK complaints to DILG and the local government. He said he would have to get back to the committee on the number of SK members suspended or removed.

thread.speaker: DILG official
thread.said: The DILG official said removal of an SK federation president followed a process based on noncompliance with the federation's constitution and bylaws.

thread.speaker: NYC official
thread.said: The NYC official said the commission could pass a resolution supporting Jambaranda's manifestation but could only encourage SKs because it could not mandate them.

thread.speaker: DILG official
thread.said: The official said DILG had already issued several memorandum circulars and would issue another round in response to the member's manifestation.

thread.speaker: Committee chair
thread.said: The chair directed that figures on SK federation hearing members be submitted to the committee.

thread.speaker: Jambaranda
thread.said: She cited 10.7 out-of-school youth figures and asked the NYC to prioritize an out-of-school-youth grade-level and senior-high-school curriculum.

thread.speaker: NYC official
thread.said: The official said available out-of-school-youth data from DepEd was limited to those applying to DepEd or CHED schools, so the data was flawed and the actual number was probably larger. He suggested that the committee provide funding for the NYC policy and research division to undertake the work.

thread.speaker: A committee member
thread.said: The member asked for a comprehensive plan and timeline for active-shooter drills that had reportedly been pushed back to September.

thread.speaker: DILG-related agency official
thread.said: The official said DepEd was spearheading school-led simulation drills under guidelines coordinated with PNP, DILG, and BFP. The guidelines were being refined to account for children's mental health and would be shared with the committee once received.

thread.speaker: A committee member
thread.said: The member requested that the refined active-shooter-drill guidelines be submitted to the committee, noting an expected September target but that no definite rescheduled date had been provided.

thread.speaker: A committee member
thread.said: The member asked what the NYC was doing regarding the constitutional or statutory prohibition on political dynasties and whether it was implementing existing provisions.

thread.speaker: NYC official
thread.said: The official said the NYC's mandate was limited to recommending and encouraging. It promoted equal political participation and youth suffrage, and said it had realigned about 4,800,000 to support a regional youth-suffrage program with the Commission on Human Rights.

thread.speaker: A committee member
thread.said: The member asked for an update on the NYC's recommendations concerning implementation of political-dynasty provisions, including data and action taken.

thread.speaker: NYC official
thread.said: The official said the NYC did not have the requested data and would have to defer to COMELEC, but was open to working with the committee on implementation.

thread.speaker: A committee member
thread.said: The member requested the NYC's historical list of recommendations to the Commission on Elections concerning the prohibition on political dynasties, as well as cases and resulting actions.

thread.speaker: NYC official
thread.said: The official said the NYC would contact COMELEC and get back to the committee because complaints were normally filed directly with COMELEC.

topics.topic: SK training, compliance, elections, and local youth governance
topics.summary: Rep. Jambaranda raised concerns about SK training, annual development plans, fiscal compliance, regular federation meetings, and the possible postponement of SK elections. Secretary Juanito Victor Remulla committed to an immediate memorandum circular on annual development plans and said noncompliant local governments could be excluded from the SGLG; he also took note of the request to regulate barangay travel. Rep. Bambi Mano asked whether DILG could hear and correct an appeal from an SK chair's dismissal, and the DILG undersecretary answered that it could under section 67 of the Local Government Code and the SK-related laws, subject to a written follow-up. The NYC described continuing SK training, auditing guidance, trainer-of-trainers arrangements, and an MOU with local government accountants, while DILG committed to revisit the one-day orientation modules. The NYC reported a training estimate of roughly 70 plus million, with the transcript also recording 72,000,000,000, and said a survey of 120 federation presidents was examining support for an extension or special elections. The agencies agreed to issue further guidance and submit information, but election timing, removal data, and out-of-school youth data remained open.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish whether SK and barangay officials were receiving adequate training, complying with planning and fiscal requirements, and subject to effective oversight and removal procedures. It also sought clarification on DILG's appellate authority over SK dismissals, the timing of SK elections or special elections, and the reliability of out-of-school youth data.
topics.agency_position: DILG maintained that it had appellate authority to resolve an appeal from an SK chair's dismissal under section 67 of the Local Government Code and that dismissal propriety could also be considered under Republic Act 10742 and the SK Reform Law of 2015. The NYC and DILG supported expanded training, auditing guidance, and compliance monitoring, but the NYC said it could encourage SK compliance rather than mandate it and deferred removal questions to DILG.
topics.outcome: The hearing produced commitments for memorandum circulars, enhanced SK orientation and training, additional compliance guidance, submission of SK membership figures, and possible NYC research funding. DILG answered the appellate-authority question affirmatively, but the dismissal case remained subject to the submission and review of Rep. Mano's documents; the election timing and reliable out-of-school youth figures were not resolved.

positions.position: Supported mandatory annual development plans, stronger SK training before federation elections, fiscal-management guidance, regular SK meetings and reporting, enforcement of compliance rules, and priority attention to out-of-school youth.
Sought a definitive written DILG position on whether it could hear and resolve an appeal from an SK chair's dismissal before the matter proceeded to plenary.
Sought stronger implementation of SK capacity-building, skills development, awareness, information programs, and mandatory training.
