thread.said: CHED and DBM were developing an equation based on a one-is-to-40 faculty-student ratio. She said increased admission should be matched by more classrooms, faculty items, and non-teaching positions.

thread.speaker: CHED Chair Shirley Agrupis
thread.said: Across 115 SUCs, five collected tuition of 50 pesos per unit; 32 collected 51 to 100 per unit; 57 collected 101 to 200 per unit; 14 collected 200 to 300 per unit; and five collected 400 pesos to 1,000 per unit.

thread.speaker: CHED Chair Shirley Agrupis
thread.said: She said full harmonization of tuition fees across 554 SUCs would require 136,000,000,000 pesos, based on a level of more than 500 per unit.

thread.speaker: CHED Chair Shirley Agrupis
thread.said: A flat 200 pesos per unit would require 11,500,000,000, compared with the existing allotment of 9,100,000,000, leaving 2,400,000,000 to implement the proposed leveling-up.

thread.speaker: CHED Chair Shirley Agrupis
thread.said: She estimated that a 300-per-unit option would require 15,000,000,000, or an additional 6,200,000,000 over 9,100,000,000.

thread.speaker: Rep. Percy
thread.said: He compared a prior 29,470,000,000 figure with 26.53 billion for 2026, describing the difference as around 3,000,000,000 pesos. He also cited 6,181,000,000 and 67,000,000 in relation to SUC funding, although the specific institutions were unclear.

thread.speaker: CHED Chair Shirley Agrupis
thread.said: She said SUCs had submitted budgets for instruction, research, and extension, including faculty training, classrooms, facilities upgrades, digital transformation, and personnel, MOOE, and capital outlay. She warned that cuts would adversely affect quality education.

thread.speaker: Rep. Percy
thread.said: He questioned an 805,000,000 budget cut to PGH.

thread.speaker: CHED Chair Shirley Agrupis
thread.said: She said PGH was affiliated with and operated by UP Manila, and referred to a proposal of 53 point 53, 295 and a DBM figure of 1.855; the figures and their units were unclear.

thread.speaker: CHED Chair Shirley Agrupis
thread.said: For equity-group programs, including special-needs education, speech pathology, occupational therapy, and clinical psychology, CHED proposed 418,000,000.

thread.speaker: Rep. Maria Cristina Lopez
thread.said: She asked CHED to confirm 68,684,852 free-higher-education beneficiaries across LUCs.

thread.speaker: CHED Chair Shirley Agrupis
thread.said: She confirmed the figure.

thread.speaker: Rep. Maria Cristina Lopez
thread.said: She also asked about 247,000 ongoing beneficiaries.

thread.speaker: CHED Chair Shirley Agrupis
thread.said: She confirmed that figure and stated that supporting these beneficiaries was CHED's mandate.

thread.speaker: CHED Chair Shirley Agrupis
thread.said: She said 93,000 beneficiaries would be covered the following year, describing them as beneficiaries who would be made happy in 2027.

thread.speaker: Rep. Renee Co
thread.said: She asked for an update on the unresolved free-higher-education deficiency, noting that DBM had reportedly released at least 9,000,000,000 and that the pending calculation was 12,000,000,000. She asked whether CHED was monitoring deficiencies through 2027.

thread.speaker: CHED official
thread.said: The official said the deficiency for 2022–2025 was not yet solved. CHED and DBM had repeatedly validated the figures and agreed on the amount to be paid.

thread.speaker: CHED official
thread.said: The official said the prior four years had been covered by a CHED-DBM joint memorandum circular, but a new deficiency was developing for 2025 and 2026. CHED, PASUC, and DBM were agreeing to use a one-is-to-40 faculty-student ratio instead of the one-is-to-25 ratio, which CHED considered unrealistic.

thread.speaker: Rep. Renee Co
thread.said: She requested documentation of the revised calculation and the deficiency position for the budget season.

thread.speaker: Rep. Renee Co
thread.said: She urged restoration of SUC budget cuts and emphasized that a 20% MOOE level was needed amid inflation and the fuel crisis.

thread.speaker: CHED Chair Shirley Agrupis
thread.said: She said renewal applications were ongoing and that 2025 beneficiaries were assured of funding. She explained that the 2026 one-time grant had created a potential continuation problem.

thread.speaker: CHED Chair Shirley Agrupis
thread.said: She said continuation of the unfunded TDP requirement amounted to 1,400,000,000 and warned that without continuing funding, 2026 support could become a one-time grant.

thread.speaker: Rep. Cheeno Almario
thread.said: He proposed that the committee consider increasing the budget allocation for TDP so learners could continue receiving support through graduation.

thread.speaker: Committee chair
thread.said: The chair said the manifestation and proposal were taken into consideration.

thread.speaker: CHED Chair Shirley Agrupis
thread.said: She said SUC faculty-student ratios ranged from one-is-to-25 and one-is-to-40 to one-is-to-81, one-is-to-71, and one-is-to-60, and offered to provide the data.

thread.speaker: CHED Chair Shirley Agrupis
thread.said: She said continued enrollment required more plantilla faculty positions and greater SUC absorptive capacity through additional classrooms. Otherwise, CHED would need to enforce stricter admission policies tied to capacity.

thread.speaker: Rep. Cheeno Almario
thread.said: He asked CHED to consider using TES or TDP to involve private institutions when public SUCs became overcrowded.

thread.speaker: CHED Chair Shirley Agrupis
thread.said: She said private institutions could be partly subsidized through the program, citing 13,500 per private enrollee. She also cited 20,000 available Presidential Merit Scholarship slots and 39,000 in the surrounding discussion, whose precise relationship was unclear.

thread.speaker: CHED official
thread.said: CHED's proposal covered 1,677,000 beneficiaries with 35,500,000,000. The NEP amount was stated as 17,098,803,000 covering 843 beneficiaries; the beneficiary figure was likely incomplete or garbled.

thread.speaker: Deputy Speaker Ferdinand Hernandez
thread.said: He confirmed that the funding fell from about 35 billion to about 17 billion and characterized the reduction as a serious problem affecting scholarship beneficiaries.

thread.speaker: CHED official
thread.said: The official said unpaid free higher education amounted to 667,000,000 and displaced 137,000 students.

thread.speaker: CHED official
thread.said: The combined total for free higher education for LUCs, TES, and TDP was stated as 29,167,557,000, covering 1,064,000 students.

thread.speaker: CHED official
thread.said: The official identified an 11,000,000,000 difference between 2026 and 2027 funding.

thread.speaker: Deputy Speaker Ferdinand Hernandez
thread.said: He described the 11,000,000,000 gap as potentially affecting almost 1,000,000 students and said the reduction was alarming and should not deprive deserving students.

thread.speaker: Rep. Antonio Tinio
thread.said: He raised constitutional concerns about post-enactment legislative intervention in scholarship implementation, citing the PDAF ruling and arguing that implementation belonged to the executive. He also questioned the legal basis and accessibility of scholarship criteria.

thread.speaker: Committee chair
thread.said: The chair said Rep. Tinio's manifestation was well noted.

thread.speaker: CHED official
thread.said: CHED reported 170 LUCs established by local governments, of which 116 had institutional recognition and 54 did not.

thread.speaker: Chair Mikaswan Singh
thread.said: She asked for the status of the previous year's free-higher-education deficiency payments to SUCs, recalling a total of 12,000,000,000, with roughly 7,500,000,000 from HEDF and roughly 4,800,000,000 from the GAA.

thread.speaker: CHED Chair Shirley Agrupis
thread.said: She said CHED and DBM had signed a joint memorandum circular and that 9,700,000,000 had been released about two weeks earlier. CHED was processing the release and had received submissions from 108 SUCs, with some still needing to complete requirements.

thread.speaker: Chair Mikaswan Singh
thread.said: She asked how the 9,700,000,000 accounted for the 12,000,000,000 total and what would happen to the remainder, noting 9,400,000,000 for 2022–2024 deficient billings and 341,000,000 without submission.

thread.speaker: CHED Chair Shirley Agrupis
thread.said: She said the initial computation had been 12,700,000,000, but discrepancies arose from the faculty-student-ratio assumptions and SUC submissions. CHED was limiting the payment to the initial submissions and was not entertaining additional claims; 108 billings covered 9,700,000,000.

thread.speaker: Chair Mikaswan Singh
thread.said: She pointed out that the reported amount covered only 108 SUCs and asked about the remaining SUCs, including possible overpayments.

thread.speaker: CHED Chair Shirley Agrupis
thread.said: She referred to an allotment of 7,800,000,000 and HEDF figures stated as 4 point something billion and 5,200,000,000; the exact allocation explanation was unclear. She agreed that about 2,000,000,000 in HEDF would no longer be spent for the deficiency.

thread.speaker: Chair Mikaswan Singh
thread.said: She recorded a commitment that the deficiencies would be settled by the third week of September, before or during plenary deliberations.

thread.speaker: Chair Mikaswan Singh
thread.said: She requested a more succinct breakdown of scholarship-funding deficiencies across the different programs and asked whether the projections accounted for changes in enrollment.

thread.speaker: CHED Chair Shirley Agrupis
thread.said: She confirmed that approximately 1,000,000 students might not be able to avail themselves of the programs under the current figures.

thread.speaker: CHED Chair Shirley Agrupis
thread.said: She identified unpaid free higher education for 2025 LUC beneficiaries as 667,000,000 for 137,000 beneficiaries, and separately cited 8,600,000,000 for a proposed tuition-fee increase.

thread.speaker: Chair Mikaswan Singh
thread.said: She cited an 11,370,000,000 deficiency for new 4Ps beneficiaries and asked whether CHED had aligned the specific numbers with DSWD.

thread.speaker: CHED Chair Shirley Agrupis
thread.said: She said CHED was cleaning up and aligning the data with DSWD.

thread.speaker: CHED Chair Shirley Agrupis
thread.said: She cited 1,700,000,000 covering only 150,000 beneficiaries for one 4Ps-related category.

thread.speaker: Chair Mikaswan Singh
thread.said: She asked CHED to distinguish ongoing 4Ps beneficiaries, new 4Ps beneficiaries, and incoming TES beneficiaries from the DSWD list so that beneficiaries would not be double-counted.

thread.speaker: Chair Mikaswan Singh
thread.said: She requested further discussions among CHED, DSWD, and the committee before plenary to align the beneficiary counts and funding categories.

thread.speaker: Chair Mikaswan Singh
thread.said: She noted a reported total of 29,200,000,000 in deficit under UACTE alone and said the committee could not realistically realign the entire amount without rationalizing and prioritizing the requirements.

thread.speaker: Chair Mikaswan Singh
thread.said: She asked whether CHED, the SUCs, and DBM had met to address the disconnect between SUC enrollment projections and DBM-funded amounts so that deficiencies would not accumulate in future years.

thread.speaker: CHED Chair Shirley Agrupis
thread.said: She said CHED was working to mitigate over-enrollment and was developing an enrollment-capacity equation based on classrooms and faculty. CHED had presented the proposed approach to DBM and PASUC and was using a one-is-to-40 ratio rather than one-is-to-25.

thread.speaker: CHED Chair Shirley Agrupis
thread.said: She said about 70 of the key milestones for the proposed formula had been completed, the formula was being tested through simulations, and CHED was preparing guidelines on SUC enrollment capacity.

thread.speaker: CHED Chair Shirley Agrupis
thread.said: She said CHED did not yet have the 2027 deficiency figure, but would stabilize enrollment using a formula tied to classrooms and faculty. She also said 7.8 from HEDF had already been allocated and could no longer be used for the 2025–2026 promise.

thread.speaker: CHED Chair Shirley Agrupis
thread.said: She reiterated that 68% of 113 SUCs, or 541 including campuses, exceeded estimated enrollment capacity, while 32% were within or below capacity.

thread.speaker: CHED Director Silvett
thread.said: The director said CHED had comparative numbers for 2024–2025 and the formula, but would update the simulation using 2025–2026 enrollment and provide new results.

thread.speaker: Chair Mikaswan Singh
thread.said: She requested the updated data within about a week and said CHED also needed to discuss the discrepancy with DBM.

thread.speaker: Chair Mikaswan Singh
thread.said: She requested a formal letter from CHED listing and prioritizing the items requiring additional funding so the committee could submit them for consideration by the budget amendments review subcommittee.

thread.speaker: CHED Chair Shirley Agrupis
thread.said: She said CHED had developed more than 15 e-systems and that, among 970,000 recipients, about 720,000 already had ATM access. She also identified 331,000,000 for an information-system strategic plan.

thread.speaker: Chair Mikaswan Singh
thread.said: She instructed CHED to prioritize its requests in the formal letter, warning that any available fiscal space should go to the agency's most important programs.

topics.topic: Tertiary scholarships, TES and TDP funding gaps
topics.summary: CHED presented a proposed 70,200,000,000 budget against a 35,430,000,000 NEP amount and identified a gap of roughly 34.8 billion, including scholarship, TES, TDP, and free-higher-education deficiencies. It said the TES proposal of about 35.5 billion was reduced to about 17.1 billion, potentially affecting roughly 833,780 beneficiaries, while TDP faced a shortfall that could affect 93,000 students. Members questioned delayed releases, unused funds, access for 4Ps and solo-parent beneficiaries, and the accuracy of CHED's overlapping beneficiary categories. CHED attributed prior delays to liquidation and validation requirements, reported that about 721,000 to 722,000 students had LandBank accounts, and committed to faster direct releases and reconciliation with DSWD. Members also challenged the scholarship reduction of 697,000,000 and requested detailed allocation and program breakdowns. The committee accepted CHED's explanations provisionally but left the funding and beneficiary totals for further reconciliation and plenary consideration.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish whether CHED's proposed funding for tertiary scholarships, TES, TDP, free higher education, and related student assistance would cover continuing and incoming beneficiaries. Members also examined delayed or unused funds, the accuracy of beneficiary counts, distribution mechanisms, and what CHED would submit or do to address funding gaps and possible reductions.
topics.agency_position: CHED maintained that the proposed scholarship, TES, TDP, and free-higher-education amounts were data-driven and reflected continuing and incoming beneficiaries rather than speculative requests. It said funding reductions could leave substantial numbers of students and faculty scholars unfunded, but asserted that LandBank distribution, validated DSWD lists, digital systems, and revised enrollment-capacity formulas had improved delivery and would help prevent future deficiencies.
topics.outcome: The committee recognized CHED's improved disbursement performance but did not resolve the proposed scholarship, TES, TDP, and free-higher-education funding gaps. CHED was directed or expected to submit allocation, beneficiary, deficiency, and prioritization data and to reconcile the figures with DSWD, DBM, PASUC, and SUCs before plenary and budget-amendment deliberations.

Insisted that student-assistance allocations be distributed equitably and requested allocation data independent of legislators' individual preferences.
Sought resolution of free-higher-education deficiencies, restoration of SUC resources, and implementation of student-welfare and academic-freedom guidelines.
Supported increasing TDP funding and continuing assistance through graduation.
Supported CHED's increased scholarship funding, LandBank distribution reforms, research investment, and AI initiatives, while seeking the breakdown of scholarship reductions.
Called the reduction affecting nearly 1,000,000 students alarming and expressed support for restoring or increasing tertiary scholarship funds.
Supported addressing genuine deficiencies but required CHED and DSWD to reconcile beneficiary counts, prioritize requests, and prevent double counting before budget amendments.

thread.speaker: CHED Chairperson Shirley Agropis
thread.said: CHED proposed a 70,200,000,000 budget for 2027, but the NEP provided only 35,430,000,000, leaving a stated gap of 34,830,000,000. She said the gap represented commitments, including scholarships, subsidies, grants, and student assistance.

thread.speaker: CHED Chairperson Shirley Agropis
thread.said: CHED identified a major scholarship gap, spoken as 697,000,000,000, together with other affected programs. The figure is unclear in the transcript because the stated magnitude appears inconsistent with the surrounding budget figures.

thread.speaker: CHED Chairperson Shirley Agropis
thread.said: For free higher education, CHED proposed 16,240,000,000, while the 2027 NEP provided 6,900,000,000 or, later, 6,970,000,000. CHED said the resulting gap was 9,200,000,000 and could leave 137,000 FHE beneficiaries behind.

thread.speaker: CHED Chairperson Shirley Agropis
thread.said: CHED proposed 35,500,000,000 for TES, while the NEP provided 17,090,000,000. She said the proposal covered verified ongoing and incoming beneficiaries, and that the shortfall could leave behind 833,780 TES beneficiaries.

thread.speaker: CHED Chairperson Shirley Agropis
thread.said: CHED proposed 5,130,000,000 for TDP, but the NEP provided 3,710,000,000. She said the gap could leave 93,000 TDP beneficiaries without funding, including continuing and incoming students.

thread.speaker: CHED Chairperson Shirley Agropis
thread.said: The NEP 2027 allocation for undergraduate student financial assistance was 3,200,000,000 and included the Bagong Filipinas Merit Scholarship and the EAS Scholarship Program. The Bagong Pilipinas program had 20,000 slots for 2026 and 39,000 applicants.

thread.speaker: CHED Chairperson Shirley Agropis
thread.said: CHED said scholarships had previously taken two or three semesters to reach students. Through its LandBank partnership, subsidies would be sent directly to students rather than passing through schools.

thread.speaker: CHED Chairperson Shirley Agropis
thread.said: CHED had delivered 721,000 ATM accounts out of an overall target of 906,000 beneficiaries, or about 80% completion, with the accounts not requiring a maintaining balance.

thread.speaker: Rep. Chel Diokno
thread.said: He asked about roughly 20,000,000,000 in unobligated allotments for the second quarter of 2026 and questioned whether the approximately 24% ratio reflected inefficiency.

thread.speaker: CHED Chairperson Shirley Agropis
thread.said: She said the approximately 20,000,000,000 unobligated amount did not indicate inefficiency because CHED operated by school year. The first semester of academic year 2026–2027 began in August, so obligations were expected to rise after the June 30 cutoff.

thread.speaker: Rep. Chel Diokno
thread.said: He questioned TES access for the poorest students, citing data that only 5.54% of 4Ps graduates enrolled in college using TES against a 40% government target.

thread.speaker: CHED Chairperson Shirley Agropis
thread.said: CHED said it had partnered with DSWD and used its validated lists. For 2026, it requested support for about 50% of the 423,000 identified 4Ps beneficiaries, while 1,200,000 applications had been received for validation.

thread.speaker: Ian Amatong
thread.said: He asked for assurance that TES would be released on time, noting that students had previously received assistance a year or even two years after the relevant semester.

thread.speaker: CHED Chairperson Shirley Agropis
thread.said: CHED attributed delays to liquidation and validation requirements and said its LandBank arrangement was intended to streamline releases. It targeted 100% distribution by the end of September, with about 721,000 of 900,000 recipients already covered, and committed that TES based on DSWD data would not go beyond the semester concerned.

thread.speaker: CHED Chairperson Shirley Agropis
thread.said: She said CHED had set an August 27 processing deadline for the relevant submissions and would return to the board thereafter.

thread.speaker: Minority member Robert Nassal
thread.said: He asked how many applications from solo parents and their children CHED had received, approved, or rejected under the law requiring scholarships for solo parents and one child of a solo parent.

thread.speaker: CHED Chairperson Shirley Agropis
thread.said: CHED reported 14,906 solo parents and 31,400 beneficiaries for the first semester of academic year 2026–2027. She undertook to submit the regional list.

thread.speaker: Minority member Robert Nassal
thread.said: He cited 2,057,000,000 in 2025 funding with zero obligation and zero disbursement, 21,700,000,000 for TES with only 25% disbursed, and 2,392,000,000 for free higher education that was allowed to lapse. He questioned why billions in education assistance remained unused.

thread.speaker: CHED Chairperson Shirley Agropis
thread.said: She said scholarship programs were governed by GAA guidelines and depended on validated DSWD data. For TES, CHED reported that 2025 disbursement had reached almost 31% during catch-up and 99.84% to date.

thread.speaker: Rep. Edgar Erice
thread.said: He requested a statistical list showing how CHED distributed program allocations in 2026 and its plan for allocating the programs in 2027, to be submitted before plenary deliberations.

thread.speaker: Rep. Maria Cristina Lopez
thread.said: She asked CHED to confirm 68,684,852 free-higher-education beneficiaries across LUCs and 247,000 ongoing beneficiaries, and asked about beneficiaries for 2027.

thread.speaker: CHED Chairperson Shirley Agropis
thread.said: She said that, if funded, 93,000 beneficiaries would be supported in the following year.

thread.speaker: Rep. Renee Co
thread.said: She asked whether the previously discussed 12,000,000,000 for free-higher-education deficiencies was sufficient, including deficiencies through 2027, and asked for updated calculations and documentation.

thread.speaker: CHED official
thread.said: CHED said the past four years' deficiency had been addressed through an agreed calculation, but a new deficiency was developing for 2025 and 2026. It said CHED, PASUC, and DBM were considering a 1:40 faculty-student ratio instead of the 1:25 ratio, which CHED considered unrealistic.

thread.speaker: Rep. Renee Co
thread.said: She requested documentation on the deficiency calculation and urged CHED to submit it during the budget season.

thread.speaker: Rep. Cheeno Almario
thread.said: He asked why TDP and TES were prioritized as they were, citing approximately 2.9 for TDP and 30.8 for TES in 2026, and sought clarification on renewal under Memorandum Circular No. 2 of 2026.

thread.speaker: CHED Chairperson Shirley Agropis
thread.said: She said beneficiaries supported in 2026 should continue to be supported in 2027 under the unified TDP policy. She warned that without continuation funding, the 2026 support could become a one-time grant and that 93,000 students could be deprived.

thread.speaker: Rep. Cheeno Almario
thread.said: He proposed that the committee consider increasing the TDP budget allocation so learners could continue accessing higher education.

thread.speaker: CHED Chairperson Shirley Agropis
thread.said: CHED reported that about 80% of the distribution had been completed, with 722,751 students stated in the real-time LandBank system; elsewhere in the exchange, the figure was stated as 722,000 out of more than 900,000.

thread.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
thread.said: He asked about the Barangay Pilipinas Merit Scholarship, including the reported 150% budget increase, the number of supported students, and how scholars were selected.

thread.speaker: CHED Chairperson Shirley Agropis
thread.said: She said the program targeted the top five graduates of senior high school who entered one of the 10 priority programs and a top-performing state or private university. The stated support was 80,000 for private-school tuition, 90,000 for a state university, and 45,000 per semester for allowance; there were 20,000 slots and more than 39,000 applicants.

thread.speaker: CHED Chairperson Shirley Agropis
thread.said: She said the merit formula considered grades, household income, and first-generation status, with priority for households with income from 0 to 2,000,000. Regional distribution was based proportionately on senior-high-school graduates.

thread.speaker: CHED Chairperson Shirley Agropis
thread.said: She reiterated that CHED proposed 70,200,000,000 and received 35,000,000,000 in the NEP, leaving a 34,000,000,000 gap. She identified 29,000,000,000 for scholarships, 697,000,000 for digital transformation, 331,000,000 for digital-system development, and 258,000,000 for monitoring and evaluation; the total gap was later stated as 34,800,000,000.

thread.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
thread.said: He confirmed that 697,000,000 had been removed from scholarships and asked which scholarship programs had lost funding.

thread.speaker: CHED Chairperson Shirley Agropis
thread.said: She confirmed the reduction and said CHED would submit the breakdown. She explained that the amount included student scholarships and advanced-degree support for faculty, including 870 ongoing scholars who could become unfunded if 2027 funding was not provided.

thread.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
thread.said: He asked whether CHED's budget included research and development funding, noting that higher education's role extended beyond graduation to research, innovation, and national competitiveness.

thread.speaker: CHED official
thread.said: CHED said faculty-researcher capacity building was included in its proposal, while project funding would come from HEDF. It cited 1,400,000,000 allocated from HEDF for funded projects, described as 15% of the HEDF program.

thread.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
thread.said: He again asked which scholarship program constituted the missing 697,000,000 and requested geographical information on scholars.

thread.speaker: CHED official
thread.said: CHED said the reduction included student and faculty advanced-degree scholarships. It also said the geographical distribution data could be submitted and that applications were handled through the online platform.

thread.speaker: Deputy Speaker Ferdinand Hernandez
thread.said: He asked about the TES reduction from a proposal of 35,500,000,000 supporting 1,677,000 beneficiaries to 17,098,803,000 supporting 843,000 beneficiaries.

thread.speaker: CHED official
thread.said: CHED confirmed the reduction and stated that about 843,000 students would be covered. The Deputy Speaker characterized the difference as a serious loss affecting nearly 1,000,000 students.

thread.speaker: CHED official
thread.said: CHED stated that the combined total for free higher education, TES, and TDP was 29,167,557,000 and covered 1,064,000 students. It later described the total funding difference as 11,000,000,000.

thread.speaker: Deputy Speaker Ferdinand Hernandez
thread.said: He said he would support the CHED budget and called the loss of 11,000,000,000 affecting approximately 1,000,000 scholarship beneficiaries alarming. He also urged coordination with the Office of the President on the Barangay Pilipinas scholarship.

thread.speaker: CHED official
thread.said: For TDP, the official cited a 400,000 family-income threshold, other guidelines, regional screening, and an online portal. The official said a private or local college needed CHED accreditation and compliance with program, faculty, facilities, and sustainability standards.

thread.speaker: Chair Mikaswan Singh
thread.said: The Chair asked for the status of the 12,000,000,000 in free-higher-education deficiency payments to SUCs, described as roughly 7,500,000,000 from HEDF and 4,800,000,000 from the GAA.

thread.speaker: CHED Chairperson Shirley Agropis
thread.said: CHED said a joint memorandum circular with DBM had been signed and that 9,700,000,000 had been released for deficiencies. It said 108 SUCs had been processed or released, subject to completion and validation of requirements.

thread.speaker: Chair Mikaswan Singh
thread.said: She questioned how the 9,700,000,000 accounted for all SUCs and asked about remaining deficiencies and the treatment of approximately 2,000,000,000 in HEDF.

thread.speaker: CHED Chairperson Shirley Agropis
thread.said: CHED explained that the amounts reflected HEDF and congressional sources and confirmed that the approximately 2,000,000,000 would no longer be spent from HEDF for the deficiency, subject to submission and validation.

thread.speaker: Chair Mikaswan Singh
thread.said: The Chair and CHED set the third week of September as the target for settling the deficiencies, coinciding with the expected plenary deliberation period.

thread.speaker: Chair Mikaswan Singh
thread.said: She requested a concise breakdown of the scholarship-funding deficiency, including the potentially affected number of students.

thread.speaker: CHED Chairperson Shirley Agropis
thread.said: CHED confirmed that approximately 1,000,000 beneficiaries could be affected. It cited 667,000,000 for unpaid free higher education involving 137,000 beneficiaries and 8,600,000,000 as a separate amount associated with increased tuition fees.

thread.speaker: Chair Mikaswan Singh
thread.said: She asked whether CHED had aligned with DSWD on the numbers for 4Ps beneficiaries and whether the various ongoing, new, and incoming TES categories might double-count beneficiaries.

thread.speaker: Chair Mikaswan Singh
thread.said: She requested CHED, DSWD, and the committee staff to reconcile the beneficiary categories before plenary and specifically asked Vice Chair Monique to facilitate the discussions.

thread.speaker: Chair Mikaswan Singh
thread.said: The Chair said the committee could not realistically realign 29,200,000,000 for UACTE alone and would need to rationalize, prioritize, and verify the deficiency figures before deciding what could be funded.

thread.speaker: CHED Director Silvett
thread.said: CHED said it would update its simulation using 2025–2026 enrollment data and provide new results showing the difference between estimated capacity and actual enrollment.

thread.speaker: Chair Mikaswan Singh
thread.said: She asked CHED to prepare the enrollment-capacity analysis, expressing concern that the 68% of SUCs reported to have exceeded estimated capacity could generate billions in future deficiencies.

thread.speaker: Chair Mikaswan Singh
thread.said: She requested a formal letter from CHED listing and prioritizing the items requiring additional funding so the request could be submitted to the budget amendments review subcommittee.

thread.speaker: CHED Chairperson Shirley Agropis
thread.said: CHED said it was ready to submit the formal request and justification, including the priority for undergraduate and faculty scholarships and the 331,000,000 information-system request.

topics.topic: CHED FY 2027 funding gap and restoration request
topics.summary: CHED Chairperson Shirley Agrupis presented a proposed budget of about 70.2 billion against an NEP allocation of about 35.43 billion, leaving a gap of roughly 34.8 billion. She identified major unfunded priorities including scholarships, free higher education, digital transformation, and monitoring and evaluation, and said the full request was data-driven. Rep. Rufus Rodriguez supported restoring the entire gap, while Brian Poe focused on the scholarship reduction and asked about AI funding; CHED reported 5,000,000 for AI initiatives. Chair Mikaswan Singh questioned the release of about 9.7 billion in SUC deficiency payments and sought assurance that remaining deficiencies would be settled by the third week of September. Singh also required CHED to reconcile scholarship and 4Ps beneficiary counts with DSWD and submit enrollment-capacity data and a prioritized formal request. The issue remained subject to validation and budget amendments review rather than being resolved at the hearing.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish the size and composition of CHED's FY 2027 funding gap, which priorities were unfunded, and whether the agency's beneficiary and deficiency estimates were accurate. Members also sought commitments for detailed breakdowns, coordination with DSWD and DBM, and settlement of SUC deficiencies.
topics.agency_position: CHED maintained that its requests were data-driven and that the FY 2027 NEP left a 34,800,000,000 gap involving scholarships, free higher education, digital transformation, monitoring and evaluation, and other commitments. CHED sought restoration of the full gap, while acknowledging that beneficiary data, 4Ps-related categories, SUC deficiencies, and priority rankings still had to be reconciled with the committee, DSWD, DBM, and SUCs.
topics.outcome: CHED's full 34,800,000,000 restoration request was not approved during the hearing. The committee requested detailed and prioritized submissions, further validation with DSWD, DBM, and SUCs, and indicated that any amendments would undergo review before plenary.

positions.position: Supported restoring the entire 34,800,000,000 CHED gap and said he would strongly recommend increasing CHED's budget.
Sought scrutiny of the 697,000,000 scholarship reduction and highlighted CHED's AI initiative and the need to examine funding for competitiveness.
Raised constitutional concerns about legislative intervention in the implementation of scholarship programs and questioned the legal basis and accessibility of scholarship criteria.

Supported increasing CHED's budget and urged attention to private higher education institutions, where more than half of college students were enrolled.

thread.said: The NEP provided 35,430,000,000, about 50% less than the proposal, leaving nearly half of CHED's identified priority projects unfunded. She described the 34,830,000,000 gap as representing commitments CHED might not fully sustain.

thread.said: She said the 34,800,000,000 gap would prevent CHED from fully sustaining its commitments and advancing reforms if it remained unaddressed.

thread.said: For free higher education, CHED proposed 16,240,000,000 but said the NEP provided only 6,970,000,000, leaving a 9,200,000,000 gap and potentially leaving 137,000 FHE beneficiaries behind.

thread.said: CHED proposed 35,500,000,000 for the tertiary education subsidy, while the NEP provided 17,090,000,000. She said the proposal was based on verified ongoing and incoming beneficiaries, not a drawing, and that an unfunded gap could affect 833,780 TES beneficiaries.

thread.said: He asked CHED to prioritize restoration of the entire 34,800,000,000 gap. He said he would signify at the proper time to move for approval of CHED's budget, the LAB budget, and the restoration request.

topics.topic: Scholarship and education-assistance utilization and validation
topics.summary: Rep. Chel Diokno and Rep. Robert Nassal questioned unobligated CHED allotments, access to TES, solo-parent scholarship implementation, and billions in unused or lapsed education-assistance funds. CHED attributed the delays to school-year timing, reliance on DSWD lists, validation requirements, and processing constraints, while reporting improved utilization and committing to submit beneficiary lists and address rejected cases. Rep. Mauricio Domogan challenged the centralized processing system and the 7,500 assistance amount, while CHED explained that regional offices validated applications before central processing and agreed to verify Baguio's submissions. Rep. Brian Poe highlighted the LandBank system, through which CHED reported about 722,000 students had received accounts, and reviewed the Barangay Pilipinas Merit Scholarship's 20,000 slots and more than 39,000 applicants. Chair Mikaswan Singh focused on SUC deficiencies, citing a 12,000,000,000 initial requirement, a 9,700,000,000 release or processing amount, and a possible 29,200,000,000 UACTE deficit. CHED committed to settle deficiencies by the third week of September, reconcile 4Ps beneficiary categories with DSWD, update its enrollment-capacity simulations, and submit a prioritized funding request.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish why CHED had unobligated or delayed scholarship and education-assistance funds, how beneficiaries were identified and validated, and whether the reported beneficiary gaps reflected funding, processing, or data problems. Members also sought assurances on the settlement of SUC deficiencies and requested beneficiary and utilization data before budget deliberations.
topics.agency_position: CHED maintained that delayed obligations and utilization were primarily caused by school-year timing, validation and listing requirements, regional processing, liquidation rules, and SUC over-enrollment rather than an inability to deliver assistance. It said utilization had substantially improved, while committing to submit lists, reconcile beneficiary data with DSWD, settle SUC deficiencies by the third week of September, and provide updated capacity and funding information.
topics.outcome: CHED provided explanations for the low or delayed utilization and reported substantial catch-up, but the committee required further beneficiary-list reconciliation, SUC-deficiency data, and regional validation information. Settlement of SUC deficiencies was committed for the third week of September, while the broader funding gaps and possible double counting remained subject to further discussions and budget review.

positions.position: Supported measures to expand 4Ps beneficiary coverage and pressed CHED to improve access, validation, and student support.
Questioned the rejection of solo-parent beneficiaries and challenged CHED over unused or lapsed education-assistance funds and the lack of response to referred qualified beneficiaries.
Argued that 7,500 per student was inadequate for poor students and that centralized processing was contributing to scholarship backlogs; he supported greater regional screening authority.
Supported the LandBank distribution reform and continued scholarship funding, while seeking assurance that CHED could efficiently disburse additional appropriations.

Sought assurance that SUC deficiencies would be settled, demanded reconciliation of potentially double-counted scholarship beneficiaries, and favored prioritizing only well-supported funding requests within limited fiscal space.

thread.said: CHED said it had launched an information caravan, partnered with DSWD for validation, and used DSWD's beneficiary list. For 2026, CHED requested coverage for about 50% of the 423,000 identified 4Ps beneficiaries.

thread.speaker: a CHED agency official
thread.said: The official said 1,200,000 applicants had applied for validation, creating an overwhelming workload. The official also referred to TES support of 12000% and another assistance amount of 7500%, although the transcript is unclear.

thread.speaker: a CHED agency official
thread.said: CHED identified daily subsistence and dormitory or accommodation bottlenecks as contributors to student attrition. It had partnered with Pag-IBIG to help SUCs finance dormitories.

thread.speaker: a CHED agency official
thread.said: CHED said more than 100 SUCs could access Pag-IBIG financing at 3% rather than 8% per annum, with dormitory needs ranging from 10,000 and above to as high as 62,000 students per SUC.

thread.speaker: Rep. Robert Nassal
thread.said: Rep. Nassal asked how many solo-parent and solo-parent-child scholarship applications CHED received, how many were approved or rejected, and why qualified applicants were not accommodated under RA 11861.

thread.speaker: a CHED agency official
thread.said: CHED said it had a regional list and would submit it to the committee. The official reported 14,906 solo parents and 31,400 beneficiaries for the first semester of academic year 2026–2027.

thread.speaker: a CHED agency official
thread.said: The official said CHED had not heard of the reported rejections but would immediately address any cases furnished to the chair's office, including identifying the person responsible for a rejection.

thread.speaker: Rep. Robert Nassal
thread.said: Rep. Nassal cited unused 2025 education-assistance appropriations, including zero obligation and zero disbursement for one program, only 25% disbursement for TES, and funds for UACTE that were allowed to lapse. He questioned how students could benefit while billions remained unused.

thread.speaker: a CHED agency official
thread.said: CHED attributed the problem to an unsystematic validation process and said it was not CHED's role to validate beneficiaries on the ground. It relied on clean DSWD data; the official said 2025 disbursement was almost 31% at one point and had reached 99.84% to date.

thread.speaker: Rep. Robert Nassal
thread.said: Rep. Nassal pressed CHED on another amount reported as having zero obligation and zero disbursement and referred to a list of 400 beneficiaries submitted by his office without a response.

thread.speaker: a CHED agency official
thread.said: CHED said it would establish a dynamic feedback mechanism, review the referred list, and activate a technical working group. The official said the agency operated on scholarship listings submitted through authorized channels and was only the disbursing agency.

thread.speaker: Rep. Mauricio Domogan
thread.said: Rep. Domogan said Baguio had submitted only about 1,300 students against 3,800 available slots and questioned whether the centralized process was delaying beneficiary identification. He proposed giving regional offices authority to conduct final screening under CHED guidelines.

thread.speaker: a CHED agency official
thread.said: CHED clarified that applications were submitted to regional offices, which validated enrollment and prepared a master list for the central office. After central validation, funds were distributed through ATM accounts, with the transcript stating 80%.

thread.speaker: Rep. Mauricio Domogan
thread.said: Rep. Domogan asked why the process could not be delegated further to CHED's regional line agencies and warned that Baguio could not fill its slots if the assistance remained at 7,500 per student.

thread.speaker: a CHED agency official
thread.said: CHED instructed Rep. Domogan to submit whatever number of beneficiaries had been identified and said it would process the submission. The agency also agreed to verify the apparent discrepancy with its staff.

thread.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
thread.said: Rep. Poe asked CHED to explain its LandBank scholarship-distribution partnership and whether the system demonstrated that additional scholarship funding could be efficiently disbursed.

thread.speaker: CHED Chair Shirley
thread.said: Chair Shirley said the CHED–LandBank program was intended to expedite grants after delays caused by intervening policies and unliquidated downloads. The process used regional and central validation before funds were downloaded directly.

thread.speaker: CHED Chair Shirley
thread.said: CHED reported that about 80% of the backlog had been distributed, with 722,751 students having accounts according to the real-time LandBank system.

thread.speaker: CHED Chair Shirley
thread.said: For the Barangay Pilipinas Merit Scholarship, CHED said the program targeted the top five senior-high-school graduates who enrolled in 10 priority programs and were accepted by a top-performing university. The reported support was 80,000 for private-school students, 90,000 for state-university tuition, and 45,000 per semester for allowances.

thread.speaker: CHED Chair Shirley
thread.said: CHED said the program had 20,000 slots for 2026 graduates but had received more than 39,000 applicants. Selection used grades, household income, first-generation status, and proportional regional distribution.

thread.speaker: Chair Mikaswan Singh
thread.said: Chair Singh asked for an update on the release of funds to cover SUC deficiencies under free higher education, citing a total of 12,000,000,000, including roughly 7,500,000,000 from HEDF and 4,800,000,000 from the GAA.

thread.speaker: CHED Chair Shirley
thread.said: Chair Shirley said CHED and DBM had signed a joint memorandum circular and that 9,700,000,000 had been released for the deficiencies. CHED was processing the claims of 108 SUCs and would act on additional requirements once submitted and validated.

thread.speaker: CHED Chair Shirley
thread.said: Chair Shirley clarified that the initial computation was 12,700,000,000, but the amount being addressed was 9,700,000,000 because CHED was adhering to the initial submissions and would not entertain additional claims.

thread.speaker: Chair Mikaswan Singh
thread.said: After asking when the deficiencies would be settled, Chair Singh recorded a commitment for settlement by the third week of September, coinciding with the expected plenary deliberations.

thread.speaker: Chair Mikaswan Singh
thread.said: Chair Singh asked for a concise breakdown of scholarship deficiencies and questioned whether the estimates included changing enrollment, new 4Ps beneficiaries, and graduates from the program.

thread.speaker: CHED Chair Shirley
thread.said: Chair Shirley confirmed that the recorded gap involved 1,000,000 beneficiaries and provided program breakdowns. She cited 458,000 ongoing TES beneficiaries and a 1,700,000,000 gap covering only 150,000 beneficiaries.

thread.speaker: Chair Mikaswan Singh
thread.said: Chair Singh warned that the categories of ongoing, new, and incoming 4Ps beneficiaries might be double-counted and requested alignment between CHED and DSWD before plenary.

thread.speaker: Chair Mikaswan Singh
thread.said: Chair Singh requested further CHED–DSWD discussions and a reconciliation of the beneficiary categories before plenary because the committee was having difficulty understanding the different counts.

thread.speaker: Chair Mikaswan Singh
thread.said: Chair Singh said the committee saw a 29,200,000,000 deficit under UACTE and could not realistically realign that entire amount. The committee would prioritize and streamline the claims based on an accurate beneficiary count.

thread.speaker: CHED Chair Shirley
thread.said: CHED attributed some utilization and slot problems to requirements and liquidation issues. It said the system imposed a cap on slots and that it would provide the committee with the relevant lists.

thread.speaker: Chair Mikaswan Singh
thread.said: Chair Singh asked how CHED, SUCs, and DBM would prevent another accumulation of deficiencies caused by differences between SUC enrollment projections and DBM funding.

thread.speaker: CHED Chair Shirley
thread.said: CHED said over-enrollment beyond institutional absorptive capacity was a major cause. It was developing an enrollment-capacity formula using classrooms and faculty, with a proposed faculty-student ratio of one to 40 rather than one to 25.

thread.speaker: Director Silvett
thread.said: Director Silvett said CHED had comparative enrollment and formula data but would update the simulation using 2025–2026 enrollment and provide new results.

thread.speaker: Chair Mikaswan Singh
thread.said: Chair Singh requested the updated capacity and deficiency data within about a week and said CHED also needed to discuss the figures with DBM to prevent new deficiencies from accumulating.

thread.speaker: Chair Mikaswan Singh
thread.said: Chair Singh requested a formal letter from CHED listing and breaking down the programs requiring additional funding, so the request could be submitted to the budget amendments review subcommittee.

thread.speaker: CHED Chair Shirley
thread.said: Chair Shirley said CHED was ready to submit its justification, including support for faculty scholarships and an information-system strategic plan. She reported that the plan would require 331,000,000.

thread.speaker: Chair Mikaswan Singh
thread.said: Chair Singh directed CHED to prioritize the items in its requested letter because any additional fiscal space should go to the agency's highest-priority needs.

topics.topic: 4Ps beneficiary alignment and access to student assistance
topics.summary: Rep. Chel Diokno raised the low participation of poor and 4Ps-linked students in TES and cited a 5.54% rate against a 40% government target. CHED said it was using DSWD data, targeting 50% of 423,000 identified 4Ps beneficiaries, and validating a larger applicant pool. Rep. Mauricio Domogan argued that the 7,500 assistance amount was inadequate against tuition of about 50,000 and suggested 15,500, while CHED said the amount was set by the UniFAST Board to broaden coverage and could be reviewed. Rep. Edgar Erice requested CHED's 2026 allocation data and 2027 plan before plenary. Chair Mikaswan Singh later questioned an 11,370,000,000 4Ps deficiency, possible double-counting, and a 29,200,000,000 UACTE deficit. CHED and the House undertook to reconcile the categories with DSWD and submit prioritized and updated data, leaving the final funding decision unresolved.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish whether TES and other student-assistance programs were reaching the poorest students, particularly 4Ps beneficiaries, and whether CHED's beneficiary counts and allocations were aligned with DSWD data. Members also sought to determine whether assistance amounts and program categories were sufficient, accurately counted, and free from duplication.
topics.agency_position: CHED said it was using DSWD data and regional validation to improve 4Ps targeting, while distinguishing 4Ps TES beneficiaries from broader TDP coverage. CHED acknowledged that beneficiary categories and funding requirements still required reconciliation with DSWD and committed to provide data, review guidelines, and submit prioritized funding requests.
topics.outcome: The issue was not finally resolved. CHED undertook to review the assistance amount, submit allocation and prioritization data, and reconcile 4Ps beneficiary counts with DSWD before plenary, while the committee left the amount of any additional funding and the final beneficiary totals open.

positions.position: The poorest and 4Ps-linked students were not receiving assistance at the intended rate, and CHED should support measures that improve their access and completion.
The 7,500 per-student amount was inadequate for poor students, and CHED should review the amount and streamline regional beneficiary validation.
Student assistance had to comply with UniFAST's equity mandate, and CHED should provide allocation data and a 2027 allocation plan.
CHED, DSWD, and the House needed to reconcile beneficiary categories and eliminate possible double-counting before considering substantial additional funding.

thread.speaker: Rep. Chel Diokno
thread.said: Diokno cited data showing that only 5.54% of 4Ps beneficiaries graduating from Grade 12 were enrolled in college and receiving TES, far below the government's 40% target. He questioned how CHED would improve access for the poorest students.

thread.speaker: CHED chair Shirley Agrupis
thread.said: Agrupis said CHED was aware of the gap and had launched the PBBM education information caravan in partnership with DSWD to validate 4Ps beneficiaries. CHED used DSWD data in requesting assistance for about 50% of the 423,000 identified 4Ps beneficiaries.

thread.speaker: CHED chair Shirley Agrupis
thread.said: Agrupis said the initiative had attracted 1,200,000 applicants for validation. She explained that 4Ps students could receive different forms of assistance, including TES and another subsidy, but the machine-generated transcript rendered the amounts as "12000%" and "7500%".

thread.speaker: CHED chair Shirley Agrupis
thread.said: Agrupis identified daily subsistence and dormitory or accommodation bottlenecks as contributing to attrition and said CHED was pursuing arrangements to expand student housing. This was presented as complementary support for 4Ps students' completion, rather than as a change to beneficiary validation.

thread.speaker: Rep. Mauricio Domogan and a CHED official
thread.said: Domogan asked whether congressional downloads were included in CHED's reported budget. The CHED official confirmed that the relevant 2026 amount was included and said a 28.5 amount corresponded to assistance at 7,500 per student, producing 3,768 slots; the transcript is unclear whether the 28.5 amount was in millions.

thread.speaker: Rep. Mauricio Domogan
thread.said: Domogan confirmed that the 7,500 per-student amount was fixed by the UniFAST Board or CHED policy rather than directly prescribed by statute. He questioned whether that amount was adequate for poor students.

thread.speaker: Rep. Mauricio Domogan
thread.said: Domogan said the financial-assistance program was intended for poor students, but 7,500 was insufficient when tuition in Baguio was about 50,000. He argued that the amount could mainly assist middle-class students and would not fulfill the program's mission to support the poor.

thread.speaker: CHED official
thread.said: The official explained that TES guidelines distinguished between 4Ps beneficiaries identified by DSWD and TDP applicants, who were not considered the poorest of the poor. The 7,500 amount was set by the UniFAST Board to provide broader numerical coverage, while CHED could revisit the guidelines.

thread.speaker: Rep. Mauricio Domogan
thread.said: Domogan asked how long CHED would take to revisit the assistance guidelines, recalling CHED's earlier commitment to review the amount.

thread.speaker: CHED official
thread.said: The official reaffirmed that CHED had committed to review the amount but said any decision had to be data-driven because increasing one allocation would affect other beneficiaries, numbering almost 500,000 students. The official said the 2026 allocation had already been released but that the guidelines could be revisited.

thread.speaker: Rep. Mauricio Domogan
thread.said: Domogan suggested an amount of 15,500, saying this would provide some leeway without increasing the allocation excessively. He also reported that Baguio had gathered only about 1,003 students out of the approximately 3,800 needed for the available assistance.

thread.speaker: Rep. Mauricio Domogan
thread.said: Domogan questioned CHED's centralized beneficiary-screening process and proposed giving regional offices authority to screen qualified beneficiaries under CHED guidelines, saying the existing process prolonged validation.

thread.speaker: CHED official
thread.said: The official clarified that applications were submitted to regional offices, which validated enrollment and eligibility and then submitted a master list to the central office. The central office validated the list and arranged direct ATM distribution; the transcript rendered the stated percentage as "80%."

thread.speaker: CHED official
thread.said: The official asked Domogan to submit whatever number of qualified beneficiaries had been gathered so CHED could process it. Domogan remained concerned that the available 7,500 amount and incomplete beneficiary list would prevent full utilization.

thread.speaker: Rep. Edgar Erice
thread.said: Erice requested a statistical list showing how CHED distributed program allocations in 2026 and CHED's plan for allocating the program in 2027. He asked that the information be submitted before plenary deliberations.

thread.speaker: CHED chair Shirley Agrupis
thread.said: Agrupis said the request was duly noted with the assistance of the sponsors. A CHED official also confirmed that the requested information would be provided.

thread.speaker: Chair Mikaswan Singh
thread.said: Singh asked about the status of assistance and scholarship funding, including 4Ps beneficiaries, and whether CHED had aligned specific beneficiary numbers with DSWD. She emphasized the need to avoid double-counting ongoing, new, and incoming 4Ps beneficiaries.

thread.speaker: Chair Mikaswan Singh
thread.said: Singh referred to a 11,370,000,000 deficiency for new and unfunded 4Ps beneficiaries in 2026 and directly asked whether CHED had aligned the specific numbers with DSWD. The CHED response was that the data were being cleaned up.

thread.speaker: CHED chair Shirley Agrupis
thread.said: Agrupis described a 1,700,000,000 amount covering only 150,000 beneficiaries and said the categories covered unfunded 4Ps assistance across specified academic periods. She acknowledged that the numbers still needed alignment.

thread.speaker: Chair Mikaswan Singh
thread.said: Singh asked CHED to distinguish ongoing 4Ps beneficiaries, new 4Ps beneficiaries, and incoming TES 4Ps beneficiaries on the DSWD list for 2027. She said the committee needed assurance that the categories did not duplicate beneficiaries.

thread.speaker: Chair Mikaswan Singh
thread.said: Singh requested that Vice Chair Monique Legdamayo facilitate discussions among CHED, DSWD, and the House before plenary so the beneficiary categories and figures could be reconciled.

thread.speaker: Chair Mikaswan Singh
thread.said: Singh said the committee saw a total 29,200,000,000 deficit under UACTE alone and could not realistically realign that amount without rationalizing and prioritizing the requirements. She called for an accurate representation of the deficiencies before any funding decision.

thread.speaker: CHED chair Shirley Agrupis
thread.said: Agrupis said CHED had developed more than 15 e-systems and synchronized data gathering. She reported that, out of 970,000 recipients, about 720,000 already had ATM access.

thread.speaker: CHED chair Shirley Agrupis
thread.said: Agrupis said CHED would submit a request and justification for an information-system strategic plan amounting to 331,000,000, describing the system as crucial to data-driven delivery and reconciliation.

thread.speaker: Chair Mikaswan Singh
thread.said: Singh asked CHED to submit a prioritized list in its formal funding request so that any available fiscal space would be directed to the agency's highest-priority programs.

topics.topic: SUC enrollment capacity, faculty plantilla items and staffing
topics.summary: Jude Acidre, Antonio Tinio, Cheeno Almario, and Chair Mikaswan Singh raised concerns about enrollment growth, overcrowded SUCs, faculty shortages, free higher education deficiencies, and regular plantilla positions. CHED reported that 68% of surveyed SUCs exceeded estimated capacity and supported a one-is-to-40 faculty-student ratio, with additional classrooms, faculty items, and nonteaching positions needed. Tinio cited 20,964 faculty plantilla items and asked CHED to address job-order staffing and the salary grade 12 entry level for instructors requiring a master's degree. CHED undertook to provide validated staffing data, consult the Civil Service Commission, and submit a position paper. On deficiencies, CHED reported a release of about 9.7 billion against a prior total of about 12 billion, while Singh cited a broader UACTE deficit of about 29.2 billion and requested reconciliation of the figures. The committee and CHED set a third-week-of-September target for deficiency settlement and requested updated capacity simulations and a prioritized funding letter, but the final staffing and funding requirements remained unresolved.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish whether SUCs had sufficient enrollment capacity, classrooms, regular faculty plantilla items, and nonteaching staff to support free higher education. It also examined the faculty-student ratio used for funding and enrollment projections, the treatment of job-order and contract-of-service faculty, and the salary grade and qualification of entry-level instructors.
topics.agency_position: CHED said enrollment growth had outpaced the absorptive capacity of many SUCs and that additional classrooms, regular faculty plantilla positions, and nonteaching staff were necessary to maintain education quality. CHED supported using a more realistic one-is-to-40 faculty-student ratio, was developing an enrollment-capacity formula with DBM and PASUC, and undertook to submit validated staffing and capacity data and a prioritized funding request.
topics.outcome: The hearing established that many SUCs exceeded capacity and that staffing and classroom shortages were linked to recurring free higher education deficiencies. CHED committed to submit validated plantilla and enrollment-capacity data, coordinate with DBM and DSWD, prepare a position paper on salary grades, and work toward settling deficiencies by the third week of September; the final number of new plantilla items and the long-term funding requirement remained open.

positions.position: Free higher education required funding to keep pace with enrollment and capacity needs.
SUCs needed additional regular plantilla items and a review of the salary grade for Instructor I positions because a master's degree was the minimum entry qualification.
The faculty shortage and overcrowding at SUCs threatened education quality and required coordinated action on plantilla positions and infrastructure.

The committee needed to ensure that existing SUC free higher education deficiencies were settled and that CHED, DBM, and SUCs corrected the coordination and enrollment-capacity problems causing recurring deficiencies.

thread.speaker: Jude Acidre
thread.said: Acidre raised free higher education funding and enrollment, citing 18,400,000,000 and 137,000 students, with around 83,833 availing of free higher education. The surrounding wording was unclear.

thread.speaker: CHED Chair Shirley Agrupis
thread.said: Agrupis said CHED's initial simulation covered 541 SUCs, including campuses. Sixty-eight percent exceeded estimated enrollment capacity, while 32% were within or below capacity.

thread.speaker: CHED Chair Shirley Agrupis
thread.said: Agrupis said faculty were insufficient and that CHED had worked with DBM on an equation based on a one-is-to-40 faculty-student ratio.

thread.speaker: CHED Chair Shirley Agrupis
thread.said: She said enrollment beyond the one-is-to-40 ratio required additional classrooms, faculty items, and nonteaching positions. She emphasized that CHED wanted graduates to be industry-ready and competitive, not merely diploma holders.

thread.speaker: CHED Chair Shirley Agrupis
thread.said: Agrupis described tuition differences across 115 SUCs: five collected 50 pesos per unit; 32 collected 51 to 100 per unit; 57 collected 101 to 200 per unit; 14 collected 200 to 300 per unit; and five collected 400 pesos to 1,000 per unit.

thread.speaker: CHED Chair Shirley Agrupis
thread.said: She said full harmonization of tuition fees across what the transcript rendered as 554 SUCs would require 136,000,000,000 pesos, based on a 500-plus-per-unit scenario.

thread.speaker: CHED Chair Shirley Agrupis
thread.said: Agrupis proposed a 200-pesos-per-unit leveling-up scenario requiring 11,500,000,000, compared with an existing allocation of 9,100,000,000, for an additional 2,400,000,000. She said the option would cover more than half of the SUCs.

thread.speaker: CHED Chair Shirley Agrupis
thread.said: Agrupis said higher tuition reimbursement could partially address the issue, but stressed that low tuition did not prevent graduates of some SUCs from performing highly.

thread.speaker: Antonio Tinio
thread.said: Tinio asked about raising SUC tuition to about 200 pesos per unit and the resulting funding scenarios. The transcript rendered one possible scenario as 18,000,000,018 billion, which is unclear.

thread.speaker: CHED official
thread.said: The agency said the 200-per-unit leveling-up option required 11,500,000,000, against 9.1 already allocated, or 2.4 in additional funding, and would benefit about 60 to 70% of SUCs.

thread.speaker: CHED official
thread.said: The agency identified a 500-per-unit maximum scenario within the SGV recommendation, requiring another 9,000,000,000 on top of the 9,000,000,000 already allocated.

thread.speaker: Antonio Tinio
thread.said: Tinio shifted to the longstanding use of job-order and contract-of-service faculty and the shortage of regular SUC plantilla items. He cited CHED's 2016 creation of 9,000 new items and asked what could be done about the continuing gap.

thread.speaker: Antonio Tinio
thread.said: Tinio cited 20,964 faculty plantilla items and raised the possibility of roughly 20,000 additional plantilla items, while acknowledging that the transcript was not fully clear.

thread.speaker: CHED official
thread.said: The agency said SUCs had been requesting plantilla items and that funding was needed to sustain staffing. The response did not establish a final number of new regular positions.

thread.speaker: Antonio Tinio

thread.speaker: CHED official
thread.said: The agency said the one-is-to-40 faculty-student ratio could be used to determine the number of positions needed.

thread.speaker: CHED official
thread.said: The agency undertook to work on more validated data and submit it to the committee, trying to do so by the following week and before plenary.

thread.speaker: Antonio Tinio
thread.said: Tinio questioned why Instructor I positions were at salary grade 12 when a master's degree was the minimum qualification, and argued that the entry level should not remain at salary grade 12.

thread.speaker: CHED Chair Shirley Agrupis
thread.said: Agrupis said CHED was scheduling a meeting with the Civil Service Commission to review concerns involving plantilla positions, including the instructor salary-grade issue.

thread.speaker: CHED official
thread.said: CHED agreed to prepare a position paper on the matter, while the committee directed the commission to submit its position paper.

thread.speaker: Cheeno Almario
thread.said: Almario returned to the nationwide faculty-student ratio and asked CHED to restate the average. He then cited Davao Oriental State University as having 17,000 students, 363 regular faculty, and 260 part-time faculty.

thread.speaker: CHED Chair Shirley Agrupis
thread.said: Agrupis said some SUCs had ratios of one to 25 or one to 40, while others had one to 81, one to 71, or one to 60. She offered to provide the data.

thread.speaker: CHED Chair Shirley Agrupis
thread.said: Agrupis said continued enrollment growth required more faculty plantilla positions and greater classroom capacity. Otherwise, CHED would need stricter admission policies tied to each SUC's absorptive capacity.

thread.speaker: Chair Mikaswan Singh
thread.said: Singh asked for the status of free higher education deficiency payments to SUCs and cited a prior total of 12,000,000,000, consisting of roughly 7,500,000,000 from the higher education development fund and roughly 4,800,000,000 from the GAA.

thread.speaker: CHED Chair Shirley Agrupis
thread.said: Agrupis said CHED and DBM had signed a joint memorandum circular and that 9,700,000,000 had been released for deficiencies. She said CHED was processing the release and had covered 108 SUCs, subject to compliance with requirements.

thread.speaker: Chair Mikaswan Singh
thread.said: Singh reconciled the reported amounts, citing 9,400,000,000 for deficient billings from 2022 to 2024 and 341,000,000 without submission, and asked what remained of the 12,000,000,000 total.

thread.speaker: CHED Chair Shirley Agrupis
thread.said: Agrupis said the initial computation had been 12,700,000,000 because of the faculty-student-ratio issue and discrepancies in SUC submissions. She said CHED was holding to the initial submissions and would not entertain additional claims.

thread.speaker: Chair Mikaswan Singh
thread.said: Singh sought assurance that no SUC deficiencies remained unpaid and asked when all deficiencies would be settled, noting that the committee needed to make good on its commitment before SUC budget deliberations.

thread.speaker: Chair Mikaswan Singh
thread.said: Singh stated the settlement commitment as the third week of September, aligning it with the expected plenary deliberation period.

thread.speaker: CHED Chair Shirley Agrupis
thread.said: Agrupis confirmed the third-week-of-September target, subject to SUC submission of additional requirements.

thread.speaker: Chair Mikaswan Singh
thread.said: Singh asked whether CHED, SUCs, and DBM had coordinated to prevent future deficiencies caused by differences between SUC enrollment projections and DBM-funded amounts.

thread.speaker: CHED Chair Shirley Agrupis
thread.said: Agrupis identified over-enrollment beyond SUC absorptive capacity as a principal cause. CHED was developing an equation based on classrooms and faculty, using a one-is-to-40 ratio rather than the earlier one-is-to-25 standard.

thread.speaker: CHED Chair Shirley Agrupis
thread.said: Agrupis said about 70 of the key milestones had been completed in developing and testing a proposed enrollment-capacity formula under RA 10931 and applicable UNIFAS guidelines. The transcript later rendered this progress as roughly 37 milestones, which is inconsistent and unclear.

thread.speaker: CHED Chair Shirley Agrupis
thread.said: Agrupis reported that a rapid survey found 68% of 113 SUCs, or 541 including campuses, exceeded estimated enrollment capacity, while 32% were within or below capacity.

thread.speaker: Director Silvett
thread.said: Director Silvett said CHED had comparative numbers for 2024-2025 and the formula but could not provide the requested degree of excess capacity during the hearing. CHED would update the simulation using 2025-2026 enrollment and provide new results.

thread.speaker: Chair Mikaswan Singh
thread.said: Singh requested the updated enrollment-capacity data within about a week and said CHED also needed to discuss the discrepancy with DBM to prevent deficiencies from accumulating.

thread.speaker: Chair Mikaswan Singh
thread.said: Singh requested a formal letter from CHED listing and prioritizing items for additional funding so the committee's budget amendments review subcommittee could consider them.

thread.speaker: CHED Chair Shirley Agrupis
thread.said: Agrupis said CHED was already preparing the requested submission and would reconcile the figures and priorities, including faculty development and scholarship-related requirements.

topics.topic: Student housing and PPP dormitory facilities
topics.summary: Rep. Chel Diokno and Ian Amatong raised student housing as an infrastructure need affecting disadvantaged students' access and graduation. CHED said more than 100 SUCs could avail of Pag-IBIG financing and proposed one dormitory per SUC, with a possible government-funded second unit through a multiyear allocation. The agency cited financing at 3% rather than 8% per annum, a 10-year period, and an initial indicative cost of about 100 to 120 million per unit. CHED said small facilities would have 20 to 30 rooms, medium facilities 50 to 80 rooms, and large facilities would be three to five stories, depending on the SUC's land and capacity. Rep. Amatong requested the design and costing, and CHED agreed to provide them and arrange further consultations. Final design, capacity, and funding commitments remained open.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish how CHED proposed to address student housing shortages affecting access and graduation, including the scale, financing, design, cost, and capacity of dormitory facilities. Members also asked whether CHED could provide the dormitory design and costing and consult more regularly with legislators and universities.
topics.agency_position: CHED stated that student accommodation was a major infrastructure bottleneck and that it was pursuing a Pag-IBIG financing arrangement, potentially through a PPP structure, to support dormitory construction. The agency proposed one dormitory per SUC, with a possible government-funded complement, but said final capacity and design would depend on each SUC's land and absorptive and payment capacity.
topics.outcome: CHED presented a proposed Pag-IBIG PPP-based dormitory approach, an initial per-unit allocation, and indicative room categories. The design, final costing, facility capacity, and broader multiyear government allocation remained subject to ongoing work and were not finally resolved during the hearing.

positions.position: Supported measures to expand dormitories and other assistance for disadvantaged students and urged colleagues to support Akbayan's dormitory-related bill.
Supported the dormitory proposal but sought a standard design, detailed costing, capacity information, a copy of the documents, and more reliable CHED consultations.
Supported developing dormitories through a standard design and a Pag-IBIG PPP or similar financing arrangement, with facilities scaled to the circumstances of individual SUCs.

topics.topic: Legal Education Board program funding
topics.summary: Rep. Rufus Rodriguez asked CHED to identify its full unfunded requirement and supported restoration of the entire 34,800,000,000 gap, including LEB funding. CHED Chairperson Shirley A. Agrupis confirmed the total and said detailed smaller requirements would be submitted to the appropriations committee. LEB Commissioner Justin Kalnapala reported that CLEP, LEAP, and LEADS each received 0 pesos in the proposed budget. An agency official presented LEB requests including 216,000,000 for CLEP, 57,000,000 for LEADS, 83,000,000 for LEAP, 24,000,000 for an unclear additional program, and 51,000,000 for LERP augmentation. Rep. Sarah Elago demanded restoration of the affected programs, including safe-spaces, faculty-development, and scholarship funding. Rep. Cheeno Almario later manifested support for increasing the Clinical Legal Education Program budget. The matter was deferred, with detailed submissions and committee review still pending.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish the amount of CHED's unfunded requirements and whether Legal Education Board (LEB) programs, including clinical legal education, scholarships, faculty development, and related support, required restoration. It also considered whether the committee should support an increase or restoration of the requested funding.

topics.outcome: The committee did not finally approve or restore the LEB funding during the hearing. CHED was expected to submit detailed requirements, while members manifested support for restoration and the chair deferred consideration to the proper time.

CHED Chairperson Shirley A. Agrupis said CHED had completed research identifying equity groups and had incorporated them into policy and scholarship priorities. CHED had proposed 418,000,000, or about 418 million, under the equity-group proposal. The exchange ended with Rep. topics.topic: Higher-education research, development and artificial intelligence
topics.summary: CHED Chairperson Shirley Agropis presented a proposed budget of about 70.2 billion against an NEP allocation of about 35 billion, identifying a roughly 34.8 billion gap that included scholarship, digital-system, and monitoring shortfalls. Rep. Brian Poe asked which items had been reduced, clarified the 697,000,000 scholarship gap, and requested its breakdown. He also asked about CHED's AI road map and research-and-development funding. CHED said it had adopted a national AI in higher education policy, allocated 5,000,000 for several AI applications, and was building faculty capacity. For research, CHED said faculty-researcher capacity building was in its proposal while project funding was placed under HEDF, including about 1.4 billion for pillar-funded projects. CHED undertook to submit the scholarship breakdown, research initiatives, and scholar-distribution data, while Rep. Poe expressed support for additional or restored CHED funding.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish which higher-education priorities were reduced or excluded from CHED's FY 2027 budget, particularly digital transformation, artificial intelligence, research and development, and scholarships. It also asked how CHED was funding AI and research initiatives and which scholars would be affected by the reported reductions.
topics.agency_position: CHED maintained that digital transformation, artificial intelligence, faculty capacity building, and research were central to its modernization and Achieve Agenda. It said the ISSP request was not funded in 2027, AI initiatives had a 5,000,000 allocation, faculty-researcher capacity building was included in the proposal, and research projects were to be funded through HEDF, including 1,400,000,000 for pillar-funded projects.
topics.outcome: CHED explained that AI and research activities were being funded through limited allocations and HEDF rather than through a clearly identified standalone research-and-development line. The scholarship breakdown and scholar-distribution data were to be submitted, but the adequacy of the AI, digital-transformation, research, and scholarship funding remained open.

positions.position: He viewed the scholarship reduction and apparent lack of a distinct research-and-development budget as concerns requiring scrutiny. He supported CHED's budget, AI initiatives, research funding, and restoration or addition of funding.
