thread.speaker: Rep. Plato
thread.said: Rep. Plato asked about DMW's database consolidation under Republic Act 11641 and whether OFW records were experiencing mismatches or glitches in the registration system.

thread.speaker: DMW Secretary
thread.said: The Secretary said DMW was enhancing its IT services and working closely with DICT under the President's e-government oversight. The coordination covered database registration as well as cybersecurity.

thread.speaker: DMW Secretary
thread.said: The Secretary said DMW had dealt with major attacks on its IT facilities and had resolved many issues, while continuing to work with DICT. Glitches in e-registration remained, but DMW was providing assistance through its systems and help lines.

thread.speaker: DMW Secretary
thread.said: The Secretary invited Rep. Plato to revisit DMW's innovation hub and referred to lobby desktop systems, monitors, and other IT services supporting e-registration and remote technical assistance.

thread.speaker: DMW Secretary
thread.said: The Secretary reported that 1,500,000 OFW passes had been issued, facilitating the digital replacement of the former OEC and allowing OFWs to exit the country through the digital issuance system.

thread.speaker: DMW Secretary
thread.said: The Secretary presented the OFW Pass and the volume of digital issuances as evidence that DMW's e-registration system was moving in the right direction. DMW would continue partnering with DICT.

thread.speaker: Rep. Plato
thread.said: Rep. Plato warned that DMW's database contained highly sensitive personal data, including passports, employment contracts, salaries, and family information. He asked about the protection budget for the IT infrastructure program in light of cyber threats and unauthorized data scraping.

thread.speaker: DMW Secretary
thread.said: The Secretary said DMW monitored cyberattacks 24/7 and that daily attacks had been thwarted. Some email accounts had been affected on certain occasions, but the database itself had not been breached.

thread.speaker: DMW Secretary
thread.said: The Secretary said DMW would continue to step up its response aggressively and was working with the CICC and DICT cybersecurity program. DMW maintained 24/7 monitoring and would act at the earliest indication, including on mere suspicion or fear of a cyberattack.

thread.speaker: Rep. Plato

topics.topic: DMW staffing, headquarters, and regional facilities
topics.summary: Rep. Rufus Rodriguez pressed DMW to explain the reduction from its proposed budget and supported restoration of about 2 billion. Secretary Hans Leo Cacdac said DMW sought the restoration for the action fund, overseas service activities, administration, facilities, NMP, the OFW Hospital, and additional migrant workers' offices, and said the agency had authority to build its main headquarters at Agham Road. OWWA separately requested about 2 billion for MOOE, operations, capital outlay, seafarer welfare and regional facilities, global centers, and scholarships; its administrator cited serious seismic-safety deficiencies in an existing building. Rep. Nico Raul Daza then questioned whether NMP could sustain newly free maritime training despite a budget reduction, and NMP answered that personnel and operating funds were adequate but requested 92 million for additional training capacity and information systems. NMP said it could train about 30,000 seafarers in 2027 and would study future centers in Cavite and Davao for a possible 2028 budget proposal. The committee requested supporting documents and manifested support, but the funding increases were not finally resolved in the excerpt.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish whether DMW and its attached agencies had sufficient personnel, operating funds, capital outlay, headquarters, regional offices, and training facilities to deliver services to overseas Filipino workers and seafarers. Members also asked what additional funding and facilities were required and whether the requested expansions were sustainable.
topics.agency_position: DMW and its attached agencies maintained that their proposed budgets were insufficient for staffing, operations, repatriation, headquarters and regional facilities, seafarer welfare centers, and expanded free maritime training. DMW requested restoration of 2,000,000,000, while OWWA separately requested 2,000,000,000; NMP said its personnel and operating funds could sustain free training but sought 92,000,000 in capital outlay for additional training capacity.
topics.outcome: The committee received the agencies' facility and staffing requirements and members expressed support for the requested increases. DMW's 2,000,000,000 restoration and OWWA's 2,000,000,000 request were not finally approved in the excerpt; DMW was asked to submit supporting details, while the Agham Road headquarters, Admin Building move, NMP training expansion, and future Cavite and Davao facilities remained implementation or planning commitments.

positions.position: Supported restoration of 2,000,000,000 for DMW, urged the committee and Speaker to support the increase, and pressed for an itemized submission. He also supported additional OWWA funding and raised the need for headquarters and regional-facility improvements.
Supported increased funding for DMW and NMP, particularly to sustain free maritime training and expand training facilities.

Sought restoration of 2,000,000,000 while stating that DMW would cooperate with the national budget framework. He supported construction of a new DMW main office at Agham Road and retention of the existing NCR facility.

positions.position: Maintained that NMP could sustain free maritime training with its proposed personnel and operating budget, but sought 92,000,000 for training-building and information-systems requirements.
Supported an additional 2,000,000,000 for MOOE, operations, capital outlay, seafarer welfare and regional facilities, global centers, and the congressional migrant workers scholarship program.

topics.outcome: The agency explained the scholarship program and included an additional 50,000,000 for it within OWA's total additional request of 2,000,000,000. The transcript ended before the committee ruled on the scholarship allocation or approved the requested increase.

hearings.title: COMMITTEE ON APPROPRIATIONS - BUDGET BRIEFING/HEARING OF THE FY 2027 PROPOSED BUDGET: (DENR)

topics.topic: DENR FY2027 budget reduction and institutional amendments
topics.summary: The DENR presented a requested FY 2027 budget of about 28.04 billion and later disclosed that it had proposed about 55.04 billion to the DBM, including tier two. Members questioned the substantial reduction and identified priority augmentations for land management, patent registration, foreshore mapping, the Land Management Bureau building, and water-resource programs. Rep. Rufus Rodriguez moved an additional 556,617,000 pesos, and the committee approved it subject to consolidation and available fiscal space. The DENR also committed to follow up on Nagat Island monitoring, Eastern Samar mining rehabilitation, and stewardship-approval thresholds. Rep. Rodriguez separately sought 400,000,000 for rehabilitation of previously planted areas, but the chair required a new written request. The Appropriations chair directed the DENR to submit a formal and prioritized list for budget amendments review before plenary deliberations.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish the DENR's FY 2027 request, the extent and reasons for the reduction from the amount proposed to the DBM, and which additional programs or institutional amendments should receive funding. It also examined whether the proposed augmentation was approved or remained subject to available fiscal space and further review.
topics.agency_position: The DENR said its proposed budget was needed to carry out its broad environmental and natural-resources mandate, but it acknowledged that priority augmentation requests were necessary after the reduction from the amount proposed to the DBM. The department agreed to submit a formal, prioritized request and undertook specific follow-up actions on monitoring, mining rehabilitation, and approval thresholds.
topics.outcome: The committee approved an additional 556,617,000 pesos in principle, but the presiding officer qualified the action as subject to executive fiscal space and final apportionment across agencies. Further DENR institutional amendments, including the proposed 400,000,000 rehabilitation funding, were left for formal submission, prioritization, and review by the budget amendments review subcommittee.

Supported additional monitoring and permanent competent staffing for Nagat Island and questioned the concentration of the budget in the Office of the Secretary.

topics.topic: Mining monitoring, enforcement, and illegal-mining operations
topics.summary: Members questioned whether the roughly 53.6 million national MGB monitoring budget and the 12.829 million Caraga regional budget were adequate for illegal-mining enforcement, particularly in Dinagat Island. DENR committed to visit Dinagat, review mining claims, issue a proper public statement, and consider closure where warranted, but no final closure decision was recorded. Rep. Alexander Pimentel pressed DENR to release 10 seized conveyances in a Surigao del Sur case, and the secretary assured him that release would occur the following day. Members also sought action on Chinese nationals in illegal mining, small-scale mining applications, white-clay extraction and stockpiles, and quarry permits; the agency committed to reports, inspections, operator lists, and coordination. The agency stated that small-scale mining was capped at 50,000 metric tons per annum and cited 3.1 billion pesos for EMB and 1.89 billion for MGB. The hearing ended with several actions committed but with the Dinagat closure, white-clay seizure order, and mangrove earth-balling suspension unresolved.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish whether DENR and the Mines and Geosciences Bureau had sufficient budget, personnel, and authority to monitor mining and quarrying, stop illegal operations, and act on confiscation, closure, and permit-compliance issues. Members also sought specific follow-through on Dinagat Island, small-scale mining, white-clay stockpiles, quarry permits, and mining claims.
topics.agency_position: DENR maintained that monitoring, enforcement, seizure, confiscation, and environmental-compliance functions were being carried out under the Mining Act and related regulations, while acknowledging regional staffing and monitoring limitations. The agency repeatedly committed to site visits, claims and permit reviews, reports, equipment release, operator lists, and coordination with regional offices, but several requested actions remained subject to evaluation or verification.
topics.outcome: The agency provided budget and regulatory explanations and made multiple commitments, including a Dinagat visit and claims review, equipment release, reports and operator lists, permit inspections, and an assessment before plenary. Closure of Dinagat mining, issuance of a white-clay seizure order, suspension of mangrove earth-balling, and several enforcement questions remained subject to further verification or agency action.

positions.position: Dinagat Island required a specific and more active monitoring response because of its mining activity and ecological vulnerability; DENR should visit the island, clarify the status of Hibusong Island and East Coast Mining Corporation, and consider closure.
DENR Caraga should comply with final and executory release orders and promptly release equipment seized in the Surigao del Sur anti-illegal-mining case.

DENR needed to investigate possible organized illegal mining involving Chinese nationals, provide reports and operator lists, and reconsider or suspend the mangrove earth-balling memorandum pending reliable scientific evidence.
Illegal logging, quarrying, and mining required stronger enforcement and permit compliance, with local governments also taking restrictive measures to protect resources.

DENR should process pending small-scale mining applications, conduct field evaluations in Davao de Oro, provide operator lists, and ensure that operations claiming to be small-scale did not exceed their legal production limits.

positions.position: The alleged white-clay operation was effectively large-scale and required DENR intervention, seizure action, and potentially a total ban to protect the district.
DENR lacked sufficient manpower to monitor small-scale mining and should augment personnel and enforce restrictions on mercury and cyanide.

actions.action: Provide the list of large-scale and small-scale operators in the region.
Provide the deputization order for provincial environmental task-force members.
Augment small-scale mining monitoring manpower and strengthen enforcement concerning mercury and cyanide.
Issue or consider issuing a DENR seizure or confiscation order for the white-clay stockpile.
Review quarry permits, ECCs, expiration dates, and compliance affecting the bypass projects, and submit a report.

actions.action: Conduct an immediate assessment of the mining operation and agreement and provide results before plenary.

thread.speaker: DENR Undersecretary for Finance
thread.said: The proposed 2027 MGB budget for monitoring and enhanced enforcement against illegal mining activities was approximately 53,600,000.

thread.speaker: Mines and Geosciences Bureau director
thread.said: The program covered large- and small-scale miners, including unregistered small-scale miners, by registering, capacitating, and training them in proper mining and ore processing, in addition to regular monitoring.

thread.speaker: DENR Undersecretary for Finance
thread.said: The monitoring budget was about 53,600,000 for the whole Philippines. The transcript also contains a fragmented reference to 3,600,000.

thread.speaker: Minority member Kaka Bag-ao
thread.said: She questioned the absence of a specific monitoring allocation for Dinagat Island, citing mining activity and the vulnerability of Hibusong Island. She said there was no approved mineral exploration in Hibusong Island, referred to East Coast Mining Corporation and a 2014 suspension order, and asked why DENR officials were not visiting the island to verify mining claims and operations.

thread.speaker: DENR Undersecretary for Finance
thread.said: Caraga had a budget of 12,829,000 for the whole region, with no specific Dinagat Island breakdown because there was no PENRO there. She said other regional allocations could be used for monitoring environmental activities on the island.

thread.speaker: Minority member Kaka Bag-ao
thread.said: She asked DENR to visit Dinagat Island, explain the status of Hibusong Island and East Coast Mining Corporation to residents, and consider declaring the affected area closed to mining. She said the area was less than 1,000 hectares and that barangays had identified more than 100 conservation areas.

thread.speaker: DENR official for Operations
thread.said: He committed to visit Dinagat Island, either personally or through the head of enforcement, and said there would be no mining in the Bonsai Forest. He also committed to a proper regional statement, a review of mining claims, and possibly assigning someone through the PENRO specifically to monitor mining areas.

thread.speaker: DENR official for Operations
thread.said: He said DENR could automatically close the area if, after checking the existing mining claims, closure was warranted. The chair also requested a copy of the suspension order for dissemination to Hibusong residents.

thread.speaker: Rep. Alexander Pimentel
thread.said: He confirmed that mining activities were governed by Republic Act number 7,942, the Philippine Mining Act, and that DENR procedures covered administrative seizure and confiscation. He then questioned why Caraga had not released equipment seized in a January 2025 anti-illegal-mining operation in the Caracan River area of Cantilan, Surigao del Sur, despite final release orders.

thread.speaker: MGB Director Larry Hirades
thread.said: He confirmed that equipment had been confiscated and that a confiscation panel had issued two sets of release orders. He said the regional office had been constrained from releasing the equipment because an enforcement agency, identified in the transcript as possibly the local PNP, had filed a motion for reconsideration.

thread.speaker: Rep. Alexander Pimentel
thread.said: He read that no motion for reconsideration or appeal had been filed within the regulatory period and that the release confiscation order had become final and executory under Section 4.14 of MDBMC number 2018-01. He challenged DENR Caraga's continued refusal to release the equipment.

thread.speaker: DENR official for Operations
thread.said: He said the regional director had reported that a motion for reconsideration was filed out of time and that the direction should therefore be to disregard it and release the equipment. The chair stated that the secretary had assured Rep. Pimentel that the equipment would be released the following day.

thread.speaker: DENR official for Operations
thread.said: Regarding a mining company's workers and service provider, he committed that both the MGB regional and central offices would coordinate with the company to ensure that workers were properly compensated. He later said an undersecretary would coordinate with the member to identify the company.

thread.speaker: Rep. Richard Gomez
thread.said: He reported illegal logging, quarrying, and mining in his district and requested DENR action. He said he had previously closed quarrying activities in Ormoc City, imposed open and closed seasons for sand and gravel, and required permits and rehabilitation plans before operations could proceed.

thread.speaker: Leila de Lima
thread.said: She said that from 2023 through April 2026 there had been 11 raids involving more than 70 Chinese nationals in nine provinces and asked whether DENR was investigating an organized nationwide illegal-mining operation.

thread.speaker: DENR secretary
thread.said: He committed to submit a full report on illegal-mining operations involving Chinese nationals in different regions. The chair additionally requested a list of bona fide mining operators, and the secretary agreed to submit the report to both the committee and Rep. Delima.

thread.speaker: MGB Director Larry Herradis
thread.said: He said there were six FTAAs approved by the President. Two were operating in Nueva Vizcaya for gold and copper, one was under exploration in Mindoro, another was in South Cotabato, one covered mixed offshore and onshore areas and was not operating, and one in Palawan had been canceled but was under court litigation. He also explained that force majeure could extend a contract's nonoperating period.

thread.speaker: Leila de Lima
thread.said: She said she was only partially satisfied with the response on mangrove earth-balling and questioned why an interim memorandum had been issued before completion of consultations and survival-rate studies. She asked whether the interim guidance had become a de facto permanent policy.

thread.speaker: DENR secretary
thread.said: He said the interim memorandum responded to numerous requests for government and private projects and was developed with the ERDB, BMB, and Forest Management Bureau. He described the mitigation hierarchy as avoidance, minimization, rehabilitation or restoration, and offsetting.

thread.speaker: DENR secretary
thread.said: He said the second phase of the mangrove earth-balling survival-rate study was targeted for completion by December of this year, with a policy expected in the early part of 2027.

thread.speaker: Leila de Lima
thread.said: She suggested suspending implementation of the earth-balling guidance, if not abandoning it altogether. The secretary said DENR would evaluate the suggestion while balancing ongoing developments.

thread.speaker: A Mindanao member
thread.said: He reported that 40 small-scale mining applicants remained pending and asked about processing and implementation in Davao de Oro.

thread.speaker: DENR secretary
thread.said: He said DENR had begun using one-stop shops to streamline small-scale mining applications and regulate miners who were operating illegally. He directed the MGB to schedule a one-stop shop in Davao de Oro and said the agency would coordinate with the member's office.

thread.speaker: DENR secretary
thread.said: He said the maximum annual extraction for small-scale mining was 50,000 metric tons. MGB Director Larry Herradis clarified that operations remained small-scale so long as they did not exceed that annual production limit.

thread.speaker: DENR official
thread.said: The 2027 EMB budget was stated as 3,100,000,000 pesos, while the MGB budget was stated as 1,890,000,000.

thread.speaker: A Mindanao member
thread.said: He requested a list of large-scale and small-scale operators in the region. MGB indicated that it would provide the list, and the member asked whether it could be delivered the following day.

thread.speaker: MGB regional official
thread.said: The official said Siroma had been known for white-clay mining since 1989 and that inspections or complaints had occurred around 2010, 2021, and 2024. The official characterized the relevant operation as appearing large-scale despite a permit issued by MGB.

thread.speaker: MGB regional official
thread.said: He said quarry resources could be seized and later confiscated when there was proof of illegal extraction. He also said residual stockpiles could ordinarily be commercially disposed of under two department administrative orders, but the former permit holder in this case had not used that procedure, so disposal of the white-clay stockpile had been disallowed.

thread.speaker: MGB regional official
thread.said: He said DENR had not authorized the taking of the stockpile. After investigating illegal mining in Siroma in 2025, DENR issued a CDO and recommended that the governor seize the stockpile.

thread.speaker: MGB regional official
thread.said: He confirmed that the provincial environmental task force members were deputized individually, not as a group. He agreed to provide a copy of the deputization order.

thread.speaker: A member
thread.said: The member urged the secretary to address the white-clay issue and called for a total ban on white-clay mining in Siroma, saying the district and its residents needed protection.

thread.speaker: Baguio member
thread.said: He said DENR manpower was insufficient to monitor small-scale mining and environmental safeguards, citing damage to rivers and rice fields and the use of mercury. He requested augmentation of the personnel responsible for small-scale mining monitoring and regulation.

thread.speaker: DENR official
thread.said: He assured the Baguio member that DENR would seek to augment manpower by coordinating with other stakeholders. He acknowledged continuing violations involving mercury and cyanide and directed MGB and EMB to strengthen enforcement.

thread.speaker: A member
thread.said: The member asked DENR to issue a confiscation or seizure order for the white-clay stockpile, stated in the transcript as 32,000 q cubic meters. The chair separately referred to 30,000 cubic meters, and no definitive DENR issuance was recorded.

thread.speaker: DENR official
thread.said: Regarding quarry permits affecting the Rosario and Santo Tomas bypasses and protected-area concerns, he said DENR would verify the permits' validity, environmental compliance certificates, expiration, and compliance. He committed to submit a full report, with the regional executive director identified as Henry Adornado.

thread.speaker: MGB Director Larry Herradis
thread.said: He said the Mount Sinai MPSA was approved in 2011 and had been under care and maintenance since 2013. He also said that, although multiple operating agreements had previously been allowed under one MPSA, a policy issued in 2021 or 2022 prohibited more than one operator per MPSA.

thread.speaker: MGB Director Larry Herradis
thread.said: He committed to conduct a general assessment of the mining operation and agreement and to take concrete action afterward. At the chair's direction, he agreed to meet the member the following day and provide the assessment result before plenary.

thread.speaker: DENR secretary
thread.said: In a later manifestation, he agreed that the mining tenements on the island identified unclearly in the transcript as “Home and Home Island” were irregular and committed to take action and put the situation in order. The operations undersecretary acceded to that commitment.

topics.topic: Mining permits, FTAAs, MPSAs, and small-scale mining regulation
topics.summary: Members questioned DENR on illegal mining involving Chinese nationals, FTAA renewals, dredging permits, MPSA assignments and operating agreements, small-scale mining applications, and contested exploration permits in Nueva Vizcaya. DENR reported six approved FTAAs, said renewal extensions could apply in force-majeure cases, and described public consultation at the project-feasibility and ECC stages. It said small-scale mining was limited to 50,000 metric tons per annum and committed to a one-stop shop in Davao de Oro, inspections, and submission of operator lists. MGB said one operator per MPSA had been prohibited by policy in 2021 or 2022 and committed to investigate the Mount Sinai and Eastern Samar arrangements. On critical minerals, DENR cited about 9,000,000 hectares of potentially mineralized land, current exploration funding of 157,000,000, a proposed MGB budget of 1,577,000,000, and only 2% of the potential area explored. The discussion landed on multiple agency commitments, while the allocation of mining proceeds for exploration and the suspension of mangrove earth-balling remained unresolved.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish the status and regulatory basis of mining permits, FTAAs, MPSAs, operating agreements, and small-scale mining applications. It also examined whether DENR had adequate guidelines, enforcement capacity, consultation procedures, rehabilitation requirements, and funding for mineral exploration and critical-mineral development.
topics.agency_position: DENR said mining regulation should proceed under existing environmental, permitting, progressive-rehabilitation, consultation, and small-scale-mining rules while new Executive Order 122 guidelines and a critical-minerals list were developed. The agency supported regulated mineral development and value addition but acknowledged the need for additional investigation, inspections, reports, policy review, and exploration funding.
topics.outcome: The hearing produced agency answers on FTAA status, small-scale mining limits, MPSA operating arrangements, exploration permits, and critical-mineral policy, but several matters remained under investigation. DENR and MGB undertook to submit reports and lists, conduct inspections and assessments, organize a Davao de Oro one-stop shop, and report on the Mount Sinai case before plenary; the proposed use of mining proceeds and the requested suspension of mangrove earth-balling were left for further action.

positions.position: She expressed concern that illegal mining involving Chinese nationals might reflect an organized nationwide operation, questioned FTAA renewal consultation, and opposed continued or premature mangrove earth-balling without completed scientific studies.
He supported the economic objectives of Executive Order 122 but demanded supplemental DENR safeguards against abusive mineral extraction.

She questioned the use of assignments and operating agreements under MPSAs, raised rehabilitation and possible circumvention concerns, and sought immediate investigation of the Eastern Samar and Mount Sinai arrangements.

He supported streamlined regulation of small-scale miners in Davao de Oro but demanded enforcement against operators claiming small-scale status while operating at large scale and causing waste-disposal and siltation problems.
He sought review or suspension of contested Nueva Vizcaya exploration permits, stronger public consultation, and assessment of forest-land reclassification.
He supported stronger critical-mineral exploration, domestic processing, and legislation allowing part of mining-related proceeds to fund further mineral-resource development.

actions.action: Conduct an immediate assessment and take concrete action on the Mount Sinai mining operation and operating agreement, with results requested before plenary.

thread.speaker: Leila de Lima
thread.said: She cited 11 raids from 2023 through April 2026 involving more than 70 Chinese nationals in nine provinces and asked whether DENR considered this an organized nationwide illegal-mining operation.

thread.speaker: Leila de Lima
thread.said: She asked about active FTAAs, exploration requirements, renewal status, and whether renewal required consultation.

thread.speaker: Leila de Lima
thread.said: She asked whether China Harbor Engineering Company or an affiliated dredging operator still had a valid DENR permit and why it was allegedly operating seven dredging vessels in the Santo Tomas River area. She also asked whether DENR had tracked the chain of custody of extracted sand allegedly transported to reclamation sites.

thread.speaker: DENR Secretary
thread.said: He said DENR would submit a full report on operations against illegal mining involving Chinese nationals in different regions. The chair also requested a list of bona fide mining operators, and the secretary agreed to submit the report to the committee and Rep. Delima.

thread.speaker: Committee Chair
thread.said: The chair stressed that extraction of natural resources was reserved for Filipino citizens under the registration permit and said the committee was concerned about the identities of legitimate mining operators.

thread.speaker: MGB Director Larry Hirades
thread.said: He reported that six FTAAs had been approved by the President. He identified operating gold-and-copper FTAAs in Nueva Vizcaya, an exploration-stage FTAA in Mindoro and South Cotabato involving Tampakan, a mixed offshore-and-onshore area that was not operating, and a canceled Palawan FTAA under court litigation.

thread.speaker: MGB Director Larry Hirades
thread.said: On renewal, he said an FTAA provision allowed the contractor to receive an extension when nonoperation resulted from force majeure. He said contractors were availing themselves of that provision.

thread.speaker: MGB Regional Director Glen Noble
thread.said: He said there was no company matching the name described by the member. The chair then identified operators reported for the Maloma, Santo Tomas, and Bucao Rivers, including Hal Ray Construction, Shaw Food Resources Incorporated, Greenfield Mineral Exploration and Development Corp., Seven West Incorporated, Safe2K Resources Incorporated, and Chosen One Land Development Corporation.

thread.speaker: Leila de Lima
thread.said: She followed up that there were two active FTAAs and asked whether they had already undergone renewal and consultation. She said she disagreed with DENR's position on renewal consultation.

thread.speaker: MGB Director Larry Hirades
thread.said: He said consultation occurred during approval of the declaration of mining project feasibility, including public scoping when the project entered the environmental-impact-assessment and ECC system. He also referred to consultation and endorsement involving the LGU and affected social community.

thread.speaker: Rep. Brian
thread.said: He asked how Executive Order 122 would affect mining operations, including silica, and what supplemental DENR guidelines would protect communities from abusive mineral extraction. He noted that section 13 placed DENR in charge of issuing supplemental guidelines.

thread.speaker: DENR Secretary
thread.said: He described progressive rehabilitation: within an MPSA or FTAA, a contractor could disturb only a maximum area based on its allowable annual extraction, and it had to rehabilitate the first area before moving to another. He said each tenure instrument lasted 25 years and a second 25-year period could bring the total to 50 years.

thread.speaker: DENR mining official Mike Abalda
thread.said: He said Executive Order 122 emphasized high environmental-protection standards, ESG requirements, and critical minerals. He said DENR was required to prepare a critical-minerals list within the first 30 days after publication, which would determine the projects covered by the order.

thread.speaker: MGB Director Larry Hirades
thread.said: In response to Rep. Mica Gonzales, he described MPSA contractors and operators in Eastern Samar, including Nickel Ace, Chromite King, Techiron, Pacific Nickel, and Global Mineral. He said some MPSAs were operating under suspension and that assignments had divided interests in an MPSA.

thread.speaker: Rep. Mica Gonzales
thread.said: She questioned why an amended MPSA was being operated through operating agreements involving contractors and subcontractors. She expressed concern that operating agreements could allow large-scale mining activity or illegal operations to be carried out indirectly.

thread.speaker: MGB Director Larry Hirades
thread.said: He said an MPSA contractor could engage more than one operator and that the MPSA provision allowed the contractor to assign the MPSA wholly or partially. The chair clarified that the MPSA holder remained the owner or holder while another entity could operate, and said the cited corporation was Filipino.

thread.speaker: DENR Juan Miguel Cuna
thread.said: He said the department was reviewing the Eastern Samar situation, which predated the current officials. He said DENR's immediate concern was rehabilitation and directed an inspection of violations, noncompliance, and tailings, with the concerned parties given until October to complete documents.

thread.speaker: Rep. Mica Gonzales
thread.said: She said she had a pending resolution to investigate the matter and emphasized that the issue involved only one of five MPSAs in the area. The chair expressed concern that multiple arrangements might be operating under one MPSA.

thread.speaker: A Mindanao member
thread.said: He said the provincial governor's office had reported more than 40 pending applicants and asked about the status of small-scale mining applications and the implementation of the process.

thread.speaker: DENR Secretary
thread.said: He said the pending applications involved small-scale mining contracts and that DENR had implemented interim small-scale mining contracts through department administrative orders beginning in April. He said DENR was using one-stop shops with other agencies to simplify requirements and bring informal miners into a regulated system so the Bangko Sentral could legally buy their production.

thread.speaker: DENR Secretary
thread.said: He said DENR had conducted one-stop-shop activities in several areas and directed the Mines and Geosciences Bureau to schedule one in Davao de Oro. The objective was to streamline applications and requirements and encourage illegal small-scale miners to become regulated.

thread.speaker: A Mindanao member
thread.said: He asked for a list of registered small-scale and large-scale miners in Davao de Oro and whether operations producing 10 or 50 truckloads a day could still be classified as small-scale mining.

thread.speaker: DENR Secretary and MGB Director Larry Hirades
thread.said: They said the maximum annual extraction for small-scale mining was 50,000 metric tons. Operations remained small-scale if they did not exceed that maximum allowable production.

thread.speaker: Committee Chair
thread.said: The chair warned that operators might claim small-scale status while conducting large-scale operations and asked DENR to inspect operations, regulate waste disposal, and address siltation and river-basin impacts in Davao de Oro.

thread.speaker: DENR official
thread.said: The official said DENR would instruct the regional MGB and EMB directors to investigate the reported small-scale-mining and waste-disposal concerns. The chair also requested a list of large-scale and small-scale operators, and an agency official agreed to provide it the following day.

thread.speaker: Rep. Clayton
thread.said: He asked DENR and MGB to confirm the status of the NLMRC exploration permit in Kasibu, Nueva Vizcaya. He cited barricades, cases, opposition from religious leaders, and concerns that the permit area overlapped a forest reserve, ancestral domain, watershed, or other protected area.

thread.speaker: Engineer Larry Hirades
thread.said: He said the Northern Luzon exploration permit was existing and that the company had been conducting exploration activities. He also acknowledged protests and barricades in the area.

thread.speaker: Engineer Larry Hirades
thread.said: He committed to investigate the allegations concerning the exploration activities and said the operation was currently suspended. Rep. Clayton also requested review of exploration applications in Santa Fe and Aritao before permits were issued and cancellation if material violations or deficiencies were established.

thread.speaker: Rep. Clayton
thread.said: He asked DENR to investigate the classification of parts of Nueva Vizcaya that remained forest or public land and to assess conversion to alienable and disposable land, citing difficulties in implementing infrastructure projects.

thread.speaker: DENR official
thread.said: The official said the regional executive director had been instructed to conduct a biophysical assessment. Areas already built up and no longer fit for forests could support a reclassification bill, which DENR said it would support.

thread.speaker: DENR Secretary
thread.said: He said about 9,000,000 hectares out of the country's total 30,000,000 hectares of land were believed to contain deposits. He said the administration had a clear policy direction supporting mining and was developing a framework to provide policy stability and investor confidence.

thread.speaker: A member
thread.said: The member asked whether DENR had determined the critical minerals, whether the country had sufficient reserves, and whether the reserves could support processing in the Philippines.

thread.speaker: MGB Director Larry Hirades
thread.said: He identified gold, nickel, copper, iron, chromium, and silica among the initially identified critical minerals, and referred to associated elements including cobalt, chromite, and scandium. He said the policy direction involved increasing exploration permits and strengthening upstream, midstream, and downstream processing capacity.

thread.speaker: DENR Secretary
thread.said: He said the current allotment for mineral exploration was 157,000,000.

thread.speaker: MGB Director Larry Hirades
thread.said: He said the MGB's proposed budget was 1,577,000,000 and that substantially more funding would be needed for effective exploration, including permit evaluation and drilling.

thread.speaker: A member
thread.said: The member proposed using at least part of the proceeds from nonmoving MPSAs and nonmoving exploration permits for mineral-resource development and exploration, rather than sending all proceeds to the national treasury.

thread.speaker: DENR mining official Isaac Mike Cavalda
thread.said: He said Executive Order 122 required a competitive-selection process for nonmoving and nonperforming tenements, including tenements held by the PMO and other agencies. He added that about 9,000,000 hectares had been identified for mineral potential but only 2% had been explored, and that 17 areas were considered highly prospective.

thread.speaker: DENR mining official Isaac Mike Cavalda
thread.said: He said royalty collections from mineral reservations had accumulated but exploration budget requests continued to receive only a small amount. For comparison, he said a company such as BHP could have a budget of about 200,000,000 US dollars for exploration.

thread.speaker: A member
thread.said: The member proposed that congressional offices and DENR work together on legislation allocating a percentage of proceeds to mineral-resource development and said Congress was willing to sponsor the proposal.

thread.speaker: Rep. Mica Gonzales
thread.said: She asked for the status of the Mount Sinai mining project and its MPSA.

thread.speaker: MGB Director Larry Hirades
thread.said: He identified Mount Sinai's approved MPSA as number 351211, approved in 2011, with a declaration of mining project feasibility also approved in 2011. He said the MPSA had been under care and maintenance since 2013.

thread.speaker: MGB Director Larry Hirades
thread.said: He said the Mining Act had allowed multiple operating agreements under one MPSA, but that in 2021 or 2022 MGB issued a policy prohibiting more than one operator per MPSA.

thread.speaker: Rep. Mica Gonzales
thread.said: She cited section 96 of Republic Act 7942, under which violation of permit or agreement terms was sufficient ground for cancellation. She pressed for action on the operating arrangements and related mining operations.

thread.speaker: MGB Director Larry Hirades
thread.said: He committed to conduct a general assessment of the mining operation and operating agreement and to take concrete action afterward. At the chair's direction, he further committed to an immediate investigation and to provide the result before plenary.

topics.topic: Land management, surveys, patents, foreshore tenure, and reversion
topics.summary: DENR presented land titling as a priority, with a target of up to 43,000 patents, while its Land Management Bureau acknowledged that survey-dispute funding was insufficient and that regional offices handled the work. Rep. Rodriguez secured committee approval of an additional 556,617,000 pesos for land management, foreshore mapping, patent issuance, the Land Management Bureau building, and water resources, subject to fiscal space. A member raised the 1,014.92-hectare Wanderlust Corporation claim in Siroma, and the Secretary said DENR was completing a survey and targeting a reversion filing in the second week of October limited to forest lands. Members also sought funding and action for Cordillera forest reserves, solid-waste disposal sites, a proposed marine protected area, and development options for built-up forest land. MGB committed to investigate contested Nueva Vizcaya exploration activities, while the Secretary committed to a biophysical assessment for possible reclassification. The chair required DENR to submit a formal, prioritized request for additional funding before further budget deliberation.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish how DENR would fund and administer land surveys, dispute resolution, patents, foreshore tenure, land classification, and reversion proceedings. Members also asked whether specific forest, protected-area, and land-management concerns would receive funding or agency action.
topics.agency_position: DENR said land surveys, dispute resolution, patent issuance, foreshore delineation, and land-management activities were being implemented through regional offices and bureau programs but were constrained by limited funding. The department maintained that timberland and bodies of water could not lawfully be included in private titles, committed to pursue the Siroma reversion case after completing the survey, and offered further assessments, coordination, and tenure or reclassification options for other land concerns.
topics.outcome: The committee approved an additional 556,617,000 pesos for DENR, but the addition remained subject to available fiscal space and final allocation. Several land matters were answered or assigned follow-up action, while the Siroma reversion filing, survey-record search, Nueva Vizcaya assessment, and formal funding submission remained commitments rather than completed outcomes.

positions.position: Pressed for adequate regional funding and clearer procedures for surveys, land disputes, private claims, tenure applications, and foreshore tenure.
Supported additional DENR funding for land management, foreshore mapping, patent issuance, the Land Management Bureau building, and water-resource programs.

positions.who: A member raising the Siroma matter
positions.position: Maintained that the Wanderlust Corporation claim appeared spurious and sought reversion of the timberland portion supported by a completed survey.
Sought additional protection and funding for Cordillera forest and water reserves and requested DENR assistance in identifying solid-waste disposal sites.
Sought protected-area action for marine habitats, forest-protection assistance, and lawful development options for built-up areas still classified as forest land.
Called for review or suspension of contested Nueva Vizcaya mining permits and a biophysical basis for possible forest-land reclassification.

thread.speaker: DENR Secretary Juan Miguel Cuna
thread.said: Secretary Cuna presented the DENR's requested FY 2027 budget of 28,040,000,000, covering the central office, 17 regional offices, bureaus, and attached agencies. He said the department managed 15,800,000 hectares of classified forest lands and more than 36,000 kilometers of coastline.

thread.speaker: DENR Secretary Juan Miguel Cuna
thread.said: He said DENR planned to issue up to 43,000 land patents in 2027, providing security of tenure to families and households.

thread.speaker: DENR Secretary Juan Miguel Cuna
thread.said: Secretary Cuna identified alienable and disposable lands, agricultural free patents, and residential free patents as land-management matters handled from the central level through the regional offices and Land Management Bureau.

thread.speaker: Rep. Eli San Fernando
thread.said: San Fernando asked whether the process determined land-classification status, confirmed an approved survey plan, established that the land was alienable and disposable public domain, and then selected the appropriate patent or tenure instrument.

thread.speaker: DENR Secretary Juan Miguel Cuna
thread.said: Secretary Cuna confirmed those steps.

thread.speaker: Rep. Eli San Fernando
thread.said: San Fernando asked about DENR resources for land surveys and the resolution of survey-related disputes.

thread.speaker: Land Management Bureau Director Emmy Talabis
thread.said: Director Talabis said the DENR budget for land surveys and survey-related disputes was insufficient to resolve all cases. Regional offices, CENROs, and PENROs had budgets for claims, conflicts, and alternative dispute resolution, but the funding was "meager".

thread.speaker: Land Management Bureau Director Emmy Talabis
thread.said: She said LGUs, applicants, and clients requested conflict resolution from DENR, which acted on requests as received and sought funds from the central office for the regions, PENROs, and CENROs, subject to available funding.

thread.speaker: Land Management Bureau Director Emmy Talabis
thread.said: In response to San Fernando's clarification, Talabis said survey funding and responsibility rested with the regional offices.

thread.speaker: DENR Secretary Juan Miguel Cuna
thread.said: Secretary Cuna said requests were made through the regions and the central finance office checked whether funding was available.

thread.speaker: DENR official Bong Teves Jr.
thread.said: Teves said DENR set targets, allocated funds for particular activities, and cascaded the allocations to PENROs across the country.

thread.speaker: Rep. Eli San Fernando
thread.said: San Fernando asked about eligible alienable and disposable private claims and whether qualified occupants could receive a tenure instrument. He raised a 40 hectare case in which occupants reportedly retained security of tenure despite a ruling against the private claim.

thread.speaker: DENR Secretary Juan Miguel Cuna
thread.said: Secretary Cuna said incomplete submission of requirements could prevent the process from proceeding.

thread.speaker: DENR Regional Executive Director, Region IV-A
thread.said: The regional executive director said he would obtain the details from the PENRO and provide them immediately.

thread.speaker: Rep. Eli San Fernando
thread.said: San Fernando asked about the process for foreshore lands and fisherfolk tenure, including whether DENR conclusively determined the legal status of a shoreline before authorizing or recognizing its use.

thread.speaker: Land Management Bureau official
thread.said: The official said foreshore areas were disposed of through foreshore leases, with the tenure documented in a foreshore lease agreement.

thread.speaker: Land Management Bureau official
thread.said: The official said DENR relied on departmental maps and was updating foreshore information through foreshore delineation and profiling, which had funding.

thread.speaker: Rep. Rufus Rodriguez
thread.said: Rodriguez asked how much DENR had proposed to DBM after the department's proposed budget was reduced.

thread.speaker: DENR Secretary Juan Miguel Cuna
thread.said: Secretary Cuna said DENR had proposed a total of 55,040,579,000, including tier two.

thread.speaker: Rep. Rufus Rodriguez
thread.said: Rodriguez asked how much additional funding was needed for land management and governance.

thread.speaker: DENR Secretary Juan Miguel Cuna
thread.said: Secretary Cuna said DENR had submitted a request for 100,000,000 to the Office of the Speaker to pay registration fees for unclaimed agricultural and residential free patents. He said many recipients could not pay the 2,500 charge per title.

thread.speaker: Rep. Rufus Rodriguez
thread.said: Rodriguez identified 181,000,000 for land management and governance, including foreshore delineation and mapping, and 61,000,000 for patent issuance, validation, lot survey, and issuance.

thread.speaker: DENR finance official Yusick Teh
thread.said: Teh said 270,000,000 was intended as phase two of an eight-story Land Management Bureau building and related DENR network infrastructure, following the destruction of the former building in 02/2018.

thread.speaker: DENR Secretary Juan Miguel Cuna
thread.said: Secretary Cuna said the 105,000,000 water-resources enforcement and regulatory request included 65,000,000 for a managed aquifer recharge system and 40,000,000 for regionalized and digital water governance, including 16 digital-facility upgrades.

thread.speaker: Rep. Rufus Rodriguez
thread.said: Rodriguez moved to approve the DENR FY 2027 budget at 28,000,000,000 plus an additional 556,617,000 for foreshore mapping, patent issuance, the Land Management Bureau building, and water resources.

thread.speaker: Appropriations presiding officer
thread.said: The motion was seconded and approved, subject to consolidation of additions for all government agencies.

thread.speaker: A member
thread.said: The member asked about the Wanderlust Corporation claim in Siroma involving 1,014.92 hectares, including alleged timberland, alienable and disposable land, bodies of water, and other land categories. The member also asked whether a transfer certificate of title could include portions of the Pacific Ocean and territorial sea.

thread.speaker: DENR Secretary Juan Miguel Cuna
thread.said: Secretary Cuna said an original or transfer title could not and should not include portions of the Pacific Ocean or territorial sea. He added that timberland belonged to the state.

thread.speaker: DENR Secretary Juan Miguel Cuna
thread.said: Secretary Cuna said DENR was finalizing the survey and a request for a reversion case, targeted for filing in the second week of October.

thread.speaker: DENR Secretary Juan Miguel Cuna
thread.said: He said the title remained valid until annulled or canceled by a court of competent jurisdiction, while confirming that it was issued spuriously.

thread.speaker: DENR Secretary Juan Miguel Cuna
thread.said: Secretary Cuna said the ongoing survey would distinguish alienable and disposable land from forest land so that any reversion case would cover only the forest lands included in the title.

thread.speaker: DENR Secretary Juan Miguel Cuna
thread.said: He said regional officials had been unable to secure the original copy of survey plan S I two six seven six despite efforts to locate it in different offices.

thread.speaker: Rep. Mauricio Domogan
thread.said: Domogan asked whether the budget included specific funding for Cordillera national parks and forest or water reserves, particularly to protect watersheds supplying major dams.

thread.speaker: DENR official
thread.said: The official cited National Greening Program activities in protection zones, including enrichment planting and assisted natural regeneration, with a 2027 target of 16,000 hectares, a unit cost of 16,000 per hectare, and a budget of about 130,000,000. The official also cited reforestation, agroforestry, site planning, protection, maintenance, and technical assistance.

thread.speaker: Rep. Mauricio Domogan
thread.said: Domogan asked DENR and the Land Management Bureau to identify and segregate suitable public-land areas for solid-waste disposal sites in provinces and cities.

thread.speaker: DENR environmental official
thread.said: The official said site selection had to comply with Republic Act 9003 criteria, including restrictions involving timberland, protected areas, and aquifers, and had to be consistent with the LGU comprehensive land-use plan and solid-waste management plan.

thread.speaker: DENR Secretary Juan Miguel Cuna
thread.said: Secretary Cuna said DENR would work with Domogan at the regional level to find suitable areas for solid-waste disposal.

thread.speaker: Rep. Howard

thread.said: Secretary Cuna said a protected-area suitability assessment had to be conducted before a recommendation for declaration could be made. He later said the regional recommendation was at the PENRO level and would be sent to the Biodiversity Management Bureau for evaluation.

thread.speaker: DENR Secretary Juan Miguel Cuna
thread.said: Secretary Cuna asked Howard to submit a request concerning the deforested area and forest-protection assistance.

He identified the sustainable forest land management agreement as a multiple-use instrument for grazing, plantations, tourism, ecotourism, or renewable energy, valid for twenty five years and renewable for another twenty five years.

thread.speaker: Rep. Clayton

thread.speaker: DENR Secretary Juan Miguel Cuna

thread.speaker: Rep. Clayton

thread.speaker: Appropriations presiding officer

thread.speaker: Appropriations chair

thread.speaker: DENR Secretary Juan Miguel Cuna
thread.said: Secretary Cuna agreed that DENR would submit the formal request and a prioritized list.

topics.topic: Solid-waste management, LGU compliance, and waste-facility funding
topics.summary: Members questioned DENR's role in LGU waste-contract oversight, RA 9003 enforcement, source segregation, flooding, and the availability of waste facilities. DENR said LGUs were primarily responsible, while DENR provided technical assistance for MRFs and solid-waste plans, conducted education campaigns, and monitored sanitary landfills for ECC compliance. Rep. Teves cited 92% LGU compliance, a 95% 2027 target, and only six of 17 Metro Manila LGUs compliant with source segregation; he also cited 2,230,000,000 in 2025 annual DENR appropriations as a possible source of assistance. The commission representative disclosed a very limited budget, described the status of ten-year LGU plans, and reported a resolution recommending activation of barangay solid-waste committees. Rep. Rise linked roughly 12,000 tons a day of Metro Manila garbage and an estimated 30% left in waterways to flooding, while proposing a regional-government approach. Rep. Domogan requested identification or reservation of suitable disposal sites, and DENR committed to coordinate regionally; other requests and enforcement concerns remained unresolved.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish whether DENR, the National Solid Waste Management Commission, and LGUs had adequate authority, funding, facilities, and enforcement mechanisms to comply with RA 9003 and address flooding caused by improper waste disposal. Members also sought commitments on technical assistance, environmental education, waste-facility siting, and requests for additional funding.
topics.agency_position: DENR maintained that LGUs bear primary responsibility for waste management under RA 9003, while DENR provides technical assistance, education, MRF and planning support, and monitors sanitary-landfill compliance with ECC conditions. The agency acknowledged enforcement and facility-use deficiencies, supported stronger coordination with DILG and DepEd, and undertook to coordinate on regional disposal-site and Metro Manila waste-management concerns.
topics.outcome: The hearing clarified that LGUs retain primary responsibility for waste management and private waste-contract renewals, while DENR monitors environmental compliance and provides technical and educational assistance. Several enforcement, funding, and disposal-site concerns remained open, with agency coordination and document or area submissions undertaken rather than a final funding or compliance resolution.

positions.position: Pressed for stronger enforcement of RA 9003, household segregation, compliance by the 11 reportedly noncompliant Metro Manila LGUs, better MRF use, and funding for waste-disposal facilities.
Linked improper solid-waste disposal and informal settlements to flooding and advocated a unified regional-government solution for Metro Manila.
Called for renewed barangay and public education on segregation and proper disposal, and sought support for affected-area boundary and control-point concerns in Bacolor.
Argued that the shortage of suitable solid-waste disposal sites required DENR to reserve or identify appropriate public-land areas for provinces and cities.
Emphasized that local-government autonomy placed much of solid-waste responsibility with LGUs and DILG rather than DENR.

topics.topic: Flood management, watershed rehabilitation, and nature-based mitigation
topics.summary: Members asked DENR to define its responsibility for waterways, flood prevention, watershed rehabilitation, and coordination with DPWH. DENR said its mandate included environmental impact assessment, wastewater regulation, water-quality management, watershed and river-basin programs, and nature-based solutions complementary to DPWH infrastructure. It cited about 28 million for nature-based solutions, 78 million for integrated water-resource management, 21 million for river-basin operations, and 33 billion for forest development, protection, soil conservation, and related rehabilitation, although the watershed-by-watershed allocation was not provided. DENR said the national and Central Luzon flood frameworks and a unified water database were still being finalized or developed, while the Pampanga initiative remained at the risk-assessment stage. Members pressed for greater mangrove and greening support, and the chair said an additional 30 million would be pursued. DENR also committed to examine the Bulacan Airport’s environmental effects, submit Manila Bay enforcement and rehabilitation information, and continue work on ECC thresholds for flood-control projects.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish DENR’s responsibility for flood prevention, watershed and waterway management, and nature-based mitigation; its coordination with DPWH; and the funding, monitoring, and environmental-clearance requirements for related projects. Members also asked what specific programs and databases would support flood-risk reduction in Central Luzon and Manila Bay.
topics.agency_position: DENR said its flood-related mandate covered environmental assessment and enforcement, watershed and river-basin management, water-quality regulation, ecosystem restoration, and coordination with DPWH. It presented nature-based solutions as complementary to DPWH’s gray infrastructure, but acknowledged that funding and implementation remained limited and that the national and Central Luzon frameworks and unified database were still being finalized or developed.
topics.outcome: DENR clarified its existing responsibilities and identified funding for watershed management, river-basin operations, nature-based solutions, and Manila Bay enforcement. The flood management framework, Central Luzon nature-based interventions, unified database, Bulacan Airport assessment, and several requested documents remained subject to further review, consultation, or submission.

positions.position: Flooding in Metro Manila required an integrated regional solution addressing waterways, solid waste, informal settlers, and governance rather than isolated agency interventions.
DENR should ensure that the national flood management framework guided and reviewed major DPWH flood-control projects.
Natural flood-control measures, especially mangrove planting, required substantially greater support in the flood-prone Pampanga and Manila Bay area.
Flood management should use a ridge-to-reef approach, with DENR exercising oversight across interconnected rivers, watersheds, floodplains, and coasts.
Watershed, forest, river, wetland, and mangrove protection were necessary to address flooding’s root causes, and nature-based solutions needed sustained budget support.
DENR should provide status and enforcement information on Manila Bay rehabilitation, including penalties and fines collected.

thread.speaker: DENR Secretary Juan Miguel Cuna
thread.said: The DENR requested a total FY 2027 budget of 28,040,000,000, covering its central office, 17 regional offices, line bureaus, and attached agencies.

thread.speaker: DENR Secretary Juan Miguel Cuna
thread.said: He said DENR would shift the National Greening Program toward forest landscape restoration, ecosystem resilience, and community livelihoods.

thread.speaker: DENR Secretary Juan Miguel Cuna
thread.said: He identified revitalization of major urban waterways, including Manila Bay, the Pasig River System, and Laguna Lake, as part of the clean-environment priority.

thread.speaker: Rep. Egay Rise
thread.said: He asked about DENR’s specific responsibility for preventing floods in waterways, including whether it had responsibility for maintaining natural waterways and flood-control facilities.

thread.speaker: DENR Secretary Juan Miguel Cuna
thread.said: He said DENR’s direct responsibility centered on the environmental impact assessment process. Where flooding was identified as a possible impact, proponents had to submit a flooding study or mitigation measures.

thread.speaker: DENR Secretary Juan Miguel Cuna
thread.said: He added that DENR handled ECCs for projects along waterways, wastewater-discharge permits, continuing cleanup, and water-quality management areas. He also cited the Estero program and governing boards that prepare management plans for particular water bodies.

thread.speaker: Rep. Egay Rise
thread.said: He argued that flooding was linked to solid waste and informal settlers and called for a single regional solution for Metro Manila, including a regional government and legislative assembly.

thread.speaker: DENR Secretary Juan Miguel Cuna
thread.said: He said he could join the relevant commission and other government agencies, including LGU representatives, to discuss the proposed Metro Manila regional-government study.

thread.speaker: Rep. Elmer
thread.said: He asked how DENR’s national flood management framework would guide or review DPWH flood-control projects and raised the scale of DPWH flood-control spending.

thread.speaker: DENR finance official
thread.said: The official said DENR’s flood-mitigation mandate fell principally under watershed management, including reforestation, river-basin offices, the National Water Resources Board, and the Water Resources Management Office.

thread.speaker: National Water Resources Board executive director
thread.said: He said the flood management framework was prepared by DENR offices and was intended to ensure that DPWH flood-control plans were coherent with DENR river-basin master plans. He described gray DPWH infrastructure and DENR nature-based solutions as complementary.

thread.speaker: Rep. Elmer
thread.said: He asked for the status of the national flood management framework and whether it had been submitted to DPWH.

thread.speaker: National Water Resources Board executive director
thread.said: He said the framework had been prepared but still required the Secretary’s final review and clearance.

thread.speaker: DENR finance official
thread.said: For FY 2027, DENR cited 78,000,000 for integrated water-resource management and operations, PHP 52,900,000 for regional water-resource utilization, PHP21 million for sustainable river-basin-office operations, and 28,000,000 for scaling up nature-based solutions.

thread.speaker: DENR finance official
thread.said: The official acknowledged that the funding was insufficient for monitoring but said DENR would prioritize 18 principal or major river basins.

thread.speaker: Congresswoman York
thread.said: She asked what DENR was doing in the Manila Bay area to use natural means of flood control, particularly for the flood-prone Pampanga basin.

thread.speaker: DENR official
thread.said: The official cited mangrove planting, Estero Rangers, and cleanup activities as DENR’s nature-based and waterway interventions. The official said the district had an allotment of 80 Estero Rangers, if the figure was correctly recalled.

thread.speaker: DENR official
thread.said: The official said the 2026 mangrove allocation was 13,900,000 and later said the 2027 allocation was 15,000,015 million.

thread.speaker: Congresswoman York
thread.said: The chair said, “I will fight for the inclusion of the additional 30,000,000” for the requested water-related intervention. The congresswoman also urged DENR to consider reprogramming its greening funds.

thread.speaker: DENR Secretary Juan Miguel Cuna
thread.said: Regarding the Bulacan Airport ECC, he said DENR would coordinate with the regional director because the ECC had been processed in the region and would examine the congresswoman’s inclusion and impact concerns.

thread.speaker: DENR Secretary Juan Miguel Cuna
thread.said: He committed to formulate terms of reference for how DENR could conduct an environmental impact assessment and inform the congresswoman.

thread.speaker: Congresswoman Sarah Elago
thread.said: She argued that flood management could not be treated in isolation because rivers, watersheds, floodplains, and coasts formed an interconnected system. She supported a DENR-led ridge-to-reef oversight approach and additional greening in Bulacan’s 5th District.

thread.speaker: NWRB Executive Director Bill David
thread.said: He said the flood management framework remained a draft requiring consultation and approval, including coordination with DPWH and other agencies, before adoption.

thread.speaker: NWRB Executive Director Bill David
thread.said: He reported an ADB-supported climate-risk assessment of the Pampanga River Basin intended to complement DPWH infrastructure and identify nature-based solutions. The work was still ongoing.

thread.speaker: NWRB Executive Director Bill David
thread.said: He confirmed that the Pampanga initiative remained at the risk-assessment and solution-identification stage rather than implementation.

thread.speaker: DENR official
thread.said: DENR said an additional FY 2027 request would establish a unified database for the National Water Resources Board, linking existing databases of NWRB, RBCO, DENR’s geospatial office, DPWH, LWUA, and MWSS.

thread.speaker: Rep. Adore Plato
thread.said: He asked whether DENR had formally adopted the IUCN Global Standard for nature-based flood mitigation and requested the specific budget for watershed rehabilitation and protection, as well as DENR-DPWH coordination.

thread.speaker: DENR finance official
thread.said: The official said about 28,000,000 was allocated for nature-based solutions under soil conservation, access to water, watershed management, and river-basin management, with augmentation from related water-resource activities. DENR coordinated with DPWH through the InfraCom to harmonize environmental, nature-based, and infrastructure solutions.

thread.speaker: Rep. Adore Plato
thread.said: He asked DENR to identify the most critical watersheds, state funding per watershed and the number of hectares being rehabilitated, and explain how it measured downstream flood reduction.

thread.speaker: Forest Management Bureau Director Art Fadrigala
thread.said: He identified 131 critical watersheds and said 2027 projects would cover 16 priority landscapes. He cited a total 33,000,000,000 budget for forest development, protection, soil conservation, and related rehabilitation initiatives, but did not provide a watershed-by-watershed allocation or downstream flood-reduction metric.

thread.speaker: Rep. Adore Plato
thread.said: He urged a substantial allocation for continued nature-based adaptation and expressed support for approval of the DENR FY 2027 budget.

thread.speaker: DENR official
thread.said: On Manila Bay rehabilitation, the official said yearly budgets were determined annually and activities were guided by key result areas covering liquid waste, solid waste, informal settlers, ecosystem rehabilitation, and enforcement.

thread.speaker: DENR official

thread.speaker: DENR official

thread.speaker: Rep. Sarah Elago

thread.speaker: A member

thread.speaker: DENR Attorney Mike Matias
thread.said: He said flood-control projects were treated in some cases as environmental enhancements, but DENR was drafting an administrative order with DPWH comments to classify which projects would require an ECC. DENR’s guidelines established thresholds for ECCs and certificates of non-coverage.

thread.speaker: DENR Attorney Mike Matias
thread.said: He clarified that establishing the thresholds was DENR’s mandate, while DPWH was being consulted. He also noted that waterway easement requirements had to be observed.

topics.topic: Protected-area funding, staffing, and forest protection
topics.summary: DENR presented protected-area management and forest landscape restoration as strategic priorities within its proposed budget of about 28 billion, covering 121 legislated protected areas and 15.8 million hectares of classified forest lands. Members questioned the 1,300,000,000 protected-area management budget and learned that allocations generally arose from regional fiscal space, equity considerations, and protected-area management-board proposals rather than a single needs-based formula. Rep. Mario cited Mount Hamiguitan's 16,923 hectares of protected land and 9,000-plus hectare buffer zone and requested a more concrete funding formula, while also criticizing ranger coverage ratios involving as much as 3,000 hectares per ranger. DENR reported National Greening Program targets of 18,000 hectares for planting, 30,375 hectares for enhancement, and 30,000 hectares with a stated budget of 408,000,000, while Rep. Rufus Rodriguez sought an additional 400,000,000 for rehabilitation. Members also raised Cordillera forest-reserve funding, Catanduanes' lack of permanent plantilla positions, and a proposed marine protected area, and DENR described requests to DBM ranging from 1,000 to 1,706 positions. The issues remained dependent on written submissions, DBM approvals, and possible budget augmentation, with DENR undertaking follow-up coordination and documents.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish whether DENR's proposed funding and staffing were sufficient to manage protected areas, protect forests, support National Greening Program priorities, and respond to local conservation and rehabilitation needs. Members also sought a needs-based protected-area funding formula, permanent plantilla positions for rangers, and clearer options for managing forest lands and reserves.
topics.agency_position: DENR stated that protected-area funding was developed through regional fiscal space, regional proposals, equity considerations, standard administrative costs, and protected-area management-board approvals rather than a single area- or needs-based formula. The agency acknowledged staffing gaps, said it had requested additional permanent positions from DBM, and committed to submit priority-area information and coordinate on local forest and protected-area concerns.
topics.outcome: DENR answered the committee's questions but did not provide a needs-based protected-area funding formula or resolve the forest-ranger and protected-area plantilla shortfalls. The agency committed to submit priority-area information, pursue staffing requests with DBM, coordinate on local protected-area and forest concerns, and support further consideration of budget augmentation.

positions.position: The National Greening Program needed a distinct and sufficient rehabilitation budget for previously planted areas, and DENR's budget should be augmented for that purpose.

Protected-area funding should be allocated according to actual conservation needs, area, and protection requirements rather than primarily regional fiscal space. Forest-ranger staffing also needed to be increased.
Cordillera forest reserves and water-source areas might require budget augmentation if the existing program was insufficient.
Protected areas, including the Catanduanes protected area, required permanent plantilla positions as a statutory and long-term conservation investment.
The proposed marine protected area and deforested forest areas in his district required DENR action, while forest land with little or no remaining forest should have lawful development options.

topics.topic: Environmental impact assessments and ECCs for major projects
topics.summary: Members raised concerns about mining-related tree cutting, quarry and exploration permits, tree-cutting requirements for ADB bridges, New Clark City data centers, the Bulacan Airport ECC, and ECC coverage for flood-control and pumping-station projects. DENR said specific projects required clear descriptions and, where applicable, EIA, ECC processing, consultation, public hearings, and cumulative-impact assessment; it also said the New Clark City master-plan ECC covered about 9,400 hectares while projects within a 1,600-hectare area would require project-specific review. The committee cited an EIA budget of about 251 million, DENR budget figures including a 2027 request of about 28.05 billion, mangrove allocations of 13,900,000 for 2026 and 15,000,015 million for 2027, and a proposed additional 30,000,000 for water-related work. DENR returned the ADB bridge application covering 17 trees, reduced from 21, pending consultation and other requirements, and stated replacement ratios of 100 for naturally growing trees and 50 for planted trees. For Bulacan Airport, DENR undertook to develop terms of reference for an environmental review addressing Pampanga impacts. The hearing ended with commitments for reports, investigations, interagency coordination, and an administrative order clarifying which flood-control projects require ECCs.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish how DENR evaluates environmental impacts, processes ECC applications, conducts consultations, and enforces mitigation requirements for major infrastructure, energy, industrial, airport, mining, quarrying, and flood-control projects. Members also asked what funding, reviews, and interagency mechanisms were available to support those functions.
topics.agency_position: DENR said specific projects must be evaluated on the basis of a clear project description and, where applicable, must undergo EIA, public consultation, and ECC processing. The agency said it was coordinating with DPWH, BCDA, regional offices, and other agencies on project reviews, tree-cutting requirements, flood-control classifications, mitigation, and environmental monitoring, but several assessments and reports remained to be completed.
topics.outcome: DENR answered the committee's questions on the general EIA, ECC, consultation, mitigation, and tree-replacement framework, but several project-specific matters were left for reports, written information, investigations, or terms of reference. The Bulacan Airport review, quarry-permit report, New Clark City information, and flood-control classification remained subject to follow-up.

positions.position: DENR should protect the environment, enforce tree-cutting and rehabilitation requirements, and not act as an agency for mining companies.
DENR's environmental responsibilities required adequate resources, and he manifested support for the DENR budget and possible program augmentation.
New Clark City data centers and manufacturing hubs required careful EIA, public consultation, cumulative-impact review, and a written assessment of potential environmental effects.

topics.topic: Water resources governance, river basins, and water-district support
topics.summary: DENR presented direct assistance of PHP 124,000,000 for local water districts and described funding for aquifer recharge and digital water governance. Rep. Rodriguez secured approval of an additional 556,617,000 pesos for the DENR budget, including water-resource priorities. Members raised delays involving the Butuan City Water District, insufficient LWUA funding, and the need for a technical review of La Mesa Dam; officials undertook follow-up actions, but the transcript did not show final resolution of those matters. DENR said its flood-management framework remained subject to final review and interagency consultation, while its 2027 water-related allocations included about 78,000,000 for integrated water-resource management, PHP21 million for river-basin organizations, and 28,000,000 for nature-based solutions. Members also pressed for a unified water database and stronger watershed rehabilitation, with DENR identifying 131 critical watersheds and 16 priority landscapes. The hearing left the framework, database, water-district financing needs, and dam review as committed or continuing actions rather than fully resolved outcomes.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish how DENR and its attached agencies would finance and coordinate water-resource management, river-basin planning, watershed rehabilitation, flood mitigation, and support for water districts. Members also asked whether agencies had adequate authority, data systems, and technical capacity to address water-district delays, dam safety, and disputes involving joint-venture operators.
topics.agency_position: DENR said its water mandate covered water-resource regulation, managed aquifer recharge, digital and regionalized water governance, river-basin operations, watershed management, and nature-based flood mitigation. It acknowledged that available funding and monitoring capacity were insufficient, and said the flood-management framework and unified database still required further review, consultation, approval, and funding.
topics.outcome: The DENR budget was approved with an additional 556,617,000 pesos, while the committee also recorded requests for more LWUA funding and follow-up on La Mesa Dam, Butuan water-district documents, the flood-management framework, and a unified database. Several technical and institutional matters remained dependent on DBM approval, interagency consultation, or future review.
