actions.action: Complete and submit updates to the major river-basin master plans, targeted for 2027 and hopefully the first half of that year.
Report to the committee how many nature-based solutions were already being implemented and how many more were planned.
Undertake the Silang-Santa Rosa diversion-channel and spillway feasibility study next year and provide progress updates.
Provide clear targets for communities protected, floodwater retained, and reductions in flood depth or duration for detention facilities.
Maintain critical flood-control pumping stations and keep them operational and on standby.
Find funding for and finish the unfinished Pampanga pumping station.
Prioritize and finish the unfinished Pampanga bridges and bypass structures.
Coordinate with Rep. Bondoc's staff on the bridge funding and completion documents.
Finish the Delta Bridge by early next year.
Fund and prioritize the Iloilo floodway phase two feasibility-study update and drainage master-plan work.
Continue dredging and desilting as a regular DPWH maintenance program.

thread.speaker: Rep. Chel Diokno
thread.said: Rep. Diokno asked whether the country still lacked the National Comprehensive Flood Control and Drainage Plan announced the previous year.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: Secretary Dizon confirmed that there was no consolidated national plan. DPWH's strategy was to prepare master plans for each major river basin and drainage master plans for urban centers.

thread.speaker: Rep. Chel Diokno
thread.said: Rep. Diokno asked whether the executive department was abandoning a national plan in favor of river-basin and urban-center plans.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: Secretary Dizon said DPWH was not abandoning the concept, but experts advised that interventions should be designed by major river basin and locality. He cited nationwide principles including upstream interventions, retarding or detention basins instead of relying only on dikes and revetments, and protecting populated areas through a needs-based approach.

thread.speaker: Rep. Chel Diokno
thread.said: Rep. Diokno asked what percentage of the major river basins and urban centers had written plans and whether the plans were current.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: Secretary Dizon said all 18 major river basins had master plans, but 14 were being updated because many plans had been formulated years earlier.

thread.speaker: Rep. Chel Diokno
thread.said: Rep. Diokno asked for DPWH's target for completing the updates.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: Secretary Dizon said DPWH was pressing its mostly foreign consultants to complete all updates by 2027, hopefully in the first half of 2027.

thread.speaker: A committee member
thread.said: A committee member suggested that the river-basin and other planning should include nature-based solutions.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: Secretary Dizon agreed that nature-based solutions were a critical component. He said experts recommended gabions instead of fully concrete revetments in many rural areas because concrete dikes could increase water velocity, while gabions were more nature-based and cheaper; he said DPWH would report how many such measures were being implemented.

thread.speaker: Rep. Roy Gonzales
thread.said: Rep. Gonzales appealed for a feasibility-based solution to flooding between Silang and Santa Rosa, including a possible spillway or diversion facility routing water toward the Tiesmo River, Kalupang, and Cabuyao and ultimately addressing flooding toward Laguna Lake.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: Secretary Dizon said DPWH had a feasibility study for a diversion channel and other flood-mitigation interventions, with 82,000,000 for the study of an important spillway tunnel. The transcript's description of the proposed connection is unclear but refers to a route toward Manila Bay.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: Secretary Dizon said the feasibility study would be undertaken next year and asked that Rep. Gonzales be called for progress updates.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: DPWH identified water detention facilities as a priority, including facilities in the National Capital Region and other major cities. Secretary Dizon said DPWH was considering available open spaces, parks, golf courses, and fields, subject to right-of-way and technical requirements.

thread.speaker: Rep. Salvador Pleyto
thread.said: Rep. Pleyto asked how the 39 potential Metro Manila rainwater detention and flood-storage sites would fit into the overall flood-management strategy. He requested clear targets for communities protected, water retained, and reductions in flood depth or duration.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: Secretary Dizon said there were 30 plus potential detention-facility sites in urban centers, but their viability was still being evaluated under the ongoing NCR flood-mitigation master plan. He said the specific detention-basin approach would be reviewed as the NCR master plan was updated.

thread.speaker: A committee chair/member
thread.said: The committee member asked Secretary Dizon to place on record a commitment on flood control, particularly the operation and maintenance of pumping stations, and asked whether DPWH would supervise such facilities.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: Secretary Dizon confirmed a commitment to maintain critical pumping stations and keep them on standby and ready for operation. The transcript is unclear on the specific director and on portions concerning supervision.

thread.speaker: Rep. Anna York Bondoc
thread.said: Rep. Bondoc described continuing flooding in six towns, including Santo Tomas, Minalin, San Simon, and Apalit, and asked about pumping stations after observing them during the President's visit.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: Secretary Dizon said the coastal towns and Pampanga River system presented a difficult situation. In the short term, mobile pumps were being deployed to pump water from populated areas into waterways, although the transcript's explanation of the waterway constraint is unclear.

thread.speaker: Rep. Anna York Bondoc
thread.said: Rep. Bondoc disclosed that one pumping station was only half finished and asked that the unfinished facility be addressed.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: Secretary Dizon said the district regional director had briefed him and that DPWH would find a way to fund the unfinished pumping station because it was a continuing critical facility. He stated, "We will finish it."

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: Secretary Dizon said DPWH would find a way to prioritize the five unfinished bridges and bypass structures in Pampanga, citing their flood, access, and national-security relevance.

thread.speaker: Rep. Anna York Bondoc
thread.said: Rep. Bondoc said the Delta Bridge was 95% completed and that the last 200,000,000 had not been funded because of a bidding-related issue.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: Secretary Dizon referred to 143,000,000 under 2026 and said DPWH personnel would coordinate with Rep. Bondoc's staff regarding the funding and completion issue.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: Secretary Dizon repeated that DPWH would finish the bridge, with completion expected by early next year.

thread.speaker: An Iloilo congresswoman
thread.said: The Iloilo member asked whether 102,000,000 for updating the Iloilo floodway phase two feasibility study and the city's comprehensive drainage master plan would be added to the 50,000,000 provided the previous year, and urged DPWH to prioritize the floodway and related projects.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: Secretary Dizon confirmed 102,000,000 for updating the Iloilo flood-mitigation feasibility study and agreed that, together with the previous year's 50,000,000, the total was 152,000,000 as stated in the exchange.

thread.speaker: Rep. Anna York Bondoc
thread.said: Rep. Bondoc asked Secretary Dizon to explain DPWH's dredging and desilting policy and also flagged the unfinished Korea-assisted flood-control project, particularly its second part.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: Secretary Dizon said dredging and desilting were critical and that DPWH had begun a full-blast program, including dredging major rivers and waterways. He said this needed to become a regular DPWH maintenance program and that the department was building its capacity to keep waterways clean.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: Secretary Dizon referred to the Korea-assisted project as requiring RDC approval; the transcript does not clearly state a funding or completion commitment for part two.

topics.topic: Right-of-way acquisition and landowner compensation funding
topics.summary: Rep. Sarah Elago sought updates and records concerning right-of-way payments and compensation for affected households and small businesses in the ADB Metro Manila Bridges Project. DPWH cited right-of-way obligations close to 90,000,000,009.00 and later described an accumulated obligation of 90,000,000,000. Rep. Mark Cojuangco urged stronger nationwide right-of-way acquisition funding, while Secretary Vince Dizon expressed support. Rep. Howard asked how funds were allocated and was told that payments were prioritized by project, voucher readiness, court order, or negotiated settlement; expropriation cases required a 15% deposit. The Secretary stated an FY 2027 allocation of 15,000,000,020.27, while the exchange also referred to 5,000,000,000 and 5,000,000,020.26 for the current year. Howard requested additional funding because right-of-way payment delays were delaying projects, and Dizon said additional funding would be welcome but made no specific appropriation commitment.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish how DPWH allocated and prioritized funds for right-of-way acquisition and landowner compensation, including the FY 2027 amount. Members also asked whether additional funding was needed to prevent project delays and requested records on affected households, businesses, and major projects.
topics.agency_position: DPWH stated that right-of-way payments were prioritized on a project basis, particularly when vouchers were ready and when payments were supported by court orders or negotiated settlements. The agency identified a cumulative obligation of 90,000,000,000 and said additional right-of-way funding would be welcome, but it did not undertake a specific additional appropriation.
topics.outcome: DPWH explained its project-based prioritization process and stated an FY 2027 right-of-way figure of 15,000,000,020.27, against an accumulated obligation cited as 90,000,000,000. Members' requests for records were accepted, but the request for additional right-of-way funding received only a general expression of welcome and no specific commitment.

topics.topic: FY2025 SAROs, discontinued projects, savings, and fund realignment
topics.summary: Rep. Robert Massal asked Secretary Vince Dizon about FY 2025 projects whose SAROs had been issued but whose SARs were not, including the disposition of their allotments. Dizon cited a total of 90,000,000,000, alternatively stated as 90,300,000,000, with more than 30,000,000,000 attributed to flood control projects, and said projects with incomplete documents were returned to DBM after additional vetting. He agreed to provide the committee with the relevant letters and a list of discontinued projects. Dizon said the funds were effectively declared savings and that much of the budget cover was used for the uplift program, relying on the GAA general provisions and describing the projects as unimplementable or abandoned. Erice then cited DBM records dated 11/27/2025 showing augmentation sourced from declared DPWH savings and sought clarification on whether the affected projects were included. DPWH did not resolve that specific question during the hearing and committed to comply with documentary requirements.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish what happened to FY 2025 projects whose SAROs had been issued but whose corresponding SARs were not issued, including the status of their allotments. It also questioned whether the funds were declared savings, how they were used or realigned, and what legal authority supported those actions.
topics.agency_position: DPWH said projects with missing or incomplete documents were subjected to additional vetting and returned to DBM when they were considered unimplementable or abandoned. It stated that the GAA general provisions provided the legal basis for treating the resulting funds as savings and realigning them, while indicating that DBM would be better positioned to clarify the specific authority and augmentation transactions.
topics.outcome: DPWH explained that the projects were subjected to additional vetting and that funds for projects deemed unimplementable or abandoned were treated as savings under the GAA general provisions. The specific project list, documentary trail, and whether the questioned funds were used for augmentation remained for written submission and further clarification, including from DBM.

positions.position: He questioned the legality and procedural sufficiency of withholding SARs after SAROs and bidding, declaring the funds as savings, and realigning or augmenting them despite the stated validity of FY 2025 capital-outlay appropriations through 2027.
He questioned whether declared savings from the affected projects had been used to augment other DPWH programs, citing DBM records that described such transactions as augmentation.

topics.topic: MVUC and the discontinued stand-alone Special Road Fund
topics.summary: Rep. Sidhu Ongwam questioned why the stand-alone Special Road Fund had disappeared from the FY 2027 PAP schedule and been placed under Asset Preservation. He cited the prior amount of 14,833,952,000 and the FY 2027 amount of 15,000,000,000, arguing that the new presentation made the earmarked fund less visible and could narrow its use because bridges were in a separate PAP. DPWH Undersecretary Nick Conti answered that Republic Act 11239 limited MVUC to roads, bridges, and road drainage and that qualifying projects under Asset Preservation Organizational Outcome No. 1 were attributed to MVUC. The agency said the 15,000,000,000 amount had been specified by DBM and offered to submit the detailed project list. Ongwam also raised constitutional, Supreme Court, and prior veto-message concerns, but those issues were not directly resolved. The immediate result was an agency commitment to provide supporting project documentation.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish whether the FY 2027 presentation of MVUC collections under the DPWH Asset Preservation Program improperly obscured or narrowed the statutory Special Road Fund. Rep. Sidhu Ongwam also asked whether DPWH requested this treatment or whether it was imposed by DBM.
topics.agency_position: DPWH stated that the MVUC collections were attributed to qualifying Asset Preservation projects under Organizational Outcome No. 1, consistent with the statutory scope under Republic Act 11239, and that the amount identified by DBM for 2027 was 15,000,000,000. The agency offered to furnish the committee with the detailed list of projects, but did not directly resolve whether DPWH requested the presentation or whether DBM imposed it, nor did it directly answer the constitutional and statutory concerns raised by Ongwam.
topics.outcome: DPWH explained that the 2027 MVUC amount was attributed to qualifying Asset Preservation projects and undertook to provide the project list. The committee's concerns about the loss of a stand-alone line, the treatment of bridges, and the constitutional and statutory implications remained open.

positions.position: The Special Road Fund should remain separately visible as an earmarked fund and stand-alone PAP. He argued that placing MVUC within Asset Preservation could obscure the fund and narrow its use, particularly because bridges were carried in a separate PAP.
MVUC proceeds were being used for projects within the statutory purposes identified in Republic Act 11239, and the relevant projects were itemized under Asset Preservation Organizational Outcome 001.

thread.speaker: Rep. Sidhu Ongwam
thread.said: Ongwam directed his question to DPWH and DBM concerning Special Provision No. 10 on the disposition of MVUC collections. He said his concern was not the amount, but how the presentation affected the earmarked special fund.

thread.speaker: Rep. Sidhu Ongwam
thread.said: He said the FY 2026 and prior budgets showed a stand-alone Special Road Fund PAP under the DPWH convergence and special support program, with the transcript stating an amount of 14.20 26 and then 14,833,952,000. He contrasted this with FY 2027, where the stand-alone PAP no longer appeared and Special Provision No. 10 was retitled as the disposition of MVUC collections.

thread.speaker: Rep. Sidhu Ongwam
thread.said: Ongwam said the 15,000,000,000 formerly shown as a stand-alone Special Road Fund was now included under the Asset Preservation Program. He asked whether it was correct that legislators could not see the Special Road Fund as a separate line unless they read Special Provision No. 10 and knew to look for it within Asset Preservation, and asked whether DPWH requested the provision or DBM imposed it.

thread.speaker: DPWH undersecretary for planning
thread.said: The DPWH official referred the question to Undersecretary Nick Conti. The response did not directly state whether DPWH requested the treatment or whether DBM imposed it.

thread.speaker: Undersecretary Nick Conti
thread.said: Conti explained that, following the amendment of Republic Act 8794 by Republic Act 11239, MVUC use was limited to the construction, upgrading, repair, and rehabilitation of roads, bridges, and road drainage. He said qualifying projects under Organizational Outcome No. 1 for Asset Preservation were attributed to MVUC collections, which were to be remitted to the Treasury under a special account in the General Fund.

thread.speaker: Undersecretary Nick Conti
thread.said: Conti said DPWH could furnish the committee with a list of the projects under Asset Preservation, Organizational Outcome No. 1, attributed to MVUC. He said the list would cover the amount specified by DBM for 2027.

thread.speaker: Undersecretary Nick Conti
thread.said: Conti identified the amount specified by DBM for 2027 as 15,000,000,000.

thread.speaker: Rep. Sidhu Ongwam
thread.said: Ongwam asked whether the Special Road Fund was a special fund under Article VI, Section 29(3) of the Constitution, consisting of money collected for a special purpose and payable only for that purpose. He contrasted it with Asset Preservation, which he characterized as a regular DPWH program funded through the General Appropriations Act.

thread.speaker: Rep. Sidhu Ongwam
thread.said: Ongwam argued that MVUC covered roads, bridges, and road drainage, while the FY 2027 Asset Preservation PAP covered preventive maintenance and rehabilitation of roads and drainage, with bridges in a separate Bridge Program. He asked whether placing MVUC within Asset Preservation narrowed the operative use of the statutory earmark because bridges were no longer within the PAP carrying the MVUC amount.

thread.speaker: Rep. Sidhu Ongwam
thread.said: Ongwam questioned the requirement that DPWH disaggregate Asset Preservation and submit to Congress a list of regular and MVUC-funded projects within fifteen days after effectivity. He said a post-effectivity report would not inform deliberations before enactment and argued that retaining a stand-alone Special Road Fund PAP would make the 15,000,000,000 visible without the need for later disaggregation.

thread.speaker: Rep. Sidhu Ongwam
thread.said: Ongwam characterized the fifteen-day disaggregation requirement as a workaround created by removing the stand-alone PAP. He further warned that post-enactment project identification had already been struck down by the Supreme Court.

thread.speaker: Rep. Sidhu Ongwam
thread.said: Ongwam informed the committee that a pending Supreme Court case challenged the constitutionality of unprogrammed funds, automatic appropriations, and earmarked funds such as special accounts in the General Fund and use of income in the General Fund, which he said included the Special Road Fund. He said the Court had already heard oral arguments five times and noted rulings that a General Appropriations Act could not amend a special law.

thread.speaker: DPWH agency official
thread.said: The official cited Republic Act 11239 and said MVUC proceeds were limited to the construction, upgrading, repair, and rehabilitation of roads, bridges, and road drainage, including safety, lighting, and cat's eye. The official said the 15,000,000,000 identified by DBM for 2027 was in Asset Preservation Organizational Outcome 001.

thread.speaker: DPWH agency official
thread.said: The official said the projects were detailed and itemized in the submitted National Expenditure Program and could be submitted to the committee. The official maintained that the projects were already reflected in the NEP.

thread.speaker: Rep. Sidhu Ongwam
thread.said: Ongwam recalled that in 2023 MVUC had likewise been included in Asset Preservation, but that the veto message stated the arrangement was allowed for that year and would not be allowed in succeeding years. He told the DPWH official that addressing this precedent was the agency's assignment.

topics.topic: Project vetting, feasibility studies, and detailed engineering capacity
topics.summary: Rep. Cherilyn Banias Lugrales questioned DPWH's allocation for detailed engineering and geotechnical studies, consultant accountability, and the basis for earthquake rehabilitation projects. Secretary Vince Dizon said the ideal allocation was about 5% to 6% of capital outlay—roughly about 30 billion based on the cited 2026 capital outlay—but only 6 billion was budgeted for the studies. He also acknowledged that DPWH lacked the personnel and specialized equipment needed to conduct studies for all 11,000 proposed 2027 projects. Rep. Antonio Tinio examined project traceability, certificates of implementability, geotagged documentation, and the central-office implementation of projects above the 50 million threshold. A congresswoman secured commitments for lists of feasibility-study and tourism-road projects and was told that projects costing 1 billion and above required a feasibility study. DPWH said tourism-road identification would be led by the concerned department, with joint technical validation with DPWH, while foreign-assisted and convergence projects would continue under documented implementation arrangements.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish whether DPWH had sufficient funding, personnel, systems, and accountability mechanisms for feasibility studies, detailed engineering, geotechnical investigations, and project validation. Members also asked how projects were assigned, technically validated, and implemented, including convergence and foreign-assisted projects.
topics.agency_position: DPWH said proper feasibility studies, detailed engineering, geotechnical work, certificates of implementability, geotagged documentation, and local-government coordination were necessary safeguards, but acknowledged that funding, personnel, and specialized equipment were insufficient for the full project workload. The agency maintained that implementation generally followed DBM thresholds and program-specific rules, with joint validation for convergence projects and commitments to submit requested lists and reports.
topics.outcome: DPWH acknowledged substantial gaps in study funding and internal technical capacity, while defending its project-vetting and implementation controls. The department undertook to provide lists, reports, and follow-up on consultant accountability and earthquake rehabilitation, but the adequacy of funding, the final responsibility for some projects, and the accountability record remained open.

positions.position: DPWH should strengthen in-house engineering and geotechnical capacity, improve consultant accountability, and ensure earthquake rehabilitation projects were based on actual damage inventories.

Project proposals needed more complete documentation, traceability, location information, and safeguards against double funding and ghost projects; the basis for central-office implementation and district allocations also required scrutiny.
Feasibility-study funding and responsibility for tourism-road identification and validation should be clearly documented under the new convergence arrangements.
Convergence and foreign-assisted projects should meet documentation, geotagging, certification, and approved-program-of-work requirements, while DPWH reforms should continue.

thread.speaker: Rep. Cherilyn Banias Lugrales
thread.said: She asked how much DPWH allocated annually for detailed engineering design, including geotechnical studies, hydrologic mapping, and related preparatory work.

thread.speaker: Rep. Cherilyn Banias Lugrales
thread.said: She said detailed engineering and geotechnical investigations were weak points in DPWH projects, citing what she described as inaccurate studies and designs in General Santos City that caused losses and problems for establishments.

thread.speaker: Rep. Cherilyn Banias Lugrales
thread.said: She said inadequate geotechnical studies could contribute to structural problems during earthquakes, including soil liquefaction, and that proper studies could have prevented such problems.

thread.speaker: Rep. Cherilyn Banias Lugrales
thread.said: She questioned whether DPWH would continue outsourcing preparatory studies and asked who would be accountable if a consultant's contract ended before construction and the project later failed.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: Secretary Dizon agreed with the concern and said he would provide data on feasibility studies, detailed engineering, and geotechnical work.

thread.speaker: Rep. Cherilyn Banias Lugrales
thread.said: She asked whether consultants responsible for technical studies and investigations had ever been held accountable, prosecuted, or blocklisted when their work caused losses to the government or local problems.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: Dizon said he would check whether a geotechnical company had previously been held accountable. He said the ideal allocation for feasibility studies, detailed engineering, geotechnical work, and related activities was 5% to 6% of DPWH capital outlay.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: Using the 2026 capital-outlay figure of 460,000,000,000, Dizon said 5% to 6% would be roughly about 30,000,000,000, while the 2026 budget for these studies was only 6,000,000,000.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: He said approximately 20,000—or 17,000 to 18,000—projects were competing for a fraction of the amount needed for proper feasibility studies, detailed engineering, and geotechnical studies. The spoken project-count wording was unclear.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: Dizon requested that the department receive more funding for detailed engineering and feasibility-study work, saying the current level of resources was a serious problem.

thread.speaker: Rep. Cherilyn Banias Lugrales
thread.said: She suggested that, instead of relying primarily on outsourcing, DPWH should develop in-house experts and invest in nationwide technical capacity because that could be more cost-efficient.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: Dizon agreed that developing in-house capacity was a good goal but said DPWH lacked the personnel and equipment to conduct the work for all 11,000 projects proposed for 2027. He said the department needed geologists, geotechnical engineers, and specialized equipment that it did not currently have.

thread.speaker: Rep. Cherilyn Banias Lugrales
thread.said: She cited 17,764 total national projects in 2026, of which she said 15,032, or 76%, had already been advertised. She asked about implementation of projects in her district and similarly situated districts.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: Dizon said he would check the releases and procurement requirements, particularly for O.O.1, and report back. He assured the member that the projects would be implemented.

thread.speaker: Rep. Cherilyn Banias Lugrales
thread.said: She said her district's previous total project amount was around 1,700,000,000 but was more or less 500,000,000 in 2027. She asked whether the reduced amount and the recommended rehabilitation funding reflected the district office's inventory of earthquake-damaged structures.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: Dizon said he would have the regional director and district engineering office address the concern. He committed to addressing yellow-tagged and red-tagged school buildings and health facilities through the department's funds, including the End-.... Fund and Quick Response Fund; the first fund's name was unclear.

thread.speaker: Rep. Antonio Tinio
thread.said: Tinio presented project-vetting and budget-reform concerns, emphasizing technical review, information, traceability, transparency, and protection against randomly proposed or unsupported projects.

thread.speaker: Rep. Antonio Tinio
thread.said: Using a district-engineering-office proposal for road construction with a stated amount of 5,000,000 and a total proposal of more or less 404,000,000, he asked whether the documentation met the Secretary's objectives for traceability and complete project information.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: Dizon said BIP projects were coordinated with local government units and required certifications from the LDC, PDC, or RDC, including certificates of implementability. He said these requirements were intended to establish accountability and prevent unsupported projects.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: Dizon identified the certificate of implementability, DEO review, project-title and budget information, and geotagged on-site photographs as safeguards against double funding and ghost projects. He said engineers uploaded location information and real-time photographs to the system.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: Dizon acknowledged that no protection was 100% foolproof, mentioning the possibility of manipulated map or photographic materials, but said the requirements provided layers of protection.

thread.speaker: Rep. Antonio Tinio
thread.said: Tinio asked whether road proposals should identify locations and station markings, including standard markings every 200 meters, to make project descriptions and validation more precise.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: Dizon said national and local roads were referenced differently but that proposals required clear descriptions, coordinates, and geotagged photographs taken on the ground.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: Dizon said the 2027 process prioritized regions and districts and that 80% of the more than 11,000 projects had RDC endorsement. He said RDC endorsement was required from the relevant districts and regions and that the distribution among legislative districts followed a formula.

thread.speaker: Rep. Antonio Tinio
thread.said: Tinio questioned the apparent allocation of 481,000,000,000 in DPWH capital outlay to the central office and 121,000,000,000 to the regions, asking for the basis of central-office and regional implementation.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: Dizon said current DBM rules generally placed projects above 50,000,000 under central-office implementation, while projects below 50,000,000 could be implemented by regional or district engineering offices, subject to program and departmental rules.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: Dizon explained that some highway projects were centrally managed even when regional offices implemented them, and that implementation depended on the program and applicable thresholds. He said flood-control implementation likewise depended on departmental decisions and thresholds.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: Dizon said DPWH would be open and willing to provide the committee with information on the implementation arrangements.

thread.speaker: Rep. Antonio Tinio
thread.said: Tinio restated his understanding that projects of 50,000,000 and above generally went to the central office while lower-value projects went to the regions, with exceptions depending on the program and implementation considerations.

thread.speaker: A congresswoman
thread.said: She referred to a 2026 allocation for the Sorcegon Summer Bridge, stated as 100,130,000,000, and asked about a proposed 130,000,000 feasibility study for 2027. The project name and amount wording were partly unclear.

thread.speaker: An agency official
thread.said: The agency official said the 130,000,000 was counterpart funding for a feasibility study with foreign funding, identified as involving the Asian Development Bank, after which the department could seek funding for implementation.

thread.speaker: An agency official
thread.said: The official identified a Southern Gate-to-Surigao long-span bridge connecting the Visayas and Mindanao and said its 2027 feasibility study allocation was 350,000,000.

thread.speaker: A congresswoman
thread.said: She asked the department to submit a list of major projects receiving feasibility-study funding.

thread.speaker: An agency official
thread.said: The agency official agreed to submit the requested list to the chair.

thread.speaker: A congresswoman
thread.said: She asked whether a minimum project-cost threshold applied before a full feasibility study was required.

thread.speaker: An agency official
thread.said: The official answered that projects costing 1,000,000,000 and above needed a feasibility study.

thread.speaker: A congresswoman
thread.said: She asked who would identify and prioritize tourism roads under the new arrangement, and who would conduct technical validation and implementation.

thread.speaker: A congresswoman
thread.said: She specifically asked whether the concerned department, rather than DPWH, would have primary responsibility for identifying and prioritizing tourism roads.

thread.speaker: An agency official
thread.said: The official said the concerned department would identify and prioritize the roads, while technical validation would be joint between that department and DPWH, similar to arrangements for classrooms and farm-to-market roads.

thread.speaker: Rep. Stephen James Tan
thread.said: Tan raised the need for approved programs of work, geotagging, certificates of implementability, and certifications or non-objection documents for convergence and foreign-assisted projects.

thread.speaker: An agency official
thread.said: The official said DPWH would serve as the primary implementing agency moving forward while coordinating with other departments, including DTI, DepEd, and DA, depending on the project.

thread.speaker: A committee member
thread.said: A committee member asked about DPWH's total amount, with the discussion referring to an amount of 200 plus billion pesos.

thread.speaker: An agency official
thread.said: The official confirmed that foreign-assisted projects were ongoing and described them as critical, with further foreign-assisted projects expected the following year.

thread.speaker: An agency official
thread.said: The official praised DPWH's reforms, saying they improved project selection and reduced the risk of ghost or substandard projects, and urged the department to continue the reforms.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: Dizon thanked the committee and indicated that DPWH would continue the reforms with the committee's support.

topics.topic: Major bridges, inter-island connectivity, and multiyear completion funding
topics.summary: Rep. Rufus Rodriguez sought support for Cagayan de Oro bypass roads and bridges, citing about 34 billion for the Coastal Bypass Road, about 7 billion for the Eastern Interior Road, and additional funding for local bridges and walkways. He also highlighted feasibility-study funding for the Mindanao-Visayas connection, including 350 million for the Surigao-to-Southern Leyte bridge study. Rep. Sarah Elago questioned the status of 944 TCAS projects and the ADB Metro Manila Bridges Project, citing more than 3 billion pesos in disbursements and requesting detailed records, traffic studies, blueprints, and compensation information. Secretary Dizon said DPWH would verify the project information and submit the requested reports, except that the MRT 7 blueprint would be referred to DOTR. Rep. Salvador Pleyto and Rep. Timothy Titan pressed for complete multiyear bridge funding, earthquake assessment, anti-overloading enforcement, and safety improvements. Rep. Anna York Bondoc raised unfinished Pampanga pumping stations and bridges, including the 95%-complete Delta Bridge; Secretary Dizon committed to fund and finish the facilities and said the Delta Bridge would be completed by early the following year.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish which major bridge, bypass-road, flood-control, and inter-island connectivity projects required funding; whether projects would be completed rather than left in phases; and what schedules, feasibility studies, project records, and implementation responsibilities applied.
topics.agency_position: DPWH said it was moving toward multiyear appropriations with clear completion timelines for bridges and other major projects, while continuing to seek foreign or counterpart financing for feasibility studies and large infrastructure. The agency acknowledged that several project statuses and records required verification, but committed to provide reports, studies, lists, and other documents and to prioritize or complete unfinished bridges and pumping facilities.
topics.outcome: The agency gave policy assurances on multiyear bridge appropriations and committed to complete or prioritize unfinished bridges and the Delta Bridge, while undertaking to submit numerous project reports and records. Several TCAS, ADB bridge, right-of-way, and feasibility-study details remained subject to agency verification or later submission.

positions.position: Supported increasing the DPWH budget and sought funding and foreign financing for Cagayan de Oro bypass roads, bridges, walkways, and the Mindanao-Visayas inter-island connection.
Pressed DPWH for documentary accountability on TCAS and the ADB Metro Manila Bridges Project, including project status, disbursements, traffic effects, blueprints, and compensation.
Advocated complete, start-to-finish funding for long bridges and requested earthquake-retrofitting and structural-integrity information for Metro Manila infrastructure.
Supported evidence-based feasibility studies, requested a list of major projects, and sought clarity on responsibility for tourism-road identification, validation, and implementation.
Called for stronger anti-overloading enforcement, additional weighing facilities, multiyear bridge funding, and pedestrian overpasses for road safety.
Urged completion and funding of Pampanga pumping stations, unfinished bridges, bypass roads, and the Delta Bridge because of flooding, connectivity, and national-security concerns.

thread.said: He thanked Secretary Vince Dizon for visiting the Cagayan de Oro Coastal Bypass Road and said Phase 1 had been completed after nine years, with Phase 2 now being pursued.

thread.speaker: Rep. Rufus Rodriguez
thread.said: He said the Cagayan de Oro Coastal Bypass Road needed 34,000,000,000 pesos and that the Secretary would seek foreign funding. He also cited about 7,000,000,000 for the Eastern Interior Road and said the Secretary had committed an additional 120,000,000 to finish the Macabalan-Bonbon Bridge.

thread.speaker: Rep. Rufus Rodriguez
thread.said: He said a feasibility-study request for the Mindanao-Leyte Bridge interlink project had been pursued for six years, with 120,000,000 included for 2026 and 350,000,000 received for the Surigao-to-Southern Leyte Bridge feasibility study.

thread.speaker: Rep. Rufus Rodriguez
thread.said: He urged implementation of the feasibility study by January of the following year, describing the proposed Mindanao-Visayas-Luzon connection as important for the movement of food, merchandise, vehicles, and people.

thread.speaker: Rep. Rufus Rodriguez
thread.said: He requested 100,000,000 for renovation of the Pelawi Sports Complex as part of a 300,000,000 cost-sharing arrangement, with 100,000,000 each from the city, province, and DPWH.

thread.speaker: Rep. Rufus Rodriguez
thread.said: He requested 200,000,000 for an elevated walkway in Cagayan de Oro, saying 83,000,000 had been provided that year and the total requirement was 570,000,000.

thread.speaker: Rep. Rufus Rodriguez
thread.said: He expressed support for the DPWH budget and moved for its increase.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon

topics.topic: Earthquake rehabilitation, bridge safety, and seismic retrofitting
topics.summary: Rep. Cherilyn Banias Lugrales questioned DPWH's allocation and capacity for geotechnical and detailed engineering studies, citing earthquake-related structural damage and soil-liquefaction risks. Secretary Vince Dizon said the department ideally needed 5% to 6% of capital outlay for such work—roughly about 30 billion based on 460 billion—but had only 6 billion in 2026. He acknowledged that DPWH lacked the personnel and equipment to conduct studies for all 11,000 proposed 2027 projects and committed to seek additional funds and report on consultant accountability and procurement requirements. Lugrales also raised her district's reduction from about 1.7 billion to more or less 500 million after a 7.8 earthquake, and Dizon committed to having regional and district officials address rehabilitation of yellow- and red-tagged facilities. Rep. Jonathan Keith Flores raised a dangerous critical bridge whose delays cost around 147 million per day, and Dizon cited retrofit and replacement amounts, including 150,000,000 and unclear figures spoken as 150.20 26 and 600,000,020.27. Rep. Salvador Pleyto requested plans for retrofitting critical infrastructure and inspecting buildings for the West Valley Fault risk, and Dizon committed to submit the ongoing World Bank-funded NCR assessment.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish whether DPWH had adequate resources, technical capacity, and accountability mechanisms for geotechnical studies and the rehabilitation or retrofitting of earthquake-damaged and critical bridges. It also sought commitments on completing bridge projects, assessing critical infrastructure, and reporting measurable resilience and rehabilitation plans.
topics.agency_position: DPWH acknowledged that funding and capacity for feasibility studies, detailed engineering, and geotechnical investigations were inadequate, and that the department was not yet equipped to perform all studies internally. It stated that it would address earthquake-damaged facilities, pursue retrofit or replacement of critical bridges through a nationwide strategy, use multiyear appropriations for major projects, and submit the ongoing World Bank-funded NCR assessment.
topics.outcome: DPWH gave assurances on district rehabilitation, critical-bridge retrofit or replacement, and a nationwide bridge strategy, but several requested details remained subject to verification, reports, or ongoing assessments. The World Bank-funded NCR assessment and specific rehabilitation and accountability information had not yet been submitted during the hearing.

positions.position: DPWH should strengthen geotechnical and engineering studies, develop internal technical expertise instead of relying excessively on consultants, ensure consultant accountability, and base earthquake rehabilitation funding on a documented inventory of damaged facilities.
The dangerous condition of the critical bridge he raised required immediate DPWH action because crossing delays imposed substantial economic costs on multiple regions.

DPWH should provide a clear plan for retrofitting critical infrastructure and inspecting national buildings before a major earthquake, and major bridge projects should be funded through completion rather than left unfinished through fragmented packaging.

Have the regional director and district engineer address the member's earthquake rehabilitation concern.

thread.speaker: Rep. Cherilyn Banias Lugrales
thread.said: She asked how much DPWH allocated for detailed engineering design, including geotechnical studies, hydrologic mapping, and other preparatory work. She cited inaccurate geotechnical investigations and inadequate consideration of soil liquefaction as causes of structural and financial losses after an earthquake.

thread.speaker: Rep. Cherilyn Banias Lugrales
thread.said: She questioned whether DPWH would continue outsourcing preparatory studies and asked who would be accountable when a consultant's contract ended before construction problems emerged.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: Secretary Dizon agreed that feasibility studies, detailed engineering, and geotechnical work were weak points and said he would provide data on the issue. His response was partly unclear in the transcript.

thread.speaker: Rep. Cherilyn Banias Lugrales
thread.said: She followed up by asking whether consultants responsible for defective technical studies had been held accountable or prosecuted, or had their firms been blocklisted, when projects caused losses to the government and problems in localities.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: Secretary Dizon said he would find out whether a geotechnical company had been held accountable in the past. He said DPWH ideally needed 5% to 6% of total capital-outlay project costs for feasibility studies, detailed engineering, geotechnical work, and related studies.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: Using the 2026 capital-outlay figure of 460,000,000,000, he said 5% to 6% was roughly about 30,000,000,000 pesos, while the 2026 budget for those studies was only 6,000,000,000. He said projects were competing for a fraction of the amount needed for proper studies.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: Secretary Dizon said he would request additional feasibility-study and detailed-engineering funds for the department. He characterized the shortage of study funding as a serious problem.

thread.speaker: Rep. Cherilyn Banias Lugrales
thread.said: She suggested that, instead of relying on outsourcing, DPWH should develop its own nationwide pool of experts because the department implemented thousands of projects every year. She said this could be more cost-efficient.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: Secretary Dizon agreed that developing internal expertise was a good goal but said DPWH lacked sufficient personnel and equipment. He said handling all 11,000 projects for 2027 would require geologists, geotechnical engineers, and specialized equipment that the department did not currently have.

thread.speaker: Rep. Cherilyn Banias Lugrales
thread.said: She cited 17,764 national projects in 2026, including 15,032 projects that she said were already advertised, and asked about the implementation status of projects in her district. The transcript's percentage associated with the advertised projects was unclear.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: Secretary Dizon said he would check the release of procurement requirements and report back to the congresswoman. He assured her that DPWH would implement the projects and later said the department would provide reports.

thread.speaker: Rep. Cherilyn Banias Lugrales
thread.said: She said her district's total project allocation had been about 1,700,000,000 previously but was more or less 500,000,000 in 2027. After the district suffered a 7.8 earthquake, she asked whether the proposed 200,000,000-plus would be based on the district office's inventory of damaged structures requiring rehabilitation, retrofitting, and related works.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: Secretary Dizon said he would have the regional director and district engineer address the concern. He committed that yellow-tagged and red-tagged school buildings and health facilities would be addressed through the department's funds, including the transcript's unclear reference to the "Endream Fund" and the Quick Response Fund.

thread.speaker: Rep. Jonathan Keith Flores
thread.said: He raised the dangerous condition of a critical bridge serving two regions, where tremors had required people to man both ends. He said delays in crossing the bridge cost around 147,000,000 per day and asked DPWH to act on the bridge's safety and completion concerns.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: Secretary Dizon said the regional director had briefed him on the bridge. He described a plan involving retrofit work and eventual replacement, with the transcript stating 150,000,000 for an earlier year, 150.20 26, and 600,000,020.27 for bridge replacement; the latter figures are unclear as spoken.

thread.speaker: Rep. Jonathan Keith Flores
thread.said: He said the bridge delays affected sugarcane, pineapples, bananas, and other economic activity not only in Bukidnon but also in nearby regions including Davao and Soccsksargen. He said the committee would wait for DPWH's action.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: Secretary Dizon said DPWH was developing a nationwide strategy for critical bridges, particularly bridges forming logistics routes from Mindanao to Luzon. Depending on the assessment, the department would retrofit, replace, rehabilitate, or construct parallel bridges.

thread.speaker: Rep. Salvador Pleyto
thread.said: He asked whether long bridges and other major projects would be funded and completed from start to finish rather than divided into packages or phases. This was raised in the context of ensuring that major infrastructure projects reached completion.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: Secretary Dizon said DPWH's policy direction was to invest on a phased basis through multiyear appropriations, with a clear completion timeline for each phase and subsequent years. The transcript did not record a specific completion date for the bridge projects.

thread.speaker: Rep. Salvador Pleyto
thread.said: He asked to be apprised of DPWH's plans for retrofitting critical infrastructure such as bridges, flyovers, and elevated expressways in Metro Manila, and for structural-integrity inspections of national buildings in preparation for a possible major earthquake associated with the West Valley Fault.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: Secretary Dizon confirmed that a World Bank-funded assessment for the "big one" in the National Capital Region was ongoing. He committed to submit the report to the committee and the congressman.

topics.topic: National-road maintenance and post-construction asset preservation
topics.summary: Rep. Sidhu Ongwam questioned why the MVUC special road fund was no longer displayed as a standalone FY 2027 program and argued that embedding it in Asset Preservation reduced legislative visibility. DPWH Undersecretary Nick Conti and Secretary Vince Dizon said the amount was attributed to itemized Asset Preservation projects pursuant to the statutory limits on MVUC use and identified the 2027 amount as about 15 billion. DPWH undertook to furnish the committee with the relevant project lists, but the record did not resolve Ongwam's concerns about bridges, post-enactment disaggregation, or the legality of the presentation. Rep. Michael Pan raised right-of-way and routine and post-construction maintenance problems affecting national highways, particularly in Samar. The secretary committed to address post-construction maintenance and said national roads remained DPWH's primary mandate, while local-road concerns involving remote and island municipalities were left for continuing coordination with regional and district offices.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish whether the motor vehicle users charge (MVUC) collections were properly and visibly appropriated for their statutory purposes, including roads, bridges, and drainage. Members also sought assurance that DPWH would adequately fund routine and post-construction maintenance of national highways while addressing right-of-way and local-road concerns in remote areas.
topics.agency_position: DPWH stated that the 2027 MVUC amount was attributed to itemized projects under Asset Preservation Organizational Outcome No. 1 and remained limited to the statutory purposes of construction, upgrading, repair, and rehabilitation of roads, bridges, and road drainage. The department said it could furnish the committee with the project list and undertook to address post-construction maintenance, while maintaining that national roads were its primary mandate and local roads would be considered through regional and district offices.
topics.outcome: DPWH explained that the 15,000,000,000 MVUC amount was attributed to itemized Asset Preservation projects and undertook to provide supporting project information, but the committee's concerns about visibility, the treatment of bridges, and possible statutory or constitutional issues were not definitively resolved. DPWH separately committed to address post-construction maintenance, while the broader Samar local-road and right-of-way concerns remained subject to further agency action.

positions.position: He objected to the disappearance of the standalone special road fund line, arguing that embedding the 15,000,000,000 MVUC amount in Asset Preservation reduced legislative visibility and potentially raised statutory and constitutional concerns.

He urged stronger funding and action for right-of-way, routine and post-construction maintenance of national highways, and local-road infrastructure in Samar and other remote or island municipalities.

He maintained that DPWH should prioritize national roads but indicated that the department would address the post-construction maintenance concern and continue working through regional directors and district engineers on local-road concerns.

thread.speaker: Rep. Sidhu Ongwam
thread.said: He noted that in FY 2026 the special road fund appeared as a standalone program under the DPWH convergence and special support program, with a stated amount of 14.20 26 and 14,833,952,000. He asked why the standalone line no longer appeared in FY 2027 and whether the change was correct.

thread.speaker: Rep. Sidhu Ongwam
thread.said: He said the 15,000,000,000 previously shown as a standalone special road fund was now included under the Asset Preservation Program through Special Provision No. 10. As a result, legislators could not see the special road fund as a separate line without examining the special provision.

thread.speaker: Rep. Sidhu Ongwam
thread.said: He asked whether his reading was correct and whether DPWH had requested the provision or whether it had been imposed by DBM.

thread.speaker: DPWH Secretary
thread.said: The secretary referred the question to Undersecretary Nick Conti for a response.

thread.speaker: Undersecretary Nick Conti
thread.said: He explained that, following the amendment of Republic Act 8794 by Republic Act 11239, MVUC collections were limited to construction, upgrading, repair, and rehabilitation of roads, bridges, and road drainage. He said the amounts were attributed to projects under Organizational Outcome No. 1, Asset Preservation, rather than shown as a separate prior-year item.

thread.speaker: Undersecretary Nick Conti
thread.said: He said DPWH could furnish the committee with a list of the Asset Preservation projects attributed to MVUC collections. He identified the amount specified by DBM for 2027 as 15,000,000,000.

thread.speaker: Rep. Sidhu Ongwam
thread.said: He asked whether the Special Road Fund was a special fund under Article VI, Section 29(3) of the Constitution, distinct from the regular DPWH program funded through general appropriations.

thread.speaker: Rep. Sidhu Ongwam
thread.said: He argued that the statutory MVUC scope covered roads, bridges, and drainage, while the 2027 Asset Preservation Program covered roads and drainage and placed bridges in a separate Bridge Program. He asked whether placing MVUC inside Asset Preservation narrowed the operative use of the statutory earmark.

thread.speaker: Rep. Sidhu Ongwam
thread.said: He questioned the requirement for DPWH to disaggregate the Asset Preservation Program and submit a project list within fifteen days after the appropriation took effect. He said that post-effectivity submission would not inform the committee's deliberations before approval.

thread.speaker: Rep. Sidhu Ongwam
thread.said: He said retaining a standalone special road fund program, as in 2024, 2025, and 2026, would have made the 15,000,000,000 MVUC amount visible during deliberation and enactment. He characterized the fifteen-day disaggregation requirement as a workaround created by removing the standalone line.

thread.speaker: Rep. Sidhu Ongwam
thread.said: He emphasized that post-enactment project identification had already been struck down by the Supreme Court and said a pending case challenged the constitutionality of unprogrammed funds and earmarked funds, including the special road fund.

thread.speaker: DPWH Secretary
thread.said: The secretary stated that Republic Act 11239 limited MVUC use to the construction, upgrading, repair, and rehabilitation of roads, bridges, and road drainage, including safety and lighting-related items such as cat's eye.

thread.speaker: DPWH Secretary
thread.said: He said DPWH's MVUC proceeds for 2027, identified by DBM under Asset Preservation Organizational Outcome No. 1, totaled 15,000,000,000. He said the projects were detailed and itemized in the submitted National Expenditure Program and could be submitted to the committee.

thread.speaker: Rep. Sidhu Ongwam
thread.said: He recalled that MVUC had been included in the Asset Preservation Program in 2023, but that the veto message said this would be allowed only for that year and not for succeeding years. He assigned the matter for the secretary's attention.

thread.speaker: Rep. Michael Pan
thread.said: He raised an update on right-of-way issues along a highway and noted that some payments were being made through the provincial government. He asked for assistance through the allocation of funds.

thread.speaker: DPWH Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: The secretary asked about maintenance funds for national roads, particularly N1 and the Mariga Highway, including routine maintenance works on national highways.

thread.speaker: Rep. Michael Pan
thread.said: He added a concern about post-construction maintenance, explaining that highway sections had begun in small segments and could deteriorate without continuing maintenance. He asked DPWH to act on the post-construction issue.

thread.speaker: DPWH Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: The secretary responded, "We will do that," undertaking to address the post-construction maintenance concern.

thread.speaker: Rep. Michael Pan
thread.said: He described infrastructure needs in Samar, including highways, local roads, hospital projects, drainage canals, and flood-mitigation programs. He said his district had 524 barangays, 15 municipalities, one city, and a 500,000 population, including island municipalities, and sought clarification on how the problem could be rectified.

thread.speaker: DPWH Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: The secretary said DPWH's primary mandate was national roads. He acknowledged local-road concerns and said regional directors and district engineers should continue addressing them while prioritizing the department's national-road mandate.

thread.speaker: Rep. Michael Pan
thread.said: He said the issue would be a major problem in Samar, particularly for far-flung and island municipalities, because local roads were difficult to support. He asked DPWH to address the concern and local projects, including assistance related to the Maharlika Highway.

thread.speaker: An agency official
thread.said: An agency official asked that the concern be written down.

topics.topic: Transparency, contractor accountability, and anti-corruption controls
topics.summary: Rep. Iris Marie Montes asked Secretary Vince Dizon to make DPWH project information, procurement records, financial data, monitoring results, contractor ratings, and complaints publicly accessible. Dizon said the Transparency Portal already covered completed and ongoing projects, bidding livestreams, satellite-based monitoring, and supporting documents for PLN 11,000 plus projects, and committed to quarterly reports. Rep. Chel Diokno pressed DPWH on the absence of a consolidated national flood-control plan, lifestyle checks, contractor disclosures, convergence-program reforms, and nature-based solutions; Dizon cited plans for all 18 major river basins, with 14 being updated, and a target of 2027 for completion. Rep. Renee Co asked about blacklisting, delayed master plans, and audits, and DPWH reported 12 blacklisted contractors and ongoing investigations. Eli San Fernando questioned Redicon and R2 Builders, including figures of 9,000,000,000 and 2,700,000,000 pesos, and raised an alleged worker-wage shortfall involving 60 pesos over an 85 pesos rate. The agency's response on that allegation was garbled, leaving that issue unresolved.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish whether DPWH had effective transparency, disclosure, monitoring, auditing, and contractor-accountability mechanisms to protect public funds. Members also asked what information would be published, how anti-corruption controls were being implemented, and whether DPWH would act on questionable contracts, project quality, and worker-wage compliance.
topics.agency_position: DPWH said it was institutionalizing transparency through a public portal containing project, bidding, monitoring, and supporting documentation, while developing quarterly reporting, enhanced disclosures, and closer coordination with the Ombudsman, SEC, and investigative agencies. It also defended river-basin-based planning and program reforms, reported that 12 contractors had been blacklisted, and said audits and master-plan updates were ongoing; however, the response on R2 Builders' wage compliance was unclear.
topics.outcome: The agency made commitments on quarterly portal reporting, enhanced contractor disclosures, nature-based-solution reporting, master-plan updates, and submission of contractor information. Blacklisting and audits were reported as ongoing, but the wage-compliance allegation involving R2 Builders and several details concerning contractor accountability remained unresolved.

positions.position: She supported a comprehensive, publicly accessible project-transparency system covering procurement, project implementation, financial accountability, contractor performance, and citizen complaints, and sought regular reporting on anti-corruption results.

He pressed for a comprehensive national framework for flood-control and drainage planning, systematic lifestyle checks and disclosures, scrutiny of convergence programs, and inclusion of nature-based solutions.
She pressed DPWH to hold contractors and project personnel accountable for questionable or substandard flood-control projects and criticized delays in producing updated master plans.
He questioned the scale of Redicon and R2 Builders' contracts and argued that contractors receiving billions in public contracts should comply with worker-wage obligations.

He maintained that DPWH had begun meaningful transparency, disclosure, contractor-review, program-streamlining, and audit reforms, while acknowledging that some systems and plans remained under development.

actions.action: Provide regular quarterly reports to Congress and the public on the Transparency Portal and anti-corruption efforts before the next budget hearing.
Finalize a DPWH-SEC memorandum of agreement and translate it into DPWH and SEC circulars establishing stronger disclosure requirements for private contractors.
Keep the committee updated on the systematic lifestyle-check and disclosure work with the Ombudsman.

thread.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Montes
thread.said: She asked DPWH to explain the Transparency Portal and what project requirements and information it contained.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: He said DPWH launched the Transparency Portal in November of last year and had uploaded documents for completed and ongoing projects over the last ten years. The portal was intended to let the public and media examine DPWH projects and supporting documents.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: He said the portal would include supporting documentation for the PLN 11,000 plus projects of the department. The transcript's reference to “PLN” is unclear.

thread.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Montes
thread.said: She asked whether the portal was a presidential initiative rather than a DPWH initiative and whether it was being institutionalized.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: He said the portal was from DPWH, although it was established upon the President's instructions.

thread.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Montes
thread.said: She urged the department to cover the full project life cycle, including procurement and bidding transparency, livestreams, complete bidding documents, real-time monitoring, locations, geotagged photographs, budget-versus-actual cost data, change-order and disbursement records, contractor performance ratings, and citizen grievance or feedback mechanisms.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: He agreed that the proposed features would support transparency and said many were already available. Biddings for ongoing projects were livestreamed and saved in the portal, while project monitoring included physical-progress updates using satellite imagery obtained through an agreement with the Philippine Space Agency.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: He said the portal already contained bidding documents and physical-accomplishment information, and suggested that disbursement information, including whether projects were fully paid, could also be included.

thread.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Montes
thread.said: She asked for a report at the next budget hearing on how the portal was helping curb corruption.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: He said the committee should not wait until the next budget hearing and committed to provide a regular quarterly report from then until the following year.

thread.speaker: Rep. Chel Diokno
thread.said: He asked DPWH to confirm whether the country still lacked a national flood-control and drainage plan.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: He confirmed that there was no consolidated national plan. DPWH's approach had been to prepare master plans for each major river basin and, particularly for drainage, on a per-urban-center basis.

thread.speaker: Rep. Chel Diokno
thread.said: He asked whether the executive department was abandoning a national plan and relying only on river-basin and urban-center plans.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: He said the national plan was not being abandoned, but that experts advised planning at the major-river-basin level. He added that common nationwide principles included upstream interventions, retarding basins, and needs-based protection of populated areas.

thread.speaker: Rep. Chel Diokno
thread.said: He asked how many major river basins had written plans and pressed for a comprehensive national approach.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: He said all 18 major river basins had master plans, but 14 were being updated.

thread.speaker: Rep. Chel Diokno
thread.said: He asked when all major river-basin plans would be updated.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: He said DPWH was pushing its consultants to complete the updates by 2027, hopefully during the first half of the year.

thread.speaker: Rep. Chel Diokno
thread.said: After noting that he would monitor the Transparency Portal, he asked how regularly DPWH conducted lifestyle checks and whether it had measures involving waivers and conflict-of-interest disclosures.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: He said DPWH was working closely with the Office of the Ombudsman and had adopted a “one strike policy.” Verified reports, including reports originating on social media, could lead to show-cause proceedings, suspension, or termination.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: He said DPWH was working with its lawyers and other agencies on possible waivers and disclosures beyond existing statements of assets and liabilities requirements. He also said DPWH and the Securities and Exchange Commission were preparing a memorandum of agreement for more stringent disclosure requirements for private contractors handling public funds.

thread.speaker: Rep. Chel Diokno
thread.said: He asked whether DPWH had similar discussions or agreements with the Ombudsman concerning waivers and conflict-of-interest disclosures.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: He said the Ombudsman had more than 200 ongoing fact-finding cases and that DPWH regularly discussed how to strengthen disclosure and lifestyle-check systems.

thread.speaker: Rep. Chel Diokno
thread.said: He asked for DPWH's response to news reports concerning alleged ghost projects and the convergence and special support programs.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: He said the reforms in the proposed budget reflected recommendations from Secretary Babe Singh Son. DPWH had removed the CPAG portion, retained a basic infrastructure program for local roads, bridges, and community infrastructure, and made program requirements more stringent.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: He said DPWH had also streamlined or removed other convergence-program portions, including roll it and Tripsy, so that the departments primarily responsible for tourism, trade and industry, transportation, and other relevant sectors would identify and fund their priority projects.

thread.speaker: Rep. Chel Diokno
thread.said: He suggested that river-basin and other planning should include nature-based solutions.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: He said nature-based solutions were a critical component of DPWH's approach, including the use of gabions instead of fully concrete structures where appropriate. He said DPWH would report how many such solutions were already being implemented and how many more were planned.

thread.speaker: Rep. Renee Co
thread.said: She asked whether contractors associated with questionable, substandard, or ghost flood-control projects had been blacklisted and whether project-engineer ratings and quality-assurance reports were being considered.

thread.speaker: A DPWH agency official
thread.said: The official said 12 contractors had already been blacklisted and that the cases had undergone information and review processes. The remainder of the response is garbled in the transcript.

thread.speaker: A DPWH agency official
thread.said: The official said updating the NCR master plan would be completed by early next year or the end of this year, while DPWH coordinated existing LGU plans with the final NCR plan.

thread.speaker: Rep. Renee Co
thread.said: She questioned why a master plan remained unavailable despite DPWH audits and warnings dating from 2016, and asked about the timeline and prior efforts.

thread.speaker: A DPWH agency official
thread.said: The official said master plans existed for all 18 major river basins and that the updates were targeted for completion by next year, or the middle of next year.

thread.speaker: Rep. Renee Co
thread.said: She asked about the status of the identification and review of flood-control projects that may have worsened flooding rather than served their intended purpose.

thread.speaker: A DPWH agency official
thread.said: The official said an audit was ongoing with investigative agencies, including NDI, CIDG, and DOJ. The remainder of the response, including references to a former congressman and experts, was garbled.

thread.speaker: Eli San Fernando
thread.said: He asked about DPWH contracts awarded to Redicon Trading and Construction Corporation and R2 Builders.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: He referred to 2016 and a figure of 174, followed by a statement that 150 were completed. The exact project description and relationship between the figures are unclear in the transcript.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: He said DPWH would run the contractor information through the portal and submit it to the committee.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: He stated that Redicon's total contracts since 20.16 amounted to 9,000,000,000. The transcript's “20.16” is reproduced as spoken.

thread.speaker: Eli San Fernando
thread.said: He stated that R2 Builders had about 2,700,000,000 pesos in contracts since 2021.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: He confirmed that figure as accurate and said Redicon was the number one contractor in asphalt and road reconstruction, in both government contracts and the private sector.

thread.speaker: Eli San Fernando
thread.said: He asked DPWH to confirm reports that R2 Builders, despite securing billions of pesos in contracts, had not paid workers an additional 60 pesos increase from the 85 pesos rate.

thread.speaker: Secretary Vince Dizon
thread.said: He referred to a location or matter involving Australia and Bendia and said corrective measures would be taken at no cost to the national government. The response is substantially garbled and does not clearly resolve the wage-compliance allegation.

thread.speaker: Eli San Fernando
thread.said: He maintained that contractors receiving billions of pesos in DPWH contracts should be able to provide the additional wages sought by their workers.

topics.topic: Classroom construction, evacuation centers, and social-facility appropriations
topics.summary: A minority member questioned the specificity and allocation basis of regional appropriations for evacuation centers, PWD facilities, and senior-citizen facilities, citing 180,000,000, 5,000,000, and 20,000,000. The agency said evacuation-center sites and amounts were governed by a five-year plan and required coordination, validation, and implementability checks, while the Chair requested a district-by-district breakdown. Congressman Joseph Tan discussed project convergence, foreign-assisted projects, and a total DPWH amount of about 200 plus billion pesos, but the exchange did not produce a detailed accounting. Another member said only 30% of the FY2026 budget had been awarded and warned that the delay threatened the 6,000-classroom target. Secretary Vince Dizon corrected the reported classroom data and cited a 20,000,000,000 DPWH budget for 6,000 classrooms, while explaining that construction commonly began in the third quarter after validation and bidding. The Chair agreed to bring forward a proposal for clearer GAA line items and closer coordination or grouping of classroom funds with DepEd, leaving the broader accountability questions unresolved.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish whether FY2027 appropriations for evacuation centers, facilities for persons with disabilities and senior citizens, and classrooms were sufficiently specific, needs-based, and implementable. Members also questioned whether project-award delays and broad GAA line items were undermining accountability and the target to complete 6,000 classrooms.
topics.agency_position: DPWH said project allocations were subject to implementability, site, coordination, and validation requirements, and that evacuation-center sites and amounts were determined under a five-year plan with other disaster-management agencies. On classrooms, DPWH said third-quarter starts and October-November bidding were longstanding consequences of coordination and validation, while supporting closer grouping of the budget with DepEd and clearer planning.
topics.outcome: The Chair undertook to raise the proposal for clearer GAA line items, but the record did not resolve the disputed allocation basis, the district figures, or the classroom-award delay. The issue therefore remained open subject to the requested breakdown and further committee consideration.

positions.position: Vague regional and district allocations were not sufficiently needs-based or specific and required a district-level breakdown and stronger accountability.
Project convergence, foreign-assisted projects, and the total DPWH program required clarification, while classroom and social-infrastructure planning needed site-specific and consolidated treatment.
Classroom-award delays and congressional insertions were contributing to an effective delay in completing the 6,000-classroom target; GAA line items should be clearer and more specific.

The reported classroom data needed correction, classroom delays reflected the usual third-quarter start and validation-and-bidding process, and grouping classroom funds with DepEd could address the recurring problem.
