thread.speaker: Gilbert Teodoro, Secretary of National Defense
thread.said: Secretary Teodoro said modernization had to prioritize core systems, support infrastructure, logistics, reserves, IT, and cyber capabilities rather than merely acquiring major platforms. He said equipment without the infrastructure to house, maintain, and access it would be unsustainable.

thread.speaker: Gilbert Teodoro, Secretary of National Defense
thread.said: He said the AFP had about 46 Black Hawk helicopters but needed larger, palletized rotary platforms. He also said the Navy continued to acquire modern corvettes and frigates and that the Army's priority was improving mobility and its footprint throughout the Philippines.

thread.speaker: Gilbert Teodoro, Secretary of National Defense
thread.said: He presented a proposed DND budget of 324,632,000,000, with 10% for capital outlay, 55% for personal services, and 35% for maintenance and other operating expenses.

thread.speaker: Gilbert Teodoro, Secretary of National Defense
thread.said: He identified 50,000,000,000 for modernization, 71,000,000,000 for AFP retirees, and JPY 11,000,000,000 for veterans ameliorations. He also said the AFP represented 49% of the total MUP budget.

thread.speaker: Gilbert Teodoro, Secretary of National Defense
thread.said: He said the modernization program had 50 and no unprogrammed amounts.

thread.speaker: Gilbert Teodoro, Secretary of National Defense
thread.said: He said the capital-outlay proposal was 239,000,000 and had been specifically matched to modernization items, but the required matching infrastructure was not included. He warned that modernization could not continue without that infrastructure.

thread.speaker: Gilbert Teodoro, Secretary of National Defense
thread.said: He said 10 modernization projects were being implemented and that, if the entire modernization fund were used, next year's payments for the multi-year obligational authority would reach at about 57 already, with the additional amount unclear.

thread.speaker: Arnan Panaligan, Deputy Majority Leader
thread.said: Deputy Majority Leader Panaligan noted that the 2027 AFP modernization program had been given PHP 50,000,000,000 without unprogrammed appropriations and asked what would be charged to the 2026 amount of PHP 40,000,000,000 and the proposed 2027 amount of PHP 50,000,000,000, particularly in relation to Horizon Three.

thread.speaker: Gilbert Teodoro, Secretary of National Defense
thread.said: Secretary Teodoro's response was garbled and did not provide a clear itemized answer to the requested 2026 and 2027 modernization line items.

thread.speaker: Arnan Panaligan, Deputy Majority Leader
thread.said: Panaligan said DBM had indicated that the release of 50,000,000,000 in unprogrammed funds would require excess revenues and another condition transcribed as “and D.” He asked the Secretary to make strong representations for access to the unprogrammed funds.

thread.speaker: Arnan Panaligan, Deputy Majority Leader
thread.said: Panaligan requested copies of the items charged to PHP 40,000,000,000 for the current year and the proposed PHP 50,000,000,000 for the next year.

thread.speaker: Arnan Panaligan, Deputy Majority Leader
thread.said: He asked whether the modernization loan ceiling should be removed or increased from the ceiling set under PD 415, which the transcript described as USD 300,000,000, to USD 1,000,000,000 for a single project under his House bill.

thread.speaker: Gilbert Teodoro, Secretary of National Defense
thread.said: Secretary Teodoro favored retaining a cap. He said DBM and DOF would set the ceiling based on the country's fiscal condition and the type of loan, with DOF ultimately entering into the loan and controlling the financial arrangement.

thread.speaker: Gilbert Teodoro, Secretary of National Defense
thread.said: He explained that the PD 415 ceiling was probably related to IMF control and currency-stabilization loans in the 1970s, when foreign-exchange controls limited foreign-loan expenditures to 300,000,000.

thread.speaker: Arnan Panaligan, Deputy Majority Leader
thread.said: Panaligan said his House bill would be discussed by a technical working group and suggested that the cap might be removed.

thread.speaker: Gilbert Teodoro, Secretary of National Defense
thread.said: Secretary Teodoro said the U.S. Senate bill identified by Panaligan had been enacted. He said U.S. funding for the following year would, in his belief, be about 100,000,000 US, while the law set a maximum of US500 million dollars per year subject to Treasury availability.

thread.speaker: Arnan Panaligan, Deputy Majority Leader
thread.said: Panaligan asked whether the U.S. foreign military financing would boost modernization and help address the budget constraint, noting that it would not be transferred to the Philippine Treasury.

thread.speaker: Gilbert Teodoro, Secretary of National Defense
thread.said: Secretary Teodoro said it would help, together with Japan's official security assistance for domain awareness. He rejected the suggestion that the lower modernization allocation was caused by the foreign assistance and attributed it to macro-level fiscal considerations.

thread.speaker: Arnan Panaligan, Deputy Majority Leader
thread.said: Panaligan asked about reports that the Navy intended to acquire two additional missile frigates in addition to two frigates ordered the previous year, which would become the fifth and sixth guided-missile frigates.

thread.speaker: Gilbert Teodoro, Secretary of National Defense
thread.said: He confirmed that there was an intent to acquire the additional frigates, but said “the trigger has not yet been pulled.”

thread.speaker: Gilbert Teodoro, Secretary of National Defense
thread.said: He said installation and completion of fitted sensors and weapon systems for the Rizal-class and Calder-class vessels were ongoing.

thread.speaker: Arnan Panaligan, Deputy Majority Leader
thread.said: Panaligan asked about multirole fighters and additional air-defense and coastal-defense missiles.

thread.speaker: Gilbert Teodoro, Secretary of National Defense
thread.said: Secretary Teodoro said those acquisitions remained under consideration depending on financing, but the DND first needed ground control, domain awareness, air-to-air refueling, and adequate hangar and maintenance facilities. He said the minimum force package was 40 at any one mission for external defense.

thread.speaker: Arnan Panaligan, Deputy Majority Leader
thread.said: Panaligan said Congress could not simply increase the President's proposed appropriations and that the main funding decision would be made at the DBCC level.

thread.speaker: Gilbert Teodoro, Secretary of National Defense
thread.said: Secretary Teodoro reiterated that connectivity and infrastructure were necessary to support the weight and logistics of the equipment being acquired.

thread.speaker: Brian Poe, Representative
thread.said: Representative Poe said he could not identify a Philippine Air Force budget line for drone technology or hardware and asked whether there was a specific allocation for drone procurement.

thread.speaker: Gilbert Teodoro, Secretary of National Defense
thread.said: Secretary Teodoro said drones were part of the modernization fund. The AFP already had a fleet of UAVs providing ISR services, but further acquisition depended on integrating the capabilities and establishing working procedures.

thread.speaker: Gilbert Teodoro, Secretary of National Defense
thread.said: He said the principal issue was not simply personnel but integration into operations, including secure, near-real-time connectivity and network capabilities.

thread.speaker: Gilbert Teodoro, Secretary of National Defense
thread.said: He said the specific drone systems were classified and could not be identified because of the risk of compromise, particularly involving artificial intelligence. He said the DND had capabilities but could not disclose them.

thread.speaker: Brian Poe, Representative
thread.said: Poe said one F-16 might cost 70,000,000 on average, which he compared with about 2,000 Shahed-class drones, arguing that the economics of drone warfare warranted greater attention.

thread.speaker: Sara Hirado, Representative
thread.said: Representative Hirado asked what agreements had been signed under the revised AFP modernization program and requested a report on the modernization program from 1995 through the current year.

thread.speaker: Gilbert Teodoro, Secretary of National Defense
thread.said: Secretary Teodoro said he could disclose only categories because the agreements were restricted. They involved major weapon systems and domain-awareness systems for external defense, including government-to-government agreements with like-minded countries.

thread.speaker: Gilbert Teodoro, Secretary of National Defense
thread.said: He said some countries could not be identified because linking a system to its country of origin could compromise the system. He said the partners shared interests with the Philippines in the West Philippine Sea and would not pose supply-chain problems.

thread.speaker: Gilbert Teodoro, Secretary of National Defense
thread.said: In response to Vice Chair Rodriguez, Secretary Teodoro said the remaining budget for the Lumbia site for 2026 was 115,000,000 and that 450,000,000 had already been budgeted, although the transcript's reference to the applicable year is unclear.

thread.speaker: Gilbert Teodoro, Secretary of National Defense
thread.said: He said there was no U.S. counterpart yet for Lumbia as an EDCA site. The United States was still scoping possible support, including a multipurpose warehouse, while the Philippine side was considering air-traffic-control enhancement.

thread.speaker: Rufus Rodriguez, Vice Chair
thread.said: Vice Chair Rodriguez asked about the proposed naval facility in Tagoloan and its expected cost once the title was finalized.

thread.speaker: Gilbert Teodoro, Secretary of National Defense
thread.said: Secretary Teodoro said a complete dry dock capable of supporting the growing fleet would cost about 40,000,000,000, including equipment. The transcript also records the spoken currency as “COP 40,000,000,000.”

thread.speaker: Gilbert Teodoro, Secretary of National Defense
thread.said: He said the dry dock was strategically located because it was relatively protected from typhoons and could accommodate even the largest vessel, while Subic could not serve as a dry dock because it was an operating naval base.

thread.speaker: Gilbert Teodoro, Secretary of National Defense
thread.said: He said the timetable depended on finalizing the title and that the DND was trying to complete titling so it could vacate Sangley, which was too shallow and small for the Navy's platforms.

thread.speaker: Gilbert Teodoro, Secretary of National Defense
thread.said: He said there was no specific guidance to transfer the Fourth Infantry Division. Instead, the Army was being directed to assess divisional and brigade locations as logistical nodes with headquarters, motor pools, medical facilities, and connectivity to strategic bases.

thread.speaker: Rufus Rodriguez, Vice Chair
thread.said: Vice Chair Rodriguez urged the DND to retain the Fourth Infantry Division in the Cagayan de Oro area and to consider the location as a continuing logistics center for Mindanao.

thread.speaker: Gilbert Teodoro, Secretary of National Defense
thread.said: Secretary Teodoro said Northern Mindanao was a prime consideration, with Lumbia serving the strike wing and OCD operations center and the proposed dockyard adding naval capability.

thread.speaker: Tony Patalbano, Representative
thread.said: Representative Patalbano asked whether the DND could develop a Marshall Plan-type program to strengthen the AFP engineering brigade and provide more funding for disaster mitigation and rehabilitation.

thread.speaker: Gilbert Teodoro, Secretary of National Defense
thread.said: Secretary Teodoro said the engineering brigades were being converted into combat engineering brigades focused on emergency bridging, demining, base development, and enabling heavy equipment to operate safely. He said the Army's strategic plan included all-weather access roads to new bases, which would support logistics, presence, deterrence, and local economic activity.

thread.speaker: Tony Patalbano, Representative
thread.said: Patalbano requested an update on the drone program, citing the strategic importance and lower apparent cost of drones in contemporary conflicts.

thread.speaker: Gilbert Teodoro, Secretary of National Defense
thread.said: Secretary Teodoro said the DND was building the framework and backbone for the drone program and developing control systems alongside the capabilities. He said the DND already had capabilities but could not disclose more.

thread.speaker: Mika Suansing, Chair
thread.said: Chair Suansing manifested support for the DND budget and said she would advocate for priority programs and projects omitted from the NEP. She said the budget amendments review subcommittee would deliberate on requests line by line.

thread.speaker: Gilbert Teodoro, Secretary of National Defense

topics.topic: AFP modernization’s proposed 50,000,000,000 and prior 40,000,000,000
topics.summary: Deputy Majority Leader Arnan Panaligan asked DND to identify the items covered by about 40 billion for 2026 and the proposed 50 billion for 2027, and urged access to 50 billion in unprogrammed appropriations. The secretary's recorded response to the itemization request was unclear, and no detailed list was supplied in the exchange. Panaligan then raised his bill to revise or remove the PD 415 loan ceiling, while Secretary Gilbert Teodoro favored retaining a cap controlled by DBM and DOF. Teodoro said enacted US legislation could provide about 100 million in the following year, with a maximum of US500 million dollars per year subject to availability, and that Japan's assistance would also help. He confirmed an intent to acquire two more missile frigates but said the acquisition trigger had not been pulled, and said multirole fighters remained dependent on financing and supporting systems. The loan-ceiling question was committed to a technical working group, while the requested allocation documents and unprogrammed-funding access remained unanswered in the transcript.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish which AFP modernization items would be charged against the proposed 2027 allocation and the prior-year allocation, including whether unprogrammed appropriations could be accessed. It also examined whether the statutory ceiling on modernization loans should be retained, increased, or removed, and how external financing could support the program.
topics.agency_position: DND supported retaining a loan cap administered by DBM and DOF, rather than removing the ceiling, because those agencies could set borrowing limits according to fiscal capacity and debt-service considerations. Teodoro said foreign military financing and Japan's security assistance would help modernization, but that the domestic allocation reflected broader fiscal constraints and that major acquisitions depended on financing and supporting infrastructure.
topics.outcome: The secretary answered the loan-policy and external-financing questions, but the transcript did not provide a clear itemization of the 2026 and 2027 modernization allocations or confirm access to the unprogrammed funds. The loan-ceiling issue was left for further consideration by the National Defense committee's technical working group.

positions.position: He sought detailed itemization of the 2026 and 2027 modernization allocations, urged strong representation for access to unprogrammed appropriations, and favored considering an increase or removal of the PD 415 loan ceiling. He also indicated that the loan-ceiling issue would proceed to a technical working group.

He preferred retaining a loan cap under DBM and DOF control, while acknowledging that external financing could supplement the modernization program. He said multirole-fighter and other major acquisition plans remained dependent on financing and the availability of necessary support systems.

thread.speaker: Deputy Majority Leader Arnan Panaligan
thread.said: Panaligan said the proposed 2027 AFP modernization program had PHP 50,000,000,000 pesos without unprogrammed appropriations and asked which items would be charged against that amount. He said the allocation could affect Horizon Three, which had undergone repeated re-horizonings.

thread.speaker: Deputy Majority Leader Arnan Panaligan
thread.said: He asked what items had been charged to the 2026 allocation and what items were proposed for the 2027 amount.

thread.speaker: Deputy Majority Leader Arnan Panaligan
thread.said: He repeated the request for the particular items to be charged to the PHP 50,000,000,000 proposed for 2027 and asked about the PHP 40,000,000,000 for 2026, referring to MICA.

thread.speaker: Secretary Gilbert Teodoro
thread.said: Teodoro acknowledged the question about 2026, but the machine-generated transcript records his response as “Your honor, 21,” which is unclear and does not identify the charged items.

thread.speaker: Deputy Majority Leader Arnan Panaligan
thread.said: Panaligan recalled asking the DBM secretary at the DBCC budget hearing whether PHP 50,000,000,000 in unprogrammed funding could be released for the year. He said he had been told release would depend on excess revenues and a second condition recorded unclearly as “and D.”

thread.speaker: Deputy Majority Leader Arnan Panaligan
thread.said: He urged the DND to make a strong representation for access to the unprogrammed funds, given the modernization program's requirements.

thread.speaker: Deputy Majority Leader Arnan Panaligan
thread.said: Panaligan requested copies of the items charged to PHP 40,000,000,000 and the proposed items for PHP 50,000,000,000 for 2027, referring again to MICA.

thread.speaker: Deputy Majority Leader Arnan Panaligan
thread.said: He recalled that Teodoro had previously preferred allowing DND and the AFP to obtain loans for modernization because of budget constraints. He asked about amending PD 415, which set the loan ceiling at USD 300,000,000 based on the 1974 exchange rate.

thread.speaker: Deputy Majority Leader Arnan Panaligan
thread.said: Panaligan said he had filed House Bill No. 1859 to increase the ceiling to USD 1,000,000,000 for a single project, with a possible alternative of removing the ceiling altogether.

thread.speaker: Deputy Majority Leader Arnan Panaligan
thread.said: He asked whether DND preferred retaining a ceiling, raising it from 300 to a billion dollars, or removing it altogether.

thread.speaker: Secretary Gilbert Teodoro
thread.said: Teodoro favored retaining a cap. He said DBM and DOF would set it based on the country's fiscal condition and the type of loan, and that DOF would ultimately enter into the loan.

thread.speaker: Secretary Gilbert Teodoro
thread.said: Teodoro said DBM and DOF would have “total control” over the financial accommodation and would set the ceiling according to what the country could afford.

thread.speaker: Secretary Gilbert Teodoro
thread.said: He said DOF's involvement provided a sufficient guarantee that the government could service the debt, noting DOF's revenue-raising mandate.

thread.speaker: Deputy Majority Leader Arnan Panaligan
thread.said: Panaligan said the House National Defense committee chair had assured him that the bill would soon be deliberated and had assigned him to head the technical working group. He said the loan-ceiling issue would be discussed further at the TWG.

thread.speaker: Secretary Gilbert Teodoro
thread.said: Teodoro suggested that PD 415's ceiling may have originated from IMF controls and currency-stabilization loans in the 1970s, when foreign-exchange controls limited expenditures on foreign loans.

thread.speaker: Secretary Gilbert Teodoro
thread.said: He said the USD 300,000,000 limit may have been connected to the grant of currency-stabilization loans by the IMF, while qualifying that this was his suspicion.

thread.speaker: Deputy Majority Leader Arnan Panaligan
thread.said: Panaligan suggested that the cap might now be removed and asked about a United States Senate measure intended to modernize Philippine defense capabilities.

thread.speaker: Secretary Gilbert Teodoro
thread.said: Teodoro asked which Senate bill Panaligan was referring to.

thread.speaker: Deputy Majority Leader Arnan Panaligan
thread.said: Panaligan identified it as Senate Bill 1497, described in the transcript as the “Pera Philippine” measure, and asked whether it had been enacted.

thread.speaker: Secretary Gilbert Teodoro
thread.said: Teodoro said the measure had been enacted by the US Congress. He added that he believed the US Government would allocate 100,000,000 for the following year and that the law set a maximum of US500 million dollars per year, depending on Treasury availability.

thread.speaker: Deputy Majority Leader Arnan Panaligan
thread.said: Panaligan listed coastal defense, long-range fires, maritime security, and integrated air defense as priorities under the US measure. He asked whether the foreign military financing would help boost modernization and address budget constraints.

thread.speaker: Secretary Gilbert Teodoro
thread.said: Teodoro said the assistance would help, together with Japan's official security assistance for domain awareness.

thread.speaker: Secretary Gilbert Teodoro
thread.said: Teodoro rejected the suggestion that foreign assistance explained the relatively small modernization allocation, saying the allocation was probably driven by the country's macro-level fiscal considerations.

thread.speaker: Deputy Majority Leader Arnan Panaligan
thread.said: Panaligan asked whether the reported plan to acquire two more missile frigates, in addition to two ordered the previous year, could be confirmed.

thread.speaker: Secretary Gilbert Teodoro
thread.said: Teodoro confirmed that there was an intent to acquire the additional frigates but said “the trigger has not yet been pulled,” meaning no final acquisition action had been taken.

thread.speaker: Deputy Majority Leader Arnan Panaligan
thread.said: Panaligan followed up on the upgrading and completion of the installation of sensors and weapons systems for the Rizal-class and Kaliber-class vessels.

thread.speaker: Secretary Gilbert Teodoro
thread.said: Teodoro answered that the work was ongoing.

thread.speaker: Deputy Majority Leader Arnan Panaligan
thread.said: Panaligan asked about plans to acquire multirole fighters and additional air-defense and coastal-defense missiles.

thread.speaker: Secretary Gilbert Teodoro
thread.said: Teodoro said the plans remained under consideration depending on financing. He stressed that ground control, domain awareness, air-to-air refueling, and adequate hangar and servicing facilities had to be in place before acquiring multirole fighters.

thread.speaker: Secretary Gilbert Teodoro
thread.said: Teodoro warned that without those supporting systems, a multirole fighter would be an unguided, pilot-controlled aircraft whose use would be marginal.

thread.speaker: Secretary Gilbert Teodoro
thread.said: He said the aircraft acquisition had to be treated as a force package and that inadequate hangar facilities would render the aircraft useless.

thread.speaker: Secretary Gilbert Teodoro
thread.said: Teodoro said the minimum force package was 40 at any one mission, in the context of external defense. The transcript does not specify the unit beyond the reference to the force package.

thread.speaker: Deputy Majority Leader Arnan Panaligan
thread.said: Panaligan said amending PD 415 could help DND obtain financing for its programs. He also noted that the executive prepared the expenditure program and that Congress could not increase the President's proposed appropriations without taking funds from other items.

thread.speaker: Secretary Gilbert Teodoro
thread.said: Teodoro added that connectivity and infrastructure were necessary to perform the mission roles. He said infrastructure capable of supporting the equipment's weight would address many logistics problems.

thread.speaker: Deputy Majority Leader Arnan Panaligan
thread.said: Panaligan ended the exchange without further questions and expressed appreciation for the AFP and DND's efforts to secure Philippine territory and sovereignty.

topics.topic: Modernization-loan ceiling and foreign defense assistance
topics.summary: Deputy Majority Leader Arnan Panaligan asked which items would be financed from the proposed PHP 50,000,000,000 2027 modernization allocation and requested the corresponding 2026 and 2027 itemization. He also proposed increasing or removing the USD 300,000,000 loan ceiling, while Secretary Gilbert Teodoro favored retaining a cap set by DBM and DOF according to fiscal capacity. Teodoro confirmed that a U.S. defense-capabilities measure had been enacted, with about 100,000,000 expected for the following year and a US500 million dollars annual maximum subject to Treasury availability. Vice Chair Rufus Rodriguez then asked about Lumbia, where DND reported 115,000,000 remaining for the current year, no U.S. counterpart funding yet, and no agreed U.S.-built structure because assistance was still being scoped. Teodoro estimated the proposed Tagoloan dry dock at about 40,000,000,000 including equipment, but said titling had to be completed before construction could proceed. The loan issue and modernization documents required further action, while Lumbia assistance and the construction timetable remained unresolved.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish which AFP modernization items would be funded under the proposed 2027 allocation and whether DND preferred retaining, increasing, or removing the statutory modernization-loan ceiling. It also examined how foreign military financing and U.S. assistance would support modernization-related facilities, including Lumbia and the proposed Tagoloan dry dock.
topics.agency_position: DND favored retaining a modernization-loan cap because DBM and DOF would determine the ceiling according to fiscal capacity and loan terms. It said U.S. assistance would support modernization but that no Lumbia counterpart funding or agreed U.S.-built structure existed yet; Lumbia assistance was still being scoped. DND supported the proposed Tagoloan dry dock in principle, subject to titling, at an estimated cost of 40,000,000,000.
topics.outcome: The loan-ceiling issue was left for further deliberation in the technical working group, while the requested modernization itemization was to be furnished. U.S. support for Lumbia remained unagreed and under scoping, and the Tagoloan dry dock remained contingent on titling, with no construction timetable given.

positions.position: Supported revisiting or increasing the modernization-loan ceiling, including possible removal of the cap, and requested itemized modernization allocations. He also viewed foreign military financing as potentially helpful in easing modernization budget constraints.

Pressed for clarity on U.S. counterpart assistance at Lumbia, supported development of Lumbia and the Tagoloan dry dock, and urged DND to retain or enlarge the Patag area as a Northern Mindanao logistics center.

Supported a loan ceiling set through DBM and DOF fiscal controls, acknowledged the value of U.S. and Japanese assistance, and expressed support for Lumbia and the Tagoloan dry dock as parts of the AFP's logistics and external-defense infrastructure.

thread.said: Rodriguez asked what counterpart funding the United States would provide for Lumbia as an EDCA site.

thread.said: Teodoro answered, "None yet," and explained that Lumbia's development was being delayed by right-of-way problems and informal settlers.

thread.said: On social costs and possible impacts of an American presence, Teodoro said relocation and right-of-way issues had to be addressed first to provide base security. He said any U.S. personnel would be guided by the SOFA.

thread.said: Rodriguez asked about the proposed naval base or dockyard in Tagoloan and, once titling was completed, how much a complete dry dock would cost.

thread.speaker: Gilbert Teodoro
thread.said: Teodoro estimated that a complete dry dock capable of supporting the growing fleet would cost about 40,000,000,000, including equipment.

thread.speaker: Rufus Rodriguez
thread.said: Rodriguez said the project would generate substantial economic activity for the area.

thread.speaker: Gilbert Teodoro
thread.said: Teodoro said the site was strategic because it was relatively free from typhoons and could accommodate even the largest vessel. He explained that Subic could not currently serve as a dry dock because it remained an operating naval base.

thread.speaker: Gilbert Teodoro

thread.said: Rodriguez asked DND to consider retaining the Patag area as a continuing logistics center because of its strategic location as a gateway to Mindanao.

topics.topic: AFP earmarked revenues, BCDA shares, and DND off-budget balances
topics.summary: Roberto Nazal Jr. raised whether about 10.285 billion in accumulated BCDA earmarked revenues and about 4.029 billion in DND off-budget balances were available before Congress provided additional funding. He asked whether the balances reflected insufficient AFP requests, DBM non-approval, deliberate conservation, or legal and regulatory restrictions. Secretary Gilbert Teodoro answered that the BCDA funds were matched to existing programs and contracts and were pledged for payments, while the off-budget funds were held in the BTR and were not earning interest. He identified ongoing projects, including the Lumbia Airbase runway, and said trust-receipt items had to be remitted to DBM before disbursement. He also stated that the resources and interest receipts were considered in the AFP submissions used to prepare the FY 2027 request. The committee requested lists of the pledged and ongoing projects, with the Chair directing the department to provide the information.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish whether AFP earmarked revenues and DND off-budget balances were genuinely available for additional programs or were already committed, legally restricted, or unused because of agency or DBM action. It also asked whether these resources had been considered in preparing the FY 2027 budget request.
topics.agency_position: The DND stated that the accumulated BCDA earmarked revenues were already matched to ongoing projects and existing contracts and were pledged for payments, rather than being freely available for new projects. It also stated that the off-budget accounts were held in the BTR, were not earning interest, were associated with implementable projects or trust-receipt items, and that interest receipts and these resources were considered in the AFP submissions underlying the FY 2027 request.
topics.outcome: The Secretary answered that the balances were committed to existing contracts or ongoing projects, were subject to DBM remittance procedures, and were considered in the budget submission. The committee requested project lists, and the Chair undertook to direct the department to submit them; the underlying off-budget balance figures and project-level documentation remained subject to submission.

positions.position: He sought assurance that off-budget and earmarked resources were fully and efficiently used before additional regular appropriations were provided, and requested project-level documentation.
She directed the department to provide the requested list of earmarked-revenue projects pledged for payment.

He maintained that the balances were committed to existing contracts or ongoing projects, subject to the applicable remittance and disbursement process, and had been considered in the budget submission.

topics.topic: Defense self-reliance, Government Arsenal cuts, and ammunition production
topics.summary: Eli San Fernando asked Secretary Gilbert Teodoro to define self-reliance and explain the Government Arsenal's roughly 21.8% budget reduction. The Secretary defined self-reliance as securing supply chains quickly and cost-effectively, rather than achieving complete domestic production. He said the Arsenal had produced 60 million rounds but was being redirected toward more advanced capabilities, while the member highlighted a 2026 target of 60 million rounds against actual output of 500,000. The Secretary attributed the shortfall to a worldwide shortage of nitrocellulose precursors and said the materials could come from a small number of foreign sources. San Fernando argued that industrial policy was essential for defense resilience, and the Secretary agreed. Representative Jay Vernego separately asked about reducing imported-arms dependence, local manufacturing, LBIT Systems procurement, and drone guidelines; the Secretary said there were no new LBIT contracts, local industry remained focused on small arms, and drone guidelines could be shared in non-sensitive form. The issue remained substantively unresolved on restoring Arsenal funding or closing the production gap, although the agency committed to support industrial policy and provide or report additional information.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish what the Department of National Defense meant by a self-reliant defense force, whether the Government Arsenal's reduced budget and low ammunition output undermined that goal, and what role local industry and industrial policy should play. Members also asked how foreign procurement, technology transfer, local arms and drone production, and operational guidelines fit within that policy.
topics.agency_position: The DND defined self-reliance as resilient, secure, cost-effective, and timely supply chains rather than complete domestic production. It supported industrial policy and domestic capability development, but said the Government Arsenal should move beyond small arms toward more advanced systems, while local industry should pursue forward-looking capabilities that could scale and provide value.
topics.outcome: The Secretary agreed in principle that industrial policy was necessary, but maintained that self-reliance did not require complete indigenous production and that current local industry was not yet suited to the DND's priority capabilities. The Government Arsenal's budget reduction and ammunition-production shortfall were attributed to capital-outlay reprioritization and precursor shortages; no funding restoration or production remedy was committed during the exchange.

positions.position: He argued that an effective defense plan required an industrial policy capable of supporting domestic production of arms, precursors, and materials, particularly during war or supply disruptions.
He pressed the DND on reducing import dependence, developing local arms and drone production, and establishing written guidelines for responsible military drone use.

positions.position: He supported industrial policy in principle but favored supply-chain security, partnerships, research and development, intellectual-property participation, and advanced defense capabilities over an exclusive focus on indigenous small-arms production.

thread.speaker: Gilbert Teodoro, Secretary of National Defense
thread.said: The Government Arsenal had provided 60,000,000 rounds of small arms ammunition. He said its strategic tasking would shift toward more technologically advanced weaponry rather than continuing to focus primarily on small arms.

thread.speaker: Elijah San Fernando
thread.said: He asked whether equipping and rationing the armed forces meant that the country should be able to provide for its own defense requirements.

thread.speaker: Gilbert Teodoro, Secretary of National Defense
thread.said: He answered that providing for the country's own needs was part of resilience, but not an absolute requirement for every item because worldwide supply chains were defined for specific products. The Philippines should provide for its own needs when it could.

thread.speaker: Elijah San Fernando
thread.said: He asked for the operational definition of the proposed outcome indicator to develop a modern, credible, self-reliant defense force.

thread.speaker: Gilbert Teodoro, Secretary of National Defense
thread.said: He defined self-reliance as securing supply chains by the most expeditious and cost-effective means possible. He stressed that “self reliance does not mean indigenous,” but meant obtaining needed capabilities on favorable terms and with the least lead time.

thread.speaker: Elijah San Fernando
thread.said: He followed up by asking whether self-reliance therefore did not necessarily require acquiring or producing items domestically.

thread.speaker: Gilbert Teodoro, Secretary of National Defense
thread.said: He distinguished self-reliance from import substitution. He said resilience could include obtaining capabilities abroad, including through partnerships or overseas production, so long as the Philippines received what it needed quickly and on an evolutionary basis.

thread.speaker: Elijah San Fernando
thread.said: He asked why the Government Arsenal budget in the NEP had been reduced by 21.8%.

thread.speaker: Gilbert Teodoro, Secretary of National Defense
thread.said: He attributed the reduction to capital outlay for structures and facilities. He said the Government Arsenal had a new roadmap as a sovereign enterprise, comparable to the Central Bank Mint, and that its future activity would concentrate on capabilities beyond small arms.

thread.speaker: Elijah San Fernando
thread.said: He noted that the 2026 first-quarter target was 60,000,000 rounds of ammunition while actual output was only 500,000, and asked the Secretary to explain the shortfall.

thread.speaker: Gilbert Teodoro, Secretary of National Defense
thread.said: He attributed the low output to difficulty sourcing precursor materials, describing a worldwide shortage and a supplier's market.

thread.speaker: Elijah San Fernando
thread.said: He asked where the Government Arsenal usually sourced its precursor materials.

thread.speaker: Gilbert Teodoro, Secretary of National Defense
thread.said: He said sourcing depended on availability and could include The United States, South Africa, Brazil, and a few other countries. He identified the material as nitrocellulose.

thread.speaker: Elijah San Fernando
thread.said: He asked whether the multibillion peso contracts in the 2027 DND program contained the legally required understudy programs to train Filipino workers and technology-transfer clauses.

thread.speaker: Gilbert Teodoro, Secretary of National Defense
thread.said: He said there were no new 2027 contracts except a few. He added that the law was unworkable without spending on research and development and acquiring equity sufficient to share in intellectual property rights, which he described as the key to a viable self-reliance program.

thread.speaker: Elijah San Fernando
thread.said: He stated that defense also involved industrial policy and that an effective defense plan required the country to develop the capacity to produce and equip its own forces.

thread.speaker: Gilbert Teodoro, Secretary of National Defense
thread.said: He agreed that defense was connected to industrial policy.

thread.speaker: Elijah San Fernando
thread.said: He asked the Secretary to comment on the reported view that the Philippines did not need to pursue industrial policy in the same way as neighboring countries, despite the Philippine Development Plan's self-reliant defense objective.

thread.speaker: Gilbert Teodoro, Secretary of National Defense
thread.said: He said the view might mean that the Philippines should not reinvent technology available through partnerships. However, he said the country still needed to address basic conditions such as ease of doing business, transaction and administrative costs, connectivity, and power costs, because industrial activity had to produce a positive outcome unless it was treated as a public good.

thread.speaker: Elijah San Fernando
thread.said: He reiterated that he supported industrial policy, citing the need to develop domestic industry so the country could obtain precursors and materials during war or other crises.

thread.speaker: Gilbert Teodoro, Secretary of National Defense
thread.said: He expressly agreed with the member's position, saying there was “no debate about it.”

thread.speaker: Jay Vernego
thread.said: He asked whether the DND had considered or entered into additional arms procurement contracts with LBIT Systems.

thread.speaker: Gilbert Teodoro, Secretary of National Defense
thread.said: He said the DND only needed to replenish missile systems used in training and had no additional or new contracts with LBIT Systems.

thread.speaker: Jay Vernego
thread.said: He asked what steps the DND had taken to reduce dependence on imported arms and whether it was exploring local arms manufacturing.

thread.speaker: Gilbert Teodoro, Secretary of National Defense
thread.said: He said the immediate capability needed was not what local arms manufacturers currently provided, since their capabilities centered on small arms. The DND instead needed domain awareness, internal hardening systems, and deterrent systems, while remaining open to local industry that could scale forward-looking production.

thread.speaker: Jay Vernego
thread.said: He asked about arms acquisition beyond small arms, including drones.

thread.speaker: Gilbert Teodoro, Secretary of National Defense
thread.said: He said drones were part of every country's toolkit, but their production was relatively easy compared with the technology and systems placed in them. He noted that the relevant technology could change every few days because of artificial intelligence.

thread.speaker: Jay Vernego
thread.said: He asked whether written operational guidelines existed for military drone use.

thread.speaker: Gilbert Teodoro, Secretary of National Defense
thread.said: He said the technology was still evolving and that the DND first needed to develop the backbone systems required for responsible drone use. He stated that, for the DND, drones currently had no offensive uses and were being used for surveillance.

thread.speaker: Jay Vernego
thread.said: He requested updates on drone operational guidelines be transmitted to the committee to help ensure responsible use.

thread.speaker: Gilbert Teodoro, Secretary of National Defense
thread.said: He said the guidelines could be disclosed insofar as they were disclosable, provided that technical details and granularity that could compromise DND systems were protected.

topics.topic: Local defense-industry procurement and technology transfer
topics.summary: Johanne Monich Bautista asked DND about uniform and fabric allocations and compliance with the Philippine Tropical Fabrics Law, including the cited 5% Philippine-fabric requirement. Secretary Gilbert Teodoro identified 162,000 for uniformed personnel but said the aggregated clothing figure and projected compliant-fabric spending were not yet available, citing safety, fireproofing, and supply-chain constraints. Bautista then asked about 2027 spending under the Self-Reliant Defense Posture Law, and Teodoro said there would be none because the law lacked equity, risk capital, research and development, and meaningful intellectual-property rights. Rep. Elijah San Fernando questioned the meaning of self-reliance, the 21.8% Government Arsenal budget reduction, and the gap between a 60,000,000 ammunition target and 500,000 actual output; DND attributed the output gap to a worldwide precursor shortage and endorsed industrial policy in principle. Rep. Vernego asked about Elbit Systems procurement, local arms production, drones, and written operational guidelines; Teodoro said only missile replenishment was planned, local industry was not yet suited to DND's priority capabilities, and drone guidelines could be disclosed subject to protecting sensitive system details. The discussion ended with information and document-related commitments, while several policy and implementation issues remained open.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish whether DND's uniform and defense procurement would comply with Philippine-made fabric requirements and strengthen local suppliers, manufacturing, maintenance, and technology transfer. Members also examined the meaning of self-reliance, the Government Arsenal's reduced budget and output, local arms production, and guidelines for drone procurement and use.
topics.agency_position: DND said self-reliance meant resilient, secure, cost-effective, and timely supply chains rather than complete indigenous production. It said the Self-Reliant Defense Posture Law was unworkable without equity, risk capital, research and development, and shared intellectual property rights; local industry should be developed where it could provide forward-looking, scalable capabilities, while sensitive operational details and technology constraints limited immediate local production and drone-guideline disclosure.
topics.outcome: The committee received DND's explanations but did not resolve the missing uniform and fabric figures, the law's implementation gap, or the precise status of local-industry support. DND undertook to provide information and consider or support further work on fabric sourcing, statutory amendments, Ombudsman-related documentation, and disclosable drone guidelines.

positions.position: Supported stronger compliance with the Philippine Tropical Fabrics Law, projected DND requirements for local fabrics, and development of local suppliers. He also indicated support for examining amendments to the Self-Reliant Defense Posture Law.
Supported a defense-related industrial policy so the country could produce or secure its own materials, precursors, and equipment during war or other crises.
Pressed DND for greater transparency on arms procurement, local manufacturing, and written guidelines to ensure responsible military drone use.

Supported industrial policy and local production where practical, but maintained that self-reliance did not require full indigenous production and that technology transfer required investment, equity, research and development, and intellectual property rights.

topics.topic: West Philippine Sea operations and maritime-security capability
topics.summary: Secretary Gilbert Teodoro framed the West Philippine Sea as the immediate focus of a broader maritime domain of about 2.4 million square kilometers and described the need for naval, Coast Guard, infrastructure, logistics, and technically trained personnel. A minority member asked about hazard pay for civilian personnel deployed in the West Philippine Sea, and Teodoro supported it while acknowledging unresolved issues concerning implementation and other benefits. The minority member also questioned alleged Chinese recruitment and influence operations; the Secretary said there were grounds for suspicion but that evidentiary determinations belonged largely to law-enforcement and financial authorities. The member manifested support for an increased West Philippine Sea budget, but no specific increase was recorded. Representative Egay Risa obtained the DND's position that EDCA and Philippine territory could be used only consistently with Philippine law, the Constitution, presidential guidance, and defensive treaty circumstances. Representative Rufus Rodriguez raised evacuation-center criteria and Eastern Seaboard surveillance and naval-basing needs; the agency undertook to provide an update on the proposed base, while the site criteria and funding questions remained open.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish how the DND was funding and strengthening operations in the West Philippine Sea and other maritime domains, including surveillance, patrols, Pag-asa Island services, and personnel capability. It also examined the legal and operational limits of the Mutual Defense Treaty, EDCA sites, and DND-supervised facilities in relation to China-related security concerns.
topics.agency_position: The DND said West Philippine Sea operations required sustained regular operating funds, naval and Coast Guard coordination, services and habitation support for Pag-asa Island, strategic infrastructure, surveillance, logistics, training, and technically qualified personnel. It maintained that Philippine law, the Constitution, presidential guidance, and the Mutual Defense Treaty limited EDCA and foreign military use of Philippine territory to defensive circumstances, while specific Eastern Seaboard basing and Ligtas Pinoy site questions remained subject to further work.
topics.outcome: The DND answered the legal and policy questions and stated that Pag-asa services would be fast-tracked, while a minority member supported increased West Philippine Sea funding. Specific funding for the maritime-security increase, the Ligtas Pinoy site list and criteria, and the proposed Eastern Seaboard naval base were not finally resolved.

He said the matter was better addressed by financial and law-enforcement authorities and that the DND cooperated on information but would not make a public determination during active evidence-gathering operations.

thread.speaker: a minority member
thread.said: The minority member asked whether Chinese influence operations on social media could cause elected officials to amplify pro-China trolls.

thread.speaker: Secretary Gilbert Teodoro
thread.said: Secretary Teodoro said some statements were undeniable and that the pronouncements spoke for themselves. He also characterized the Chinese embassy website as having become a propaganda institution.

thread.speaker: a minority member
thread.said: The minority member turned to West Philippine Sea and maritime-security tensions, asking about the operational response and the capability needed to address the security concern.

thread.speaker: Secretary Gilbert Teodoro
thread.said: Secretary Teodoro said West Philippine Sea operations were supported through the regular operational budget and involved the Philippine Coast Guard and Philippine Navy. He linked the mission to the northern portion of the machine lock, as transcribed, and to the wider maritime domain.

thread.speaker: Secretary Gilbert Teodoro
thread.said: He said Pag-asa Island required habitation and normalization of life, and that he had instructed WESCOM to fast-track the deployment of services by other agencies to Pag-asa.

thread.speaker: Secretary Gilbert Teodoro
thread.said: He described the Philippine Rise, the West Philippine Sea, the Pacific Ocean, and major transit points including the Verde Island Passage and Surigao Strait as part of the mission area requiring strategic support and operations.

thread.speaker: a minority member
thread.said: The minority member manifested support for increasing the budget for West Philippine Sea operations, although the specific amount was not intelligible in the transcript.

thread.speaker: Secretary Gilbert Teodoro
thread.said: Secretary Teodoro said maritime capability depended not only on equipment but also on original manufacturers, long-term service contracts, supply chains, training, and technically qualified personnel. He emphasized investment in knowledge, education, and skills application.

thread.speaker: Secretary Gilbert Teodoro
thread.said: He said the DND was considering a direct commission program to attract people who were highly technically qualified even if they were less physically fit, alongside continuing training to apply specialized knowledge and skills.

thread.speaker: Representative Pimentel
thread.said: Representative Pimentel said the security concerns discussed were among the reasons for filing an anti-spy unit bill and an anti-foreign-interference bill, both pending in the Committee on National Defense.

thread.speaker: Representative Egay Risa
thread.said: Representative Risa asked what exactly triggered the Mutual Defense Treaty.

thread.speaker: Secretary Gilbert Teodoro
thread.said: Secretary Teodoro said Article five could be triggered by a call from the Philippine or US government after an attack on either country's public vessel or similar protected entity. He said the Philippine trigger would be a call by the President based on an attack on a public vessel.

thread.speaker: Representative Egay Risa
thread.said: Representative Risa asked whether the Philippines might participate if China and the United States entered a Taiwan war, and whether US forces could use EDCA sites to launch attacks.

thread.speaker: Secretary Gilbert Teodoro
thread.said: Secretary Teodoro said the President had made clear that the Philippines was constitutionally prohibited from offensive activity and could act only defensively. He described the possibility of EDCA sites being used in such a conflict as speculative and said they could not be used contrary to the President's guidance.

thread.speaker: Representative Egay Risa
thread.said: Representative Risa asked whether US forces could use Philippine territory and EDCA sites during a Taiwan conflict.

thread.speaker: Secretary Gilbert Teodoro
thread.said: Secretary Teodoro said Philippine territory and EDCA sites could be used only if the Philippines was under attack or threat. He said the treaty and the EDCA agreement were clear and could not violate Philippine law or the Constitution.

thread.speaker: Representative Egay Risa
thread.said: Representative Risa asked whether US offensive missiles could be permanently positioned in the Philippines and launched from Philippine territory.

thread.speaker: Secretary Gilbert Teodoro
thread.said: Secretary Teodoro said offensive use from Philippine territory was not allowed unless Article five was activated, in which case the purpose would be to defend the Philippines. He said missiles would be welcomed only if they became part of the Philippine Armed Forces or Philippine arsenal.

thread.speaker: Representative Egay Risa
thread.said: Representative Risa asked for the Philippines' long-term objective in the West Philippine Sea.

thread.speaker: Secretary Gilbert Teodoro
thread.said: Secretary Teodoro said the objective remained constitutionally grounded: to explore and exploit for Filipinos each resource in the area that could be developed. He said any joint oil exploration arrangement with China would remain subject to Philippine law and the Constitution.

thread.speaker: Secretary Gilbert Teodoro
thread.said: Regarding the Philippine Veterans Industrial Estate, Secretary Teodoro said it was supervised by or attached to the DND through Phibidec and that illegal activity had led to a closure order by the DNR and revocation of its ECC.

thread.speaker: Representative Egay Risa
thread.said: Representative Risa asked what specific illegal activity had been identified and whether there was a spying or military issue.

thread.speaker: Secretary Gilbert Teodoro
thread.said: Secretary Teodoro identified production of substandard steel, environmental damage, and radioactively tainted scrap metals that endangered workers. He said there was no evidence of espionage, and that law-enforcement authorities had obtained a court search warrant before entering the area.

thread.speaker: Representative Rufus Rodriguez
thread.said: Representative Rufus Rodriguez said the proposed 2027 Ligtas Pinoy program would establish permanent evacuation centers and asked whether the specific sites or priority local government units had already been identified and what selection criteria would apply.

thread.speaker: Secretary Gilbert Teodoro
thread.said: Secretary Teodoro's response, as transcribed, referred to municipalities and cities, hazard mapping by the DNR, and identifying areas that would benefit evacuees. He indicated that areas would need to support temporary or preemptive evacuation, but the specific site list and criteria were not clearly stated.

thread.speaker: Representative Rufus Rodriguez
thread.said: Representative Rodriguez raised surveillance and monitoring needs along the Eastern Seaboard and asked for updates on a possible naval base in his province to support patrols, as well as related Philippine Coast Guard requirements.

thread.speaker: an agency official
thread.said: An agency official said the Secretary would receive a response regarding the proposal to establish a naval base in the province identified in the transcript as Gatangos, to support Eastern Seaboard patrols. The transcript did not record a final decision or timetable.

topics.topic: EDCA, U.S. facilities, and defense-cooperation infrastructure
topics.summary: Representative Egay Risa questioned Secretary Gilbert Teodoro on what would trigger the Mutual Defense Treaty and whether EDCA sites could be used in a Taiwan conflict or for offensive missile operations. Teodoro answered that treaty activation required a government call after an attack and that EDCA sites could not be used offensively unless the Philippines was under attack or threat, subject to the Constitution and Philippine law. Vice Chair Rufus Rodriguez asked about Lumbia's budget and U.S. counterpart funding; DND cited about 115 million for the current-year remaining amount, while the reference to 450 million for the following year was unclear, and it said no U.S. counterpart contribution had yet been agreed. DND said Lumbia development was delayed by right-of-way and informal-settlement issues and that U.S. officials were still scoping a possible warehouse. The proposed Tagoloan dry dock was estimated at about 40 billion including equipment, but titling and a construction timetable remained pending. Congressman Antonio Tinio warned that dual-use U.S. facilities and critical infrastructure could become targets and expose the Philippines to supply-chain risks, while Teodoro defended broader partnerships and resilient domestic supply chains as necessary for deterrence.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish the legal and operational limits of the Mutual Defense Treaty and EDCA, including whether U.S. forces could use Philippine territory for offensive operations. It also examined the Philippine and U.S. contributions to EDCA-related infrastructure, the status and cost of planned facilities, and the security and supply-chain risks associated with expanded defense cooperation.
topics.agency_position: DND said EDCA and other security-cooperation arrangements strengthened deterrence, interoperability, training, technology access, and defense resilience. It maintained that the Mutual Defense Treaty and EDCA did not authorize offensive use of Philippine territory absent an attack or threat to the Philippines, while acknowledging that U.S. contributions to Lumbia had not yet been agreed and that key infrastructure projects remained subject to land, titling, and scoping issues.
topics.outcome: The legal limits on offensive use of EDCA sites were stated by DND, but U.S. counterpart funding and specific Lumbia construction commitments remained unsettled. The Tagoloan dry dock remained dependent on land titling, with no construction timetable given, while broader concerns about dual-use facilities and regional supply-chain vulnerability remained matters for continuing policy and budget consideration.

positions.position: Raised concerns that closer U.S. interoperability and EDCA facilities could entangle the Philippines in a Taiwan conflict and create risks in relations with China. He sought clear limits on treaty activation, use of EDCA sites, and the positioning of offensive missiles.

Supported further development of Lumbia, the Tagoloan dry dock, and the Patag Army area as strategic and logistics facilities for Northern Mindanao and the broader defense of Mindanao. He also pressed for clarity on U.S. counterpart funding and social safeguards around EDCA activity.
Warned that dual-use U.S. facilities and critical economic infrastructure could become targets in a regional conflict and expose the Philippines to supply-chain and economic vulnerabilities.

Supported expanded defense cooperation and resilient infrastructure as necessary for deterrence, interoperability, and access to critical technology, while insisting that Philippine law, the Constitution, and presidential guidance constrained offensive use of EDCA sites.

actions.action: DND said it was pursuing legal proceedings and relocation arrangements to resolve Lumbia's right-of-way and informal-settlement problems.
DND said it would continue scoping possible U.S. support at Lumbia, including a multipurpose warehouse, while Philippine authorities considered air-traffic-control enhancements.
DND said it was working to complete titling for the proposed Tagoloan dry-dock site.
Vice Chair Rodriguez requested that DND consider retaining the Patag area as a continuing logistics center for the Armed Forces.

thread.speaker: Secretary Gilbert Teodoro
thread.said: Secretary Teodoro said the Philippines needed to build infrastructure, logistical bases, and strategic bases to maintain presence across its maritime domain and ensure reliable supply chains. He emphasized that modernization required infrastructure capable of housing, maintaining, and providing access to military capabilities.

thread.speaker: Secretary Gilbert Teodoro
thread.said: He said infrastructure was a major gap because capital outlay had not been adequately financed and modernization had been equipment-heavy rather than support-heavy. He also said security-cooperation agreements provided deterrence, interoperability, training, and access to technology.

thread.speaker: Secretary Gilbert Teodoro
thread.said: Secretary Teodoro described security-cooperation agreements as important for deterrence, interoperability, operational experience, and access to technology that would otherwise be unavailable. He cited the Philippine participation in an exercise in Australia as evidence of the capabilities gained through cooperation.

thread.speaker: Representative Egay Risa
thread.said: Representative Risa said Philippine defense interoperability with the United States was increasing, particularly through EDCA sites, while relations with China involved significant economic ties. He raised concerns that declining trust between the United States and China could create risks for the Philippines.

thread.speaker: Representative Egay Risa
thread.said: Risa asked what specifically triggers Article five of the Mutual Defense Treaty.

thread.speaker: Secretary Gilbert Teodoro
thread.said: Secretary Teodoro answered that the treaty is triggered by a call from the Philippine or U.S. government after an attack on either country's public vessel or similar protected entity. He said the Philippine trigger would be a decision by the President based on an attack and the President's determination that Article five applies.

thread.speaker: Representative Egay Risa
thread.said: Risa asked whether the Philippines could participate if China and the United States went to war over Taiwan.

thread.speaker: Secretary Gilbert Teodoro
thread.said: Secretary Teodoro said the President had made clear that the Philippines was constitutionally prohibited from engaging in offensive activity and could act only defensively.

thread.speaker: Representative Egay Risa
thread.said: Risa asked whether the United States might use EDCA sites in the Philippines to launch attacks during a Taiwan conflict.

thread.speaker: Secretary Gilbert Teodoro
thread.said: Secretary Teodoro called that possibility speculative and said that, under the President's guidance, EDCA sites could not be used for an external offensive action. He added that the sites could be used only if the Philippines were under attack or threat.

thread.speaker: Representative Egay Risa
thread.said: Risa asked whether EDCA sites could be used during a Taiwan conflict and whether the restriction was clearly established in the treaty and agreement.

thread.speaker: Secretary Gilbert Teodoro
thread.said: Secretary Teodoro answered that the restriction was clear and that the EDCA agreement could not violate Philippine law or the Constitution.

thread.speaker: Representative Egay Risa
thread.said: Risa asked whether U.S. offensive missiles could be permanently positioned in the Philippines.

thread.speaker: Secretary Gilbert Teodoro
thread.said: Secretary Teodoro said offensive missiles could not be used from Philippine territory unless Article five had been activated, in which case their purpose would be to defend the Philippines. He said the Philippines would welcome missiles if they became part of the Philippine Armed Forces and arsenal.

thread.speaker: Vice Chair Rufus Rodriguez
thread.said: Vice Chair Rodriguez asked for the 2027 DND budget for further development of the Lumbia fighter-wing and EDCA site.

thread.speaker: Secretary Gilbert Teodoro
thread.said: Secretary Teodoro initially cited 115,000,000 for the current year and described it as the remaining amount. The exchange then referred to a 450,000,000 budget for the following year, although the transcript is unclear as to whether this was the Secretary's answer or the member's restatement.

thread.speaker: Vice Chair Rufus Rodriguez
thread.said: Rodriguez asked what counterpart contribution the U.S. government would provide for Lumbia as an EDCA site.

thread.speaker: Secretary Gilbert Teodoro
thread.said: Secretary Teodoro answered, "None yet," and said U.S. officials were still determining what they could do at the site.

thread.speaker: Vice Chair Rufus Rodriguez
thread.said: Rodriguez questioned why there had not yet been an infusion of U.S. funds to develop Lumbia Airport.

thread.speaker: Secretary Gilbert Teodoro
thread.said: Secretary Teodoro said development had been hampered by right-of-way problems and informal settlements. He said legal proceedings and relocation work were underway so Lumbia could support the strike wing and serve as the Northern Mindanao operations center for disaster response.

thread.speaker: Vice Chair Rufus Rodriguez
thread.said: Rodriguez asked what structures the U.S. government planned to build at Lumbia and raised possible social costs, including risks to women in Cagayan de Oro.

thread.speaker: Secretary Gilbert Teodoro
thread.said: Secretary Teodoro said the U.S. was still scoping a multipurpose warehouse, while the Philippine side was considering air-traffic-control enhancements. He said no structure had yet been agreed and that relocation and base security were the immediate priorities; any U.S. personnel would be guided by the Status of Forces Agreement.

thread.speaker: Secretary Gilbert Teodoro
thread.said: Responding to questions about the proposed Tagoloan facility, Secretary Teodoro said it would be a naval dockyard in the southern portion of the Phibidec area and was awaiting finalization of its title.

thread.speaker: Vice Chair Rufus Rodriguez
thread.said: Rodriguez asked how much a complete dry dock would cost once the land title was finalized.

thread.speaker: Secretary Gilbert Teodoro
thread.said: Secretary Teodoro estimated the complete dry dock, including equipment, at about 40,000,000,000. The transcript also records the amount as "COP 40,000,000,000."

thread.speaker: Secretary Gilbert Teodoro
thread.said: He said the dry dock was strategically located because it was relatively protected from typhoons and could accommodate the largest vessels. He explained that Subic was operating as a naval base and could not serve the same dry-dock function.

thread.speaker: Vice Chair Rufus Rodriguez
thread.said: Rodriguez asked for the timetable for completion of the title and commencement of construction.

thread.speaker: Secretary Gilbert Teodoro
thread.said: Secretary Teodoro did not provide a timetable. He said the department was making every effort to complete the titling because Sangley was shallow, small, and increasingly difficult for naval platforms to maneuver in.

thread.speaker: Vice Chair Rufus Rodriguez
thread.said: Rodriguez urged DND to retain the Patag area as a logistics center because of its strategic location and access to Northern Mindanao and the rest of Mindanao.

thread.speaker: Secretary Gilbert Teodoro
thread.said: Secretary Teodoro said Lumbia, the proposed dockyard, and the Army presence in the area were prime considerations in the department's logistics and operations planning. He said Lumbia would support the strike wing and the Northern Mindanao operations center.

thread.speaker: Congressman Antonio Tinio
thread.said: Congressman Tinio raised the risk that expanded U.S. military and civilian or dual-use facilities— including at Subic and New Clark City—could become targets during a U.S.-China or Taiwan conflict. He cited possible ammunition and fuel facilities, semiconductor-related activity, and dependence on critical infrastructure and supply chains.

thread.speaker: Secretary Gilbert Teodoro
thread.said: Secretary Teodoro acknowledged the concern and said China had already shown its intentions through overt acts. He argued that the Philippines needed to build resilience with as many partners as possible and develop resilient supply chains and critical technologies rather than remain vulnerable.

thread.speaker: Secretary Gilbert Teodoro
thread.said: Secretary Teodoro said he was not familiar with the corporate workings of PacSilica but that the defense sector needed the end product and supply chain as quickly as possible. He said combat experience indicated that systems could require retooling every three days, or faster with artificial intelligence.

thread.speaker: Secretary Gilbert Teodoro
thread.said: He said Philippine capabilities were intended to deter rather than merely react to threats, and that the country needed to stand up for territorial integrity and sovereignty amid China's expansion.

topics.topic: Drones and unmanned systems for the AFP
topics.summary: Brian Poe asked whether the Philippine Air Force and Navy budgets contained specific drone-procurement line items and whether modernization planning was preparing for rapidly changing drone technology. Secretary Gilbert Teodoro answered that drones were covered by the modernization fund, while specific systems were classified, and emphasized integration, secure connectivity, and operational control rather than hardware alone. Poe cited an approximate 70 million cost for one F-16 and compared it with about 2,000 Shahed-class drones. Rep. Vernego then asked about local drone production and written operational guidelines; Teodoro said drone production was relatively easy, but payload technology and AI-related systems were the critical elements, and that current use was for surveillance. Vernego requested guideline and program updates, with Teodoro indicating that disclosable material could be provided without compromising sensitive details. Tony Patalbano separately requested a status report on the drone program, and Teodoro said the DND was building its framework and backbone and developing control systems.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish whether drone procurement was specifically funded in the FY 2027 DND or service budgets, how drones were treated under the AFP modernization program, and whether the AFP had the personnel, network, control systems, and guidelines needed to use them responsibly. Members also sought an update on the drone program and related reporting to the committee.
topics.agency_position: The DND said drone procurement was covered by the AFP modernization fund, although specific systems and budget details were classified. It maintained that the priority was integrating drones into operations, building secure connectivity and control systems, and developing responsible-use guidelines; current drone use was for surveillance rather than offensive operations.
topics.outcome: The DND assured the committee that drones were covered under modernization and that the AFP was developing the necessary integration, backbone, and control systems, but it withheld specific procurement details as classified. The committee requested guideline and program updates; the extent and timing of those submissions were not specified.

positions.position: Supported continued investment in drone technology and sought assurance that it was funded and being incorporated into modernization planning, given its perceived cost and operational advantages over larger platforms.
Pressed for written operational guidelines and committee reporting to ensure that military drones were used responsibly.
Supported faster development of the AFP drone program and requested a progress report, citing its importance to national defense.
