thread.speaker: Rep. Perci Cendaña
thread.said: He asked DTI to disclose the fine print of the Paxilica project so the public would know what would be built in the area.

thread.speaker: DTI Secretary Cristina Roque
thread.said: She said Paxilica was one of several economic zones the Philippines planned to build and referred the detailed explanation to Undersecretary Perry Rodolfo.

thread.speaker: DTI Undersecretary Perry Rodolfo
thread.said: He welcomed both positive and negative comments, saying public discussion could improve the policy direction. He said the two signed documents had been posted on the BOI website for transparency.

thread.speaker: DTI Undersecretary Perry Rodolfo
thread.said: He distinguished the Paxilica partnership from individual projects, describing the partnership as a nonbinding statement or declaration involving the Philippines and 23 other countries and economies to secure the AI technology supply chain.

thread.speaker: DTI Undersecretary Perry Rodolfo
thread.said: He said New Clark City was only one Philippine project under the partnership and would focus on advanced manufacturing for equipment used in AI data centers, not on hosting the AI data centers themselves.

thread.speaker: DTI Undersecretary Perry Rodolfo
thread.said: He said locators would have to build their own roads, bring their own power, and secure and reuse their own water. Data centers could be located elsewhere where appropriate power was available, subject to the same resource obligations.

thread.speaker: Rep. Perci Cendaña
thread.said: He requested that DTI submit prospective sites for other Paxilica projects, particularly to clarify where resources such as water and electricity would come from.

thread.speaker: DTI Undersecretary Perry Rodolfo
thread.said: He referred to ongoing consultations involving the BCDA and said that, for the specific Clark project, New Clark City was an existing master-planned industrial zone.

thread.speaker: DTI Undersecretary Perry Rodolfo
thread.said: He described the relevant area within the New Clark City industrial zone as 1,620 hectares and said discussions remained ongoing.

thread.speaker: Rep. Perci Cendaña
thread.said: He requested the status of ongoing consultations with communities on the ground concerning project implementation.

thread.speaker: Rep. Antonio Tinio
thread.said: He cited public statements that there was no data-center discussion for Paxilica and asked officials to clarify whether data centers were contemplated in Clark, including the environmental implications.

thread.speaker: An agency official
thread.said: The official responded that the concerns and inputs from various parties were being taken into account.

thread.speaker: Rep. Antonio Tinio
thread.said: He asked officials to explain Israel's possible role in Paxilica and raised concerns about the partnership's connection to AI, intelligence, and defense-related supply chains.

thread.speaker: An agency official
thread.said: The official said the US side was being led by Jacob Helberg but indicated that the official could not provide all details about the private companies or advisers involved.

thread.speaker: Rep. Antonio Tinio
thread.said: He characterized the US objective as securing supply chains for its defense industrial base and asked how that objective related to the Philippines and the proposed economic-security zone.

thread.speaker: Rep. Antonio Tinio
thread.said: He asked what the economic-security-zone and joint-governance concepts would mean in practice, including whether they could cover modular nuclear power plants, AI data centers, or AI hyperscalers.

thread.speaker: Rep. Antonio Tinio
thread.said: He requested that officials submit and publicly share information and documents concerning New Clark City, the identified projects, and other Paxilica-related projects.

thread.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
thread.said: After reviewing the roughly five pages posted online, he asked whether the agreements included provisions on knowledge transfer or technology transfer.

thread.speaker: DTI Undersecretary Perry Rodolfo
thread.said: He said knowledge transfer was currently being discussed. He added that the New Clark City project was selected partly because institutions such as UP Open University Extension Office and Philippine Science High School could help the Philippines absorb the ecosystem's technology.

thread.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
thread.said: He requested copies of further details on how knowledge transfer was taking shape in the agreement.

thread.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
thread.said: He asked whether workers in Paxilica factories and corporations would be protected and whether their wages would be competitive internationally.

thread.speaker: DTI Undersecretary Perry Rodolfo
thread.said: He said all locators would at minimum have to comply with local laws and expected them to pay more than locally mandated wages, as observed in other zones.

thread.speaker: DTI Undersecretary Perry Rodolfo
thread.said: He reiterated that locators would build their own roads, bring their own power, and secure and reuse their own water. He clarified that the New Clark City project concerned advanced manufacturing rather than a data center.

thread.speaker: DTI Undersecretary Perry Rodolfo
thread.said: For water, he said options under discussion included surface water and rainwater, as well as a Middle East company's possible desalination facility in Subic with piping to Clark.

thread.speaker: DTI Undersecretary Perry Rodolfo
thread.said: He said Subic was 75 kilometers from Clark and argued that this distance was manageable compared with water-piping distances in the Middle East.

thread.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
thread.said: He asked for more information on the terms for mineral extraction and processing in the Philippines under Paxilica.

thread.speaker: DTI Undersecretary Perry Rodolfo
thread.said: He said mining and mineral processing terms were still under discussion as part of securing the supply chain and adding value to minerals exported in unprocessed ore form. He said processing would occur near the mines rather than in Clark and that Philippine environmental and labor laws would prevail, with each locator required to secure an ECC.

thread.speaker: Rep. Brian Poe
thread.said: He asked when the proposed Paxilica signing would take place and requested that the committee be kept informed of the terms before signing.

thread.speaker: DTI Undersecretary Perry Rodolfo
thread.said: He identified November as the target for signing but stressed that it was only a tentative target.

thread.speaker: Rep. Antonio Tinio
thread.said: He asked whether Philippine law would always prevail in implementing Paxilica projects despite references to joint governance.

thread.speaker: BCDA/DTI official Perry
thread.said: The official said invitations, registration terms, and conditions would be governed by the BCDA law and the Bases Conversion and Development Authority's legal framework, with commercial terms to be set in a contract between BCDA and the US side.

thread.speaker: Rep. Antonio Tinio
thread.said: He asked how the bring-your-own-electricity, supply-your-own-water, and build-your-own-roads conditions would work if data centers or manufacturing facilities were proposed for New Clark City.

thread.speaker: BCDA/DTI official Perry
thread.said: The official said New Clark City covered 1,620 hectares and discussed a possible LNG regasification import terminal and regas facilities in Subic, with a gas-powered plant embedded in the area.

thread.speaker: Rep. Antonio Tinio
thread.said: He asked whether the possible LNG-powered facilities would be exclusive to the project.

thread.speaker: BCDA/DTI official Perry
thread.said: He said the facilities would be subject to Department of Energy and ERC regulations and that permits would be governed by Philippine laws.

thread.speaker: Rep. Antonio Tinio
thread.said: He followed up on the water supply, including rainwater and the environmental effects of water used to cool data centers.

thread.speaker: BCDA/DTI official Perry
thread.said: He said facilities, whether manufacturing or data centers, would have to comply with environmental requirements, obtain an ECC, follow environmental laws, and provide water-treatment facilities.

thread.speaker: Rep. Antonio Tinio
thread.said: He asked about Paxilica-related projects outside New Clark City and how they would be identified and coordinated.

thread.speaker: BCDA/DTI official Perry
thread.said: He said the administration's priorities for the next 2.5 years included mining and mineral processing, digital infrastructure, advanced manufacturing including semiconductors and electronics, and tourism. He identified mining, advanced manufacturing, and digital infrastructure as the areas most relevant to Paxilica, with the Department of Information and Communications Technology's AI infrastructure roadmap helping identify sites such as data centers.

thread.speaker: Rep. Antonio Tinio
thread.said: He raised barangay concerns and suggested a specific briefing by the department on the controversial tax-relief issue.

thread.speaker: Committee chair
thread.said: The chair said further discussion was needed and noted that officials had expressed openness to continuing the discussion.

topics.topic: CARS and RACE automotive incentives and funding
topics.summary: Representatives Perci Cendaña and Renee Luizco questioned DTI on the restoration and design of RACE, the completed CARS program, and the treatment of local automotive manufacturers. DTI said CARS had awarded two slots to Toyota and Mitsubishi, while RACE was still being finalized and would be opened to more participants. DTI also described EV incentives and said the policy was to shift the sector toward electric vehicles, but Luizco questioned whether the PHP5 billion capitalization requirement and other standards would exclude local manufacturers. Secretary Cristina Roque undertook to contact Francisco Motors and submit or provide requested program and policy information. Antonio Tinio then asked how CARS would be funded; DTI initially stated 5,100,000,000 and linked the funding to DPWH savings, but an agency official later corrected the savings figure to 4,081,000,000, with other figures in the exchange unclear. The issue therefore led to agency commitments and a funding clarification, but the requested documentation and final RACE budget were not yet presented.

Secretary Maria Cristina Roque reported that the SB Corporation e-transport loan had approved 18 applications and released 47,000,000 pesos, while the chair promoted electric transport as cheaper to operate than conventional vehicles. Rep. Renee Luizco challenged whether the CARS, RACE, and EV programs would support genuine local manufacturing rather than foreign companies and flagged the PHP5 billion capitalization requirement. DTI said local suppliers and partnerships were included, but acknowledged that Filipino companies supplying foreign participants were not necessarily vehicle manufacturers. DTI undertook to contact Francisco Motors and other local manufacturers and to submit requested data. Rep. Tina Pancho later sought priority for Filipino jeepney manufacturers, and DTI assured her that it would assist them and provide an update after consultations.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish whether DTI's electric-vehicle incentive policies would overcome capitalization barriers, require meaningful local manufacturing and local-content participation, and prioritize Filipino jeepney and vehicle manufacturers. Members also asked how electric transport operators could access financing and whether DTI would provide policy, program, and consultation documents.

It maintained that local participation would be supported through SME purchasing requirements, local partnerships, supply-chain participation, industry consultations, and direct coordination with Francisco Motors and other local manufacturers.
topics.outcome: DTI answered the policy and financing questions and made several commitments to submit information, coordinate with manufacturers, and assist local firms. The capitalization barrier, the distinction between local parts supply and local vehicle manufacturing, and the eventual prioritization of Filipino manufacturers remained open for follow-up.

topics.topic: SB Corporation P3 loans and consolidated fund accountability
topics.summary: Rep. Iris Marie Montes first asked DTI for SB Corporation loan-release, repayment, rate, and MSME-reach data, while Secretary Cristina Roque described collateral-free loans of up to 5,000,000 and a one-year payment grace period. DTI also reported 274 Women Enterprise Fund approvals and 56,000,000 disbursed, and 18 approved e-transport applications with 47,000,000 released. Rep. Roberto Nazal Jr. then questioned the proposed 140,170,000 P3 allocation and requested consolidated accounting of all SB Corporation government funds. SB Corporation President Bobby reported around PHP 10,000,000,000 received since 2017, more than 500,000 P3 beneficiaries, and a portfolio figure transcribed as R10 billion dollars, while the transcript also recorded 30,000,000 yen in releases with unclear currency wording. Nazal highlighted the gap between 19,373 beneficiaries and the 40,000 target despite 1,000,000,000 being reported as fully disbursed, and asked for a detailed status and rate breakdown. The agency committed to provide the records and consult the SB Corporation board, leaving the accounting and effective-rate issues pending.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish how SB Corporation had used and managed P3 and other government funds, including the borrowers reached, amounts released, repayments, loan portfolio status, and the meaning of reported disbursements. It also questioned whether P3 borrowers were being charged rates consistent with the program's purpose and whether the proposed 140,170,000 allocation should be released before consolidated accounting was provided.
topics.agency_position: DTI maintained that SB Corporation financing was a key MSME intervention and that demand exceeded available funds. It defended simplified, collateral-free loans and one-year payment relief, but did not provide during the hearing the requested consolidated accounting, portfolio-status breakdown, or effective-rate analysis; those matters were referred for submission and discussion with the SB Corporation board.
topics.outcome: The agency committed to submit borrower-level and consolidated portfolio information and to return with the SB Corporation board's assessment of P3 rates and charges. The proposed allocation, accounting status, and rate concerns were not resolved during the hearing.

positions.position: She sought current, detailed performance information on SB Corporation loans, including releases, repayments, rates, MSME reach, and access by women and young women in remote areas.

thread.said: He requested a list of borrowers and the amount released to each.

thread.speaker: Secretary Cristina Roque

thread.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal Jr.
thread.said: He noted that the 2026 P3 subsidy was 1,000,000,000 and that the report showed the full amount obligated and disbursed by 06/30/2026, while physical accomplishment was around 19,373 beneficiaries against a 40,000 annual target. He asked whether “disbursed” meant the money had reached 40,000 microentrepreneurs or had merely been transferred to a conduit.

thread.speaker: Secretary Cristina Roque
thread.said: She said disbursement meant that loans had actually been released either through wholesale conduits or direct retail borrowers. She gave the approximate P3 portfolio distribution as 55% direct retail and 45% wholesale.

thread.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal Jr.
thread.said: He requested a breakdown showing what had reached borrowers, what remained outstanding, what had been collected and revolved, what was past due or nonperforming, what had been written off, and what remained as cash or investments with SB Corporation or conduits.

thread.speaker: Secretary Cristina Roque
thread.said: She replied that SB Corporation would provide the requested breakdown.

thread.speaker: Rep. Roberto Nazal Jr.
thread.said: He questioned why taxpayers subsidized the capital while P3 borrowers could pay an all-in rate of up to 2.5% monthly or around 30% annually. He asked for the actual weighted-average effective rate, including interest, service charges, processing fees, insurance, compulsory deposits, and every other charge, as well as the amount charged by SB Corporation to conduits and added by conduits before reaching borrowers.

topics.topic: MSME market access, financing, and bottom-up priorities
topics.summary: DTI presented market access, trade-fair, MSME financing, and provincial-support programs, including about 100,000,000 pesos in proposed additional international-marketing funding, 33 trade fairs in 2025, and 38 planned local fairs in 2026. Secretary Roque said SB Corp. offered collateral-free loans of up to 5,000,000 with a one-year payment holiday, but available funds were insufficient. Rep. Montes sought trade-deficit measures and details on the Women Enterprise Fund, which had approved 274 applicants and disbursed 56,000,000 pesos. Rep. Garcia requested restoration of bottom-up priorities and documentation of investment gains, while Rep. Sagarbarria sought more than 66,000,000 for the Negros Island Region. Rep. Nazal questioned retail access, P3 fund accounting, beneficiary counts, and loan rates, prompting commitments for detailed records and possible policy changes. A minority member supported more Halal funding after DTI reported 277 certified MSMEs and a proposed 81,000,000 pesos allocation, although the transcript contained unclear Halal budget figures.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish how DTI would expand MSME financing, market access, trade promotion, and provincial support within the proposed budget. Members also asked whether DTI would restore locally identified priorities, protect MSMEs from restrictive retail practices, account for SB Corp. funds, and strengthen the Halal industry.
topics.agency_position: DTI maintained that MSME development required simultaneous market access, affordable financing, skills and technology support, and stronger provincial implementation. It said demand for SB Corp. loans and Halal certification exceeded available funds, while committing to provide requested SB Corp. and investment documents and to consider further budget or policy changes.
topics.outcome: DTI defended its strategy and stated that it needed additional funding, but several matters remained open. The agency committed to submit investment and SB Corp. records, consult on retail practices and P3 pricing, and seek more support for the Negros Island Region and Halal programs.

positions.position: Pressed DTI to address the trade deficit through export diversification, import substitution, industry modernization, interagency coordination, and wider access to the Women Enterprise Fund.

thread.speaker: Secretary Cristina Roque

topics.topic: Halal industry assistance and certification
topics.summary: Former President Gloria Macapagal Arroyo questioned DTI about why Philippine Halal exports lagged despite trade missions and said multiple certifying bodies and logos confused Muslim-country buyers. DTI acknowledged the certification problem, said exporters were being directed to bodies accredited in destination markets, and undertook to provide a list of companies that had engaged with those bodies. DTI reported 277 certified MSMEs and assistance to 140 MSMEs for 2026, with a Halal allocation stated inconsistently as PHP 90,000,000 and 90,000,000,000 and a target of 81,000,000 pesos for the following year. The secretary said more funding was needed for certification, trade shows, slaughterhouses, and market expansion, citing 13,000,000 Muslims in the Philippines and a global market estimated at 2 to 3,000,000,000,000 US dollars. A minority member and Rep. Brian Poe supported increased Halal funding, while DTI said domestic violations were not recorded but export-market partners had raised certification concerns. The issue landed with continued DTI coordination and funding requests, but without resolution of the single-certifying-body proposal, export-growth evidence, or the conflicting budget figures.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish whether the proposed Halal budget was sufficient, how widely DTI's assistance reached provincial MSMEs, and whether Philippine Halal certification was credible and recognized in export markets. Members also asked what institutional and whole-of-government measures were being taken to address fragmented certification and expand Halal exports.
topics.agency_position: DTI acknowledged that fragmented and sometimes unreliable certification was limiting Philippine Halal exports. It said it was working with certifying bodies recognized by destination markets, assisting MSMEs across regions, coordinating through the Halal board, and seeking more funding for certification, promotion, trade shows, and related facilities.
topics.outcome: DTI acknowledged certification credibility and market recognition problems, but said it was aligning exporters with certifying bodies recognized by destination markets and supporting MSMEs across eight regions. The committee expressed support for increased Halal funding, while export-growth results, the exact budget figures, and the future single-certification framework remained open.

positions.who: Gloria Macapagal Arroyo, former president and member
positions.position: She argued that multiple Philippine certifying bodies, logos, and standards confused importing countries and pressed for a single credible certification framework. She also questioned whether DTI's interventions had produced meaningful export growth and challenged the agency to track pending legislation.
The member supported increased DTI funding for Halal because of its domestic and global market potential and supported the Halal industry budget.
Poe supported increasing Halal funding as a means of expanding jobs, income, and government revenue, while seeking evidence that the program and budget were effective.

topics.topic: Creative-industries funding and Center for Excellence
topics.summary: Rep. Sarah Elago requested a detailed breakdown of the Film Academy of the Philippines' proposed appropriation; its director general said the original proposal was 267,000,000 and had been reduced to 104,000,000. Rep. Javi Benitez then pressed DTI on creative-industries funding, citing the sector's 7.8% GDP contribution, an estimated 30% budget decline, a previous high of 300,000,000, and a reported zero in the FY2027 national expenditure program. DTI said the current regular creative-industry budget was 50,000,000, acknowledged the reduction, and said it would seek more funding because the sector could drive trade, tourism, jobs, and ASEAN engagement. DTI also confirmed that creative industries were a priority for ASEAN activities and that they would be featured in meetings, trade shows, and dedicated areas, including a potential Center for Excellence. The committee chair identified creative-industries development as a restoration priority and requested DTI's priority programs for submission to the budget review process. The issue remained open pending those submissions and committee deliberation.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish the proposed funding for creative industries, including whether a previously higher allocation had fallen to zero or to a lower regular line-item amount. Members also asked whether creative industries and a proposed Center for Excellence were priorities for DTI and ASEAN-related activities, and what funding restoration or documents the agency would seek.
topics.agency_position: DTI said creative industries were a priority and could drive trade, tourism, employment, ASEAN engagement, and global market access. It acknowledged that funding had fallen substantially, citing a 50,000,000 regular budget and confirming that the FY2027 proposal was at zero, and said it would seek a larger allocation.
topics.outcome: The committee recognized creative industries as a priority and indicated that funding reductions, including the reported zero FY2027 proposal, would be considered for restoration. topics.topic: Trade deficit, export diversification, and tariff effects
topics.summary: Representative Iris Marie Montes asked which DTI budget measures would address the trade deficit through export diversification, import substitution, and industry modernization. Secretary Cristina Roque pointed to export promotion, trade shows, foreign trade attaches, domestic market access, free-trade agreements, and interagency industry training, citing an 8,000,000 investment that generated 150,000,000 in sales. Representative Antonio Tinio separately questioned the source and amount of CARS funding, and the agency ultimately cited DPWH savings of 4,081,000,000, after other figures were stated or corrected. Tinio also asked about United States tariffs and forced-labor compliance; DTI said the 12.5% tariff covered 30% of exports to the United States, with several sectors affected and specified products exempted. DTI said the Philippines had a legal framework addressing forced labor but that United States evaluation and negotiations remained ongoing. The committee requested supporting documents and asked DTI to submit budget-restoration priorities for further deliberation.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish which 2027 DTI budget allocations would reduce the trade deficit through export diversification, import substitution, and industry modernization. It also examined the effect of United States tariffs and forced-labor compliance requirements on Philippine exports, and clarified the funding source and amount for the CARS program.
topics.agency_position: DTI said the trade deficit should be addressed by expanding exports, diversifying products and markets, strengthening domestic market access and local industrial capacity, and using free-trade agreements to secure preferential tariffs. On United States tariffs, DTI said the Philippines had a legal and administrative framework addressing forced labor, but the United States evaluation and negotiations were still ongoing; DTI also said it would help affected exporters find alternative markets.
topics.outcome: The trade-deficit and tariff issues were not finally resolved during the hearing. DTI was to submit tariff documentation and identify budget items for possible restoration, while the committee reserved the matters for further budget deliberation.

topics.topic: Investment promotion authorities and foreign direct investment
topics.summary: DTI presented BOI and PEZA investment approvals as evidence that investment-promotion authorities were attracting projects and generating employment. It reported BOI approvals of about 1.56 trillion in 2025 linked to 40,175 projected jobs, and PEZA approvals of roughly 216.46 billion in the first eight months of 2026 linked to 27,000 projected direct jobs. Rep. Albert Garcia questioned whether the Create More framework, investment-promotion authorities, and free ports had actually increased FDI and requested documents showing the investment gains and sunk investment in the country. Secretary Cristina Roque cited a 94.4% PEZA increase from January to June and committed to provide the requested documents. Rep. Jay Vergara separately raised a Korean agricultural-machinery project in Cabanatuan, and Undersecretary Perry committed to examine and support it. A DTI official also cited an investment pipeline of about 18 billion for renewable energy, but the hearing did not resolve the documentation or project follow-through.
topics.question: The committee was trying to establish whether investment-promotion authorities, free-port structures, and related agreements were producing actual foreign direct investment, employment, industrial activity, and regional gains. Members also sought documentation supporting the agency's reported investment results and clarification on a Korean agricultural-machinery project in Cabanatuan.
topics.agency_position: DTI maintained that BOI, PEZA, the Create More Act, the SIPP, Green Lanes, economic zones, and free-trade or digital agreements were attracting investment, encouraging expansions, and generating jobs. It presented BOI and PEZA approvals, projected employment, an investment pipeline, and examples of investor activity as evidence, while acknowledging that additional budget and documentation could support further gains.
topics.outcome: DTI defended the investment-promotion framework with reported approvals, projected jobs, expansion activity, and an investment pipeline. The committee required supporting investment documentation, and DTI committed to provide it; the Korean project was also left for agency review and assistance.

positions.position: He supported restoring bottom-up, demand-driven priorities and pressed DTI to demonstrate with documents that investment-promotion authorities and related programs were producing actual investment gains for the country.

He pressed DTI to follow through on the Korean agricultural-machinery initiative in Cabanatuan, emphasizing the expected employment and industrial benefits associated with the presidentially supported project.

topics.topic: DTI industry-development strategy and job quality
topics.summary: Secretary Cristina Roque presented DTI's strategy of investment and export promotion, MSME market access and finance, consumer protection, and skills development, citing about 1.56 trillion in BOI-approved investments and 40,175 projected jobs, as well as 216.46 billion in PEZA investments and 27,000 projected direct jobs. Representative Roberto Nazal Jr. questioned the reduced DTI budget, MSME programs, retailer charges, and the accountability of P3 funds; DTI and SB Corp. cited about 10 billion in GAA allocations since 2017, more than 500,000 beneficiaries, and a loan portfolio described unclearly in the transcript as R10 billion dollars. Nazal also challenged the reported 100% disbursement of 1 billion against 19,373 beneficiaries and questioned rates of up to 2.5% monthly or around 30% annually. Representative Eli San Fernando challenged DTI's claim that industry development was producing high-paying, quality jobs, citing 225,000 jobs and a separate unclear figure of 177,000. DTI said employment ranged from high-end technical work to mass factory and BPO jobs, acknowledged the need for higher-paying employment, and pointed to skills programs and industrial-policy coordination. The agency undertook to provide documents, obtain data, consult the SB Corp. board, and seek more industrial-development resources, leaving the quality-of-jobs issue contested.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish whether DTI's 2027 industry-development strategy would generate high-paying, quality jobs rather than mainly low-wage or retail employment. Members also tested how DTI would coordinate industrial policy, develop skills, support priority industries, expand MSME market access, and account for SB Corp. funds.
topics.agency_position: DTI said its strategy combined investment and export promotion, consumer protection, MSME market access and finance, skills development, and sector-specific industrial programs. It maintained that industrial development could generate both high-end and mass employment, acknowledged that not all current jobs were high-paying, and committed to seek more resources and provide requested SB Corp. data.

thread.speaker: Secretary Cristina Roque
thread.said: Secretary Roque described DTI's three mandates as foreign trade and international investment, consumer protection and fair trade, and MSME development. She said investment growth was intended to provide high-paying jobs so Filipinos could remain with their families.

thread.speaker: Secretary Cristina Roque
thread.said: She requested a 100,000,000 pesos additional budget for international marketing and expanded participation by local businesses and growing SMEs in international trade shows.

thread.speaker: Secretary Cristina Roque
thread.said: She said the Board of Investments approved COP1.56 trillion in investments in 2025, with 322 approved projects projected to generate 40,175 jobs nationwide.

thread.speaker: Secretary Cristina Roque
thread.said: She reported that PEZA had approved 216,460,000,000 in investments during the first eight months of 2026 across 196 new and expansion projects, projected to generate 27,000 direct jobs.

thread.speaker: Secretary Cristina Roque
thread.said: She said DTI's Tatak Pinoy industrialization policy sought to elevate local industries across nine key sectors and create world-class products for domestic and global markets.

thread.speaker: Secretary Cristina Roque
thread.said: She said DTI had set aside 2,000,000,000 pesos for a women's enterprise fund to support home businesses and business expansion.

thread.speaker: Secretary Cristina Roque

thread.said: She said DTI would conduct 38 local trade fairs in 2026, free to government-compliant MSMEs.

thread.speaker: Secretary Cristina Roque
thread.said: She said SB Corp. loans could reach 5,000,000 with no collateral and no payment of principal and interest for one year, supported by 12,000,000,000 in funds.

thread.speaker: Secretary Cristina Roque
thread.said: She said DTI had set aside 1,000,000,000 pesos for a youth enterprise fund, with the same one-year payment holiday.

thread.speaker: Representative Roberto Nazal Jr.
thread.said: He noted that the DTI OSEC budget would fall from 7,392,000,000 in 2026 to 6,744,000,000 net in 2027 and asked for DTI's principal 2027 economic strategy and measurable results in businesses, jobs, investments, and exports.

thread.speaker: Secretary Cristina Roque
thread.said: She identified investment and foreign trade promotion, consumer protection and fair trade, and MSME development as DTI's three priorities. She said the focus was income and trade, including exports and expansion of existing investors.

thread.speaker: Secretary Cristina Roque
thread.said: She said MSMEs comprised 99.6% of business establishments and 62% of the labor force, making them a quick avenue for economic growth and job creation.

thread.speaker: Representative Roberto Nazal Jr.
thread.said: He asked DTI to identify its main MSME-development programs.

thread.speaker: Secretary Cristina Roque

thread.speaker: Representative Roberto Nazal Jr.
thread.said: He questioned whether local retailers' listing, merchandising, and other charges were prohibitive for MSMEs and whether retailers could disadvantage locally manufactured products.

thread.speaker: Secretary Cristina Roque

thread.speaker: Representative Roberto Nazal Jr.
thread.said: He pressed DTI to protect MSMEs from predatory retail practices rather than relying only on alternative platforms.

thread.speaker: Secretary Cristina Roque
thread.said: She agreed to talk to the different establishments regarding the reported practices.

thread.speaker: Representative Roberto Nazal Jr.
thread.said: Before another 140,170,000 for P3 in 2027, he requested one consolidated accounting of all government funds entrusted to SB Corp. since P3 began.

topics.topic: Bureau of Philippine Standards enforcement and consumer penalties
topics.summary: Rep. Mauricio Domogan questioned whether the Bureau of Philippine Standards had sufficient funding and personnel to inspect products nationwide, including materials used in infrastructure. Secretary Cristina Roque said DTI had 18 regional offices but needed more staff and funding, while a DTI official said the requested amount was 150,000,000, compared with 90,000,000 requested the previous year. The official cited estimated retail values for specified substandard steel products of 400,000 in 2024, 24,800,000 in 2025, and about 88,800,000 as of June 2026, with the final unit unclear. Domogan asked what cases had been filed and whether the Republic Act 7394 penalty of 1,000 to 10,000 and imprisonment of two months to one year was too low. DTI committed to submit annual case details and said it was recommending a bill expanding visitorial powers and allowing higher penalties. The chair also requested the basis of the budget request and its specific line item.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish whether the Bureau of Philippine Standards had sufficient funding, personnel, and regional reach to inspect products and enforce standards, particularly for materials used in infrastructure. It also examined the value of substandard steel products, the cases against violators, and whether penalties under Republic Act 7394 were adequate.
topics.agency_position: DTI said its product standards enforcement was constrained by insufficient personnel and funding despite having 18 regional offices and nationwide inspection responsibilities. It requested 150,000,000 for the current year, committed to submit annual case details, and said it was recommending legislation to expand visitorial powers and allow higher penalties.
topics.outcome: The committee received DTI's explanation that enforcement needed additional personnel and funding and that 150,000,000 was requested for the current year. DTI undertook to submit case details and the budget basis, while the adequacy of Republic Act 7394 penalties remained unresolved pending possible legislation.

positions.position: Supported an additional budget for the Bureau of Philippine Standards and argued that penalties under Republic Act 7394 were insufficient in relation to the harm caused by substandard products.

topics.topic: Price monitoring and the PHP78 food benchmark
topics.summary: Representative Sarah Elago asked DTI about enforcement of prices for basic necessities and prime commodities and whether its monitoring reached public markets. Secretary Maria Cristina Lopez said DTI monitored supermarkets and groceries daily through 18 regional offices, while the Department of Agriculture handled wet and public markets. Asek Malayari reported very good compliance and said DTI issued letters of inquiry when prices exceeded suggested retail prices. Elago then questioned whether PHP78 per person per day, derived from the PHP111 per-person poverty threshold and a 70% food threshold, realistically covered basic nutritional needs. Lopez said she was not aware of the basis for PHP78 and committed to coordinate with SECRC and Balisakan, leaving the benchmark's adequacy unresolved.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish how DTI monitored and enforced prices for basic necessities and prime commodities, including the limits of its jurisdiction over public markets. It also asked whether the PHP78 per-person food benchmark realistically covered basic nutritional needs.
topics.agency_position: DTI stated that it monitored basic necessities and prime commodities daily through 18 regional offices, primarily in supermarkets and groceries, where it reported generally good compliance. It did not take a position on whether PHP78 was nutritionally adequate, saying it needed to coordinate with SECRC and Balisakan and that public-market and food-logistics matters belonged principally to the Department of Agriculture.
topics.outcome: DTI explained its price-monitoring jurisdiction and reported generally good compliance in supermarkets and groceries, while public markets and food logistics were left to the Department of Agriculture. The adequacy of the PHP78 food benchmark remained unanswered, subject to DTI's promised coordination with SECRC and Balisakan.

positions.position: She pressed DTI on the scope and enforcement of price monitoring and questioned whether PHP78 per person per day could realistically meet basic nutritional requirements.
She maintained that DTI had kept prices stable and monitored compliance in supermarkets and groceries, but acknowledged that DTI could not immediately assess the PHP78 benchmark.

topics.topic: Cooperative development officers under Republic Act No. 11535
topics.summary: Rep. Presley De Jesus, who said he authored Republic Act No. 11535 during the 18th Congress, asked whether the cooperative development officer requirement had been fully implemented. The CDA reported compliance of 73.22, or about 74%, in provinces, cities, and municipalities. It said local government units commonly cited inadequate funds and reported that the CDA and DILG had signed a joint memorandum of understanding to complete implementation. The CDA said the DILG should ensure compliance because the law requires local government units to include the position in their plantilla. Rep. De Jesus asked that the 74% implementation status and the DILG's role be taken up during budget plenary.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish whether Republic Act No. 11535 had been fully implemented, specifically the requirement for cooperative development officers in provinces, cities, and municipalities. positions.position: The cooperative development officer requirement under Republic Act No. 11535 should be fully implemented and supported through the budget, with the DILG held responsible for ensuring that local government units create the required plantilla positions.

topics.topic: Abaca industry decline and integrated value-chain support
topics.summary: Rufus Rodriguez raised the sharp decline in national and Catanduanes abaca production and asked about its effects on the entire value chain, including employment, income, and markets. DTI said it provided MSME assistance, market access, product development, shared service facilities, and cluster coordination through 18 regional offices and 1,400 Negotio centers. The regional DTI official acknowledged that industry-wide resources were lacking and identified both reduced raw-material supply and shrinking markets as concerns. The DTI Secretary said abaca production was under the Department of Agriculture but reported that abaca fiber exports rose by 25% in 2025 to 21,700,000. Rodriguez then asked for an integrated FY2027 plan, citing 4,300,000 in shared service facilities for Catanduanes producers. DTI committed to coordinate with the province and offered a report, but did not present specific FY2027 programs or investments.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish the causes and effects of declining abaca production across the value chain, including producers, traders, processors, handicraft and furniture makers, employment, income, and markets. It also asked whether DTI had an integrated industry-development plan and what specific FY2027 programs and investments would support higher-value abaca products and expanded markets.
topics.agency_position: DTI stated that it supported abaca enterprises mainly at the MSME level through market access, product development, shared service facilities, cluster coordination, and regional and Negotio Center services. It acknowledged that industry-wide resources were lacking, while pointing to increased abaca fiber exports and committing to coordinate with the province and help producers access domestic and global markets.
topics.outcome: DTI answered that it had existing MSME and market-access mechanisms but lacked resources for additional industry-wide programs. It offered coordination and a report on possible interventions, but the requested integrated FY2027 abaca industry plan and specific investments were not clearly provided.

positions.position: He treated the decline in abaca production as an urgent value-chain and livelihood concern requiring an integrated industry-development plan, targeted FY2027 programs and investments, stronger processing and manufacturing, higher-value products, and expanded markets.
She stated that abaca needed support beyond existing MSME interventions and that industry-wide resources, including support for community-based and agribusiness industries, should be considered.

She emphasized DTI's existing market-access and financing channels, regional offices, trade shows, export assistance, and e-commerce, while noting that abaca production itself was under the Department of Agriculture.

topics.topic: Bamboo development transfer and interagency coordination
topics.summary: Gloria Macapagal Arroyo raised the pending proposal to transfer bamboo development from DTI to DA and asked whether DTI had already ceded the function. DTI said its role concerned finished bamboo products and market access, but it did not clarify the transfer status or confirm compliance with the DepEd bamboo procurement requirement. Arroyo also questioned DTI's whole-of-government coordination and argued that multiple halal certifiers and logos confused importing countries. DTI acknowledged the certification problem, said exporters were directed to destination-country-accredited certifiers, and said some companies had engaged with them. Arroyo requested evidence of actual purchases and export growth in Malaysia and Pakistan, but DTI did not provide figures. DTI committed to provide a list of companies and speak with Seksani again, while the broader coordination and legislative questions remained unresolved.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish whether DTI was aware of pending legislation to transfer bamboo development to the Department of Agriculture and whether DTI had voluntarily ceded that function. It also examined whether DTI's whole-of-government approach was producing concrete coordination on bamboo procurement and halal certification, including the proposed move toward a single certifying body.
topics.agency_position: DTI said its bamboo role focused on finished bamboo products and market access, while bamboo development was described as being with DA. It acknowledged problems with halal certification, said exporters could use certifiers accredited in destination countries, and stated that some companies had already engaged with those bodies. DTI did not provide the requested export figures or resolve whether the bamboo procurement requirement was being implemented.
topics.outcome: DTI acknowledged coordination and certification problems but did not establish that it had voluntarily transferred bamboo development to DA, provide the requested halal export results, or confirm compliance with the bamboo procurement requirement. It undertook to submit a company list and follow up with Seksani, leaving the substantive issues open.

hearings.title: COMMITTEE ON APPROPRIATIONS (DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE) AUGUST 24, 2026

topics.topic: DOJ FY2027 budget reductions and restoration requests
topics.summary: The DOJ presented a FY2027 recommended budget with major reductions affecting OSEC programs, BI, NBI, OADR, corrections, OSAIC, IACAT, and cybercrime-related work. Members Pajernos, Ann Matibag, Adelima, and Rodriguez expressed support for the DOJ budget and for restoring or increasing priority allocations. DOJ officials requested restoration to FY2026 levels, including OSEC MOOE and priority enforcement programs, while the NBI sought restoration of about 882 million and hazard pay of PHP15000 monthly. PAO sought additional lawyers and staff costing about 700 million, BI requested capital outlay for its new building and IT systems, and OSG identified about 123 million for digitalization. The committee said it would work on these requests, but no final restoration was adopted during the exchange.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish the scale and operational effects of the reductions in the DOJ's FY2027 recommended budget, and which DOJ offices and programs required restoration. It also sought specific restoration amounts, staffing and capital-outlay needs, and agency commitments to improve budget utilization.
topics.agency_position: The DOJ stated that the FY2027 recommended budget could sustain its performance targets but acknowledged that reductions in OSEC, NBI, BI, OSAIC, IACAT, cybercrime, ICT, OADR, PAO, and other programs would constrain operations. DOJ officials requested restoration to FY2026 levels for priority programs and identified specific needs for NBI hazard pay, PAO staffing, BI capital outlay, OSG digitalization, and PPA computerization.
topics.outcome: The committee broadly supported restoring reductions to FY2026 levels but did not adopt a final department-wide restoration figure. Specific agency requests were identified for further committee action, while the BI fee and some capital-outlay amounts remained under review or unclear.

Supported restoring and increasing DOJ funding, especially for programs such as the revised CPN plus D protocol and law-enforcement responses to violence against women and children.

Supported legislative expansion of the PCGG mandate and undertook to coauthor the relevant bill.

thread.speaker: Committee chair
thread.said: The chair said the committee was deliberating on the proposed FY2027 budget of the DOJ and attached agencies, including automatic appropriations. The budget was described as about 2% higher than the previous budget, while several offices faced substantial reductions.

thread.speaker: Committee chair
thread.said: The chair identified reductions of 35.8% for the Bureau of Immigration, 22.3% for the NBI, and 16.3% for the Office for Alternative Dispute Resolution. The corrections program was described as facing a 21.05% reduction, including a cut in victims compensation from PHP 19,000,000 to PHP 8,000,000.

thread.speaker: DOJ budget presenter
thread.said: The DOJ presenter said the proposed FY2027 budget, including constituent and attached agencies, amounted to 46.446435000000, while the comparison with the FY2026 approved budget was garbled. The FY2027 budget was retained at 0.64% or less than 1% of the published total net budget of trillion, with the amount unclear.

thread.speaker: DOJ budget presenter
thread.said: The department-wide budget proposal was stated as 121.63 billion, while the total FY2027 net recommended budget was stated only as billion, with the amount unclear, or 38.18% of the submitted proposal.

thread.speaker: DOJ budget presenter
thread.said: The Office of the Secretary was provided a total budget of 13,930,000,000. The special enforcement and protection subprogram was reduced to 204,000,000 from current appropriations of 402,000,000.

thread.speaker: DOJ budget presenter
thread.said: The recommended corrections budget was reduced by 21.05%. Pardons and parole services were reduced by 2.63% to 37,000,000, while victims compensation fell from 19,000,000 in 2026 to 8,000,000 in 2027.

thread.speaker: DOJ budget presenter
thread.said: The Bureau of Immigration's recommended FY2027 budget was 2,980,000,000, 35.8 percent lower than the 2026 budget. The NBI's recommended budget was 3,030,000,000, down from 3,900,000,000 in 2026.

thread.speaker: DOJ budget presenter
thread.said: The Land Registration Authority's recommended budget was 3,280,000,000, compared with 2,880,000,000 in 2026. The presenter said the NBI would process more than 6,600,000 clearances and conduct at least 50,000 investigations.

thread.speaker: DOJ budget presenter
thread.said: The Office of the Solicitor General's recommended budget was stated as 2,140,000,000, compared with 1,000,000,000 in the current year, although the stated percentage variance was 13.15%. The PPA recommendation was 1,250,000,000, compared with 1,300,000,000 in 2026.

thread.speaker: DOJ budget presenter
thread.said: The PCGG recommendation was stated as R339 million, compared with R310 million in current appropriations, and its target was at least 846,000,000 in surrendered or sequestered assets submitted to the Bureau of Treasury. The PAO recommendation was 7,101,000,000, compared with 6,693,000,000 in 2026.

thread.speaker: DOJ budget presenter
thread.said: The OADR recommended budget was 139,000,000, 16.27% below the current appropriation. The agency said it would train eighteen eighty ADR practitioners and implementers and act on 100 of applications for accreditation.

thread.speaker: Rep. Jan JP Pajernos
thread.said: Rep. Pajernos said DOJ performance indicators supported the department's work, citing a 99.12% case disposition rate and a prosecution success rate above 90%. He manifested full support for the DOJ proposed budget and for increases, particularly for the NBI and BI.

thread.speaker: DOJ official
thread.said: The DOJ official attributed the reductions to DBM assessment of agency absorptive capacity and said catch-up plans for 2026 would help the NBI and BI cope with budget releases.

thread.speaker: Rep. Ann Matibag
thread.said: Rep. Ann Matibag expressed dismay at the reductions affecting DOJ law-enforcement offices, particularly the BI and NBI. She supported the revised CPN plus D protocol for coordinated, child-sensitive handling of violence against women and children cases and said she would support restoring and increasing funding before plenary.

thread.speaker: Rep. Laila Adelima
thread.said: Rep. Adelima supported the department-wide DOJ budget and restoration of cuts affecting OSAIC and IACAT. She cited a 61.82% DOJ-wide cut against the proposed budget, an 84.18% cut for BuCor, and a 65.84% cut for the NBI, and asked the agencies to identify specific priority items for restoration.

thread.speaker: Bureau of Immigration official
thread.said: In response to questions about Dr. Calumard's blacklisting, the BI official said the basis was a national-security concern and that the official could provide a full and detailed report based on records and reports from the National Security Agency.

thread.speaker: Bureau of Immigration official
thread.said: After the committee asked about the motion to lift the blacklist and the 15-working-day rule, the BI official undertook to act on the matter right away, by the following day.

thread.speaker: Bureau of Immigration official
thread.said: The BI official said the proposed CAIS fee was part of a public-private partnership and that no alternative funding source had been discussed. The private proponent would provide capitalization of 10,700,000,000 over the next five years, with system upgrades every four years for the next twenty-year period at no cost to the government.

thread.speaker: Bureau of Immigration official
thread.said: The official clarified that the proposed fee was 240 per ticket, or 4.80 for a round-trip ticket, and said the proposal remained under review by the DOF and other agencies. No contract had been signed.

thread.speaker: DOJ Secretary Eric Bida
thread.said: Secretary Eric Bida asked that DOJ OSEC MOOE be restored to FY2026 levels and identified the Office of Cybercrime, the NBI, OSAIC, and IACAT as priorities whose reductions should be restored to maintain momentum.

thread.speaker: DOJ Secretary Eric Bida
thread.said: For the identified agencies, Secretary Vida stated 45.17 and then approximately 30,000,000; the intended restoration figure was unclear in the transcript. He reiterated the request to return them to 2026 levels.

thread.speaker: DOJ Secretary Eric Bida
thread.said: Secretary Vida additionally requested restoration of the NBI's ICT projects and programs, citing the agency's cybercrime and investigative requirements.

thread.speaker: Rep. Rufus Rodriguez
thread.said: Rep. Rodriguez asked whether the NBI budget had fallen from 3,791,000 to 2.9, a decrease of 882000023.2%, as stated in the transcript.

thread.speaker: NBI Director Melvin Matibag
thread.said: Director Melvin Matibag attributed the reduction to utilization issues involving ICT projects that needed alignment and completion. He said the NBI expected 90% utilization by December, with the remaining 2% for maintenance of ICT already obligated.

thread.speaker: Rep. Rufus Rodriguez
thread.said: Rep. Rodriguez proposed working for restoration of 882,000,000 for the NBI and asked whether that would satisfy the agency. Director Matibag instead raised a separate request for higher hazard pay.

thread.speaker: NBI Director Melvin Matibag
thread.said: Director Matibag requested that NBI agents' hazard pay be increased from MXN4000 monthly to PHP15000 monthly, citing transfers, 24/7 operations, and work involving OSAIC and cybercrime.

thread.speaker: Rep. Rufus Rodriguez
thread.said: Rep. Rodriguez said, "15,000? Approved," clarifying that this was his own support and that the committee would work for the request.

thread.speaker: Chief Public Attorney Persida Ruida Acosta
thread.said: Chief Public Attorney Persida Ruida Acosta said PAO needed five fifty nine lawyers, could accept half the number, and also needed staff positions. She estimated the combined requirement for lawyers and staff at around 600,000,000, later stating around 700,000,000.

thread.speaker: Rep. Rufus Rodriguez
thread.said: Rep. Rodriguez said the committee would try to provide 700,000,000 for additional PAO lawyers and staff, citing the continuing creation of courts and the need for fiscals and public attorneys.

thread.speaker: Bureau of Immigration official
thread.said: The BI official requested capital outlay for post-construction work on the new BI building and for locally funded IT systems and infrastructure projects. The total amount was transcribed as billion 227,800 and is unclear.

thread.speaker: OSG official
thread.said: The OSG official said a 248,000,000 increase would support the first-year installment for a building procured through the GSIS lease-to-own framework. The transcript also states IISP 123,000,000 for the computerization and digital-transformation program.

thread.speaker: OSG official
thread.said: The OSG official stated that the whole OSG building would cost PHP4.5 billion and that the first-year GSIS installment would be PHP 255,000,000, while another exchange referred to 250,000,000.

thread.speaker: OSG official
thread.said: The OSG identified its computerization and digital-transformation program as a priority, with a stated amount of 123,000,000. Rep. Rodriguez endorsed digitalization as important.

thread.speaker: Rep. Rufus Rodriguez
thread.said: Rep. Rodriguez asked OADR what it wanted restored after a reduction stated as 26,000,000.

thread.speaker: OADR official
thread.said: The OADR official requested restoration to the original January level for 2027. The precise restoration amount was not clearly stated.

thread.speaker: Parole and Probation Administration official
thread.said: The PPA official said the agency's reduction was 49,000,000 and identified ISSP computerization and a three-year leadership-improvement program for probation officers as restoration priorities. The latter was stated as 8,198,000 for three years and then as 8,000,000.

thread.speaker: Rep. Rufus Rodriguez
thread.said: Rep. Rodriguez said the committee would try to work on the 8,000,000 PPA request.

thread.speaker: PCGG official
thread.said: The PCGG official said its principal need was institutional rather than budgetary: legislation expanding its mandate from a limited group of individuals to all public officials. The official said PCGG had recovered more than R300 billion through civil forfeiture.

thread.speaker: Rep. Rufus Rodriguez
thread.said: Rep. Rodriguez said there was already a bill concerning expansion of the PCGG mandate and that he would be a coauthor.

topics.topic: Anti-trafficking, cybercrime, and OSAEC budget cuts
topics.summary: Rep. Jonathan Keith Flores, a Gabriela member, and Rep. Percy Sandania questioned the proposed reductions affecting anti-trafficking, cybercrime enforcement, OSAEC, and the NCC. DOJ officials said the cuts would weaken capacity-building, local task forces, rescue operations, IT infrastructure, international data sharing, and the response to AI-enabled exploitation. The figures cited included reductions of 71%, 58%, 41%, 58.93%, and 14%, while the DOJ requested restoration of the relevant budgets to 2026 levels and identified additional NCC plantilla positions as a need. The DOJ later provided budget figures for the NCC, anti-trafficking secretariat, and Office of Cybercrime, including an unclear transcribed 2027 cybercrime figure. Members Ann Matibag and Laila Adelima manifested support for restoring or increasing the affected funding and asked to work with the DOJ on specific priority items. No final committee restoration was recorded, but the issue was committed for further work before plenary.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish why the proposed budgets for anti-trafficking, cybercrime enforcement, and OSAEC-related programs were sharply reduced, whether the reductions reflected absorptive-capacity problems, and how they would affect enforcement, rescue operations, staffing, and responses to AI-enabled crimes. Members also sought the DOJ's requested funding levels and whether the cuts should be restored to 2026 levels.
topics.agency_position: The DOJ said the reductions would undermine national and local responses to trafficking, OSAEC, cybercrime, and AI-enabled exploitation, delay capacity-building, weaken rescue operations, and threaten the Philippines' Tier One status in the U.S. TIP report. It requested restoration of the relevant budgets to 2026 levels, additional NCC plantilla positions, stronger IT and investigative capacity, and continued international information-sharing mechanisms.
topics.outcome: DOJ officials consistently requested restoration of the affected programs to 2026 levels, and several members expressed support for that position. The transcript did not record a committee ruling or final restoration, although members indicated that the issue would be pursued before plenary.

positions.position: Questioned the reductions and supported restoring the affected budgets to 2026 levels.
Expressed grave concern over the proposed cuts and pressed for funding reflecting the units' operational needs.
Warned that the cuts threatened children's safety and supported immediate restoration to 2026 levels.
Supported restoring and increasing DOJ funding, particularly for programs such as the revised CPN plus D protocol and OSAEC-related work.
Supported the DOJ-wide budget and restoration of cuts affecting OSAEC and IACAT, while asking the DOJ to identify specific priority items.

thread.said: Flores cited a 41% anti-trafficking reduction, a 71% cybercrime reduction, and a 58% OSAEC reduction, and asked whether the issue was the programs' absorptive capacity.

thread.speaker: Lapus, DOJ official
thread.said: Lapus acknowledged limitations in procuring high-level programs and in the capacity of local task forces to act on cases. He said those limitations required sustained capacity-building rather than budget cuts.

thread.speaker: Rep. Jonathan Keith Flores
thread.said: Flores asked whether the OSAEC-related program was included in the reduction and noted that it was a LEDAC priority despite a stated 58.93% reduction.

thread.speaker: Lapus, DOJ official
thread.said: Lapus said the reduction would take the NCC and OSAEC initiatives “two or three steps back.” He said the DOJ had just rolled out the national strategic action plan against OSAEC and needed to maintain the Philippines' Tier One status in the U.S. TIP report.

thread.speaker: Lapus, DOJ official
thread.said: Lapus warned that losing Tier One status could have economic implications and said the country's response mechanisms had to show constant improvement. He said restoring the budget would provide sufficient support for that goal.

thread.speaker: Rep. Jonathan Keith Flores
thread.said: Flores asked what impact a 71% reduction in the anti-cybercrime enforcement budget would have, given that many crimes were committed through the Internet and other devices.

thread.speaker: DOJ agency official
thread.said: The official said many cyber-enabled crimes were already being perpetrated through AI systems and that the DOJ needed to catch up in its response.

thread.speaker: DOJ agency official
thread.said: The official requested restoration of the Office of Cybercrime budget to 2026 levels to maintain the pace of response. The needs identified were IT infrastructure, personnel capability-building, additional investigative and policy personnel, and international cooperation for information exchange, victim identification, and rescue operations.

thread.speaker: Rep. Jonathan Keith Flores
thread.said: Flores asked whether the reductions resulted from the DOJ's inability to procure needed items and questioned what had gone wrong with the prior budget figures.

thread.speaker: DOJ agency official
thread.said: The official attributed the concern to procurement of high-ticket or high-level programs and the need to ensure that procurement was completed on time. The official also cited a directive to reduce MOOE expenses by 20%.

thread.speaker: DOJ agency official
thread.said: The official said the DOJ needed alternative procurement modes, including empowering regional bids and awards committees, to improve absorptive capacity and keep pace with procurement needs.

thread.speaker: Rep. Jonathan Keith Flores
thread.said: Flores asked whether the offices were experiencing manpower problems.

thread.speaker: DOJ agency official
thread.said: The official said NCC plantilla positions were completely filled but that more plantilla positions were needed. As a temporary measure, the DOJ was using job orders and contracts of service, while also managing secondary trauma and workload effects on current personnel.

thread.speaker: DOJ agency official
thread.said: The official asked for support in advocating the creation of 79 or so plantilla positions for the NCC.

thread.speaker: DOJ agency official
thread.said: On international data sharing concerning foreign sex offenders, the official said European data-privacy laws restricted the sharing of information. The DOJ was pursuing police assistance, mutual legal-assistance arrangements, and continuing engagement with foreign NCC counterparts.

thread.speaker: Rep. Jonathan Keith Flores
thread.said: Flores said the committee should do something to restore the budgets to 2026 levels.

thread.speaker: Gabriela member
thread.said: The Gabriela member expressed grave concern over the proposed cuts to the special enforcement and protection subprogram, particularly anti-trafficking enforcement, anti-cybercrime enforcement, and the NCC, and asked DOJ officials to explain the proposed 2027 funding.

thread.speaker: DOJ agency official
thread.said: The official said the NCC secretariat's 2026 budget was 111,500,000, while the 2027 net budget was R35.6 million, and requested an increase of 75,900,000 to restore it to 2026 levels.

thread.speaker: DOJ agency official
thread.said: The official said the Interagency Council Against Trafficking Secretariat's 2026 budget was 119,000,000 and its 2027 net budget was 70,000,000, requesting “more or less 50 ms or 49 ms to be exact.” The Office of Cybercrime had 102,200,000 in 2026 and a 2027 net figure transcribed as 12,270,120,273,000.

thread.speaker: DOJ agency official
thread.said: The official characterized the Office of Cybercrime reduction as 90% from 2026.

thread.speaker: Gabriela member
thread.said: The Gabriela member pressed for the original proposed 2027 budget and questioned the limits placed on the agencies' proposals.

thread.speaker: DOJ agency official
thread.said: The official said the DOJ had been constrained in its proposals but emphasized that the units' real operational needs remained at the level of the same 2026 budget.

thread.speaker: DOJ agency official
thread.said: The official reiterated that absorptive capacity and timely, reliable procurement were concerns, as was the need for additional plantilla positions. The official nevertheless underscored the units' actual operational requirements.

thread.speaker: Rep. Percy Sandania
thread.said: Sandania asked how DOJ could perform its duties in responding to OSAEC and trafficking when program cuts ranged from 71%, 58%, and 14%.

thread.speaker: DOJ agency official
thread.said: The official said the cuts would impair implementation of the four-year national strategic action plan by forcing the DOJ to proceed to other programs before building the necessary foundations. The cuts would also weaken local task-force capabilities and fragment the national and local response.

thread.speaker: DOJ agency official
thread.said: The official said insufficient resources would affect important rescue operations, victim identification, and the ability to remove children from abusive situations quickly. The official advocated restoring the NCC and anti-trafficking secretariat budgets to 2026 levels.

thread.speaker: Rep. Percy Sandania
thread.said: Sandania asked how the DOJ could respond to the larger problem created by AI-enabled exploitation and other evolving crimes if the proposed cuts remained.

thread.speaker: DOJ agency official
thread.said: The official said the DOJ needed to catch up with constantly evolving and complicated mechanisms of recruitment, grooming, and exploitation, including cases in which an AI agent could entice young people. IT infrastructure and a corresponding, timely response were needed to stay ahead of the threats.

thread.speaker: Rep. Percy Sandania
thread.said: Sandania said the budget itself was a threat to children's safety, expressed support for restoring the budgets to 2026 levels, and said the affected children deserved immediate rescue assistance.

thread.speaker: Rep. Ann Matibag
thread.said: Matibag said members were disheartened by the deductions affecting OSAEC cases and commended the DOJ's revised CPN plus D protocol for standardizing and coordinating the handling of violence-against-women-and-children cases.

thread.speaker: Rep. Ann Matibag
thread.said: Matibag noted that the revised protocol had been launched nationally in August 2025, followed by provincial implementation in Cavite in March 2026 and Cebu in July 2026. She said this was the kind of program that deserved support in the 2027 budget.

thread.speaker: Rep. Ann Matibag
thread.said: Matibag manifested support for increasing the DOJ budget and said members would work with the department before plenary to explain and discuss the funding needed to restore the DOJ's requested levels.

thread.speaker: Rep. Laila Adelima
thread.said: Adelima supported the department-wide DOJ budget and restoration of cuts, including those for OSAEC and IACAT, and asked the agencies to identify specific priority items that members could help restore.

topics.topic: NBI funding, hazard pay, staffing, and overseas attaches
topics.summary: Brian Poe asked whether the NBI had funding for overseas attaches and was told that attaches were a future objective requiring additional agents; the NBI had only about 300 agents in the Philippines. Poe also urged increased funding for DOJ legal-aid services and PAO staffing, while PAO requested 559 lawyers and additional staff. Rufus Rodriguez pursued restorations for reduced DOJ and attached-agency budgets, including a proposed 882,000,000 restoration for the NBI. The NBI requested that agent hazard pay rise from MXN4000 monthly to PHP15000 monthly, and Rodriguez said it was approved from his position. PAO estimated that its requested lawyers and staff would cost around 700,000,000, while BI sought capital outlay and OSG sought 123,000,000 for digitalization. Sarah Elago asked about gender-sensitive investigation training, and the NBI said it was covered through GAD, academy, international training, behavioral science, and social-worker coordination. Final appropriations were not established in the transcript.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish whether the NBI had funding for overseas attaches, sufficient resources and personnel for its investigative mandate, and an adequate hazard-pay level. Members also examined proposed reductions and restoration requests affecting the NBI, PAO, BI, and OSG, including staffing, capital outlay, and digitalization.
topics.agency_position: The NBI said overseas attaches were a future objective but would require additional agents and funding; it reported only about 300 agents in the Philippines. It supported restoration of reduced ICT funding, requested an increase in hazard pay from MXN4000 to PHP15000 monthly, and said gender-sensitive training was covered by GAD, academy, and international-training resources.
topics.outcome: The committee expressed support for restoring reduced NBI and attached-agency funding and for increasing NBI hazard pay, but the transcript did not show final budget enactment. NBI overseas-attach funding remained a future request, while PAO staffing, BI capital outlay, and OSG digitalization were left as committee restoration or support commitments.
