thread.speaker: PAGCOR assistant vice president Cheryl DeGuilla
thread.said: She reported that PAGCOR's 2025 total income was 106,030,000,000 and its total contributions to nation building were around 67,000,000,000. The contributions included the government share, taxes, host-city share, socio-civic projects, and other mandated contributions.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR assistant vice president Cheryl DeGuilla
thread.said: For 2026, PAGCOR estimated total revenues of around 7,000,000,000 and nation-building contributions of around 61,000,000,000. For 2027, it projected total revenues of 88,330,000,000 and nation-building allocations of around 63,000,000,000.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR assistant vice president Cheryl DeGuilla
thread.said: She said total contributions to nation building reached 66,950,000,000 in 2025, down from 68,200,000,000 in 2024 because of lower revenues. PAGCOR also remitted 8,310,000,000 in taxes to the Bureau of Internal Revenue and declared 5,670,000,000 in dividends.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR assistant vice president Cheryl DeGuilla
thread.said: She reported that the 2025 allocation for universal health care was around 22,560,000,000. During the first semester of 2026, total income was 43,320,000,000, of which 30,160,000,000 went to nation-building programs.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR assistant vice president Eric Balcos
thread.said: PAGCOR committed PHP 7,500,000,000 for a nationwide school-building program with the Department of Education. The commitment covered one hundred and twenty five three-storey, 12-classroom school buildings, or approximately 1,500 classrooms, over two years.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR assistant vice president Eric Balcos
thread.said: PAGCOR had donated close to two fifty patient transport vehicles to local governments, public hospitals, frontline agencies, and nongovernment organizations.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR assistant vice president Eric Balcos
thread.said: In 2025 and the first semester of 2026, PAGCOR spent PHP 300,000,000 on food and non-food packs for communities affected by typhoons, floods, earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, and fires.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR assistant vice president Eric Balcos
thread.said: PAGCOR contributed 360,000,000 worth of medical equipment to the Jose B. Lingad Children's Medical Center. The Bloomberg Cultural Foundation Incorporated provided PHP 1,000,000,000 for construction and development.

thread.speaker: Committee Chair Mika Suansing
thread.said: She asked PAGCOR to explain the decline in total income from 2025 to 2026, noting an 18% decrease from the 2025 actual total income projection of R106 billion to R86.94 PHP 95,000,000,000 in 2026.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR chairman Alejandro H. Tengco
thread.said: He attributed the decline partly to the delinking of e-wallets from online gaming, which caused about a 40% decline in gaming activity, and to the Middle East crisis, which affected both land-based and online gaming. He said gaming activity increased about 10% in July and remained at that level in August.

thread.speaker: Committee Chair Mika Suansing
thread.said: She commended PAGCOR because, despite an approximately 20 billion decrease in estimated total income, nation-building contributions declined by only point 3% or R5.5 billion, according to the transcript.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR chairman Alejandro H. Tengco
thread.said: He explained that PAGCOR was implementing the Supreme Court's final ruling effective 01/01/2026, requiring the Philippine Sports Commission remittance to be computed at 5% of gross income rather than under the previous interpretation based on gaming revenue.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR chairman Alejandro H. Tengco
thread.said: He said the ruling was retroactive to 1993 and created a Philippine Sports Commission obligation of 37,000,000,000 pesos. PAGCOR had filed a motion for reconsideration and was in ongoing talks with PSC regarding payment.

thread.speaker: Committee Chair Mika Suansing
thread.said: She said the committee would account for the increased PAGCOR remittances when scrutinizing the PSC budget. She later requested copies of PAGCOR's PSC remittances for all of 2025 and from the start of 2026.

thread.speaker: Committee Chair Mika Suansing
thread.said: She noted that social-civic projects increased from PHP12.4 billion in 2024 to PHP12.8 billion in 2025 and PHP13.99 billion in 2026, and commended PAGCOR for retaining those commitments despite lower income.

thread.speaker: Representative Salvador Pleyto
thread.said: He asked what concrete measures PAGCOR would implement to reverse the reported 26.864% decline in first-semester 2026 total revenues and the 85.59% decline in net income, particularly in electronic online gaming.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR chairman Al
thread.said: He said PAGCOR regularly reviewed and updated its structures, guidelines, and online-gaming rules. He also cited participation in conventions and exhibits abroad to promote Philippine land-based casinos and online gaming.

thread.speaker: Vice Chair Brian Poe
thread.said: He said 44 of 52 illegal websites identified after the previous hearing had initially been taken down, but some were accessible again. He submitted a list of the sites to the committee for PAGCOR follow-up.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR chairman Al
thread.said: For 2026, he estimated gross gaming revenue from land-based casinos and online gaming at about 370,000,000,000 pesos or less.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR chairman Al
thread.said: He estimated total wagers placed in 2026 at about 3,000,000,000,000 pesos, explaining that gross gaming revenue was total bets less payouts.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR chairman Al
thread.said: He said PAGCOR had not issued licenses to the referenced applications and websites because of a moratorium on licenses for the previous two years, and that they therefore remained illegal operators.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR chairman Al
thread.said: In response to a question about gambling addiction and mental-health assistance, he said the issue was covered by PAGCOR's responsible-gaming programs, including a partner foundation and a 247 call center. He undertook to submit the programs to the committee for dissemination.

thread.speaker: Vice Chair Brian Poe
thread.said: He requested copies of PAGCOR's responsible-gaming programs, the number of people helped, and the amount of funding provided, saying gambling addiction required public assistance options.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR chairman Al
thread.said: He said PAGCOR had worked with DICT and CICC to identify tools needed to track operators using VPNs and that equipment was being procured or was about to be procured. He also cited continuing cooperation with DICT, CICC, NTC, and other enforcement bodies to close illegal sites.

thread.speaker: Vice Chair Brian Poe
thread.said: He requested a list of equipment procurement and related law-enforcement costs so the committee could compare the investment with potential additional government revenue from better monitoring and takedowns.

thread.speaker: Committee Chair
thread.said: The chair said the committee would share the websites and screenshots with PAGCOR and raise the broader enforcement issue during the ICT budget hearing, including with CICC.

thread.speaker: Representative Jean Baronda
thread.said: She asked whether PAGCOR had a five-year contingency plan to continue supporting universal health care in light of the Supreme Court ruling and its retroactive financial impact.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR chairman Alejandro Tengco
thread.said: He said PAGCOR would continue reaching as many Filipinos as possible while making the necessary financial adjustments and maintaining the universal-health-care fund.

thread.speaker: Representative Jean Baronda
thread.said: She asked PAGCOR to consider helping equip the cancer center of Western Visayas Medical Center, noting that hospital-bed capacity had expanded from four twenty to 700.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR chairman Alejandro Tengco
thread.said: He said PAGCOR would consider support for equipment and programs for children with special needs and would place the proposal on the agenda of a meeting with the relevant foundation and former congresswoman.

thread.speaker: Representative Shirlyn Bañas-Nograles
thread.said: She asked what technical safeguards prevented minors, government employees, low-income earners, and 4Ps beneficiaries from using easily accessible online gaming portals and micro-bets of 1 peso to 5 pesos. She also asked about relief for General Santos City and support for classrooms damaged by a seven point eight earthquake.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR chairman Alejandro H. Tengco
thread.said: He identified the know-your-customer process as the principal safeguard, requiring a valid government ID before registration. He said legal operators represented 50% of the total industry.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR chairman Alejandro H. Tengco
thread.said: He said PAGCOR had assisted General Santos victims with financial and relief packages in coordination with the Office of Civil Defense. He added that more than a 100,000 relief packs had been sent throughout the Philippines in the previous week and a half.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR chairman Alejandro H. Tengco
thread.said: Regarding damaged classrooms, he cited the program for 125 new school buildings, described in the transcript as equivalent to about a 200 classrooms, and invited the representative to submit a written request.

thread.speaker: Representative Antonino Roman III
thread.said: He asked how PAGCOR determined its social-civic budget and whether allocations were based on a percentage of income. He also followed up on pending requests for school buildings and the projected 2027 allocation.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR chairman Alejandro H. Tengco
thread.said: He said PAGCOR budgeted for the year rather than applying a fixed percentage to income. For relief, it might budget, for example, 200,000 relief packs and coordinate with the Office of Civil Defense based on weather forecasts.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR chairman Alejandro H. Tengco
thread.said: He confirmed that the school-building budget covered 125 school buildings and said PAGCOR would review the member's district request. He said the district had three entries on the list but might receive at most one because of the 125-building limit.

thread.speaker: Representative Marco Wangkol
thread.said: He asked whether PAGCOR funded hospitals and whether it could help reduce the Department of Health's burden for a Pangasinan hospital project estimated at around the 1,000,000,000 mark.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR chairman Alejandro H. Tengco
thread.said: He explained that PAGCOR generally did not fund hospital construction directly; foundations connected to licensees usually funded major projects. PAGCOR could provide equipment, and he cited more than MXN 1,000,000,000 spent by Bloomberry Foundation for the Clark hospital and 100,000,000 pesos previously given to Conrado Australia Hospital in Pangasinan.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR chairman Alejandro H. Tengco
thread.said: He cautioned that assistance had to be liquidated and that an incomplete project could restrict the recipient from receiving further PAGCOR aid. He suggested that PAGCOR might instead support equipment for a completed hospital building.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR chairman Alejandro H. Tengco
thread.said: He said PAGCOR could potentially work with the Pangasinan project on hospital equipment or other equipment needed to make a completed project operational. He requested a letter so the parties could arrange a further meeting.

topics.topic: Nationwide school-building program and classroom allocations
topics.summary: PAGCOR presented a nationwide program to build 125 three-storey school buildings, or approximately 1,500 classrooms, from 2026 through 2027. The agency stated that the program was funded at PHP 7.5 billion, while a member cited initial funding of 1,370,000,000 pesos and another referred to almost 8 billion. PAGCOR said it had earmarked close to about 3.5 billion for the 50% down payment, with later payments tied to construction progress. Rep. Sarah Elago requested a breakdown of fund utilization, but no such breakdown was submitted during the hearing. Members also questioned whether the program displaced community wellness centers, e-libraries, and evacuation centers, and PAGCOR said it could consider balancing those priorities. PAGCOR undertook to review assistance for earthquake-damaged classrooms and a district request, while conflicting transcript figures for classroom totals remained unresolved.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish the scope, funding, implementation period, and allocation of PAGCOR's nationwide school-building program. Members also asked how much had been earmarked or utilized, how schools and local government units were selected, and whether other proposed infrastructure projects would be displaced.
topics.agency_position: PAGCOR stated that its nationwide school-building program, undertaken with the Department of Education, would fund 125 three-storey, 12-classroom buildings and approximately 1,500 classrooms from 2026 through 2027. It said the program had a total funding commitment of PHP 7,500,000,000, with close to about 3,500,000,000 earmarked for the 50% down payment, and that site selection and project recommendations would be handled by the Department of Education while LGUs would conduct procurement and construction.
topics.outcome: PAGCOR explained the program's total commitment, implementation period, down-payment plan, and allocation process, but the requested utilization breakdown was not presented during the hearing. PAGCOR also left open the possibility of balancing the school-building allocation with other infrastructure priorities and undertook to review a district-level request.

positions.position: Suggested reconsidering or balancing the school-building program with school information-dissemination activities and the use of facilities as evacuation centers.
Sought clarification on the initial funding and requested a detailed breakdown of PAGCOR's utilization of school-building funds.

Questioned whether the large school-building allocation had displaced funding for community wellness centers, e-libraries, and evacuation centers, and urged consideration of balancing these priorities.
Pressed PAGCOR to assist with classrooms damaged by the earthquake in Jansen and indicated that her office would submit a written request.
Sought a fair allocation for his district and accepted that it might receive only one school-building project under the fixed nationwide allocation.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR Assistant Vice President Eric Balcos
thread.said: PAGCOR said that, in partnership with the Department of Education and under the President's instructions, it had launched a nationwide school-building program on 03/25/2026. PAGCOR committed PHP 7,500,000,000 for 125 three-storey, 12-classroom school buildings, equivalent to approximately 1,500 classrooms, over the next two years.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR Assistant Vice President Eric Balcos
thread.said: He said each facility would include student chairs and tables, PWD-friendly amenities, electric fans, microphones, a 75 inches smart TV, and a one year Internet subscription. The Department of Education would recommend sites, while the capability of recipient local government units to complete the buildings would also be considered.

thread.speaker: Rep. Bong Thebes Jinger
thread.said: Rep. Jinger raised the nationwide school-building program and asked about its coverage for elementary and high schools. He suggested that PAGCOR consider using the program instead for information-dissemination activities in schools and as evacuation centers during calamities.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR official
thread.said: PAGCOR said it would take note of the suggestions. The official explained that the program had been overtaken or defined by the memorandum of agreement with the Department of Education and said PAGCOR would consider how to balance the suggestions with its current programs.

thread.speaker: Rep. Sarah Elago
thread.said: Rep. Elago asked about the initial funding of 1,370,000,000 pesos and whether it was for the current or following year. She sought clarification on the program's total funding and implementation.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR Chairman Alejandro Tengco
thread.said: Chairman Tenko said the memorandum of agreement with the Department of Education covered 125 three-storey, 12-classroom school buildings at a total cost, including equipment and furniture, of roughly about 7,500,000,000. He said the projects would provide about 1,500 classrooms, with chairs, tables, 75 inches TVs, amplifiers, and other equipment, and would run from 2026 to the end of 2027.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR Chairman Alejandro Tengco
thread.said: He said the Department of Education would vet and recommend the school buildings, while PAGCOR would fund construction through the different local government units. PAGCOR had earmarked close to about 3,500,000,000 for the year's 50% down payment, followed by progressive billing based on each building's completion.

thread.speaker: Rep. Sarah Elago
thread.said: Rep. Elago requested that PAGCOR submit to the committee a breakdown of the utilization of funds for the nationwide school-building program.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR Chairman Alejandro Tengco
thread.said: Chairman Tenko said the Department of Education and the concerned local government units had numerous requirements, which PAGCOR collated. After a memorandum of agreement with the LGU or district, PAGCOR would release the first tranche to the LGU, which would handle the bidding process.

thread.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Montes
thread.said: Rep. Montes asked whether PAGCOR's new flagship infrastructure projects, including school buildings, e-learning centers, community wellness centers, social-civic centers, and evacuation centers, were part of the JMC zero one series of 2024 memorandum. She then asked whether the school-building allocation had displaced funding for the other projects.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR Chairman Alejandro Tengco
thread.said: Chairman Tenko said PAGCOR had realigned its budget for infrastructure projects such as community wellness centers, evacuation centers, and e-libraries, with priority given to the 125-school-building construction program. He stated that more classrooms would mean better education for the country's youth.

thread.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Montes
thread.said: Rep. Montes referred to almost 8,000,000,000 for constructing 125 school buildings and 1,500 classrooms, and asked whether PAGCOR could still fund the wellness centers and evacuation centers that had previously been prioritized.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR Chairman Alejandro Tengco
thread.said: Chairman Tenko said it was very possible that PAGCOR could consider the other projects, subject to balancing or rebalancing. He indicated that the 125 school buildings and 1,500 classrooms remained the current program while the agency considered how to accommodate other priorities.

thread.speaker: Rep. Shirlyn Bañas-Nograles
thread.said: Rep. Bañas-Nograles asked whether PAGCOR had committed assistance for classrooms in Jansen that were badly damaged by a seven point eight earthquake. She said the damage involved about 1,400 classrooms.

thread.speaker: Rep. Shirlyn Bañas-Nograles
thread.said: Rep. Bañas-Nograles asked PAGCOR to help with classroom reconstruction and said her office would write to the agency.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR Chairman Alejandro Tengco
thread.said: Chairman Tenko said PAGCOR could not undertake repairs or rehabilitation under the program but was providing new construction through 125 school buildings. The transcript's reference to the equivalent number of classrooms is unclear, rendered as "about a 200 classrooms."

thread.speaker: PAGCOR Chairman Alejandro Tengco
thread.said: Chairman Tenko described PAGCOR's commitment with the Department of Education to build 125 school buildings nationwide. The transcript rendered the corresponding classroom figure as "a 500 new classrooms," which conflicts with the agency's other stated figure of approximately 1,500 classrooms.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR Chairman Alejandro Tengco
thread.said: In response to questions about pending requests and the projected budget, Chairman Tenko referred to the construction of school buildings and the computation for 2027. The response did not provide a clear separate figure for pending school-building requests.

thread.speaker: Rep. Antonino Roman III
thread.said: Rep. Roman followed up on a district request and asked about the projected 2027 budget request for school buildings.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR Chairman Alejandro Tengco
thread.said: Chairman Tenko again referred to the 125-school-building program and said PAGCOR would hopefully address the matter in the 2027 or 2028 budget request. The exact budget timing and amount were not clearly stated.

thread.speaker: Rep. Antonino Roman III
thread.said: Rep. Roman asked about the allocation process, saying he needed to advocate for his district.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR Chairman Alejandro Tengco
thread.said: Chairman Tenko said the 100 percentile budget was for 125 school buildings throughout the Philippines. He said the program would follow the design agreed upon by the Department of Education, the LGU or district, and PAGCOR.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR Chairman Alejandro Tengco
thread.said: Chairman Tenko said PAGCOR would look into Rep. Roman's district request and discuss it after the hearing. He said the agency's list showed three possible projects in the district, but that, at most, the district might receive one because the program had a fixed allocation for 125 buildings.

thread.speaker: Rep. Antonino Roman III
thread.said: Rep. Roman accepted the possibility of one project, saying, "One is better than nothing."

topics.topic: Online-gaming revenues, e-games decline, and regulatory strategy
topics.summary: The chair and several members questioned PAGCOR about declining gaming income, especially the effects of e-wallet delinking, the Middle East crisis, illegal operators, and weaker land-based casino activity. PAGCOR attributed the decline to a roughly 40% fall in activity after payment-app delinking, while reporting a later increase of about 10% in July and August. Members also challenged PAGCOR on advertising approvals, influencer liability, foreign operators, KYC enforcement, minors' access, and the adequacy of responsible-gaming programs. PAGCOR cited fines, coordination with BSP, DICT, NTC, CICC, and police authorities, regular rule updates, a 1% gross-gaming-revenue allocation for responsible gaming, and a possible PAGCOR application for identifying legitimate operators. Revenue figures discussed included projected 2026 gaming operations of 80,000,000,000 pesos, digital e-games revenue of 38,000,000,000 to 40,000,000,038, Casino Filipino revenue of between 9 and 10,000,000,000, and licensed-casino revenue of about 31 and a half billion. The committee requested remittance and revenue documents and left further regulatory strengthening and several enforcement concerns for follow-up.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish why PAGCOR's projected and reported gaming revenues were declining, particularly in online and e-games operations, and how payment restrictions, illegal operators, advertising, and market conditions affected collections. It also examined whether PAGCOR had sufficient regulatory, responsible-gaming, and monitoring measures to protect players and sustain revenues and remittances.
topics.agency_position: PAGCOR attributed the revenue decline to e-wallet delinking, the Middle East crisis, weaker economic conditions, and reduced land-based and online gaming activity. It maintained that it was updating its rules, monitoring operators, coordinating with BSP and other enforcement agencies, pursuing illegal operators, supporting responsible-gaming programs, and exploring new revenue sources, while acknowledging that illegal operations and regulatory capacity remained significant challenges.
topics.outcome: PAGCOR explained the revenue decline and described regulatory, payment, enforcement, and responsible-gaming measures, but the committee remained concerned about illegal operators, e-wallet restrictions, minors' access, and the agency's capacity to police online platforms. The agency undertook to provide remittance and revenue documents, continue the helpline, consider a player-verification application, and further strengthen its regulatory framework.

positions.position: Commended PAGCOR for largely maintaining nation-building and social civic commitments despite lower income, but said the committee would scrutinize the PSC budget in light of increased PAGCOR remittances.
Pressed for stronger control over gambling advertisements, content creators, influencers, and online operators, particularly because many players were from low-income and minimum-wage groups.
Sought accountability for foreign illegal gambling companies and clarification of funding and continuity for the 24/7 problem-gambling helpline and related prevention programs.

Called for concrete measures to reverse revenue declines, strengthen digital monitoring and collections, expand legitimate gaming, and address illegal operators while attracting responsible investment.

Raised concerns that e-wallet restrictions could drive players toward unsafe payment channels and emphasized stronger KYC enforcement against mule accounts, third-party funding, minors' access, and illegal operators.

Accepted that online gaming could generate revenue but argued that PAGCOR needed stronger regulatory powers and practical policing measures before allowing the sector to expand, especially to protect CDE players and minors.
Requested an income breakdown and suggested redirecting some social-project resources toward responsible-gaming information campaigns in schools and communities.

thread.speaker: Mika Suansing, committee chair
thread.said: The chair highlighted an 18% decrease from the 2025 actual total income projection of R106 billion to 2026 projected income of R86.94 PHP 95,000,000,000, and asked PAGCOR to explain the downturn, especially in gaming operations income.

thread.speaker: Alejandro H. Tengco, PAGCOR chairman
thread.said: He attributed the decline partly to the delinking of e-wallets used by online-gaming customers after a Senate hearing requested that the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas implement the restriction. PAGCOR observed about a 40% decline in gaming activity because customers had to go through an additional payment process.

thread.speaker: Alejandro H. Tengco, PAGCOR chairman
thread.said: He said the Middle East crisis further affected land-based casinos and online gaming, whose main customers came from the CDE market. Gaming activity increased by about 10% in July and remained at that level in August, while tourism at integrated resorts also began to improve.

thread.speaker: Mika Suansing, committee chair
thread.said: The chair noted that despite an R20 billion decrease in estimated total income, contributions to nation building declined by only 5.5 billion or 0.3% as transcribed, and commended PAGCOR for maintaining its commitments.

thread.speaker: Alejandro H. Tengco, PAGCOR chairman
thread.said: He explained that PAGCOR was implementing effective 01/01/2026 the Supreme Court ruling interpreting the 5% remittance to the Philippine Sports Commission as 5% of gross income rather than gaming revenue only. The ruling was issued with finality in the last quarter of 2025 and was retroactive to 1993.

thread.speaker: Alejandro H. Tengco, PAGCOR chairman
thread.said: He said the retroactive PSC assessment was 37,000,000,000 pesos. PAGCOR had filed a motion for reconsideration and was in discussions regarding the time and manner of payment, while respecting the Supreme Court decision.

thread.speaker: Alejandro H. Tengco, PAGCOR chairman
thread.said: He said the PSC contribution had increased from an average of 190,000,000 pesos per month and that the new interpretation effectively doubled the impact.

thread.speaker: Mika Suansing, committee chair
thread.said: The chair said the committee would consider the increased PAGCOR remittances when scrutinizing the PSC budget and would seek a PSC funding level sufficient for its utilization, programs, and projects.

thread.speaker: Mika Suansing, committee chair
thread.said: The chair cited social civic projects increasing from PHP12.4 billion in 2024 to PHP12.8 billion in 2025 and PHP13.99 billion in 2026, and commended PAGCOR for retaining those commitments despite lower income.

thread.speaker: A committee member
thread.said: A member said the committee needed to examine the PSC budget in light of a payment of 3,300,000,000 every year for the next ten years.

thread.speaker: Mika Suansing, committee chair
thread.said: The chair requested copies of PAGCOR's remittances to the PSC for the whole of 2025 and from the beginning of 2026 so the committee could account for them in reviewing the PSC budget.

thread.speaker: Elijah San Fernando, minority member
thread.said: The member referred to 30,000,000 registered and 10,000,000 active online-gaming players, largely from the CDE market, and asked about compliance with advertising restrictions and responsible-gaming requirements.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR chairman
thread.said: PAGCOR said the Ad Standards Council rules covered online gaming and land-based casino advertising, including prime-time advertisements between five and 08:00 in the evening. It also described responsible-gaming measures and billboard requirements.

thread.speaker: Elijah San Fernando, minority member
thread.said: He asked whether PAGCOR was aware of ASC Circular 2025-010, requiring all gambling advertisements in all forms to secure ASC approval before implementation.

thread.speaker: Elijah San Fernando, minority member
thread.said: He clarified whether billboard and online advertisements required ASC clearance and asked whether PAGCOR exercised regulatory power over content creators and influencers promoting online gambling.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR chairman
thread.said: PAGCOR said it had fined an online-gaming company 1,000,000 pesos and issued a stern warning over an online endorser. Further violations could lead to suspension and ultimately cancellation of the operator's license.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR chairman
thread.said: PAGCOR stated that 50% of current online-gaming operators were illegal and outside its jurisdiction. It said reforms had increased the proportion of legal operators to 8% to 10%, although the transcription of the comparison was unclear.

thread.speaker: Elijah San Fernando, minority member
thread.said: He asked how PAGCOR addressed content creators with millions of followers who identified or promoted online-gaming sites, including sites that might not be PAGCOR-licensed.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR chairman
thread.said: PAGCOR said it was pursuing endorsers of illegal or non-PAGCOR-licensed sites and was working with the police, DICT, NTC, and CICC because police power and enforcement against foreign or illegal operators did not rest solely with PAGCOR.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR chairman
thread.said: PAGCOR described responsible-gaming projects, including a 24/7 hotline, nationwide billboards, partnerships with the Seagulls Flock Foundation, advice and referrals to rehabilitation centers, and self-exclusion for land-based and online players.

thread.speaker: Bong Thebes Jinger, majority member
thread.said: The member asked for a breakdown of PAGCOR income, including the share attributable to online gaming.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR official
thread.said: PAGCOR said gaming operations were estimated at 80,000,000,000 pesos, divided approximately 50% between land-based casinos and online gaming, with online gaming contributing 40,000,000,000.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR official
thread.said: In response to a suggestion for responsible-gaming information campaigns in schools and evacuation centers, PAGCOR said it would take note of the proposal and consider how to balance it with current programs.

thread.speaker: Sarah Elago, committee member
thread.said: Elago asked how PAGCOR addressed foreign gambling companies operating illegally, beyond local endorsers and influencers.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR official
thread.said: PAGCOR said it depended on the police, DICT, CICC, and NTC to act against foreign and illegal operators and their social-media platforms. Elago said she would pursue the matter with DICT and CICC.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR official
thread.said: PAGCOR said it was not aware of a national-government budget for the 24/7 problem-gambling helpline but committed under the chairman's administration to ensure that the initiatives continued.

thread.speaker: Sarah Elago, committee member
thread.said: Elago asked how much was allotted for helpline counseling, prevention, and awareness campaigns.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR official
thread.said: PAGCOR said online-gaming operators would allocate 1% of gross gaming revenue to responsible-gaming and certain social civic projects, amounting to about a billion pesos per annum.

thread.speaker: Salvador Pleyto, majority member
thread.said: Pleyto cited a 26.864% decline in total revenues and an 85.59% decline in net income in the first half of 2026, then asked what concrete measures PAGCOR would implement to reverse the trend and increase gross gaming revenue, particularly from electronic online gaming.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR chairman
thread.said: PAGCOR described efforts to address illegal operators, monitor online operators' gross gaming revenue, and use a third-party auditor. It also referred to possible revenue from BPO operations and expressed hope for improvement.

thread.speaker: Salvador Pleyto, majority member
thread.said: Pleyto asked for PAGCOR's strategy to improve its regulatory framework, expand the legitimate market, strengthen digital monitoring and collection, address illegal and unlicensed operators, and attract responsible investment.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR chairman
thread.said: PAGCOR said it regularly reviewed and updated its structures, guidelines, and online-gaming rules based on prevailing conditions and market trends. It also promoted Philippine gaming internationally and said it competed with gaming markets such as Macau and Singapore.

thread.speaker: Jan Rurik Padiernos, committee member
thread.said: Jan Rurik Padiernos asked how PAGCOR would balance BSP restrictions on direct gambling links in e-wallets with the need to support legitimate e-games operators, given that players were being pushed toward third-party channels and unauthorized aggregators that created fraud, data-theft, and money-laundering risks.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR official
thread.said: PAGCOR said it was in constant dialogue with the central bank regarding illegal payment aggregators and legal payment applications that served unlicensed operators. It was also considering a PAGCOR application, possibly for launch in the fourth quarter of the year, to help players identify legitimate operators.

thread.speaker: Jan Rurik Padiernos, committee member
thread.said: Jan Rurik Padiernos followed up on the decline of more than 41% in e-games revenue in the first half of 2026 and asked what regulatory response would support the legitimate e-games sector.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR official
thread.said: PAGCOR cited revenue-generating measures involving special-class BPO operations, continued efforts to move players from illegal to licensed operators, and studies of other revenue-generating schemes. It also said online gaming increased in July.

thread.speaker: Jan Rurik Padiernos, committee member
thread.said: Jan Rurik Padiernos asked about KYC enforcement and pre-verified or mule e-wallet accounts that could enable money laundering, fraud, third-party funding, or access by minors, and whether operators would be fined, suspended, or otherwise sanctioned.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR official
thread.said: PAGCOR said it monitored KYC compliance and imposed fines and suspensions on legal operators when warranted. It also said payment providers should not process customers of illegal operators.

thread.speaker: A minority member
thread.said: The member asked for PAGCOR's 2026 income from Casino Filipino operations, licensed casinos, and digital or e-games operations, and requested detailed lists of properties and revenues.

thread.speaker: Alejandro Tengco, PAGCOR chairman
thread.said: Tengco projected Casino Filipino gross gaming revenue at about 10,000,000,000 pesos, later clarifying that it would be between 9 and 10,000,000,000. He projected about 31 and a half billion from six licensed casinos excluding Casino Filipino.

thread.speaker: Alejandro Tengco, PAGCOR chairman
thread.said: Tengco undertook to send the committee a complete detailed list of revenues from licensed casinos, Casino Filipino, and online gaming, which he identified as PAGCOR's three major revenue drivers.

thread.speaker: Alejandro Tengco, PAGCOR chairman
thread.said: He projected 2026 digital e-games revenue at 38,000,000,000 to 40,000,000,038, as transcribed.

thread.speaker: A minority member
thread.said: The member asked whether the heavier reliance on e-games and online gaming was a positive development or a source of concern, given the social profile of many players and the difficulty of policing online activity.

thread.speaker: Alejandro Tengco, PAGCOR chairman
thread.said: Tengco said the development was both positive and negative: online gaming had growth potential because of technological advances, but he was concerned that major licensees were experiencing declining revenues and that economic and geopolitical conditions affected the industry.

thread.speaker: A minority member
thread.said: The member questioned the use of about 15 to 18,000,000,000 for social projects when online gaming income came heavily from the CDE market, and argued that stronger regulatory powers were needed before allowing online gaming to expand.

thread.speaker: Alejandro Tengco, PAGCOR chairman
thread.said: Tengco agreed that online gaming required stronger policing and said PAGCOR was strengthening its structures, guidelines, rules, and regulations and updating them regularly based on market trends. He acknowledged that illegal operators remained a major challenge.

thread.speaker: A minority member
thread.said: The member clarified that he was not opposed to online gaming itself but wanted to know how PAGCOR would properly police platforms, prevent access by minors, and protect CDE players from gambling-related harm.

thread.speaker: A committee member
thread.said: The member asked what concrete steps PAGCOR had taken to regulate rapidly evolving online platforms and warned that operators should not be allowed to function without an adequate regulatory framework.

thread.speaker: Alejandro H. Tengco, PAGCOR chairman
thread.said: Tengco said PAGCOR would look into how to further strengthen its structures. The member then expressed hope that the committee and agency would develop ways to properly regulate online gaming.

topics.topic: Illegal online-gaming operators, enforcement, and monitoring capacity
topics.summary: Rep. Sarah Elago asked how foreign illegal operators were being addressed and how the 24/7 problem-gambling helpline and related counseling programs were funded. PAGCOR said it lacked police powers, depended on DICT, CICC, NTC, and other partners, and would continue responsible-gaming initiatives supported by 1% of online gross gaming revenue, estimated at about a billion pesos per annum. Rep. Jan Rurik Padiernos questioned e-wallet restrictions, unauthorized payment channels, mule accounts, and KYC enforcement; PAGCOR cited coordination with the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas, monitoring, fines, and suspensions. Vice Chair Brian Poe reported that 44 of 52 illegal websites had initially been taken down but that some had returned, and PAGCOR said the sites had not been licensed because of a moratorium lasting two years. PAGCOR projected 2026 gross gaming revenue at about 370 billion and estimated total wagers at about 3 trillion, while acknowledging that only legal operators were tracked. The committee requested website lists, responsible-gaming data, and equipment-procurement and revenue projections, with further enforcement discussion assigned to the DICT budget hearing.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish how PAGCOR and other enforcement agencies were addressing illegal online-gaming operators, reopened websites, unauthorized payment channels, mule accounts, and gaps in KYC monitoring. Members also asked what resources, programs, and interagency equipment were needed to protect consumers and recover revenue that might otherwise be lost to illegal wagering.
topics.agency_position: PAGCOR said illegal online operators and payment channels required continuing coordination with DICT, CICC, NTC, the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas, and other entities because PAGCOR lacked police powers and tracked only licensed operators. It maintained that responsible-gaming programs, the planned PAGCOR application, KYC enforcement, site takedowns, and additional VPN-tracking equipment were the principal responses, but acknowledged that illegal sites could reopen and that more enforcement tools were needed.
topics.outcome: The committee received PAGCOR's explanations but did not resolve the scale of illegal wagering, the revenue lost from reopened sites, or the funding and equipment needed for stronger enforcement. The matter was carried forward through documentary requests, PAGCOR commitments, and a planned discussion during the DICT budget hearing.

positions.position: Foreign illegal operators, gambling advertising, and gambling-related harm required stronger interagency action, continuing helpline support, and clear funding for counseling, prevention, and awareness.
E-wallet restrictions needed to be balanced against the risks posed by unauthorized aggregators, mule accounts, fraud, money laundering, and minors' access, while legitimate operators were protected.

Reopened illegal sites and untracked wagering represented a substantial potential loss of government revenue, and investment in enforcement technology should be assessed against the revenue it could recover.

topics.topic: Gambling advertising, influencers, and penalties
topics.summary: Rep. Elijah San Fernando raised concerns about advertising controls and influencer promotion in light of approximately 30 million registered and 10 million active online-gaming players. PAGCOR said gambling advertisements required Ad Standards Council clearance and that a licensed operator had been fined 1,000,000 pesos, with suspension and license cancellation available for repeated violations. The agency said 50% of current online-gaming operators were illegal and that it relied on DICT, NTC, CICC, and social-media platforms for enforcement against operators and endorsers outside its jurisdiction. Rep. Sarah Elago pressed for action against foreign operators and asked about support for the 24/7 helpline; PAGCOR committed to continuing the initiative and cited 1% of online gross gaming revenue, or about a billion pesos per annum, for responsible-gaming and social civic projects. Rep. Presley de Jesus challenged whether the first-offense 1,000,000 penalty was sufficient, and PAGCOR said it had been increased from 50,000 and was not the maximum sanction. The chair committed to consolidating documentary requests and following up, leaving interagency enforcement and supporting documents pending.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish whether PAGCOR's controls over gambling advertisements, content creators, influencers, and foreign operators were sufficient to protect vulnerable players and deter violations. Members also examined the adequacy of the first-offense penalty, the responsible-gaming helpline and programs, and the enforcement authority available against illegal operators and endorsers.
topics.agency_position: PAGCOR stated that advertisements required Ad Standards Council clearance and that it could penalize licensed operators, suspend them for a second offense, and cancel their licenses for a third offense. It also said enforcement against illegal foreign operators and some influencers depended on DICT, NTC, CICC, and social-media platforms, while responsible-gaming programs and the 24/7 helpline would continue through PAGCOR funding and partnerships.
topics.outcome: PAGCOR answered that 1,000,000 was only the first-offense penalty, with suspension and cancellation available for subsequent offenses, and committed to continue responsible-gaming initiatives. Enforcement against foreign operators and some influencers remained dependent on other agencies and platforms, with documentary follow-up still pending.

positions.position: He maintained that the large population of registered and active online-gaming players, particularly low-income earners, made stronger oversight of gambling advertising, content creators, and influencers necessary.
She treated gambling as a public-health concern and pressed for action against foreign illegal operators and continued funding for counseling, prevention, awareness, and the 24/7 helpline.
He questioned whether the 1,000,000 first-offense advertising penalty was an adequate deterrent when an offending advertisement could remain widely visible.

topics.topic: Responsible-gaming, addiction treatment, and player safeguards
topics.summary: Members questioned PAGCOR about advertising clearance, influencer regulation, illegal foreign operators, and protections for vulnerable online gamblers. PAGCOR described a 24/7 helpline and responsible-gaming programs with the Seagulls Flock Foundation, supported in part by 1% of online gross gaming revenue, or about a billion pesos per annum. The agency said it used KYC and secondary screening to exclude government employees and maintained a restricted-persons list of 15,000 names, while online deposit and activity caps had not yet been set. Vice Chair Brian Poe raised the reopening of illegal sites, cited about 3,000,000,000,000 pesos in estimated annual wagers, and sought enforcement and program-funding documents. PAGCOR committed to continue the helpline and submit responsible-gaming information, while the chair directed that equipment and enforcement questions also be taken up during the ICT budget deliberation.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish how PAGCOR regulated online gambling and advertising, protected vulnerable players, and funded or operated responsible-gaming, counseling, rehabilitation, and player-exclusion programs. Members also examined enforcement against illegal operators and the safeguards available to minors, government employees, and low-income earners.
topics.agency_position: PAGCOR said it operated responsible-gaming programs through a 24/7 helpline, the Seagulls Flock Foundation, counseling and rehabilitation referrals, prevention and awareness activities, and self- or family-exclusion mechanisms. It said KYC and secondary screening were used to exclude government employees and other restricted players, while enforcement against illegal operators depended substantially on DICT, CICC, NTC, and other agencies with police powers. PAGCOR had not yet established online betting or deposit caps but expected proposed legislation to provide them.
topics.outcome: PAGCOR answered the committee's questions on existing safeguards and responsible-gaming services, but online caps and the adequacy of funding and technical enforcement remained dependent on proposed legislation, interagency action, and requested submissions. PAGCOR committed to continue the helpline and responsible-gaming programs and to provide program information; the committee deferred broader enforcement and equipment-funding questions to the ICT budget deliberation.

positions.position: Advertising by gambling operators and influencers needed effective clearance and regulation because online gambling was accessible to low-income earners and could be addictive.
Gambling should be treated as a public-health concern, with sustained funding for counseling, prevention, awareness, and rehabilitation.
Illegal gambling sites and untracked wagers were depriving the government of potential revenue, and enforcement technology and mental-health programs should be strengthened.
Online gambling required player caps, effective screening of government employees, and mechanisms to permanently exclude problem gamblers.
PAGCOR needed stringent technical safeguards to protect minors, government employees, low-income earners, and 4Ps beneficiaries from accessible online gambling.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR chairman Alejandro Tengco
thread.said: The chairman replied that online players were screened through the KYC process, which required identification and occupation information. He described the process as very strict, although the transcript's reference to a percentage was unclear.

thread.speaker: Rep. Mica Gonzales
thread.said: Rep. Gonzales asked whether players could be permanently blocked from entering casinos or playing on online platforms.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR chairman Alejandro Tengco
thread.said: The chairman said PAGCOR's restricted-persons list contained 15,000 names. Those persons could not enter casinos or play on online platforms, and the restrictions could arise from self-exclusion or family-exclusion requests.

thread.speaker: Rep. Sherlyn Bañas-Nograles

thread.speaker: PAGCOR chairman Alejandro Tengco
thread.said: The chairman said the principal safeguard was KYC: players had to present a valid government ID and provide information that could identify government employees. He added that legal operators composed 50% of the total industry.

topics.topic: Casino Filipino employee transition, retirement, and incentive packages
topics.summary: Bong Thebes Jinger and Jan Attorney Jan Rurik Padiernos raised the status of Casino Filipino privatization and the safeguards for approximately 10,000 employees across about 40 properties. PAGCOR said affected employees would receive regular retirement benefits plus a special incentive package, while acquiring entities would absorb employees where feasible. PAGCOR reported 5,000 completed training initiatives, initial Civil Service-related training for about 80 to 100 people, and a target of about 10,000 training initiatives by year-end. Roberto Nazal Jr. asked whether the 50% UHC earmark would continue after PAGCOR ceased operating casinos and requested projected contributions and a possible stabilization fund. PAGCOR said it had remitted 50,000,000,000 pesos to the national treasury in 2025, implying 25,000,000,000 should have gone to the UHC Fund, but it did not control the national government's onward remittance. The chairman estimated retirement needs at about 28 billion to 30 billion, an existing retirement fund of about 12 billion, and privatization proceeds of about 25 billion to 30 billion, while prioritizing employee retirement before any UHC fund. PAGCOR committed to provide the requested computations and documents within forty eight hours, leaving absorption rules and the UHC stabilization mechanism open.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish how Casino Filipino privatization would protect approximately 10,000 employees through absorption, training, retirement, and special incentive packages. It also sought to determine how privatization would affect the Universal Health Care earmark and whether PAGCOR or the Executive would provide transition funding or projected remittance figures.
topics.agency_position: PAGCOR said employee protection would rely on regular retirement benefits, a separate special incentive package, absorption by acquiring entities where feasible, and training and Civil Service Commission transition programs. It said retirement costs would take priority over any UHC stabilization fund, but that PAGCOR would provide internal projections and study whether residual privatization proceeds could support such a fund.
topics.outcome: PAGCOR answered the employee-protection questions by identifying retirement, special incentive, training, and CSC-transition measures, but the final absorption requirement and privatization decision remained pending. The UHC impact and possible stabilization fund were not resolved; PAGCOR undertook to submit computations and documents within forty eight hours and to study the use of residual proceeds.

positions.position: He emphasized protecting approximately 10,000 regular and contractual employees and asked PAGCOR to weigh an employee-absorption requirement against the goal of maximizing privatization proceeds.
He sought a clear legal and financial guarantee that the UHC and PhilHealth earmark would be protected after privatization, including consideration of a transition stabilization fund.
He sought the status of privatization and elicited PAGCOR's position that involuntary retirements required a special incentive package in addition to regular retirement benefits.
He stated that protecting affected employees through retirement benefits and the special incentive package was PAGCOR's priority before considering residual proceeds for UHC support.

thread.speaker: Bong Thebes Jinger
thread.said: He asked about the status of the Casino Filipino privatization initiatives and the related revenue implications.

thread.speaker: a PAGCOR official
thread.said: The official said the matter was awaiting a decision by the Governance Commission for GOCCs (GCG), expected in the last quarter of this year, and that PAGCOR was waiting for the GCG recommendation to the Office of the President.

thread.speaker: a PAGCOR official
thread.said: The official said PAGCOR was considering the regular retirement package and a special incentive package because the retirements would be involuntary, separate from the normal retirement package.

thread.speaker: Jan Attorney Jan Rurik Padiernos
thread.said: He asked what safeguards PAGCOR planned against displacement and mass layoffs if about 40 Casino Filipino properties were privatized, potentially affecting approximately 10,000 regular and contractual employees. He raised a proposed 50% to 70% employee-absorption requirement and asked whether this would reduce bids, given the choice between maximizing proceeds and protecting existing jobs.

thread.speaker: Alejandro Tengco
thread.said: The PAGCOR chairman said the agency would begin with the regular retirement package and add a special incentive package. He said buyers would absorb whoever they could absorb, with continuity of business making employee absorption on new terms the most logical approach.

thread.speaker: Alejandro Tengco
thread.said: He said PAGCOR had started programs to mitigate employee anxiety and asked its vice president for human resources to describe the measures already being implemented.

thread.speaker: Lito Domingo
thread.said: The vice president for human resources said PAGCOR had four training categories, including management, self-development, and personality-development training, and had concluded 5,000 training initiatives for individuals, including programs lasting two to five days.

thread.speaker: Lito Domingo
thread.said: He said PAGCOR was expanding specialized gaming training, including dealer cross-training for slot machines, to improve employees' ability to work for integrated resorts or acquiring entities.

thread.speaker: Lito Domingo
thread.said: He said PAGCOR was aligning with the Civil Service Commission and had conducted initial training for about 80 to 100 people in the previous two months. Almost 12 had registered for an examination, and PAGCOR was requesting an exemption to permit an online examination.

thread.speaker: Lito Domingo
thread.said: He said PAGCOR was developing an in-house program through which the CSC would provide vacancies at other government entities for affected employees to apply for. He expected PAGCOR to complete about 10,000 training initiatives by year-end and further strengthen its CSC initiatives.

thread.speaker: Roberto Nazal Jr.
thread.said: He asked how privatization would affect the Universal Health Care earmark under Section 37 of the UHC Act, under which 50% of the national government's share from PAGCOR income is earmarked for PhilHealth. He asked whether the base would continue to include regulatory fees and license-fee shares from private casinos, e-games, and other licensees, and requested projected PAGCOR contributions for 2026, 2027, 2028, and the first full year after privatization.

thread.speaker: Alejandro Tengco
thread.said: The chairman referred to the GCG and its role in the decoupling and privatization process, noting that the GCG commission secretary, the Secretary of Finance, and the DBM Secretary were involved in the governance structure.

thread.speaker: Alejandro Tengco
thread.said: He said PAGCOR's properties generated rental costs of 1,500,000,000 pesos a month and maintained a contribution of a minimum of 50% of net profit, which he said could neutralize revenue adjustments over the longer term.

thread.speaker: Alejandro Tengco
thread.said: He clarified that PAGCOR remitted its share to the national government, while the national government was responsible for remitting 50% of that amount to PhilHealth or the Universal Health Care Fund. PAGCOR did not control whether the national government completed the onward remittance.

thread.speaker: Roberto Nazal Jr.
thread.said: He pressed the chairman on whether PAGCOR had figures for the amount actually remitted to PhilHealth.

thread.speaker: Alejandro Tengco
thread.said: He said PAGCOR did have figures for its own remittances, but not control over the subsequent remittance. For 2025, PAGCOR had remitted more or less 50,000,000,000 pesos to the national treasury, which under the law meant 25,000,000,000 should have been remitted by the national government to the Universal Health Care Fund.

thread.speaker: Roberto Nazal Jr.
thread.said: He asked whether Congress needed to legislate a guarantee for the UHC share after privatization, including a possible stabilization fund sourced directly from privatization proceeds.

thread.speaker: Alejandro Tengco
thread.said: The chairman said PAGCOR would forward its internal computations to the committee, while making clear that projections after decoupling and privatization would be involved.

thread.speaker: Alejandro Tengco
thread.said: He said PAGCOR could examine a transition mechanism for the UHC share, but the priority use of privatization proceeds was the retirement of affected employees. He described the retirement benefits and special incentive package as a commitment to protect PAGCOR employees.

thread.speaker: Alejandro Tengco
thread.said: In response to a question on retirement costs, he estimated the amount needed for retirement at about 28,000,000,000 to 30,000,000,000, with about 12,000,000,000 available to be subsidized from the sale.

thread.speaker: a committee member
thread.said: The member asked for the expected windfall from the privatization.

thread.speaker: Alejandro Tengco
thread.said: He estimated the privatization proceeds at about 25,000,000,000 to 30,000,000,000. He said PAGCOR had a current retirement fund of about 12,000,000,000 pesos in cash in the bank.

thread.speaker: Alejandro Tengco
thread.said: He said any remaining amount after retirement benefits and other privatization expenses would normally become extraordinary income, from which PAGCOR would remit 50% to the national treasury. He agreed to look into whether the remaining proceeds could support a UHC stabilization fund.

thread.speaker: Alejandro Tengco
thread.said: He committed that the requested documents would be delivered within forty eight hours.

thread.speaker: Chair Alt Enco
thread.said: The chair stated that, as committed by the PAGCOR chairman, all documentary requirements would be provided within forty eight hours after the hearing.

topics.topic: Integrated resorts, gaming service administrators, and PAGCOR’s mandate
topics.summary: Rep. Presley de Jesus asked PAGCOR to define integrated resorts and explain the consequences for other casinos as the sector developed. PAGCOR cited a minimum investment of at least 1,000,000,000 US dollars for an integrated resort, a lowest category of 100,000,000 US dollars, and a license-fee range of 25 to 30 percent; the member described the billion-dollar threshold as around 60 billion in local currency. The member also questioned whether privatization would separate PAGCOR’s operator and regulator roles, but the agency’s response was unclear. On penalties, PAGCOR said the cited first-offense penalty was not the maximum: repeat violations could lead to suspension and then cancellation, with the prior 50,000 penalty calibrated to 1 million. PAGCOR said GSAs had fallen from 74 at their peak to 48, largely because operators surrendered after losing money, and it cited a 9,000,000 pesos minimum guarantee fee effective July 1, 2026. The agency confirmed that casino and online gaming were within PAGCOR’s mandate, while horse racing was under the Philippine Racing Commission; the operator-regulator transition and some financial figures remained unresolved.
topics.question: The committee sought to clarify what qualifies as an integrated resort, how casino privatization would affect PAGCOR’s operator-regulator role, and how penalties and gaming service administrator rules would work. It also asked how many gaming service administrators remained, why some surrendered their licenses, and which games fell within PAGCOR’s mandate.
topics.agency_position: PAGCOR stated that integrated resorts were investment-based classifications, with the highest category requiring at least 1,000,000,000 US dollars and the lowest cited at 100,000,000 US dollars. It said GSAs were licensed online gaming operators, that their number had declined because of suspensions and business losses, and that a minimum guarantee fee was intended to stabilize the online gaming industry. PAGCOR also maintained that its mandate covered casino and online gaming but not horse racing, which was assigned to the Philippine Racing Commission.
topics.outcome: The agency answered the definitional, penalty, GSA-count, fee, and mandate questions, but did not provide a clear answer on the operator-regulator transition or assure the committee about the remaining operators. The discussion ended without a recorded document request or further resolution of the privatization issue.

positions.position: He sought clarification on the meaning and investment thresholds of integrated resorts, the consequences of casino privatization, the adequacy and escalation of penalties, the decline in GSAs, and the limits of PAGCOR’s gaming mandate.
The official supported investment-based resort classifications, escalating penalties for repeat violations, the minimum guarantee fee, and PAGCOR’s regulatory coverage of casino and online gaming.

topics.topic: Online-gambling limits, KYC, and government-employee screening
topics.summary: Rep. Jan Rurik Padiernos raised concerns about e-wallet restrictions, illegal payment aggregators, declining e-games revenues, and KYC bypasses involving mule accounts and minors. PAGCOR said it was coordinating with the central bank, enforcing KYC and sanctions, and considering a PAGCOR app, while citing more than 106 billion in revenues and other public-purpose allocations. Rep. Michael Gonzalez asked about daily or weekly online-gambling caps, government-employee screening, and permanent player bans; PAGCOR said caps had not yet been set but were expected in proposed legislation, while KYC and screening had prevented close to 5 billion in winnings and covered a restricted list of 15,000 names. Rep. Sherlyn Banas-Nograles asked for stronger safeguards for minors, government employees, low-income earners, and vulnerable sectors, including people affected by micro-bets. PAGCOR identified KYC as its safeguard and said it had provided more than 100,000 relief packs and was constructing 125 school buildings equivalent to about 200 classrooms. The committee left specific General Santos classroom assistance to a written request, while the broader cap issue remained dependent on proposed legislation.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish how PAGCOR was controlling online-gambling access and risks, including e-wallet use, illegal operators, KYC compliance, wager or deposit limits, government-employee participation, and exclusion of vulnerable or prohibited players. Members also asked what safeguards and assistance programs PAGCOR maintained for affected communities.
topics.agency_position: PAGCOR said it was enforcing KYC, secondary screening, fines, suspensions, payment-provider controls, and exclusion lists to prevent prohibited or vulnerable persons from accessing gambling. It acknowledged that player caps had not yet been set but said proposed online-gaming legislation was expected to include deposit and gaming-activity caps.
topics.outcome: PAGCOR answered that KYC, screening, exclusion lists, and sanctions were in place, but acknowledged that online deposit and gaming-activity caps had not yet been established. Further assistance for General Santos classroom reconstruction was left to a written request and was not specifically confirmed.

positions.position: Supported tighter controls on e-wallets, payment aggregators, KYC compliance, proxy accounts, third-party funding, and minor access, while commending PAGCOR's revenue and assistance programs.
Advocated limits on online gambling and stronger mechanisms to prevent government employees from gambling and to exclude prohibited or self-excluded players.
Pressed for stringent safeguards for minors, government employees, low-income earners, and other vulnerable sectors, and sought PAGCOR assistance for disaster relief and damaged classrooms.

thread.said: Rep. Michael Gonzalez asked what mechanism ensured that government employees, who were not allowed to play in casinos, could not participate in online gaming.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR chairman Alejandro Tengco
thread.said: The PAGCOR official said the agency strictly implemented the KYC process and secondary screening. He stated that the process had prevented government employees from receiving winnings and that close to COP 5,000,000,000 worth of winnings had been avoided in the last two years.

thread.speaker: Rep. Michael Gonzalez
thread.said: Rep. Michael Gonzalez clarified that he was asking specifically about online gaming, including access through mechanisms such as Facebook advertisements, and whether PAGCOR could determine that a player was a government employee.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR chairman Alejandro Tengco
thread.said: He answered that online and land-based players were subject to KYC. The process required identification and occupation information, and he described online KYC enforcement as very strict, with the transcript rendering one percentage reference as “90s in percentage.”

thread.speaker: Rep. Michael Gonzalez
thread.said: Rep. Michael Gonzalez asked whether PAGCOR permanently blocked players from casinos or online platforms, including through self-exclusion or other player-restriction mechanisms.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR chairman Alejandro Tengco
thread.said: The PAGCOR official said the agency had a list containing 15,000 names of people not allowed to enter casinos or play on online-gaming platforms. He cited self-exclusion and family-exclusion programs and said the bans could remain for years.

thread.speaker: Rep. Sherlyn Banas-Nograles
thread.said: Rep. Sherlyn Banas-Nograles asked what stringent technical protocols licensees were required to use to prevent minors, government employees, low-income earners, and vulnerable sectors from gambling online. She specifically noted micro-bets of 1 peso to 5 pesos and the potential effect on 4Ps beneficiaries.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR chairman Alejandro Tengco
thread.said: He identified KYC as the stringent measure, saying a person could not readily register as a regular online-gaming customer without completing KYC. He said applicants had to present a valid government ID and that the process addressed whether a player was a government employee.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR chairman Alejandro Tengco
thread.said: The PAGCOR official said legal operators composed 50% of the total industry.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR chairman Alejandro Tengco
thread.said: On General Santos relief, he said PAGCOR had provided financial and relief packages, coordinated with the Office of Civil Defense, and provided airlift support. He invited members to submit a letter requesting assistance.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR chairman Alejandro Tengco
thread.said: He said PAGCOR had sent out more than a 100,000 relief packs all over the Philippines in the last week and a half and would respond to written requests to the best of its ability.

thread.speaker: Rep. Sherlyn Banas-Nograles
thread.said: Rep. Sherlyn Banas-Nograles asked whether PAGCOR could also help reconstruct classrooms damaged by the earthquake in General Santos City.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR chairman Alejandro Tengco
thread.said: He said PAGCOR had a program for the construction of 125 new school buildings, equivalent to about a 200 classrooms. He did not expressly confirm a specific commitment for the damaged General Santos classrooms.

thread.speaker: Rep. Sherlyn Banas-Nograles
thread.said: Rep. Sherlyn Banas-Nograles said she and her colleagues would write PAGCOR regarding assistance for classroom construction.

topics.topic: Infrastructure, hospital, cancer-center, and special-needs-school assistance
topics.summary: Rep. Iris Marie Montes questioned PAGCOR's UHC remittances, privatization proceeds, and infrastructure priorities, and PAGCOR undertook to submit a remittance listing within 48 hours. PAGCOR said it was current with National Treasury remittances and estimated possible privatization proceeds at about 20 billion to 30 billion, while the detailed PhilHealth treatment of those proceeds remained partly unclear. Rep. Jean Baronda sought support for cancer-center equipment and schools serving children with special needs, and PAGCOR said it would seriously consider those requests. Rep. Shirlyn Bañas-Nograles asked about General Santos relief and roughly 1,400 damaged classrooms; PAGCOR cited more than 100,000 relief packs and a program for 125 new school buildings. Rep. Marco Wangkol sought help for a Pangasinan hospital project estimated at about 1 billion, but PAGCOR advised that equipment for a completed building was more feasible than partial construction funding. The requests landed as conditional commitments requiring follow-up letters, coordination, and project completion.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish whether PAGCOR was complying with its Universal Health Care remittance obligations and whether its social funds, infrastructure programs, and affiliated foundations could support hospitals, cancer-center equipment, damaged classrooms, and schools serving children with special needs. Members also sought to identify the process and conditions for obtaining such assistance, including for a Pangasinan hospital project.
topics.agency_position: PAGCOR said it was current on its National Treasury remittances, while the national government—not PAGCOR directly—remitted the applicable share to PhilHealth. It said hospital construction was generally handled by licensee foundations, but PAGCOR could provide equipment or other targeted assistance on a case-by-case basis, subject to project completion and liquidation requirements; it also committed to consider cancer-center, special-needs-school, classroom, and Pangasinan hospital-equipment requests.
topics.outcome: PAGCOR answered the principal questions and made several conditional commitments, but most project assistance remained subject to letters, coordination, project completion, and liquidation. The remittance report, cancer-center assistance, special-needs support, classroom support, and Pangasinan equipment assistance were not yet finally delivered or approved during the hearing.

positions.position: Supported verifying PAGCOR's UHC remittances and urged a possible rebalancing of PAGCOR infrastructure priorities to include wellness centers, evacuation centers, and other projects.
Supported continued PAGCOR assistance for Universal Health Care, cancer-center equipment at Western Visayas Medical Center, and schools and equipment for children with special needs.
Sought PAGCOR relief and classroom-construction assistance for General Santos City and its damaged classrooms.
Sought PAGCOR assistance to reduce DOH's burden for a Pangasinan hospital project, ultimately accepting equipment assistance as a practical alternative.

thread.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Montes
thread.said: She asked whether PAGCOR had complied with the Universal Healthcare Act provision requiring remittances for the National Treasury for UHC and PhilHealth.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR chairman and CEO Alejandro Tengco
thread.said: He said PAGCOR had regularly remitted its share to the national government and that PAGCOR was not responsible for remitting directly to PhilHealth; the national government makes the PhilHealth remittance.

thread.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Montes
thread.said: She summarized the handout figures, stating that 50% of the government share for 2023 was 34,600,000,000, with half or 17.3 going to the National Treasury for PhilHealth; for 2024, she cited '46' and 23.1, and for 2025, 45 and 22.5.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR chairman and CEO Alejandro Tengco

thread.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Montes

thread.speaker: PAGCOR chairman and CEO Alejandro Tengco
thread.said: He said PAGCOR was awaiting the Governance Commission for GOCCs' recommendation to the Office of the President. If approved, close to about 30 Casino Filipino properties would be privatized, with proceeds currently estimated at 20,000,000,000 to 30,000,000,000, subject to valuation.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR chairman and CEO Alejandro Tengco
thread.said: He said PAGCOR could commit only to disposing of the properties at the best possible price, noting that the current revenue situation could lower the valuation.

thread.speaker: Rep. Iris Marie Montes
thread.said: She followed up on whether PhilHealth would still receive its 50% share from privatization proceeds.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR chairman and CEO Alejandro Tengco
thread.said: He indicated that the national government would receive the privatization proceeds, including amounts needed for employee retirement costs, while the 50% PhilHealth share would continue in the medium term. Parts of this answer were unclear in the transcript.

thread.said: She asked whether PAGCOR's flagship projects—school buildings, e-learning centers, community wellness centers, social civic centers, and evacuation centers—formed part of the 2024 joint memorandum framework.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR chairman and CEO Alejandro Tengco
thread.said: He said PAGCOR remained committed to reaching as many Filipinos as possible and would make adjustments to preserve its financial health and the Universal Health Care fund. The detailed response was largely unclear in the transcript.

thread.said: She said PAGCOR and a foundation had helped expand Western Visayas Medical Center's bed capacity from 420 to 700 and construct a children's hospital, then asked for help equipping its cancer center and for assistance in liaising with the Integrated Resource Foundation.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR chairman and CEO Alejandro Tengco
thread.said: He indicated that support for medical equipment to expand specialty hospitals could be considered, although the remainder of his response was unclear.

thread.speaker: PAGCOR chairman and CEO Alejandro Tengco
thread.said: He called the proposal laudable and said it would be considered as an agenda item in PAGCOR's meeting with former congresswoman Aguinaldo.
