thread.said: He asked whether the Department of Finance opposed any discussion of removing or reducing VAT on electricity.

thread.speaker: Secretary Frederic Goh
thread.said: Secretary Goh said DOF was neutral if VAT removal were paired with another tax or revenue source, but would oppose removing a tax without replacement revenue.

thread.speaker: Rep. Elijah San Fernando
thread.said: He raised fragmented coordination and implementation as factors affecting energy costs and asked whether the DEPDev Secretary agreed.

thread.speaker: Secretary of DEPDev
thread.said: The Secretary agreed that weak coordination, including between national and local governments, could delay projects and impair efficient implementation.

thread.speaker: Rep. Elijah San Fernando
thread.said: He asked how the government would use the remaining two years of the PBBM administration to create quality jobs and pursue industrial policy while addressing high energy costs.

thread.speaker: Secretary of DEPDev
thread.said: The Secretary disagreed that the government lacked ambition and cited the Philippine development plan's long-term ambition. He said industrial policy could work, but basic structural problems had to be addressed, especially high energy costs, roads, connectivity, and Internet access.

thread.speaker: Rep. Elijah San Fernando
thread.said: He pushed back that industrial policy and structural reforms could be pursued simultaneously, and criticized what he viewed as a defeatist approach while manufacturing and industrial jobs had declined.

thread.speaker: An executive economic official
thread.said: The official referred the committee to the Philippine development plan and its update, arguing that the evidence showed substantial progress over the last fifteen years and that sustaining momentum, rather than dismissing the government's record, was the appropriate focus.

thread.speaker: Senior Deputy Speaker Ferdinand Hernandez
thread.said: He asked the DOF and BIR for their position on removing VAT from system loss, arguing that electricity lost before reaching consumers was not consumed and should not be taxed as delivered electricity. He said a new rule or regulation might be sufficient without legislation.

thread.speaker: BIR Commissioner Charlie Mendoza
thread.said: Commissioner Mendoza said the BIR had issued a revenue memorandum circular exempting certain mandated pass-through charges, including the Green Energy Auction Allowance and Lifeline Subsidy. He explained that system-loss charges were currently bundled into distributors' gross sales, making them part of the VAT base.

thread.speaker: BIR Commissioner Charlie Mendoza
thread.said: Commissioner Mendoza said the BIR was working with the ERC and that the ERC had a draft regulation addressing the issue, which was expected to undergo public consultation the following week.

thread.speaker: The Chair
thread.said: The Chair said the BIR and ERC should coordinate on a new list of chargeable and exempt items and noted that the issue appeared capable of resolution without legislation.

thread.speaker: The Chair
thread.said: The Chair said the committee had already met with the Commissioner and ERC and hoped the system-loss VAT issue would be resolved soon.

topics.topic: Revenue measures, tax exemptions, and proposed new taxes
topics.summary: Rep. Iris Marie Montes established that the PhilHealth subsidy was tied to the sin-tax allocation, while Rep. Percival Sindania pressed officials on falling revenue forecasts and the fiscal cost of tax exemptions or reductions. Officials said the Progress bill included personal-income-tax and MCIT relief alongside eight revenue-enhancing measures intended to offset the lost revenue. The effective VAT rate was described as about 6% despite a statutory rate of 12% because of exemptions. Minority Representative Sarah Elago raised additional taxes on tobacco, plastics, sweetened beverages, alcohol, luxury assets, and billionaires; the last proposal was left for internal study. Senior Deputy Speaker Ferdinand Hernandez argued that electricity system loss should not be subject to VAT, and the BIR said it was working with the ERC on draft regulations and public consultation. The committee directed the DBCC to submit several fiscal and revenue reconciliations, while the system-loss issue remained under agency action.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish whether proposed tax exemptions, tax reductions, and new revenue measures were fiscally sustainable and whether replacement revenues had been identified. Members also asked how revenue assumptions, tax reforms, and VAT treatment would affect public services, taxpayers, and fiscal consolidation.
topics.agency_position: The agency position was that tax removals or exemptions should proceed only when replacement revenues were identified, because the proposed national budget had to be funded. Officials said the Progress bill paired revenue-eroding relief measures with eight revenue-enhancing measures, while the BIR and ERC were pursuing a regulatory solution to VAT on electricity system loss rather than relying necessarily on new legislation.
topics.outcome: Officials maintained that tax relief or tax removal required replacement revenue, while the Progress bill was presented as pairing exemptions with new revenue measures. The billionaires-tax proposal remained for internal study, and VAT on electricity system loss remained under BIR-ERC regulatory work rather than being resolved during the hearing.

positions.position: Pressed for clarity on whether PhilHealth's national-budget subsidy was funded through sin-tax collections and whether additional national funding would be available.
Sought credible revenue assumptions and replacement funding for tax exemptions or reductions, including possible VAT reduction or a wealth tax.
Supported examining tax relief alongside revenue-generating reforms affecting tobacco, plastics, sweetened beverages, alcohol, luxury assets, and high-income taxpayers.
Supported removing VAT from electricity system loss because consumers were being taxed on electricity not actually consumed, preferably through rules and regulations rather than legislation.

topics.topic: Tourism Development and Tourism Promotions Fund balances
topics.summary: Dette Escudero asked DBM how the Tourism Development Fund and Tourism Promotions Fund could be accessed and requested their balances, releases, obligations, and unreleased balances for at least three years. DBM said agencies had to submit special budget requests and that it programmed only the portion of special-account balances agencies could use during the fiscal year. The DBM official said the 2027 Tourism Promotions Fund program expenditure was 1,119,000,000, compared with PHP 1.339 in 2026, while Escudero cited a decline from 19.3% to 16.1% of total collections. DBM attributed the reduction to utilization data and 2026 commitments for one-off ASEAN-hosting activities. Escudero sought a more efficient, potentially uniform risk-based access mechanism, and DBM committed to work with her and share the basis for the programmed levels. The requested historical balance and release data remained unprovided in the excerpt.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish how the Tourism Development Fund and Tourism Promotions Fund were accessed, including their actual balances, releases, obligations, and unreleased balances over at least three years. It also asked why the proposed 2027 programming for tourism promotions differed from the 2026 amount and whether DBM's fiscal-programming process imposed an additional layer of approval.
topics.agency_position: DBM maintained that special accounts in the general fund were automatically appropriated but could be used only after submission of a special budget request and DBM fiscal programming. It said the 2027 Tourism Promotions Fund level reflected available data, 2026 utilization, and the one-off ASEAN-hosting activities, and offered to share the basis for the programmed levels.
topics.outcome: DBM explained the fiscal-programming and special-budget-request process and identified the 2027 Tourism Promotions Fund program expenditure as 1,119,000,000, attributing the reduction to utilization data and one-off ASEAN-hosting activities. The requested three-year fund balance and release data were not provided in the excerpt, while DBM committed to further work and to sharing its basis for the funding levels.

positions.position: Escudero sought more efficient access to earmarked tourism funds, questioned the lower 2027 programming, and proposed examining a uniform risk-based mechanism for special accounts while retaining fiscal and audit safeguards.

The DBM official defended fiscal programming as necessary to align releases with agency spending capacity and avoid contributing to a higher deficit, while expressing willingness to work with the committee.

thread.said: The DBM official said that use of any special account in the general fund required the agency to submit a special budget request. thread.speaker: DBM official

He explained that this fiscal programming avoided increasing the deficit by preventing programming beyond an agency's needs or spending capacity, and offered to share DBM's basis for the tourism funding levels.

topics.topic: Creative-industries digital VAT earmark
topics.summary: Representative Javi Benitez raised the gap between the creative economy's reported scale and proposed cultural-agency budgets, then pressed the agencies to implement the statutory 5% digital-VAT earmark. He cited BIR-certified collections of about 6.36 billion for August to December 2025 and a creative-industries share reported at about 318.08 million, although parts of the certification were unclear in the transcript. The DOF official confirmed 318,000,000 for the cited period and gave a running figure of 5% of 9,400,000,000, without fully explaining the calculation. Benitez asked whether a special account had been created and whether the share would flow as automatic appropriations. DBM Secretary Kim said the agencies were establishing the UACS code and would consult with DOF and other agencies on the proper booking and fund arrangement. The chair ended the exchange by saying the committee would monitor creation of the fund, leaving the automatic-appropriation issue unresolved.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish whether the statutory 5% share of incremental digital VAT collections had been collected, accounted for, and earmarked for the creative industries. It also sought commitments on the creation of the special account and whether the funds would be treated as automatic appropriations or require annual appropriations.
topics.agency_position: The agencies confirmed a 2025 creative-industries share of 318,000,000, while the DOF official stated a running figure of 5% of 9,400,000,000 without elaboration. DBM said it was working with DTI, DOF, and other agencies to establish the UACS coding and finalize the proper booking and arrangement of the Creative Industry Development Fund, but did not definitively resolve whether the share would be automatic appropriations.
topics.outcome: The agencies acknowledged the cited 2025 share and committed to work on the account, UACS coding, and legal and accounting treatment of the fund. Whether the share would be automatically appropriated and the complete current collections figure remained unresolved, subject to interagency finalization and committee monitoring.

positions.position: The statutory 5% digital-VAT share should be collected, placed in a properly established special account, and fully reflected for creative-industry development, whether as automatic appropriations or under another legally appropriate mechanism.
The committee would monitor the agencies' creation of the fund.

topics.topic: Negros Island regional offices, plantilla positions, and funding
topics.summary: Deputy Speaker Chedeng Alvarez raised concerns that, more than two years after Republic Act 12,000 was signed, the Negros Island regional structure still lacked fully established offices, staffing, vehicles, and funding. DBM said it had prioritized the region and reported that 30 agencies had approved plantilla positions and offices as of 07/28/2026, with eight additional requests under evaluation. Alvarez questioned whether delays came from central or regional offices, and DBM said requests had to be endorsed by agency heads at the central office. BLGF reported an interim head, vehicles, proposed funding, and consideration of a Dumaguete City satellite office, while the Bureau of the Treasury said it would review the regional-office proposal. Alvarez requested budget and staffing breakdowns and a definite implementation timeline, and DBM committed to submit them through the committee within one week. The matter therefore landed as a commitment, with several organizational and funding issues still unresolved.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish why Negros Island regional offices, plantilla positions, vehicles, and funding remained at different stages of evaluation or approval, and whether delays originated with agency central offices or regional offices. It also sought the status of staffing and the timeline for fully operationalizing the Negros Island region.
topics.agency_position: DBM said it had prioritized proposals supporting the establishment of Negros Island regional offices, including offices, vehicles, equipment, and staffing, and said 30 national government agencies had approved plantilla positions and offices as of 07/28/2026, with eight additional requests under evaluation. BLGF said it had an interim head, vehicles, and proposed funding, while the Bureau of the Treasury said it would review the creation of a regional office because of its budget and organizational implications.

thread.speaker: Deputy Speaker Chedeng Alvarez
thread.said: Alvarez said he was one of the principal authors of Republic Act 12,000, which created the Negros Island region and was signed in June 2024. More than two years later, residents of Negros Occidental, Negros Oriental, and Siquijor were awaiting a fully functional and funded regional structure.

thread.speaker: Deputy Speaker Chedeng Alvarez
thread.said: He asked whether the agencies already had offices in the Negros Island region or were still relying on LGU facilities, and whether they had vehicles and complete staffs. He asked why regional offices and plantilla positions remained at varying stages of evaluation, finalization, and approval, and why some proposed 2027 budgets had reportedly been reduced.

thread.speaker: DBM Secretary Kim De Leon
thread.said: De Leon said DBM had given higher priority to agency proposals supporting the establishment of Negros Island regional offices. DBM prioritized basic operating needs such as office setup or rent, vehicles, and necessary office equipment, and said the 2027 regional allocation for Negros Island was higher than allocations for other regions.

thread.speaker: DBM Secretary Kim De Leon
thread.said: On plantilla approval, De Leon said there was no one-size-fits-all formula for the structure and staffing of each agency. Agency-specific proposals were being evaluated against available personnel funding.

thread.speaker: DBM Secretary Kim De Leon
thread.said: De Leon reported that, as of 07/28/2026, 30 national government agencies had approved plantilla positions and offices for their Negros Island regional offices. DBM had also received requests from an additional eight agencies that it was evaluating.

thread.speaker: DBM Secretary Kim De Leon
thread.said: De Leon said the requests were being given priority and assured the committee that the remaining Negros Island regional-office position requests would be acted upon before the end of the year.

thread.speaker: Deputy Speaker Chedeng Alvarez
thread.said: Alvarez asked where the staffing and office proposals originated—whether from the regional offices or the agencies' central offices. He noted that information available to him had shown only 25 out of 30 agencies completed as of June of that year.

thread.speaker: DBM Secretary Kim De Leon
thread.said: De Leon said that, as a matter of procedure, all requests had to be endorsed by the head of the agency from the central office.

thread.speaker: Deputy Speaker Chedeng Alvarez
thread.said: Alvarez cited the Bureau of Local Government Finance and the Bureau of the Treasury as agencies that had reportedly not yet submitted proposals. He asked whether the delay came from the regional offices or the central offices and requested that the Department of Finance address the issue.

thread.speaker: Secretary Goh
thread.said: Secretary Goh said the matter was new to him and undertook to speak with BLGF the following day to determine why it had not submitted its proposal.

thread.speaker: Deputy Speaker Chedeng Alvarez
thread.said: Alvarez reiterated that he wanted to identify the source of the delay, whether the central office or the regional office, and said he was concerned that other regions were receiving new vehicles while Negros Island regional staff continued to face deficiencies.

thread.speaker: Bureau of the Treasury official
thread.said: The Treasury official said the Bureau was considering the creation of a Negros Island regional office, although it already had provincial offices in the region. The Bureau would review and revisit the proposed creation because it would affect the Bureau's overall budget and organization.

thread.speaker: Deputy Speaker Chedeng Alvarez
thread.said: Alvarez said the issue involved not only budget implications but also service delivery, because LGUs dealt with BLGF and the Bureau of the Treasury on their concerns. He again asked where the delay originated.

thread.speaker: BLGF executive director
thread.said: The BLGF executive director said an interim head had already been designated for the Negros Island region, concurrently serving as the Region 6 regional director. BLGF was already providing vehicles and had proposed funding in its budget for establishing the regional office.

thread.speaker: BLGF executive director
thread.said: The BLGF official said the agency was considering a satellite office in Dumaguete City because of the distance between the proposed main office in Negros Occidental and Negros Oriental and Siquijor.

thread.speaker: Deputy Speaker Chedeng Alvarez
thread.said: Alvarez corrected the description of the geography, saying Negros Island was one main island and that Siquijor was about twenty minutes away. He welcomed the possible satellite office and invited departments to visit the region and consult their staff about operational needs.

thread.speaker: BLGF executive director
thread.said: The BLGF official said the agency had recently visited the Negros Island region and had discussed the issue with the mayor of Dumaguete City. The mayor was willing to provide free space for a BLGF satellite office, and the agency was considering that option.

thread.speaker: BLGF executive director
thread.said: The BLGF official said that once positions were filled, the agency hoped its regional office would normalize by next year.

thread.speaker: Deputy Speaker Chedeng Alvarez
thread.said: Alvarez asked whether the problem was the budget or the agencies' proposals, noting that DBM had indicated the regional structure would be fully functional before the end of the year while BLGF was referring to next year.

thread.speaker: BLGF executive director
thread.said: The BLGF official said the agency had submitted its proposal the previous year and believed the requests were being processed in phases.

thread.speaker: Deputy Speaker Chedeng Alvarez
thread.said: Alvarez requested a year-by-year breakdown for 2024, 2025, the present, and proposed 2027 budgets of all agencies, including PS, MOE, and capital outlay. He also requested the number of approved positions, the number funded and unfunded, and DBM's definite timeline for the full fiscal and organizational operation of the Negros Island region.

thread.speaker: DBM Secretary Kim De Leon
thread.said: De Leon agreed to comply with the requested submission.

thread.speaker: DBM Secretary Kim De Leon
thread.said: De Leon requested at least a week to collate the information and submit it to Alvarez through the Committee on Appropriations.

thread.speaker: Chair
thread.said: The chair asked whether the one-week period was acceptable, and Alvarez agreed.

thread.speaker: Chair
thread.said: The chair confirmed that the requested submission was expected within one week and said the DBM Secretary had guaranteed its delivery.

thread.speaker: Deputy Speaker Chedeng Alvarez
thread.said: Alvarez said he was relaying concerns raised by regional staff and emphasized that Republic Act 12,000 was intended to make services more convenient for constituents. He urged national-government prioritization, particularly in light of the recurring Mount Canlaon eruptions and problems in the sugarcane industry.

topics.topic: Military modernization and AFP unprogrammed funding
topics.summary: Congressman Arnan Panaligan asked DBM how much of the 50,000,000,000 unprogrammed AFP modernization appropriation had been released, noting the separate 40,000,000,000 regular appropriation. The DBM official referred to a release for the revised AFP modernization program but did not provide a clear amount or definitive release status in the transcript. Asked about a release before year-end, the official said it would depend on a trigger identified as excess revenue. Arnan Panaligan argued that naval modernization could help secure fisheries and possible oil and natural gas resources and should not be treated only as a fiscal burden. DBM agreed in principle and said it would evaluate the entire AFP request after receiving complete documentation. The release question remained open, with an agency evaluation committed.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish whether any portion of the 50,000,000,000 unprogrammed appropriation for the 2026 AFP modernization program had been released and whether a further release would occur before year-end. Congressman Arnan Panaligan also asked whether naval modernization should be viewed as an investment that could help secure and develop the country's maritime resources rather than solely as a fiscal burden.
topics.agency_position: DBM indicated that release of the unprogrammed appropriation for the revised AFP modernization program depended on a trigger identified as excess revenue. It also stated that the entire AFP request, including naval modernization, would be evaluated upon receipt of complete documentation.
topics.outcome: The DBM response did not disclose how much of the 50,000,000,000 unprogrammed appropriation had been released. A possible release before year-end was left dependent on the excess-revenue trigger and DBM evaluation of complete documentation.

positions.position: He regarded AFP and particularly naval modernization as potentially enabling the protection and development of maritime resources, and therefore as contributing to poverty reduction rather than merely imposing a financial burden.

topics.topic: FY2027 National Expenditure Program and budget priorities
topics.summary: The chair opened the FY2027 budget deliberations and reaffirmed transparency and public-participation reforms. DEPDEB Secretary Balisacan reported slower growth, labor-market deterioration, and poverty gains, and urged funding for vulnerable households, healthcare, education, infrastructure, skills, and food security. He cited growth of 2.6% in the first half of the year, a rise in unemployment to 4.2%, and a decline in poverty incidence to 9.7% in 2025. Acting DBM Secretary De Leon presented the proposed NEP at about 7.2 trillion, against agency requests of more than 11 trillion, emphasizing prioritization based on fiscal space and implementation capacity. Social services received about 2.46 trillion, infrastructure about 1.47 trillion, agriculture and food security about 261.7 billion, and DSWD about 241.6 billion. The presentation ended with DBM's commitment to transparent and disciplined budget execution, but no member questioning or resolution was recorded.
topics.question: The committee was establishing the framework, priorities, fiscal limits, and implementation basis of the proposed FY2027 National Expenditure Program (NEP). It also sought to understand how the proposed allocations would address slower growth, poverty, employment pressures, health and social services, infrastructure, and food security.
topics.agency_position: The executive branch, through DEPDEB and DBM, said the FY2027 budget should combine fiscal discipline with investments that restore growth, protect vulnerable households, strengthen health and social services, improve food security, and address implementation bottlenecks. DBM maintained that the 7,200,000,000,000 pesos NEP reflected deliberate prioritization within limited fiscal space and would emphasize implementation-ready programs.
topics.outcome: The committee received the executive branch's economic context and DBM's presentation of the proposed FY2027 NEP, including its fiscal framework and priority allocations. No member interpolation or contested issue on the topic occurred in the provided transcript.

positions.position: Supported a people-centered, transparent, participatory, and accountable budget process, with emphasis on education, healthcare, workforce upskilling, and inclusive and resilient growth.
Supported completing the DBCC presentations before opening interpolation and discussion.
Supported directing limited resources toward implementation-ready investments in social services, primary healthcare, food security, infrastructure, skills, and productivity-enhancing reforms.

positions.position: Supported a rules-based, fiscally disciplined NEP that prioritized agency readiness, absorptive capacity, measurable outcomes, regional delivery, and essential public services.

thread.speaker: Chair
thread.said: The chair formally opened deliberations on the proposed FY2027 national budget and highlighted reforms intended to make the budget process open, transparent, accountable, and participatory.

thread.speaker: House Speaker Faustino Bozziidi III
thread.said: The proposed budget was described as anchored on people-centered growth for an inclusive and resilient future, with priorities including quality education, healthcare, and workforce upskilling.

thread.speaker: House Speaker Faustino Bozziidi III
thread.said: The chair announced that the DBCC presentations would proceed in sequence—BSP, DEPDEB, DOF, and DBM—and requested that members allow all four presentations to finish before interpolation and discussion.

thread.speaker: DEPDEB Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
thread.said: Secretary Balisacan said the FY2027 budget should protect development gains, address structural bottlenecks, and restore faster, durable, and inclusive growth.

thread.speaker: DEPDEB Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
thread.said: He reported that real GDP grew by an average of 5.1% annually from 2010 to 2025, compared with 4.2% during the preceding fifteen years; growth averaged 5.8% from 2022 to 2025 but slowed to 2.6% in the first half of this year.

thread.speaker: DEPDEB Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
thread.said: He said post-pandemic expansion generated 4,000,000 net jobs between the first half of 2022 and the first half of 2026, but total employment declined by 166,000 in the past year and unemployment rose to 4.2% in June 2026 from 3.1% a year earlier.

thread.speaker: DEPDEB Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
thread.said: Preliminary 2025 estimates showed poverty incidence falling from 18.1% in 2021 to 9.7% in 2025, which he said meant 8,800,000 Filipinos were lifted out of poverty.

thread.speaker: DEPDEB Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
thread.said: Near-term priorities were to protect poor and low-income families from elevated food prices and supply disruptions, accelerate high-impact infrastructure through catch-up plans, restore confidence, and strengthen transparency and accountability.

thread.speaker: DEPDEB Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
thread.said: He identified implementation-ready investments in learning, classrooms, future-ready skills, primary healthcare in underserved areas, climate-resilient agriculture, post-harvest infrastructure, transport, logistics, energy, and digital infrastructure.

thread.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
thread.said: Secretary De Leon presented the FY2027 NEP as a prioritized spending plan rather than a compilation of agency requests, guided by presidential priorities, implementation readiness, absorptive capacity, past performance, project maturity, expected outcomes, and fiscal space.

thread.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
thread.said: He said agencies submitted more than 11,000,000,000,000 pesos in proposals, while the proposed total expenditure program was 7,200,000,000,000 pesos, so not every request could be accommodated.

thread.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
thread.said: The proposed 7,200,000,000,000 peso national budget was equivalent to 21.7% of GDP and was 4.00 7,000,000,000 peso or 6% higher than the FY2026 budget; the comparison figure was garbled in the transcript.

thread.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
thread.said: The NEP consisted of programmed appropriations of 4,494,000,000,000 pesos and automatic appropriations of 2,706,000,000,000 pesos.

thread.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
thread.said: Major automatic appropriations included 1,320,000,000,000 pesos for the national tax allotment, 1,114,000,000,000 for interest payments, 104,200,000,000 pesos for the Bangsamoro block grant, and 89,000,000,000 for retirement and life insurance premiums.

thread.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
thread.said: Unprogrammed appropriations were reduced to 112,000,000,000 pesos, described as the lowest nominal NEP proposal since 2019 and 1.56% of the total expenditure program. DBM clarified that unprogrammed appropriations were standby authority and were not automatically available for release.

thread.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
thread.said: DBM said the proposed budget was based on agency funding requirements, utilization, and implementation capacity, with the objective of ensuring that appropriations were effectively implemented rather than merely approved or released.

thread.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
thread.said: By sector, social services received the largest share at 34.1% or 2,456,000,000,000 pesos, followed by economic services at 25.5% or 1,833,000,000,000 pesos.

thread.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
thread.said: The Department of Education was assigned 975,960,000,000, while higher education received 176,500,000,000; basic and higher education together amounted to 1,326,000,000,000, nearly 4% of GDP.

thread.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
thread.said: The proposed infrastructure investment was 1,467,000,000,000, or 4.4% of GDP, 178,000,000,000 or 13.8% higher than the FY2026 GAA infrastructure level.

thread.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
thread.said: For agriculture and food security, 261,700,000,000 was proposed across the agriculture sector. DSWD was assigned 241,600,000,000, including 99,080,000,000 for the Pantaweed Pamilion Filipino program.

thread.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
thread.said: The National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Fund was proposed at 45,670,000,000, including 14,670,000,000 for disaster rehabilitation and reconstruction assistance and 1,000,000,000 for the People Survival Fund.

thread.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
thread.said: DBM committed to funding government priorities and ensuring delivery through transparency, accountability, fiscal discipline, and integrity, while funding only what was necessary, ready, and capable of delivering public benefit.

thread.speaker: An unnamed presentation voice
thread.said: The accompanying presentation referenced regional hospitals, health facilities, zero-balance billing, PhilHealth, LGU hospitals, and healthcare workers; it also mentioned 352 LGU hospitals for 2027.

topics.topic: Fiscal consolidation, deficit reduction, and spending compression
topics.summary: Secretary Frederic Diko presented fiscal consolidation as a strategy combining stronger revenue collection with better-targeted spending, with the deficit-to-GDP ratio projected to fall from about 5.4% in 2026 to 3.5% by 2030. Minority Leader Marcelino Libanan questioned whether the improvement instead reflected compression of spending, citing declines in revenue and disbursement ratios to GDP. The agency answered that revenues were expected to grow by about nine and a half percent annually and expenditures by 5% to 6% annually in absolute terms, even if both declined relative to GDP. Libanan also highlighted interest payments of 1,114,000,000,000 and their size relative to basic-education funding. The agency attributed the interest burden to debt-financed deficits, citing borrowing of about 1,600,000,000,000 pesos in 2026 and approximately 1,700,000,000,000 pesos the following year, with interest payments of approximately 1,000,000,000,000 pesos and 1,100,000,000,000 pesos, respectively. The agency reaffirmed its commitment to fiscal discipline, but the potential effect of spending compression on priority services remained contested.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish whether the projected reduction in the fiscal deficit would result mainly from stronger revenue collection or from compressing government spending. Members also questioned the level of interest payments and their implications for fiscal discipline and future borrowing.
topics.agency_position: The agency said fiscal consolidation would not require shrinking revenues or expenditures in absolute terms. Revenues were projected to continue growing, while expenditures would also rise but more slowly relative to GDP; reducing the deficit was necessary to contain debt and interest costs.
topics.outcome: The agency answered that both revenues and expenditures would continue to grow in absolute terms, while their ratios to GDP would decline as part of fiscal consolidation. The concern about whether spending compression could affect priority services was raised but not definitively resolved.

positions.position: He questioned whether fiscal consolidation was relying primarily on spending compression, potentially affecting health, social services, and infrastructure, rather than improved revenue collection. He also raised concern about the scale of interest payments relative to other budget priorities.
He maintained that the government was pursuing gradual fiscal consolidation through stronger revenues and better-targeted expenditures, not simply spending less.
The official said revenues and expenditures would continue to grow in absolute terms, but the deficit would be reduced to control debt accumulation and interest payments.

actions.action: The agency undertook to continue practicing fiscal consolidation and reducing the fiscal deficit over time.
The minority leader asked the agency to examine whether the consolidation strategy would compress health, social-service, and infrastructure spending instead of improving collection efficiency.

thread.speaker: Secretary Frederic Diko
thread.said: Secretary Diko presented the government's medium-term fiscal framework as a path of gradual fiscal consolidation intended to reduce the deficit and debt while continuing support for economic recovery and long-term growth.

thread.speaker: Secretary Frederic Diko
thread.said: He said the administration inherited 12,790,000,000,000 in debt in 2022, much of it incurred for pandemic spending.

thread.speaker: Secretary Frederic Diko
thread.said: He said the government aimed to reduce the deficit-to-GDP ratio from 5.4% this year to 3.5% by 2030, while strengthening revenues without relying on new taxes.

thread.speaker: Secretary Frederic Diko
thread.said: Total revenues had grown at an annual average of 10.5% over the preceding four years, tax revenues had grown by an average of 10.47%, and the BIR surpassed 3,000,000,000,000 in tax collections in 2025.

thread.speaker: Secretary Frederic Diko
thread.said: As of June 2026, collections had reached 49.7% of the full-year target. Tax collections in the first half reached 2,140,000,000,000, 5.4% higher than in the same period the prior year.

thread.speaker: Secretary Frederic Diko
thread.said: Disbursements in the first half of 2026 amounted to R3.175 trillion, or 49 percent of the full program. He said the objective was not to spend less but to spend better.

thread.speaker: Secretary Frederic Diko
thread.said: He reported that the fiscal deficit had declined from 8.6% in 2021 and 7.3% in 2022 to 5.6 over the last four years.

thread.speaker: Secretary Frederic Diko
thread.said: The first-half 2026 deficit-to-GDP ratio was 5.46, compared with 5.65% in the same period the prior year. He projected 5.44% in the second half and a full-year ratio of 5.45%.

thread.speaker: Secretary Frederic Diko
thread.said: He said disbursements would grow moderately from 2026 to 2028 and that the government would prioritize spending with the greatest economic and social returns, particularly infrastructure, health, and education.

thread.speaker: Secretary Frederic Diko
thread.said: He said revenues were expected to grow faster than disbursements, with the deficit-to-GDP ratio projected to decline from 5.4% in 2026 to 3.5% by 2030.

thread.speaker: Minority Leader Marcelino Libanan
thread.said: Libanan asked whether the deficit improvement was essentially the result of compressing government spending rather than improving revenue effort, noting that revenues were projected to fall from 15.8% to 15.6% of GDP while disbursements fell from 21.2% to 19.1%.

thread.speaker: An agency official
thread.said: The agency official said revenues were not declining in absolute terms and were projected to grow by an average of about nine plus percent, or nine and a half percent. The reduction cited by Libanan referred to revenues as a percentage of GDP.

thread.speaker: An agency official
thread.said: The official said expenditures would also continue to grow in absolute terms, even though they were expected to slow as a percentage of GDP. Expenditures were expected to grow by 5% to 6% every year.

thread.speaker: An agency official
thread.said: The official said fiscal consolidation meant bringing down the deficit over time, citing a decline from 7.3% to 6.2%, 5.7%, and 5.6%, with a target of 5.45%. This was described as a commitment to the international community and credit-rating agencies.

thread.speaker: Minority Leader Marcelino Libanan
thread.said: Libanan urged the agency to examine whether the consolidation strategy would compress spending for health, social services, and infrastructure instead of relying on more efficient collection.

thread.speaker: Minority Leader Marcelino Libanan
thread.said: Libanan cited total interest payment of 1,114,000,000,000 and compared it with budget figures for basic education, including 909,100 something billion and 948,000,000,000. He asked for the agency's comment.

thread.speaker: An agency official
thread.said: The official said fiscal consolidation was necessary because the deficit was funded by debt. The government was borrowing about 1,600,000,000,000 pesos in 2026 and planned to borrow approximately 1,700,000,000,000 pesos the following year.

thread.speaker: An agency official
thread.said: The official explained that a higher fiscal deficit increased national-government debt relative to GDP and therefore increased interest payments. The government would pay approximately 1,000,000,000,000 pesos in interest payments this year and approximately 1,100,000,000,000 pesos next year.

thread.speaker: Minority Leader Marcelino Libanan
thread.said: Libanan said the budget was more than 5,000,000,000,005 trillion pesos and again emphasized that interest payments alone were 1,114,000,000,000. His references to domestic principal, interest, and percentage comparisons were partly garbled.

thread.speaker: An agency official
thread.said: The official said the budgetary view focused on the cost of the loans, including 1,000,000,000,000 this year and 1,100,000,000,000 next year, while also accounting for loan rollovers and the net interest cost of new loans.

thread.speaker: An agency official
thread.said: The official reiterated that the government's desire to practice fiscal discipline and reduce the fiscal deficit was the reason for the consolidation program.

topics.topic: Public debt and projected interest payments of about 1.114 trillion
topics.summary: The DOF presented fiscal consolidation and debt sustainability as necessary responses to inherited debt and continuing borrowing needs. Minority Leader Marcelino Libanan questioned whether the projected deficit reduction relied mainly on compressing spending, noting that revenue and disbursement shares of GDP were also projected to decline. The DOF answered that revenues and expenditures would continue growing in absolute terms, while their GDP shares would fall, and said expenditures would grow by about 5% to 6% annually. Libanan then highlighted total interest payments of 1,114,000,000,000 and compared them with basic education budget figures. The DOF said borrowing was about 1,600,000,000,000 pesos in 2026 and approximately 1,700,000,000,000 pesos in 2027, with interest payments of approximately 1,000,000,000,000 pesos and 1,100,000,000,000 pesos, respectively. The exchange ended with the agency reiterating fiscal discipline, but the minority's concern about the effect of debt service on program spending was not resolved.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish whether the projected reduction in the deficit would result mainly from compressing government spending rather than improving revenue effort. It also examined the scale of interest payments, borrowing, and debt-service costs relative to the national budget and domestic principal.
topics.agency_position: The DOF maintained that fiscal consolidation was necessary because deficits were financed through debt, and higher debt generated higher interest payments. It said revenues and expenditures would continue growing in absolute terms, while their shares of GDP would decline, and projected interest payments of approximately 1,000,000,000,000 pesos in 2026 and 1,100,000,000,000 pesos in 2027.
topics.outcome: The agency explained the relationship between deficit, borrowing, debt, and interest payments, and defended fiscal consolidation as necessary to contain future debt-service costs. Libanan's concerns about spending compression and the size of interest payments remained contested, with no additional document or corrective calculation provided.

positions.position: He questioned whether deficit reduction was being achieved mainly by compressing spending rather than improving revenue effort, and expressed concern that interest payments of 1,114,000,000,000 were competing with major budget allocations.
He supported gradual fiscal consolidation, a predominantly domestic and fixed-rate debt mix, and a 2027 borrowing program intended to reduce borrowing costs and keep debt sustainable.
The official defended the consolidation path, saying both revenues and expenditures would grow in absolute terms and that reducing deficits was necessary to contain debt and interest costs.

topics.topic: Tax collections and revenue projections under proposed tax measures
topics.summary: Rep. Ryan Recto raised concerns that the projected revenue growth from 2026 to 2030 was optimistic and asked whether it included the progress bill's revenue loss and proposed excise-tax increases. He cited a revenue loss of 85,000,000,000 and noted that rates for measures such as vape excise taxes were not final. The DOF answered that neither the revenue-enhancing nor revenue-eroding measures had been included in the submitted projections. The agency reported strong collection performance, including about 2.14 trillion in first-half 2026 tax collections and projected total national government tax revenues of about 4.4 trillion for the year. It also projected tax-collection growth of about 9% annually through 2028 and total revenues exceeding PHP6 trillion by 2030. The final impact of the proposed measures was left dependent on the legislature's completion of the progress-bill deliberations.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish whether the revenue projections for the budget period already incorporated the effects of proposed revenue-enhancing and revenue-eroding tax measures, including the progress bill and possible excise-tax increases. It also sought to determine whether collections would remain adequate if those measures were enacted with different rates or revenue effects.
topics.agency_position: The DOF stated that the submitted revenue projections excluded both the revenue-enhancing and revenue-eroding effects of the proposed progress-bill measures. It said the ultimate revenue outcome could not yet be determined because the legislature had not finalized the tax rates and other provisions, particularly for excise taxes.
topics.outcome: The DOF confirmed that the proposed revenue-enhancing and revenue-eroding measures were not included in the submitted revenue projections. The final fiscal effect remained dependent on legislative deliberations and the rates ultimately enacted.

positions.position: He viewed the 2026-to-2030 revenue projections as optimistic and sought clarification on whether the projections accounted for the progress bill's potential revenue loss and proposed excise-tax increases.
He maintained that the proposed tax measures were excluded from the projections and that the fiscal effect would depend on the legislation ultimately approved.

topics.topic: Inflation targets, external risks, and contingency subsidies
topics.summary: The BSP reported that inflation had risen to 7.2% in April 2026 before easing to 6.2% in July, and projected averages of 6.4% in 2026, 4.5% in 2027, and about 3.1% in 2028. It based the 2027 budget on headline inflation of about 4% to 5% and Dubai crude oil of roughly 70 to 90 per barrel, while warning that risks remained tilted upward. Secretary Balisacan said elevated inflation threatened recent poverty gains and called for targeted and timely assistance to vulnerable households. Representative Ryan Recto challenged the inflation path as potentially too optimistic in light of the Middle East conflict, trade uncertainty, underspending, and capital-flow risks. He also cited a 105 pesos Dubai crude scenario and the possible risk to 1,400,000 Filipinos. A DBCC budget official answered that regular 2027 budget line items could be mobilized for targeted subsidies and fuel assistance, but no specific amount or operational contingency plan was committed.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish whether the BSP's inflation assumptions for 2026–2028 were realistic given oil-price, Middle East, trade, capital-flow, and domestic implementation risks. It also sought to determine whether the DBCC and the budget contained contingency measures or targeted subsidies if those risks caused renewed inflation and threatened vulnerable households.
topics.agency_position: The BSP said inflation was elevated and risks remained tilted to the upside, but its projections were regularly updated and supported by a 3% target with a plus or minus 1% tolerance range. The DBCC budget official said existing regular budget line items in the 2027 budget could be mobilized for targeted assistance and fuel subsidies if another oil crisis occurred.
topics.outcome: The BSP defended its inflation projections as regularly updated forecasts rather than fixed promises, while acknowledging significant upside risks. The DBCC identified existing 2027 budget line items as a possible source of targeted subsidies and fuel assistance, but no specific contingency amount or detailed trigger mechanism was presented.

positions.position: He questioned whether the BSP's projected decline in inflation was too optimistic given domestic and external risks, and sought assurance that contingency measures would address a renewed oil-price shock.
He maintained that elevated inflation threatened poverty gains and supported targeted, timely assistance for poor and low-income households alongside measures to strengthen domestic food supply.
He stated that the BSP would use monetary policy as necessary to return inflation to target while recognizing the temporary weakness in growth.

thread.speaker: BSP Governor Eli Remolona Jr.
thread.said: Governor Remolona said inflation had eased over the preceding three months but remained well above the BSP's target of three percent, largely because of global supply shocks and their domestic spillovers. He said the BSP had tightened monetary policy twice and was prepared to take further steps as necessary.

thread.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Abenoja
thread.said: Deputy Governor Abenoja said inflation rose from 2.4% in February 2026 to a recent peak of 7.2% in April, then eased to 6.2% by July, but remained above the target of 3%.

thread.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Abenoja
thread.said: He said the BSP raised its target policy rate from 4.25% by 25 basis points each in April and June 2026, bringing the policy rate to 4.75%. The move was intended to anchor inflation expectations and reduce second-round risks while supporting growth.

thread.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Abenoja
thread.said: The BSP's June monetary policy outlook projected headline inflation averaging 6.4% in 2026 and 4.5% in 2027, both above the inflation target of 3%. It said inflation could be around 3.1% by 2028, with risks tilted upward because of global oil prices and inflation expectations.

thread.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Abenoja
thread.said: Abenoja said the external sector provided a buffer against volatile global conditions, although the balance-of-payments deficit was about 1.2% of GDP. He said international reserves stood at almost 105,000,000,000 as of June 2026, equivalent to about seven months of imports of goods and services.

thread.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Abenoja
thread.said: For purposes of the proposed 2027 national budget, the BSP assumed headline inflation of around 4% to 5% for 2027. It also said markets pointed to Dubai crude oil averaging about 70 to 90 per barrel in 2027, while noting that oil prices remained volatile and highly uncertain.

thread.speaker: DEPDEB Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
thread.said: Secretary Balisacan said inflation was expected to remain elevated in 2026, ease to 4% to 5% in 2027, and return to the government's 2% to 4% target range by 2028. He warned that high inflation could slow or reverse recent poverty-reduction gains, particularly because food-price increases disproportionately affect poor and low-income families.

thread.speaker: DEPDEB Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
thread.said: Balisacan identified delayed public investment, governance concerns, severe weather, the prolonged Middle East conflict, elevated global oil and commodity prices, geopolitical tensions, and supply-chain disruptions as risks to the growth and inflation targets. He said the response required timely and coordinated policies.

thread.speaker: DEPDEB Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan

He asked for the basis of the downward targets.

thread.speaker: BSP deputy governor
thread.said: The deputy governor explained that the figures were BSP projections, updated whenever the Monetary Board met, rather than fixed assumptions. The BSP target was 3% average inflation with a plus or minus 1% tolerance range, and policy options would respond to emerging risks.

thread.speaker: Representative Ryan Recto

thread.speaker: Representative Ryan Recto

topics.topic: Infrastructure investment and implementation capacity
topics.summary: Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan and Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon both linked infrastructure execution to economic growth and warned that spending increases alone would not ensure results. DBM proposed capital outlays of about 1.16 trillion, up 13.8%, and Build Better More infrastructure investment of about 1.47 trillion, also 13.8% above the fiscal year 2026 GAA infrastructure level. Rep. Ryan Recto questioned whether the increase could be implemented without recurring underspending, citing a 27.33% shift of resources from GOCCs to DPWH and the economy's two point three percent second-quarter slowdown. Secretary De Leon answered that 2027 infrastructure projects had complete documentary requirements, allowing agencies to begin early procurement before budget enactment. He said this would permit immediate award and implementation after passage of the budget. He confirmed that early procurement would become standard operating practice in the coming years, although actual resolution of underspending remained dependent on agency execution.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish whether the proposed increase in infrastructure and capital-outlay spending could be implemented effectively despite recent underspending and procurement bottlenecks. It said early procurement could address delays by allowing agencies to begin procurement before budget enactment, and confirmed that this mechanism would continue as standard practice in the coming years.
topics.outcome: The committee received DBM's explanation that early procurement, enabled by completing documentary requirements before budget enactment, would address procurement-related implementation delays. DBM confirmed that the mechanism would continue as standard practice, but the broader question of whether the larger infrastructure budget would eliminate underspending remained subject to implementation.

topics.topic: DPWH allocations by district, region, and party-list proponent
topics.summary: Rep. Toby Tiangco renewed his request for an accessible breakdown of DPWH funding by district and party-list representative, noting that the DPWH budget ran to 772 pages. The chair and an agency-side response said the NEP already contained regional and district engineering office totals and project line items, but did not identify project proponents by party-list or congressional district. Rep. Romeo Momo and Rep. Janette Garin clarified that district engineering offices were not necessarily equivalent to congressional districts, while Garin requested regional totals as a better basis for assessing equitable distribution. A member then asked DBM to explain the allocation parameters, including need, population, and land area. Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. topics.question: The committee was trying to establish why proposed NEP amounts for foreign-assisted projects were substantially higher than prior GAA levels, and whether the difference created fiscal space for budget insertions. topics.topic: Electricity prices and their effect on inflation
topics.summary: Rep. Salvador Pleyto raised the effect of rising electricity rates on households and on the prices of goods and services. An agency official said electricity accounted for 5.3% of average household spending, or about 17,057 pesos per year, while the BSP's detailed response on electricity's CPI treatment was partly unclear. Rep. Ryan Recto questioned whether the projected decline in inflation was too optimistic amid domestic and external risks. The BSP cited projections including 6.4% average inflation, a 3% target with a plus-or-minus 1% tolerance range, and regular Monetary Board updates. Recto also raised Dubai crude assumptions of 70 to 90 pesos against a cited 105 pesos and warned that 1,400,000 Filipinos could fall below the poverty threshold. A budget official said regular 2027 budget lines remained available for targeted subsidies and fuel assistance if another crisis occurred.
topics.question: The committee sought to establish how rising electricity prices affected household spending, production costs, and inflation, and how the BSP's inflation targets accounted for domestic and external risks. Members also asked whether the government had contingency measures if energy-price shocks worsened.
topics.agency_position: The BSP presented inflation projections and said forecasts were updated at each Monetary Board meeting, with a 3% average-inflation target and a plus-or-minus 1% tolerance range. The budget side said existing regular line items in the 2027 budget remained available for mobilization, including targeted assistance and fuel subsidies, if another energy-price crisis occurred.
topics.outcome: The BSP defended the inflation framework as a regularly updated projection, but Rep. Recto's concern that the targets might be too optimistic was not fully resolved in the transcript. The budget official stated that existing 2027 budget lines could be used for emergency energy-related assistance.

positions.position: Rising electricity rates were a serious concern because electricity costs affected household expenses and the prices of goods and services, particularly in industrial and manufacturing sectors.

The BSP's declining inflation targets might be too optimistic given domestic underspending, the Middle East crisis, global trade uncertainty, and volatile capital flows; contingency plans were needed for a renewed energy-price shock.
The inflation figures were projections subject to regular updates, and monetary policy would account for identified risks.
Existing regular budget items could be mobilized for targeted subsidies and fuel assistance if a similar crisis occurred.

topics.topic: Economic growth, employment, and poverty-reduction assumptions
topics.summary: DepDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan presented the economic basis for the proposed 2027 budget, reporting strong longer-term growth but a recent slowdown. He cited weaker domestic demand, a contraction in investment, elevated inflation, and confidence and governance concerns, while noting that employment had fallen by 166,000 and unemployment had risen to 4.2%. He reported that poverty incidence had declined from eighteen point one percent in 2021 to nine point seven percent in 2025, lifting 8,800,000 Filipinos out of poverty. Balisacan projected growth of 5% to 6% in the next two years, inflation of 4% to 5% in 2027, and a return to the 2% to 4% target range by 2028. He identified targeted assistance, accelerated infrastructure, implementation-ready social and productive investments, and structural and legislative reforms as the response. The matter remained informational, with no recorded committee question or unresolved disagreement.
topics.question: The committee was seeking the socioeconomic basis for the proposed 2027 national budget: the causes of slower growth, the effects on employment and poverty, and the growth, inflation, and employment assumptions guiding budget priorities. It also sought to establish which structural reforms and public investments DepDev considered necessary to restore inclusive growth.
topics.agency_position: DepDev said the economy had achieved significant growth, employment, and poverty-reduction gains but had recently lost momentum because of weaker demand, confidence problems, inflation, and structural constraints. It maintained that restoring growth required coordinated execution, high-impact public investment, protection for vulnerable households, and legislative and structural reforms.
topics.outcome: DepDev presented the growth, employment, poverty, and inflation assumptions and linked them to budget priorities and structural reforms. No committee challenge, document request, or specific agency undertaking was recorded in the provided stretch.

topics.topic: House budget transparency and pre-plenary treatment
topics.summary: Independent Representative Toby Tiangco asked why the House budget did not receive the same pre-plenary review as other departments and sought equal treatment in the interest of transparency. The committee chair and Kim Robert C. De Leon said that the House budget had historically proceeded directly to plenary, while some other agencies and SUCs followed the same practice. They did not reject the request, but said the decision required House leadership. Tiangco cited House-budget figures including about 30 plus billion, 35,000,000,000, 17,000,000,000, 27,000,000,000, and 10,000,000,000, although several comparisons were unclear in the transcript. Members proposed referring the concern to the Committee on Appropriations and possibly taking it up in plenary. The chair committed to raise the matter with House leadership, but no final ruling or approval was recorded.
topics.question: The committee was trying to establish whether the House of Representatives was legally or constitutionally exempt from pre-plenary budget deliberations. Representative Toby Tiangco also sought to determine whether the House budget would undergo the same transparency review as the budgets of other departments.
topics.agency_position: The committee's stated position was that the House or Congress budget had historically proceeded directly to plenary, as had the budgets of certain other agencies, SUCs, and executive offices, and was not necessarily exempt by a specific ruling established in the exchange. Committee officials supported transparency in principle but said they lacked authority to decide immediately whether a pre-plenary hearing would be held and would refer the request to House leadership.
topics.outcome: The request for equal pre-plenary treatment was referred for consideration by the Committee on Appropriations and House leadership. No final yes-or-no decision or ruling on the point of order was recorded before the requested suspension.

positions.position: The House budget should undergo exactly the same pre-plenary process as the budgets of other departments, as a matter of transparency and equal treatment.

thread.said: Tiangco asked whether any law exempted the House of Representatives from presenting its budget to colleagues before it went to plenary.

thread.speaker: Committee chair
thread.said: The chair said that in previous years some agencies, state universities and colleges, and other executive offices had gone directly to plenary without pre-plenary hearings. She said the practice was not limited to the House or Congress.

thread.speaker: Toby Tiangco, independent representative
thread.said: Tiangco contrasted the House budget with the DOST budget, saying the House budget was 30 plus billion and that DOST received a pre-plenary hearing.

thread.speaker: Toby Tiangco, independent representative
thread.said: He referred to the 2025, 2026, and 2027 House budget proposals and described an original budget, a proposed House insertion, and a net total budget. The relationships among the figures were unclear in the transcript.

thread.speaker: Toby Tiangco, independent representative
thread.said: Tiangco requested that the House budget be subjected to the same process as other departments, invoking transparency and asking about the constitutional provisions or legal basis for any exemption.

thread.speaker: Committee chair
thread.said: The chair said the House budget had been presented during plenary in the previous year, with deliberations opened by the vice chairpersons and members given an opportunity to ask questions.

thread.speaker: Kim Robert C. De Leon, committee official
thread.said: De Leon said that if the request was for a pre-plenary hearing on the Congress budget, it would be submitted for consideration by House leadership because the decision was not solely about the Congress of the Philippines budget.

thread.speaker: Toby Tiangco, independent representative
thread.said: Tiangco challenged why the matter had to be submitted elsewhere, saying the issue was transparency and asking for a clear yes-or-no response.

thread.speaker: Kim Robert C. De Leon, committee official
thread.said: De Leon said the committee was one with Tiangco on transparency, but the exchange did not establish an immediate approval.

thread.speaker: Kim Robert C. De Leon, committee official
thread.said: De Leon clarified that he was not saying no, but could not say yes because the decision belonged to House leadership. He cited reforms to promote transparency, including bar-by-bar and line-by-line review and scrutiny of bicameral conference committee amendments.

thread.speaker: Toby Tiangco, independent representative
thread.said: Tiangco said the response was neither a yes nor a no and asked what the problem was and why the House leadership could not be asked directly.

thread.speaker: Kim Robert C. De Leon, committee official
thread.said: De Leon repeated that he could not decide the matter during the hearing and would submit it for deliberation by House leadership. He asked for time to obtain that decision.

thread.speaker: Toby Tiangco, independent representative
thread.said: Tiangco said the response provided no assurance and cited figures for 20.25, 1,016,000,000,000, an insertion of 17,000,000,000, and a 35,000,000,000 House budget; the comparison was unclear in the transcript. He also cited 20.26, 17,000,000,000 net, 27,000,000,000 insertion, and 10,000,000,000.

thread.speaker: Kim Robert C. De Leon, committee official
thread.said: De Leon disputed the characterization of the amounts as an insertion, saying the Congress budget had been deliberated in plenary even though it had not received a pre-plenary hearing. He said all members had been given an opportunity to question the budget sponsor.

thread.speaker: Tony Bell, member
thread.said: Bell raised a point of order, arguing that the issue could be taken up with House leadership rather than consuming the time allotted for members' questions to the DBCC and other guests.

thread.speaker: Toby Tiangco, independent representative
thread.said: Tiangco said he wanted the chair to rule on whether he was out of order and continued referring to department-level budget treatment. His intervening figures, including 11,000,000,000,000 and 11,000,000,007 trillion, were unclear in context.

thread.speaker: Committee chair
thread.said: The chair said she would rule on the point of order after recognizing Deputy Speaker Janette Garin.

thread.speaker: Janette Garin, deputy speaker
thread.said: Garin proposed referring Tiangco's concern to the Committee on Appropriations for deliberation as soon as possible, while allowing the hearing to proceed with the DBCC's pre-plenary deliberations.

thread.speaker: Tony Bell, member
thread.said: Bell maintained that the point of order should be addressed first, while allowing Tiangco to use his remaining time for questions relevant to the DBCC discussion. He argued that an unrelated procedural issue should be taken up with leadership.

thread.speaker: Committee chair
thread.said: The chair asked Tiangco to accept referral of the matter to the executive committee of the Committee on Appropriations instead of ruling on the point of order during the DBCC hearing. She assured him that she would raise it with House leadership for deliberation and decision and report back as soon as possible.

thread.speaker: A member identified as Representative Arisa
thread.said: The member suggested that after discussion by the executive committee, the issue should be deliberated in plenary, including the question of equitable treatment of resources among representatives.

thread.speaker: Committee chair
thread.said: The chair acknowledged the concerns raised by Tiangco and the other member and again asked for time to refer the matter to House leadership and for the Committee on Appropriations to take appropriate action.

thread.speaker: Toby Tiangco, independent representative
thread.said: Tiangco reiterated that he had raised the matter during the hearing and again asked the chair to rule on Deputy Speaker Garin's point of order.

thread.speaker: Janette Garin, deputy speaker
thread.said: Garin requested a brief suspension. The transcript does not record a final ruling on the point of order or a decision on the requested pre-plenary treatment.

topics.topic: Regional and local government allocations and barangay development program
topics.summary: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon presented the regional and local-government components of the proposed FY 2027 budget. He said local government units would receive about 1.533 trillion, including a proposed NTA of COP 1,320,000,000,000, roughly P129.3 billion above the current-year amount. He reported that about 4.603 trillion, or 63.9% of the proposed national budget, would be directly allocated to the regions, with allocations for the National Capital Region, Luzon, the Visayas, and Mindanao. He also identified 115,620,000,000 pesos for the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao and 58,530,000,000 for the Local Government Support Fund. The latter included LGU financial assistance, the Growth Equity Fund, and the barangay development program. The presentation was informational, with no recorded committee objection or follow-up action.
topics.question: How did the proposed FY 2027 National Expenditure Program distribute resources among regions, local government units, and barangays, and what funding was provided for local-government support and development programs?
topics.agency_position: The DBM presented the proposed allocations as a deliberate effort to direct a substantial share of national resources to regions and local governments. It emphasized that the NTA, Bangsamoro funding, Local Government Support Fund, Growth Equity Fund, and barangay development program were intended to support devolved services, local infrastructure, social services, and community development.
topics.outcome: The DBM completed its presentation of the regional and local-government allocations, including the proposed funding for the barangay development program. No committee challenge, amendment, document request, or separate undertaking on this topic was recorded.

thread.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
thread.said: Secretary De Leon said a major source of the budget increase was the higher national tax allotment for local government units, along with other mandatory fiscal obligations.

thread.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
thread.said: He presented automatic appropriations including 1,320,000,000,000 pesos for the national tax allotment of local government units and 104,200,000,000 pesos for the annual block grant of the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao.

thread.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
thread.said: He said local government units would receive 1,533,000,000,000 pesos. The proposed NTA was COP 1,320,000,000,000, compared with around P1.191 trillion in the current year, an increase of roughly P129.3 billion.

thread.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
thread.said: He reported that 4,603,000,000,000, or 63.9% of the proposed national budget, would be directly allocated to the regions. The regional amounts were 1,112,000,000,000 for the National Capital Region, 1,659,000,000,000 for Luzon, 744,800,000,000 for the Visayas, and 1,088,000,000,000 for Mindanao.

thread.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
thread.said: He said the remaining 36.1%, or 2,597,000,000,000 pesos, was non-regionalized, consisting of nationwide allocations and central-office allocations. He clarified that nationwide allocations should not be mistaken for Metro Manila because they would eventually benefit regions and beneficiaries nationwide.

thread.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
thread.said: He said 1,320,000,000,000 would be provided for the national tax allotment so local government units could deliver devolved services, and 115,620,000,000 pesos would support peace, self-governance, and long-term development in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao.

thread.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
thread.said: He said 58,530,000,000 would be allocated for the Local Government Support Fund, including financial assistance to LGUs, the Growth Equity Fund, and the barangay development program.

thread.speaker: Acting DBM Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon
thread.said: He said the Local Government Support Fund and its components would enable local governments to implement priority infrastructure, social-service, and community-development projects that directly benefit their constituents.

hearings.title: PART II COMMITTEE ON APPROPRIATIONS - BUDGET BRIEFING/HEARINGS OF THE FY 2027 PROPOSED BUDGET (DOH)

topics.topic: DOH budget consideration
topics.summary: The committee was considering the proposed DOH budget when the Deputy Minority Leader raised the need to defer further consideration. He said approximately 29 majority members had already raised questions and issues concerning the DOH budget and its leadership. The committee approved suspension of consideration without objection and scheduled resumption for Monday, September 7.

topics.topic: Pending interpellation of the Health Secretary
topics.summary: The Deputy Minority Leader stated that members still intended to interpellate the Health Secretary. The pending questions were cited as the reason not to complete consideration of the DOH budget during the sitting. No substantive answers from the Health Secretary were recorded in these sections.

topics.topic: Questions and issues raised by majority members
topics.summary: The Deputy Minority Leader reported that approximately 29 majority members had provided input, questions, or issues concerning the DOH budget and its leadership. The transcript does not enumerate those issues or provide agency responses to them. Their consideration was therefore deferred with the budget.

topics.topic: DOH leadership
topics.summary: The Deputy Minority Leader referred to the DOH under Secretary Mercado while explaining the leadership-related issues raised by members. The precise wording and context of the reference are partly unclear in the machine-generated transcript. No leadership action or agency response was recorded before suspension.

topics.topic: PhilHealth leadership
topics.summary: The exchange also referred to PhilHealth under President-CEO Beverly. The transcript does not clearly state the full name of Beverly or the specific issue concerning PhilHealth leadership. No resolution or response on the PhilHealth matter was recorded.

topics.topic: Suspension of DOH budget consideration
topics.summary: The Deputy Minority Leader moved to suspend consideration of the proposed DOH budget. The motion was seconded and the Chair asked whether there was any objection. Hearing none, the committee approved the suspension.

topics.topic: Resumption schedule for the DOH budget
topics.summary: The Chair stated that consideration of the DOH budget would resume on Monday, September 7. The time was to be determined by the Chair of the Committee on Appropriations. The record does not show the resumption itself within the provided sections.

topics.topic: Suspension of House Bill No. 10858 hearing
topics.summary: A member identified by the Chair as Tongjila moved to suspend the committee hearing at Ramaldas Hall on House Bill No. 10858. The Deputy Minority Leader seconded the motion. With no objection, the Chair declared the hearing suspended until September 3, 2026, at 9 AM.
